name: Napa
uses: Commonly used in Nepal for fever and mild headache.

name: Flexon
uses: Used for toothache, body ache, and joint pain.
side_effects: Can cause acidity or gastric irritation.

name: ALUMINIUM HYDROXIDE
indications: Ulcer and non ulcer dyspepsia; gastro-oesophageal reflux.
dosage_schedule: Tablets: 1-2 tablets chewed 4 times a day and at bed time or as required; Suspension: 5-10 ml 4 times daily between meals and at bedtime; Children (6-12 years): up to 5 ml 3 times daily
adverse_effects: Constipation, haemorrhoids, fissures, faecal impaction

name: MAGNESIUM HYDROXIDE
indications: Ulcer and non ulcer dyspepsia, gastro-oesophageal reflux
dosage_schedule: 250-500 mg, per oral 3-4 times a day
adverse_effects: Diarrhoea in renal impairment, respiratory depression, hypotension, loss of tendon reflexes, cardiac arrest

name: ATROPINE SULPHATE
indications: Gastrointestinal spasm, renal colic, anesthetic premedication, OP poisoning
dosage_schedule: Premedication: intravenous injection, 200-600 micrograms immediately before induction of anesthesia and in incremental doses of 100 micrograms for the treatment of bradycardia; intramuscular injection, 300-600 micrograms 30-60 minutes before induction; child 20 micrograms/kg; For control of muscarinic side effects of neostigmine: in reversal of competitive neuromuscular block, by intravenous injection, 0.6-1.2 mg; Bradycardia: particularly complicated by hypotension after myocardial infarction, intravenous injection of 300 micrograms, increasing to 1 mg if necessary; Antidote to organophosphorous poisoning: by intramuscular or intravenous injection, 1 to 2 mg, repeated in 20-30 minutes as soon as cyanosis has cleared
adverse_effects: Dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention, blurred vision

name: DROTAVERINE
indications: Gastrointestinal colicky pain, renal colic, 1st stage of labour (dilation of cervical opening)
dosage_schedule: 40-80 mg 3 times per day
adverse_effects: Nausea, vomiting, fainting, dry mouth

name: FLAVOXATE HYDROCHLORIDE
indications: Increased urinary frequency and incontinence, bladder spasms due to catheterization, urgency, dysuria
dosage_schedule: 200 mg 3 times daily
adverse_effects: Same as in hyoscine, fatigue, vertigo

name: HYOSCINE BUTYL BROMIDE
indications: Symptomatic GI and pain to urinary spasm, irritable bowel syndrome, excessive respiratory secretion, bowel colic
dosage_schedule: 10 mg 3 times a day; 4 to 20 mg 4 times a day
adverse_effects: Headache, confusion, dizziness, hallucination, palpitation, tachycardia, blurred vision, tachycardia, blurred vision, photophobia, cycloplegia, dry mouth, constipation, paralytic ileus

name: MEBEVERINE HYDROCHLORIDE
indications: Irritable bowel syndrome, other spasmodic conditions
dosage_schedule: 135-150 mg 3 times a day to be taken 20 minutes before meal
adverse_effects: Allergic reaction, angioedema, urticaria, rash

name: CIMETIDINE
indications: see Ranitidine
dosage_schedule: Benign ulcer (oral): 400 mg twice daily followed by 800 mg once at night for 4 weeks, maintainence 400 mg at night; Child: 25-30 mg/kg; Infant: 20 mg/kg in divided doses; Injection(IM): 200 mg every 4-6 hrs, Injection(IM): 200 mg slowly over 2 minutes; IV infusion: 400 mg in 100 ml of normal saline over ½-1 hours, 50-100 mg/hour over 24 hrs for continuous infection
adverse_effects: See ranitidine, gynaecomastia, microsomal enzyme inhibition and hepatotoxicity are higher

name: ESOMEPRAZOLE
indications: See omeprazole
dosage_schedule: Duodenal ulcer associated with H. pylori: 20 mg twice daily; NSAID associated GU: 20mg once daily for 4-8 weeks; for prophylaxis with increase rate of gastroduodenal complication who require continued NSAID treatment 20 mg daily; GERD: 40 mg once daily for 4 weeks, continued for further 4 weeks if not fully healed or symptom persist, maintenance 20 mg daily
adverse_effects: See omeprazole

name: FAMOTIDINE
indications: See ranitidine
dosage_schedule: Benign ulcer: Oral 40 mg at night for 4-8 weeks, maintenance dose 20 mg at night; Reflux oesophagitis: 20-40 mg twice daily for 5-12 weeks; Zollinger–Ellison syndrome: 20 mg every 6 hours
adverse_effects: See ranitidine

name: LANSOPRAZOLE
indications: See omeprazole
dosage_schedule: Duodenal ulcer: 30 mg daily in morning for 4 week, maintenance 15 mg daily; Benign gastric ulcer: 30 mg daily in morning for 8 week; NSAID associated duodenal or gastric ulcer: 15-30 mg once daily for 4 weeks continued for further 4 weeks if not fully healed; Reflux oesophagitis: 30 mg daily in morning for 4 weeks, continued for further 4 weeks if not fully healed; Zollinger-Ellison syndrome: initially 60 mg once daily adjusted according to response, daily dose of 120 mg or more given in two divided doses; Reflux oesophagitis refractory to other treatment: 40 mg for 8 weeks
adverse_effects: See omeprazole

name: OMEPRAZOLE
indications: Benign gastric and duodenal ulcer, NSAID associated duodenal or gastric ulcer, duodenal or benign gastric ulcer associated with Helicobacter pylori, reflux oesophagitis, Zollinger–Ellison syndrome, stress ulcer
dosage_schedule: Adult: 20 mg/day for 4-8 week
adverse_effects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal colic, skin rash, headache and dizziness

name: PANTOPRAZOLE
indications: See omeprazole
dosage_schedule: Duodenal ulcer: 40 mg daily in the morning for 2 weeks; Benign gastric ulcer: 40mg daily in the morning for 2 weeks
adverse_effects: See omeprazole

name: RABEPRAZOLE
indications: See omeprazole
dosage_schedule: Benign gastric ulcer: 20 mg daily in the morning for 6 weeks, continued for further 6 weeks if not fully healed; Duodenal ulcer: 20 mg daily in the morning for 4 week continued for further 4 week if not fully healed; GERD: 20 mg once daily for 4-8 weeks, maintenance 10-20mg daily
adverse_effects: See omeprazole

name: RANITIDINE
indications: Benign duodenal and gastric ulcer, reflux oesophagitis, Zollinger–Ellison syndrome, GERD, stress ulcer
dosage_schedule: Benign ulcer: oral 150 mg twice daily, 300 mg at night for 4-8 weeks; Chronic episodic dyspepsia: 6 weeks; NSAID induced ulcer: for 8 weeks; Reflex oesophagitis: 150 mg twice daily, 300 mg at night for 8 weeks, or if necessary 12 weeks; Gastric acid reduction (Prophylaxis of acid aspiration in obstetric): oral – 150 mg at onset of labour, then every 6 hours; Surgical procedure: IM or slow IV injection, 50 mg 45-60 minutes before induction of anaesthesia, oral 150 mg 2 hours before induction of anaesthesia, IM 50 mg every 6-8 hours IV infusion, 25 mg/hour for 2 hours, repeated every 6-8 hours
adverse_effects: Headache, dizziness, myalgia, nausea, skin rash and diarrhoea or constipation

name: SUCRALFATE
indications: Benign gastric and duodenal ulceration, chronic gastritis
dosage_schedule: 2 g twice daily (on rising and at bed time) for 4-6 week or in resistant case 12 weeks, morning 8 g daily; Prophylaxis of NSAIDs induced ulcer (suspension) 1 g 6 times daily (maximum 8 g daily)
adverse_effects: Not listed yet

name: CYCLIZINE
indications: Prevention and treatment of nausea, vomiting and vertigo associated with motion sickness
dosage_schedule: Motion sickness: 50 mg 30 minutes before traveling, can be repeated in 6 hours (up to 200 mg/day), 6-12 hours, 25 mg up to 3 times/day not to exceed 75 mg/day
adverse_effects: Drowsiness, xerostomia, headache, dermatitis, urinary retention, diplopia

name: DIMENHYDRINATE
indications: Prevention of motion sickness, Meniere’s disease
dosage_schedule: Prevention of motion sickness: 50-100 mg 4-6 hours or 30 minutes before traveling (not to exceed 400mg/day); Meniere’s disease: 50 mg intra-muscular for acute attack, 25-50 mg 8 hourly for maintenance
adverse_effects: Paradoxical CNS stimulation (children & occasionally in adults), CNS depression, dizziness

name: DOMPERIDONE
indications: Antiemetic, gastrokinetic to accelerate gastric emptying, dyspepsia, GERD (Gastro esophageal reflux disease)
dosage_schedule: Acute nausea and vomiting: 10-20 mg 6-8 hours (child 0.25-0.5 mg/kg); Functional dyspepsia: 10-20 mg 3 times daily before food for maximum of 12 hours
adverse_effects: Galactorrhoea, gynaecomastia, decreased libido, skin rashes

name: METOCLOPRAMIDE
indications: Nausea and vomiting in GI disorders and treatment with cytotoxic or radiotherapy, GERD, gastroparesis, premedication and post operatively
dosage_schedule: Nausea and vomiting, GERD, Gastroparesis: Adult: 10 mg 3 times daily (children 2-5 mg/kg); Premedication: 10 mg single dose; Aid to gastrointestinal procedure: 10-20 mg as single dose 5-10 minutes before examination
adverse_effects: Extrapyramidal symptoms (children and young adult), tardive dyskinesia on prolonged use, hyperprolactinemia, drowsiness, dizziness, restlessness, headache, neuroleptic malignant syndrome, rashes, pruritus, cardiac conduction abnormalities following IV administration

name: ONDANSETRON
indications: Chemotherapy induced nausea and vomiting, post operative nausea and vomiting, radiation induced nausea and vomiting, uremic pruritus, rosacea, hyperemesis gravidarum
dosage_schedule: Chemotherapy induced nausea and vomiting: moderate - 8 mg started 30 minutes prior, highly emetogenic 24 mg; IV - 0.15 mg/kg over 15 minutes, 30 minutes prior to chemotherapy then 4 and 8 hours; Postoperative nausea and vomiting : 4 mg IV/IM before anaesthesia as after procedures; Radiation induced nausea and vomiting: 8 mg PO 1-2 hours before radiation, subsequent doses every 8 hours; Cholestatic pruritus: 8 mg 12 hours or 8 hours for 7 days; Uremic pruritus: 8 mg 12 hours or 8 hours for 14 days, Child below 4 years of age: Safety and efficacy not established, can be given 0.1 mg/kg IV in postoperative nausea & vomiting
adverse_effects: Headache, constipation, hiccups, flushing, transient visual disturbances, involuntary movements, dizziness, arrhythmia, hypotension

name: PROCHLORPERAZINE
indications: Postoperative nausea and vomiting, chemotherapy induced nausea and vomiting, vertigo, psychosis
dosage_schedule: Acute attack of vomiting: 20 mg initially then 10 mg after 2 hours; Prevention of nausea and vomiting: 5-10 mg 2-3 times daily (0.25 mg/kg); Labyrinthine disorders: 5 mg 3 times daily (up to 30 mg daily in divided doses)
adverse_effects: Muscle dystonia and other extrapyramidal side effect, dry mouth, drowsiness

name: PROMETHAZINE
indications: Nausea, vomiting, motion sickness, pre-operative and post-operative sedation, obstetric sedation
dosage_schedule: Nausea and vomiting: PO/PR 12.5-25 mg 4-6 hours, IV/IM 12.5-25 mg 4-6 hours; Motion sickness: 25 mg PO/PR 30-60 minutes before travel; Pre-operative sedation: 50 mg PO/PR on night before procedure; Post-operative: 25-50 mg IV/IM combined with reduced doses of analgesics; Allergic conditions: 25 mg at bedtime or 12.5 mg (PO/PR), 25 mg may be repeated in 2 hours (IV/IM)
adverse_effects: Sedation, blurred vision, confusion, hallucination, disorientation, extrapyramidal symptoms

name: DIPHENOXYLATE
indications: Acute diarrhoea, chronic mild ulcerative colitis
dosage_schedule: Initial dose for adults is 4 tablets, followed by 2 tablets every 6 hours until diarrhoea is controlled. Maintenance dose as low as ¼th of initial dose
adverse_effects: Blurred vision, sedation, nausea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort, dryness of mouth, urinary retention

name: LOPERAMIDE
indications: Acute nonspecific diarrhoea, chronic diarrhoea, faecal incontinence, pain of intestinal colic
dosage_schedule: Acute diarrhoea: Initially 4 mg, followed by 2 mg for up to 5 days; usual dose 6 to 8 mg daily; maximum 16 mg per day; Chronic diarrhoea: Initially 4 to 8 mg daily in divided doses; subsequently adjusted accordance to response, maintenance up to 16 mg daily in 2 divided doses
adverse_effects: Dizziness, drowsiness, fatigue, flatulence, headache, nausea

name: ORAL REHYDRATION SALTS
indications: Dehydration from acute diarrhoea
dosage_schedule: Fluid and electrolyte loss in acute diarrhoea: oral - adult 200-400 ml solution after every loose motion; infant 1-1.5 times usual feed volume; child 200 ml after every loose motion
adverse_effects: Vomiting (too rapid administration), hypernatremia and hyperkalaemia (overdose in renal impairment or administration of too concentrated solution)

name: RIFAXIMIN
indications: Traveller’s diarrhoea, hepatic encephalopathy, irritable bowel syndrome
dosage_schedule: Traveller’s diarrhoea: oral, 200mg TDS for 3 days; Hepatic encephalopathy (maintenance of remission): oral, 550mg BD; Irritable bowel syndrome: oral, 550 mg TDS for 14 days
adverse_effects: Flatulence, rectal tenesmus, abdominal pain, defecation urgency, constipation, nausea, vomitting

name: ZINC SULFATE
indications: Adjunct to ORS in acute diarrhoea
dosage_schedule: Infants<6 months: 10 mg daily for 10-14 days; Child 6 months-5 years ronic diarrhoea: 20 mg daily for 10-14 days
adverse_effects: Abdominal pain, dyspepsia, Nausea, Vomiting, Diarrhoea, Headache, Gastric irritation

name: ISPAGHULA HUSK
indications: Constipation
dosage_schedule: 0.5-2 gm/day (3 tea spoonful) at bed time, children ½ of adult dose
adverse_effects: Abdominal distension, flatulence

name: DOCUSATE SODIUM
indications: Constipation, adjunct to radiological procedure (with Barium meal 400 mg)
dosage_schedule: 50-300 mg per oral single or divided dose (up to 500 mg), initially large dose, gradually decrease dose, with barium meal 400 mg
adverse_effects: Rashes, transient abdominal cramping pain

name: LIQUID PARAFFIN
indications: Constipation
dosage_schedule: 10-30 ml at night
adverse_effects: Lipoid pneumonia due to aspiration, interfere fat soluble vitamin absorption, Foreign body granulomatous lesion on mesenteric, liver and spleen

name: BISACODYL
indications: Constipations, bowel preparation for radiology and surgery
dosage_schedule: Constipation: 5-10 mg (oral) at night, 10 mg at morning suppository; Radiological procedure: 10 mg per oral at night then 10 mg suppository at morning, 1 hour before procedure; Paediatric: >6 yr, 5 mg per oral at night, <10 yrs, 5 mg suppository; Radiological procedure: 5 mg by mouth at night, 5 mg per rectal at morning
adverse_effects: Abdominal cramp, local irritation

name: SENNA
indications: Constipation, bowel preparation for radiological and surgical procedure
dosage_schedule: Constipation: Adult: 2-4 tablets at night, Children (>6 years): ½ of adult dose; Bowel preparation: 1 mg/kg in two divided doses
adverse_effects: Abdominal cramps

name: LACTULOSE
indications: Constipation, hepatic encephalopathy
dosage_schedule: Constipation: adult, 15 ml per oral twice daily (not more than 60ml/day) gradually titrate the dose to produce 2-3 soft stool/day; Children: <1 year, 2.5 ml twice a day titrate according to stool frequency, 1-5 years, 5 ml twice a day titrate according to stool frequency, >6-12 years – 10 ml twice a day, titrate according to stool frequency; Hepatic encephalopathy: 30-45 ml (20-30 g) per oral to induce rapid detection, 30-45 ml per oral after 6-8 hours
adverse_effects: Dehydration, hypernatremia, abdominal distension

name: MACROGOL 3350
indications: Constipation, fecal impaction
dosage_schedule: Constipation: dissolve 1 sachet in 125 ml of water, to be taken 1-3 times/day as required; Fecal impaction: dissolve 1 sachet in 125 ml of water, 8 sachets to be taken within 6 hours, up to 3 days if required
adverse_effects: Diarrhoea, dehydration, indigestion, pain abdomen, allergic reactions

name: MAGNESIUM HYDROXIDE (MILK OF MAGNESIA)
indications: Constipation, acid peptic disease
dosage_schedule: Constipation: 30-60 ml/day per oral at bed time (400 mg/5ml); Acid peptic disease: 5-15 ml (400 mg/5ml) per oral in 4 divided doses, 2-4 tab/day chewable tables
adverse_effects: Abdominal cramp, electrolyte imbalance, hypotension

name: MAGNESIUM SULPHATE
indications: Constipation, hypomagnesemia, eclampsia/severe preeclampsia, preterm labor, torsades de pointes
dosage_schedule: Constipation: 5-10 g dissolved in 24 ml of water
adverse_effects: Flaccid paralysis, circulatory collapse, nausea, vomiting, electrolyte and fluid disturbance

name: POLYETHYLENE GLYCOL 3350
indications: Constipation
dosage_schedule: Constipation: 17 g, after reconstitution in a glass of water
adverse_effects: Nausea, abdominal bloating, cramping and flatulence, diarrhoea and excessive stool frequency

name: ADALIMUMAB
indications: Crohn’s disease, ulcerative colitis, rheumatic and psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, plaque psoriasis
dosage_schedule: Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis: subcutaneous, initial: 160 mg (given on day 1 or split and given over 2 consecutive days), then 80 mg 2 weeks later (day 15), maintenance: 40 mg every other week beginning day 29
adverse_effects: Hypersensitivity, abdominal pain, increased serum ALT, infection, infusion related reaction

name: BUDESONIDE
indications: Treatment of mild to moderate active Crohn’s disease
dosage_schedule: Treatment of mild to moderate active Crohn’s disease: 9 mg orally once daily for up to 8 weeks; Maintenance of clinical remission of mild to moderate Crohn’s disease: 6 mg orally once daily for maintenance of clinical remission up to 3 months (if symptom control maintained, taper doses to complete cessation)
adverse_effects: Increased risk of infection, abdominal pain, flatulence, vomitting and other corticosteroid related systemic adverse effects

name: HYDROCORTISONE ACETATE
indications: Ulcerative colitis, proctitis, proctosigmoiditis
dosage_schedule: Suppository 25 mg twice daily for 2 weeks – can be increased up to 25 mg 3 times daily or 50 mg twice daily
adverse_effects: Local pain/burning sensation, rectal bleeding, exacerbation of untreated infections

name: INFLIXIMAB
indications: Crohn’s disease, ulcerative colitis
dosage_schedule: Crohn disease: adult, IV: 5 mg/kg at 0, 2, and 6 weeks, followed by 5 mg/kg every 8 weeks thereafter; Children ≥6 years and adolescents, IV: 5 mg/kg at 0, 2, and 6 weeks, followed by 5 mg/kg every 8 weeks thereafter; Ulcerative colitis: IV: 5 mg/kg at 0, 2, and 6 weeks, followed by 5 mg/kg every 8 weeks thereafter, children ≥6 years and adolescents, IV, 5 mg/kg at 0, 2, and 6 weeks, followed by 5 mg/kg every 8 weeks thereafter
adverse_effects: Hypersensitivity, abdominal pain, increased serum ALT, infection, infusion related reaction

name: MESALAZINE
indications: Ulcerative colitis (acute attack, maintenance of remission). maintenance of remission of Crohn’s ileo-colitis
dosage_schedule: Maintenance of remission of ulcerative colitis (UC) and Crohn’s ileo-colitis: Adult 1.2-2.4 g daily in divided dosage, child 12-17 years 400-800 mg 3 times/day; Treatment of mild to moderate UC and acute attack: Adult 2.4 g daily in divided dosage, child 12-17 years 800 mg 3 times a day
adverse_effects: Dizziness, oligospermia, abdominal pain, flatulence and headache

name: SULFASALAZINE
indications: Ulcerative colitis, active Crohn’s disease, active rheumatoid arthritis
dosage_schedule: Ulcerative colitis: adult (oral) - 1-2 g QID in acute attack until remission maintenance dose 500 mg QID, child > 2 yrs 400 -60 mg/kg in acute attack, reducing to maintenance dose 20-30 mg/kg daily; Active Crohn’s disease: adult (oral) 1-2 g QID in acute attack until omission occurs, child >2 year 40-60 mg/kg daily in acute attack; Ulcerative colitis, Crohn’s disease: by reactive suppositories, 0.5-1 g morning & evening after bowel movement, by rectum (retention enema), 3 gm at night for at least an hour
adverse_effects: Nausea, vomiting, exacerbation of colitis, diarrhoea, loss of appetite, fever, blood disorders, hypersensitivity, lung complications (eosinophilia, fibrosing alveolitis), periorbital edema

name: OCTREOTIDE
indications: Esophageal variceal bleeding, acromegaly, carcinoid tumor, VIPoma
dosage_schedule: Esophageal variceal bleeding: 50 mcg IV bolus, then 25-50 mcg/hr for 1-5 days
adverse_effects: See under section 12.6

name: TERLIPRESSIN
indications: Bleeding from esophageal varices
dosage_schedule: Initially 2 mg every 4-6 hours until bleeding is controlled, then 1 mg every 4-6 hour for maximum up to 48 hours
adverse_effects: Abdominal cramps, headache, cardiac arrhythmias

name: URSODEOXYCHOLIC ACID
indications: Used in dissolution of gallstones, primary biliary cirrhosis
dosage_schedule: Dissolution of gall stones: 8-12 mg/kg daily as a single dose at bedtime or in two divided doses, for up to 2 years; treatment is continued for 3-4 months after stones dissolve; Primary biliary cirrhosis: 10-15 mg/kg daily in 2-4 divided doses
adverse_effects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, gallstone calcification, pruritus

name: PROBIOTICS
indications: Infective diarrhoea, antibiotic associated diarrhoea, risk of traveller’s diarrhoea
dosage_schedule: Since there are so many different probiotic organisms, there is no set dosage. Probiotics are dosed by number of live organisms (cells) they contain. Typical dosage of lactobacillus ranges between 1-10 billion cells divided into 3 or 4 doses
adverse_effects: Infection, acidosis (rare)

name: ALUMINIUM HYDROXIDE
indications: Ulcer and non ulcer dyspepsia; gastro-oesophageal reflux.
dosage_schedule: Tablets: 1-2 tablets chewed 4 times a day and at bed time or as required; Suspension: 5-10 ml 4 times daily between meals and at bedtime; Children (6-12 years): up to 5 ml 3 times daily.
contraindications: Hypophosphatemia, undiagnosed GI or rectal bleeding, appendicitis, porphyria.
precautions: Renal impairment (aluminium may accumulate), constipation, hepatic impairment, dehydration.
adverse_effects: Constipation, haemorrhoids, fissures, faecal impaction.

name: MAGNESIUM HYDROXIDE
indications: Ulcer and non ulcer dyspepsia, gastro-oesophageal reflux.
dosage_schedule: See under ALUMINIUM HYDROXIDE; Adult: 250-500 mg, per oral 3-4 times a day.
precautions: Renal impairment, hepatic impairment.
adverse_effects: Diarrhoea in renal impairment, respiratory depression, hypotension, loss of tendon reflexes, cardiac arrest.

name: ATROPINE SULPHATE
indications: Gastrointestinal spasm, renal colic, anesthetic premedication, OP poisoning.
dosage_schedule: Premedication (Adult): IV 200-600 mcg immediately before anesthesia or IM 300-600 mcg 30-60 min before induction; Child: 20 mcg/kg. Bradycardia: IV 300 mcg increasing up to 1 mg. OP Poisoning: IM/IV 1-2 mg every 20-30 min.
contraindications: Angle closure glaucoma, hypersensitivity, tachycardia secondary to cardiac insufficiency or thyrotoxicosis.
precautions: Use in pregnancy only when potential benefits justify possible risk to fetus.
adverse_effects: Dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention, blurred vision.

name: DROTAVERINE
indications: Gastrointestinal colicky pain, renal colic, 1st stage of labour (dilation of cervical opening).
dosage_schedule: 40-80 mg 3 times per day.
contraindications: Paralytic ileus, gall bladder disease, diabetes, depression, ulcerative colitis, heart disease, liver disease, kidney disease.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Nausea, vomiting, fainting, dry mouth.

name: FLAVOXATE HYDROCHLORIDE
indications: Increased urinary frequency and incontinence, bladder spasms, urgency, dysuria.
dosage_schedule: 200 mg 3 times daily.
contraindications: Obstructive uropathy, ileus, GI obstruction, GI bleeding, glaucoma.
precautions: Do not perform tasks requiring motor co-ordination/alertness.
adverse_effects: Same as in HYOSCINE BUTYL BROMIDE, fatigue, vertigo.

name: HYOSCINE BUTYL BROMIDE
indications: Symptomatic GI pain, urinary spasm, irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), excessive respiratory secretion, bowel colic.
dosage_schedule: 10 mg 3 times a day; 4 to 20 mg 4 times a day.
contraindications: Pregnancy, geriatric patient, hyperthyroidism, dysarrhythmias, ulcerative colitis, hypertension, renal/hepatic disease, urinary retention.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Headache, confusion, dizziness, palpitation, tachycardia, blurred vision, photophobia, dry mouth, constipation, paralytic ileus.

name: MEBEVERINE HYDROCHLORIDE
indications: Irritable bowel syndrome, other spasmodic conditions.
dosage_schedule: 135-150 mg 3 times a day to be taken 20 minutes before meal.
precautions: To be taken 20 minutes before meal.
adverse_effects: Allergic reaction, angioedema, urticaria, rash.

name: CIMETIDINE
indications: See RANITIDINE.
dosage_schedule: Benign ulcer (Adult): 400 mg twice daily or 800 mg at night; Maintenance: 400 mg at night; Child: 25-30 mg/kg; Infant: 20 mg/kg.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: See RANITIDINE; also gynaecomastia, microsomal enzyme inhibition, and higher hepatotoxicity.

name: ESOMEPRAZOLE
indications: See OMEPRAZOLE.
dosage_schedule: H. pylori ulcer: 20 mg twice daily. NSAID associated GU: 20 mg once daily for 4-8 weeks. GERD: 40 mg once daily for 4 weeks.
precautions: See OMEPRAZOLE.
adverse_effects: See OMEPRAZOLE.

name: FAMOTIDINE
indications: See RANITIDINE.
dosage_schedule: Benign ulcer: Oral 40 mg at night for 4-8 weeks. Reflux oesophagitis: 20-40 mg twice daily for 5-12 weeks. Zollinger-Ellison: 20 mg every 6 hours.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: See RANITIDINE.

name: LANSOPRAZOLE
indications: See OMEPRAZOLE.
dosage_schedule: Duodenal ulcer: 30 mg daily for 4 weeks. Benign gastric ulcer: 30 mg daily for 8 weeks. NSAID associated ulcer: 15-30 mg once daily for 4 weeks.
precautions: See OMEPRAZOLE.
adverse_effects: See OMEPRAZOLE.

name: OMEPRAZOLE
indications: Benign gastric and duodenal ulcer, NSAID associated ulcer, reflux oesophagitis, Zollinger–Ellison syndrome, stress ulcer.
dosage_schedule: Adult: 20 mg/day for 4-8 weeks.
precautions: Breast-feeding, patients with liver disease.
adverse_effects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal colic, skin rash, headache and dizziness.

name: PANTOPRAZOLE
indications: See OMEPRAZOLE.
dosage_schedule: Duodenal ulcer: 40 mg daily for 2 weeks. Benign gastric ulcer: 40 mg daily for 2 weeks.
contraindications: See OMEPRAZOLE; Report severe diarrhoea, black tarry stools, or abdominal pain.
precautions: See OMEPRAZOLE.
adverse_effects: See OMEPRAZOLE.

name: RANITIDINE
indications: Benign duodenal and gastric ulcer, reflux oesophagitis, Zollinger–Ellison syndrome, GERD, stress ulcer.
dosage_schedule: Benign ulcer: oral 150 mg twice daily or 300 mg at night for 4-8 weeks. Reflex oesophagitis: 150 mg twice daily for 8-12 weeks. Gastric acid reduction (obstetric): oral 150 mg at onset of labour, then every 6 hours.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, pregnancy, impaired renal function, children < 12 years.
precautions: Sexual dysfunction in male (loss of libido, impotence, gynaecomastia).
adverse_effects: Headache, dizziness, myalgia, nausea, skin rash, diarrhoea or constipation.

name: SUCRALFATE
indications: Benign gastric and duodenal ulceration, chronic gastritis.
dosage_schedule: 2 g twice daily (on rising and at bed time) for 4-6 weeks; Prophylaxis of NSAID induced ulcer (suspension): 1 g 6 times daily.
precautions: Safety and efficacy in children have not been established.
adverse_effects: N/A

name: CYCLIZINE
indications: Prevention and treatment of nausea, vomiting and vertigo associated with motion sickness.
dosage_schedule: Motion sickness (Adult): 50 mg 30 minutes before traveling, repeat in 6 hours (up to 200 mg/day); Child (6-12 years): 25 mg up to 3 times/day.
contraindications: Asthma, glaucoma, emphysema, chronic pulmonary disease.
precautions: Should not be concurrently used with sedatives, tranquilizers and anticholinergic medication.
adverse_effects: Drowsiness, xerostomia, headache, dermatitis, urinary retention, diplopia.

name: DIMENHYDRINATE
indications: Prevention of motion sickness, Meniere’s disease.
dosage_schedule: Motion sickness (Adult): 50-100 mg 4-6 hours or 30 minutes before traveling (max 400mg/day); Meniere’s (Adult): 50 mg IM for acute attack, 25-50 mg 8 hourly for maintenance.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, pregnancy and neonates, breast-feeding, seizures, angle closure glaucoma, prostatic enlargement.
precautions: Masks early signs of ototoxicity if given with ototoxic drugs.
adverse_effects: Paradoxical CNS stimulation (children), CNS depression, dizziness.

name: DOMPERIDONE
indications: Antiemetic, gastrokinetic for gastric emptying, dyspepsia, GERD.
dosage_schedule: Acute nausea/vomiting (Adult): 10-20 mg 6-8 hours; Child: 0.25-0.5 mg/kg. Functional dyspepsia: 10-20 mg 3 times daily before food.
contraindications: GIT obstruction, urinary outflow obstruction, paralytic ileus, comatose condition, hepatic/cardiovascular disease, glaucoma.
precautions: Avoid grapefruit juice during therapy.
adverse_effects: Galactorrhoea, gynaecomastia, decreased libido, skin rashes.

name: METOCLOPRAMIDE
indications: Nausea and vomiting in GI disorders or radiotherapy, GERD, gastroparesis, premedication.
dosage_schedule: Adult: 10 mg 3 times daily; Children: 2-5 mg/kg. Aid to GI procedure: 10-20 mg as single dose.
contraindications: GI obstruction, perforation, pheochromocytoma, epilepsy, Parkinson’s, pregnancy, breast feeding.
precautions: Assess for extra-pyramidal side effects (rigidity, tremor), signs of depression.
adverse_effects: Extrapyramidal symptoms, tardive dyskinesia, hyperprolactinemia, neuroleptic malignant syndrome.

name: ONDANSETRON
indications: Chemotherapy induced nausea and vomiting (CINV), post operative (PONV), radiation induced nausea, uremic pruritus.
dosage_schedule: CINV (moderate): 8 mg 30 min prior; IV: 0.15 mg/kg. PONV: 4 mg IV/IM before anaesthesia.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, co-administration with apomorphine, pregnancy, breastfeeding, severe liver impairment.
precautions: Safety not established in children below 4 years.
adverse_effects: Headache, constipation, hiccups, flushing, arrhythmia, hypotension.

name: PROCHLORPERAZINE
indications: Postoperative nausea and vomiting, chemotherapy induced nausea, vertigo, psychosis.
dosage_schedule: Acute vomiting: 20 mg initially then 10 mg after 2 hours. Prevention: 5-10 mg 2-3 times daily (0.25 mg/kg).
precautions: Should be protected from light.
adverse_effects: Muscle dystonia, other extrapyramidal side effects, dry mouth, drowsiness.

name: PROMETHAZINE
indications: Nausea, vomiting, motion sickness, sedation.
dosage_schedule: Nausea/vomiting: 12.5-25 mg 4-6 hours. Motion sickness: 25 mg 30-60 min before travel.
precautions: May cause photosensitivity; avoid prolonged exposure to sunlight.
adverse_effects: Sedation, blurred vision, confusion, hallucination, extrapyramidal symptoms.

name: DIPHENOXYLATE
indications: Acute diarrhoea, chronic mild ulcerative colitis.
dosage_schedule: Adult: Initial 4 tablets, then 2 tablets every 6 hours until controlled.
contraindications: Children < 4 years, hypersensitivity, pregnancy, breast feeding, hepatic disease, ulcerative colitis.
precautions: Monitor for pseudomembranous colitis.
adverse_effects: Blurred vision, sedation, nausea, abdominal discomfort, dryness of mouth.

name: LOPERAMIDE
indications: Acute nonspecific diarrhoea, chronic diarrhoea, faecal incontinence, intestinal colic pain.
dosage_schedule: Acute: 4 mg initially, then 2 mg (max 16 mg/day). Chronic: 4-8 mg daily in divided doses.
contraindications: Active ulcerative colitis, pseudomembranous colitis, age < 2 years, bloody diarrhoea.
precautions: Avoid use as primary therapy in acute dysentery. Discontinue if no improvement in 48 hours.
adverse_effects: Dizziness, drowsiness, fatigue, flatulence, nausea.

name: ORAL REHYDRATION SALTS
indications: Dehydration from acute diarrhoea.
dosage_schedule: Adult: 200-400 ml after every loose motion. Child: 200 ml after every loose motion.
precautions: Renal impairment; protect from moisture.
adverse_effects: Vomiting (too rapid administration), hypernatremia, hyperkalaemia.

name: RIFAXIMIN
indications: Traveller’s diarrhoea, hepatic encephalopathy, irritable bowel syndrome.
dosage_schedule: Traveller’s: 200 mg TDS for 3 days. HE: 550 mg BD. IBS: 550 mg TDS for 14 days.
precautions: Discontinue if symptoms persist > 24-48 hours. Hepatic impairment.
adverse_effects: Flatulence, rectal tenesmus, abdominal pain, defecation urgency, nausea.

name: ZINC SULFATE
indications: Adjunct to ORS in acute diarrhoea.
dosage_schedule: Infants < 6 months: 10 mg daily for 10-14 days. Child 6 months-5 years: 20 mg daily.
precautions: Inform doctor if tarry stools or severe nausea occurs.
adverse_effects: Abdominal pain, dyspepsia, nausea, vomiting, gastric irritation.

name: ISPAGHULA HUSK
indications: Constipation.
dosage_schedule: 0.5-2 gm/day at bed time; Children: half of adult dose.
precautions: Increase fluid intake; bulk forming foods in diet.
adverse_effects: Abdominal distension, flatulence.

name: DOCUSATE SODIUM
indications: Constipation, adjunct to radiological procedure.
dosage_schedule: 50-300 mg per oral single or divided dose (max 500 mg).
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, intestinal obstruction, prolonged use, children.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Rashes, transient abdominal cramping pain.

name: LIQUID PARAFFIN
indications: Constipation.
dosage_schedule: 10-30 ml at night.
precautions: Avoid aspiration.
adverse_effects: Lipoid pneumonia, interference with fat soluble vitamin absorption, granulomatous lesions.

name: BISACODYL
indications: Constipation, bowel preparation for radiology/surgery.
dosage_schedule: Adult: 5-10 mg at night. Paediatric (>6 yr): 5 mg at night.
precautions: Swallow whole; do not take with antacid within 1 hour.
adverse_effects: Abdominal cramp, local irritation.

name: SENNA
indications: Constipation, bowel preparation.
dosage_schedule: Adult: 2-4 tablets at night. Child (>6 years): half of adult dose.
precautions: Avoid except when straining.
adverse_effects: Abdominal cramps.

name: LACTULOSE
indications: Constipation, hepatic encephalopathy.
dosage_schedule: Adult: 15 ml twice daily. HE (Adult): 30-45 ml per oral.
precautions: Pregnancy; ensure adequate water intake.
adverse_effects: Dehydration, hypernatremia, abdominal distension, flatulence.

name: MACROGOL 3350
indications: Constipation, fecal impaction.
dosage_schedule: Constipation: 1 sachet in 125 ml water daily. Impaction: 8 sachets within 6 hours.
contraindications: Gut obstruction/perforation, severe IBD, cardiovascular diseases.
precautions: Take plenty of fluids.
adverse_effects: Diarrhoea, dehydration, indigestion, pain abdomen.

name: MAGNESIUM HYDROXIDE (MILK OF MAGNESIA)
indications: Constipation, acid peptic disease.
dosage_schedule: Constipation: 30-60 ml at bed time. Acid peptic: 5-15 ml in 4 divided doses.
contraindications: Renal failure, acute abdomen, undiagnosed abdominal pain.
precautions: Shake before use; take on empty stomach.
adverse_effects: Abdominal cramp, electrolyte imbalance, hypotension.

name: MAGNESIUM SULPHATE
indications: Constipation, hypomagnesemia, eclampsia, torsades de pointes.
dosage_schedule: Constipation: 5-10 g dissolved in 24 ml water.
contraindications: Renal impairment, heart block, acute surgical abdomen.
precautions: Not for long term use; do not give at bedtime.
adverse_effects: Flaccid paralysis, circulatory collapse, electrolyte disturbance.

name: POLYETHYLENE GLYCOL 3350
indications: Constipation.
dosage_schedule: 17 g reconstituted in a glass of water.
precautions: Report unusual cramps or bloating.
adverse_effects: Nausea, abdominal bloating, cramping, excessive stool frequency.

name: ADALIMUMAB
indications: Crohn’s disease, ulcerative colitis, rheumatic and psoriatic arthritis.
dosage_schedule: Crohn's/UC: Initial 160 mg, then 80 mg (day 15), maintenance 40 mg every other week.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Hypersensitivity, increased serum ALT, infection.

name: BUDESONIDE
indications: Mild to moderate active Crohn’s disease.
dosage_schedule: Active disease: 9 mg orally daily for 8 weeks; Maintenance: 6 mg daily.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Increased infection risk, abdominal pain, flatulence, corticosteroid effects.

name: HYDROCORTISONE ACETATE
indications: Ulcerative colitis, proctitis, proctosigmoiditis.
dosage_schedule: Suppository: 25 mg twice daily for 2 weeks.
precautions: Proctoscopic examination required before treatment.
adverse_effects: Local pain/burning, rectal bleeding.

name: INFLIXIMAB
indications: Crohn’s disease, ulcerative colitis.
dosage_schedule: Adult: IV 5 mg/kg at 0, 2, 6 weeks, then every 8 weeks.
precautions: Risk of lymphoma in children; consider antihistamine premedication.
adverse_effects: Hypersensitivity, abdominal pain, infusion related reaction.

name: MESALAZINE
indications: Ulcerative colitis acute attack and maintenance, Crohn’s ileo-colitis.
dosage_schedule: Maintenance (Adult): 1.2-2.4 g daily. Acute (Adult): 2.4 g daily.
contraindications: Salicylate hypersensitivity, breastfeeding, active peptic ulcer, severe renal failure.
precautions: Empty stomach prior to rectal administration.
adverse_effects: Dizziness, oligospermia, abdominal pain, headache.

name: SULFASALAZINE
indications: Ulcerative colitis, active Crohn’s disease, rheumatoid arthritis.
dosage_schedule: Adult (Acute): 1-2 g QID. Child (>2 yrs): 40-60 mg/kg.
contraindications: Salicylate/sulfonamide hypersensitivity, child < 2 yrs, intestinal obstruction.
precautions: G6PD deficiency, renal/hepatic impairment; ensure hydration.
adverse_effects: Nausea, vomiting, exacerbation of colitis, blood disorders, lung complications.

name: OCTREOTIDE
indications: Esophageal variceal bleeding, acromegaly, carcinoid tumor.
dosage_schedule: Variceal bleeding: 50 mcg IV bolus, then 25-50 mcg/hr for 1-5 days.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: N/A

name: TERLIPRESSIN
indications: Bleeding from esophageal varices.
dosage_schedule: Initially 2 mg every 4-6 hours until controlled, then 1 mg up to 48 hours.
contraindications: Seizure, migraine, asthma, heart failure, renal disease.
precautions: Use in pregnancy only if clearly needed.
adverse_effects: Abdominal cramps, headache, cardiac arrhythmias.

name: URSODEOXYCHOLIC ACID
indications: Dissolution of gallstones, primary biliary cirrhosis.
dosage_schedule: Gallstones: 8-12 mg/kg daily. Cirrhosis: 10-15 mg/kg daily.
precautions: Avoid aluminium antacids; pregnant and lactating mothers.
adverse_effects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, pruritus.

name: PROBIOTICS
indications: Infective diarrhoea, antibiotic associated diarrhoea, traveller’s diarrhoea risk.
dosage_schedule: Typical dosage: 1-10 billion cells divided into 3 or 4 doses.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Infection, acidosis (rare).

name: GLYCERYL TRINATRE (NITROGLYCERINE)
indications: Prophylaxis and acute attack of angina pectoris, Hypertensive emergencies, acute decompensated heart failure
dosage_schedule: Angina (acute attack): Intravenous infusion, adult: initially 5–10 mcg/min. The rate may be increased by 10 mcg/min every 3–5 min until symptoms relieved, systolic arterial pressure falls to <100 mm Hg, or dose reaches 200 mcg/min. Hypertensive emergencies: Intravenous infusion, adult: 5-10 mcg/min initial dose up to 200 mcg/min. Acute decompensated heart failure: Intravenous infusion, adult: 10–20 mcg/min, increase up to 200 mcg/min; Children: Initially 0.25- 0.5 mcg/kg/min to titrate to 0.5-1.0 mcg/kg/min. Maximum dose 20 mcg/kg/min.
contraindications: Avoid in hypersensitivity to nitrates, hypotension, hypovolemia, hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy, aortic stenosis, cardiac tamponade, constrictive pericarditis, mitral stenosis, marked anemia, head trauma, cerebral hemorrhage, angle-closure glaucoma.
precautions: Use caution in severe hepatic impairment, hypothyroidism, malnutrition, hypothermia, recent history of myocardial infarction. Renal impairment (10-50 ml/min): never administer. Uninterrupted infusion > 24 hours produces tolerance.
adverse_effects: Throbbing headache (most frequent in early therapy), flushing, dizziness, postural hypotension, Tachycardia, syncope, paradoxical bradycardia

name: ISOSORBIDE DINITRATE
indications: Prophylaxis and treatment of angina, left ventricular failure.
dosage_schedule: Angina (acute attack): Sublingual, adult: 5–10 mg repeated as required. Angina (prophylaxis): Oral, adult: 30-120 mg daily in divided doses. Intravenous infusion: 2-10 mg daily, maximum dose 20 mg/hour. Left ventricular failure: Oral, adult 40-160 mg daily in divided doses, maximum dose 240 mg daily; Intravenous infusion: 2-10 mg daily, maximum dose 20 mg/hour.
precautions: See under glyceryl trinitrate. Patients may develop tolerance; avoid by giving the second of 2 daily doses of longer-acting oral preparations after an 8-hour rather than a 12-hour interval.
adverse_effects: See under glyceryl trinitrate, tolerance (in long term, uninterrupted use)

name: ISOSOBIDE MONONITRATES
indications: Prophylaxis of angina pectoris, adjunct in congestive heart failure.
dosage_schedule: Prophylaxis for angina: Oral (immediate release), adult: initially 20 mg 2-3 times daily or 40 mg twice daily or 10 mg twice daily (in those who have not previously received nitrates) maximum dose 120 mg in 2-3 divided doses daily.
precautions: See under glyceryl trinitrate
adverse_effects: See under glyceryl trinitrate

name: ATENOLOL
indications: Chronic stable angina, secondary prevention after myocardial infarction, supra ventricular arrhythmia, mild CHF, hypertension, migraine prophylaxis.
dosage_schedule: Hypertension: Oral, adult: 25 – 50 mg daily. Oral, child: 0.5-1.0 mg/kg/dose in 1-2 divided doses daily. Maximum dose- 2mg/kg/day or 100 mg/day. Angina: Oral, adult: 100 mg, maximum dose 200 mg daily 1 or 2 doses. Arrhythmias: Oral, adult: 50-100 mg daily. Intravenous, adult: 2.5 mg at rate of 1 mg/min repeated at 5 min interval to a maximum of 10 mg/dose. Early intervention Myocardial infarction: slow intravenous infusion, adult: 5 mg by then oral 50 mg after 15 minutes then oral 50 mg after 12 hours then 100 mg daily. Migraine prophylaxis: Oral, adult: 50–200 mg daily in divided doses.
contraindications: Avoid in history of asthma or bronchospasm, uncontrolled heart failure, prinzemetal angina, bradycardia (heart rate <50 bpm), hypotension, sick sinus syndrome, second and third degree atrioventricular block, cardiogenic shock, metabolic acidosis, severe peripheral arterial disease, pheochromocytoma (unless used with an alpha blocker).
precautions: Use caution in patients with first –degree atrioventricular block, portal hypertension, renal impairment (reduce dose), diabetes mellitus. Pregnancy- avoid (IUGR, neonatal hypoglycemia and bradycardia). Breast feeding: avoid. Monitor lung function. Symptoms of hypoglycemia and thyrotoxicosis may get masked.
adverse_effects: Bradycardia, gastrointestinal disturbances including nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, abdominal cramp, fatigue, cold hands and feet, hypertriglyceridemia.

name: BISOPROLOL
indications: Hypertension, angina, adjunct in heart failure
dosage_schedule: Hypertension and angina: Oral, adult: 5-10 mg once daily, 20 mg daily (maximum). Adjunct in heart failure: Oral, adult: initially 1.25 mg once daily (in the morning) for 1 week then, if well tolerated, increased to 2.5 mg once daily for 1 week, then 3.75 mg once daily for 1 week, then 5 mg once daily for 4 weeks, then 7.5 mg once daily for 4 weeks, then 10 mg once daily, maximum 10 mg daily.
precautions: See under atenolol
adverse_effects: See under atenolol

name: CARVEDILOL
indications: Angina, hypertension, adjunct to diuretics/digoxin/ACE inhibitors in heart failure
dosage_schedule: Hypertension: Oral, adult: Initially 12.5 mg once daily for 2 days, then increased to 25 mg once daily; increased if necessary up to 50 mg daily. Angina: Oral, adult: initially 12.5 mg once daily, increased after 2 days to 25 mg twice daily. Adjunct in heart failure: Oral, adult: initially 3.125 mg twice daily to 6.25 mg twice daily, then to 12.5 mg twice daily then to 25 mg twice daily. Dose increased at intervals of at least 2 weeks
contraindications: See under atenolol. Avoid in acute decompensated heart failure requiring intravenous inotropes.
precautions: See under atenolol. Check for edema in feet, legs daily. Rise slowly from sitting or lying position to minimize orthostatic hypotension
adverse_effects: Allergic skin reactions, angina, AV block, changes in liver enzymes, depressed mood, disturbances of micturition, influenza-like symptoms, leucopenia, nasal stuffiness, postural hypotension, thrombocytopenia, wheezing, headache, dizziness, bradycardia and impotence

name: METOPROLOL
indications: Angina, hypertension, arrhythmias, migraine prophylaxis, hyperthyroidism adjunct, early intervention in myocardial infarction.
dosage_schedule: Angina: Oral, adult: 50- 100 mg, 2-3 times daily. Hypertension: Oral, adult: initially 100 mg daily, maximum dose 400 mg daily. Arrhythmias: Oral, adult: 50-100 mg, 2-3 times daily; Intravenous, adult: up to 5 mg at rate 1-2 mg/minute repeated after 5 minutes if necessary, total dose 10-15 mg. Early intervention in myocardial infarction: Intravenous, adult: 5 mg every 2 minutes to a maximum dose of 15 mg, followed after 15 minutes by oral 50 mg every 6 hours for 48 hours; maintenance oral 200 mg daily. Hyperthyroidism (adjunct): Oral, adult: 50 mg 4 times a day. Oral, child: 1-2 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses daily. Maximum dose 6 mg/kg/day up to 200 mg/day.
precautions: See under atenolol. Abrupt withdrawal may cause MI, ventricular arrhythmias, myocardial ischemia; taper dose over 7-14 days.
adverse_effects: See under atenolol

name: PROPRANOLOL
indications: Chronic stable angina, hypertension, secondary prevention after acute myocardial infraction, anxiety, thyrotoxicosis, migraine prophylaxis, pheochromocytoma (only with alpha blocker), prophylaxis of variceal bleeding, mitral valve prolapse, essential tremor, child with cyanotic spells.
dosage_schedule: Hypertension: Oral, adult: initially 80 mg twice daily; maintenance dose 160-320 mg daily. Oral, child: 1-4 mg/kg/day in 3-4 divided doses. Prophylaxis of variceal bleeding: Oral, adult: initially 40 mg twice daily increased to 80 mg twice daily. Angina: Oral, adult: initially 40 mg 2-3 time daily; maintenance 120-240 mg daily. Arrhythmias: Oral, adult: 10-40 mg in 3-4 divided doses daily. Anxiety: Oral, adult: 40 mg once daily; may increase to 40 mg 3 times daily. Essential tremor: Oral, adult: initially 40 mg 2-3 times daily; maintenance 80-160 mg daily. Cyanotic spells: Child, intravenous: 0.15-0.25 mg/kg/day in 4 divided dose; Oral, child: 2-4 mg/kg/day in 4 divided doses. Infantile hemangioma: Oral, child: 1-2 mg/kg/day in 3 divided doses.
precautions: See under atenolol. Reduce oral dose in renal and hepatic impairment. Monitor blood glucose. Do not discontinue abruptly.
adverse_effects: See under atenolol. Hallucination, nightmare, sexual dysfunction.

name: DILTIAZEM
indications: Angina pectoris
dosage_schedule: Angina: Oral, adult: Initially 60 mg 3 times a day, adjusted according to response; maximum 360 mg/day. Elderly: Initially 60 mg twice daily. Oral, child: 1.5-2 mg/kg/day in 3-4 divided doses (maximum dose: < 6mg/kg/day up to 360 mg/day).
contraindications: Avoid in acute porphyria, left ventricular failure with pulmonary congestion, second- or third-degree AV block (unless pacemaker fitted), severe bradycardia, sick sinus syndrome.
precautions: Avoid if bradycardia is severe. Hepatic impairment: reduce dose. Renal impairment: start with smaller dose.
adverse_effects: Asthenia, AV block, bradycardia, dizziness, gastro-intestinal disturbances, headache, hot flushes, hypotension, malaise, edema, palpitation, Sino-atrial block

name: VERAPAMIL
indications: Angina pectoris, supra ventricular arrhythmias, hypertension, migraine prophylaxis, supraventricular tachycardia in children
dosage_schedule: Angina, supraventricular arrhythmia: Oral, adult: 40-120 mg 3 times daily. Hypertension: Oral, adult: 240-480 mg daily in 2- 3 divided doses. Hypertensive emergency: Slow intravenous injection over 2 minutes, 5 - 10 mg. Paroxysmal tachyarrhythmia: slow intravenous injection, adult: initially 5-10 mg further 5 mg after 5-10 minutes if required. Supraventricular tachycardia: Child, intravenous: 0.1-0.3 mg/kg/dose may be repeated in 30 min. Maximum first dose 5 mg, second dose 10 mg.
contraindications: Hypotension, bradycardia, second- and third-degree heart block, sick sinus syndrome; cardiogenic shock, history of heart failure, atrial flutter or fibrillation complicating Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome, acute porphyria. Avoid if ventricular failure present.
precautions: Hepatic impairment; children (specialist advice only). Not to discontinue abruptly. Avoid use in neonate and young infants.
adverse_effects: Constipation; nausea, vomiting, flushing, headache, dizziness, fatigue, ankle edema; rarely allergic reactions; myalgia, arthralgia; increased prolactin; gynecomastia and gingival hyperplasia; hypotension, heart failure, bradycardia, heart block, and asystole.

name: ADENOSINE
indications: Paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia (including Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome)
dosage_schedule: Rapid intravenous injection: 3 mg over 2 seconds; if necessary followed by 6 mg after 1-2 minutes and then by 12 mg after a further 1-2 minutes. Neonate, intravenous: 0.05 mg/kg over 1-2 sec; maximum dose 0.25 mg/kg. Child, intravenous: 0.1-0.2 mg/kg (initial max 6 mg) over 1-2 sec; maximum of 0.25 mg/kg.
contraindications: Pre-existing second or third degree AV block, asthma and sick sinus syndrome.
precautions: Use cautiously in arterial fibrillation or flutter and heart transplant. Assess cardiopulmonary and respiratory status.
adverse_drug_reactions: Chest pain, transient facial flush, bronchospasm, nausea and severe bradycardia, difficult or labored breathing, chest tightness

name: AMIODARONE
indications: Paroxysmal supraventricular, nodal and ventricular tachycardia, atrial fibrillation or flutter, ventricular arrhythmia, ventricular fibrillation.
dosage_schedule: Arrhythmias: Oral, adult: 200 mg 3 times daily for 1 week reduced to 200 mg twice daily. Ventricular fibrillation: intravenous infusion, adult: 300 mg over at least 3 minutes. Drug resistant refractory cardiac arrhythmia: Oral, child: < 1 year: 600-800 mg/1.73m2/day in 1-2 divided dose for 1-14 days. > 1 years: 10-15 mg/kg/day in 1-2 divided doses for 14 days. Child, intravenous: 5 mg/kg over 30 min followed by continuous infusion at rate of 5 mcg/kg/min (Max: 15-20 mcg/kg/min).
contraindications: Avoid in sinus bradycardia, SA heart block, Iodine sensitivity, cardiogenic shock, second or third degree AV block, thyroid dysfunctions, severe hepatic, pneumonitis, pulmonary fibrosis, hypokalemia, CHF (with inadequate compensation).
precautions: Pregnancy: risk of neonatal goiter. Breast feeding: avoid. Clinical monitoring of serum potassium, chest X-ray, pulmonary function tests, liver and thyroid function tests recommended.
adverse_effects: Nausea, vomiting, raised serum transaminases, bradycardia, ventricular arrhythmia, neurologic dysfunction (dizziness, tremor), thyroid dysfunction, pulmonary toxicity on long term use.

name: DIGOXIN
indications: Supraventricular arrhythmias, particularly atrial fibrillation; heart failure
dosage_schedule: Atrial fibrillation: Oral, adult: initially 1–1.5 mg in divided doses over 24 hours followed by 62.5–500 mcg daily. Emergency control: intravenous infusion over at least 2 hours, adult: 0.75–1 mg. Pediatric (mcg/kg/day): Premature neonate 20 (Total daily PO), 15 (IV/IM); Full Term 30 (PO), 20 (IV/IM); 1 month-2 years 40-50 (PO), 30-40 (IV/IM); 2-10 years 30-40 (PO), 20-30 (IV/IM); >10 years 10-15 (PO), 8-12 (IV/IM). Initially, half the total daily dose, then other half every 8 hours in 2 divided doses.
contraindications: Avoid in hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy; Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome; ventricular tachycardia or fibrillation; intermittent complete heart block; second-degree AV block.
precautions: Use caution in recent MI, sick sinus syndrome, renal impairment. Monitor apical pulse; withhold if rate is <60 bpm (adult), <70 bpm (child), <90 bpm (infant). Therapeutic drug monitoring advised.
adverse_effects: GI disturbances (anorexia, nausea, vomiting), visual disturbances, headache, fatigue, drowsiness, confusion, dizziness, all arrhythmias except Mobitz type II block; rarely rash; gynecomastia; thrombocytopenia.

name: DISOPYRAMIDE
indications: Atrial and ventricular arrhythmias including those resistant to lignocaine.
dosage_schedule: Oral (immediate release), adult: 300-800 mg daily in divided doses. Slow intravenous injection, adult: 2 mg/kg over at least 5 minutes to a maximum of 150 mg with ECG monitoring.
contraindications: Avoid in preexisting second or third degree AV block, cardiogenic shock, heart failure (can produce severe hypotension). Renal or hepatic insufficiency, third trimester of pregnancy, glaucoma, myasthenia gravis or urinary retention.
precautions: Use caution in the elderly and children. Do not drive or operate machinery. Do not stop the drug suddenly.
adverse_effects: Angle-closure glaucoma, antimuscarinic effects, AV block, blurred vision, cholestatic jaundice, dry mouth, hypoglycemia, hypotension, myocardial depression, psychosis, urinary retention, ventricular tachycardia, torsade de pointes.

name: ISOPRENALINE
indications: Torsade de pointes, bradycardia in patients with heart block, control attacks of Stokes Adam syndrome.
dosage_schedule: Intravenous injection, adult: 0.5-10 mcg/minute. Oral, adult: initially 30 mg every 6 hours, range, 90-840 mg daily (rarely used).
precautions: N/A

name: LIDOCAINE/ LIGNOCAINE
indications: Ventricular arrhythmias (especially after myocardial infarction), local anesthesia
dosage_schedule: Ventricular arrhythmias: intravenous injection, adult: loading dose of 50-100 mg at rate 25-50 mg/minute, followed immediately by infusion 1-4 mg/minute. Intravenous, child: 1 mg/kg/dose slow IV, may repeat 10-15 min. Max total dose: 3-5 mg/kg within first hour.
contraindications: Avoid in Sino atrial nodal disorder, any grade of atrioventricular block, severe myocardial depression, acute porphyria, hypovolemia, Wolff-Parkinson-White, Stokes Adams syndrome.
precautions: Lower dosage in CHF, cardiac surgery, bradycardia, hepatic impairment. Pregnancy and breastfeeding. Monitor for ECG.
adverse_effects: Flushing, dizziness, paresthesia, drowsiness, confusion, apnea, respiratory depression, coma, seizure, hypotension, arrhythmia, heart block, bradycardia (may lead to cardiac arrest), nystagmus.

name: PROCAINAMIDE
indications: Severe ventricular arrhythmias; atrial tachycardia, atrial fibrillation; maintenance of sinus rhythm after cardioversion.
dosage_schedule: Oral, adult: up to 50 mg/kg daily in divided doses every 3-6 hours. Slow intravenous injection, adult: rate not exceeding 50 mg/minute, 100 mg repeated at 5 minute intervals until controlled; maximum 1g. Intravenous infusion, adult: 500-600 mg over 25-30 minutes, maintenance 2-6 mg/minute.
contraindications: Avoid in Torsade’s de pointes, SLE, 2nd and 3rd degree heart block, heart failure, hypotension, elderly, renal/hepatic impairment, asthma, myasthenia gravis, pregnancy, breastfeeding, electrolyte imbalance.
precautions: Discontinue if leukocyte/platelet count drops. Perform CBC twice a week for 3 months. Monitor continuously by ECG during IV use.
adverse_effects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, rash, pruritus, fever, myocardial depression, heart failure, angioedema, dizziness, psychosis; leukopenia, hemolytic anemia, agranulocytosis, SLE like syndrome.

name: CAPTOPRIL
indications: Mild to moderate essential hypertension, adjunctive treatment in congestive heart failure, severe hypertension resistant to other treatment, following myocardial infraction, diabetic nephropathy.
dosage_schedule: Hypertension: Oral, adult: initially 5 mg once daily; usual maintenance 20 mg once daily; maximum 40 mg once daily. Take 1-2 hours after meals.
contraindications: Avoid in bilateral renal artery stenosis, pregnancy, hyperkalemia, pre-existing cough.
precautions: Use caution in severe aortic stenosis. Monitor renal function. Rise slowly to minimize orthostatic hypotension. Not to discontinue product abruptly.
adverse_effect: alopecia, rash, profound hypotension, dehydration, taste impairment, leucopenia, proteinuria, persistent dry cough, sleep disorder, dyspnea, neutropenia, Raynaud’s syndrome.

name: ENALAPRIL
indications: Hypertension, heart failure
dosage_schedule: Hypertension: Oral, adult: 5 mg once daily (2.5 mg daily initially if on diuretic or renal impairment); maintenance 20 mg once daily: maximum 40 mg once daily. Oral, child: 0.1- 0.6 mg/kg/day in 1-2 divided doses. Maximum dose 40 mg/day.
contraindications: See under captopril. Avoid in renal impairment when GFR < 30 ml/1.73m2/min.
precautions: Use cautious in impaired liver function and neonates. Monitor renal function.
adverse_drug_reaction: Dizziness, headache, nausea, diarrhea, dry cough, fatigue, asthenia, angioedema, urticaria, rashes, hyperkalemia, impaired perspiration

name: LISINOPRIL
indications: Essential and renovascular hypertension, adjunctive treatment in congestive heart failure, following myocardial infarction, diabetic nephropathy.
dosage_schedule: Hypertension: initially 10 mg daily (2.5-5 mg if renal impairment); usual maintenance 20 mg once daily (max 80 mg). Heart failure (adjunct): Oral, adult: initially 2.5 mg daily; usual maintenance 5-20 mg daily. Diabetic nephropathy: Oral, adult: initially 2.5 mg daily; usual range 10-20 mg daily. Prophylaxis after MI: Oral, adult: 5 mg within 24 hours, followed by 5 mg 24 hours later, then 10 mg after a further 24 hours, and continuing with 10 mg once daily for 6 weeks.
contraindications: Avoid in pregnancy, hereditary angioedema, breast-feeding. See under captopril.
precautions: Drink plenty of water. Avoid potassium rich diet.
adverse_effects: Profound hypotension, hyperkalemia, rash, tachycardia, myocardial infarction, sweating, impotence, dizziness, upper respiratory tract infection, fatigue, diarrhea.

name: RAMIPRIL
indications: Hypertension, congestive heart failure, prophylaxis after myocardial infarction, prophylaxis of cardiovascular events or stroke.
dosage_schedule: Hypertension: Oral, adult: initially 1.25 mg once daily; usual range 2.5-5 mg once daily; maximum 10 mg once daily. CHF (adjunct): Oral, adult: initially 1.25 mg once daily; maximum 10 mg daily. Prophylaxis after MI: Oral, adult: initially 2.5 mg twice daily, increased to 5 mg twice daily; maintenance 2.5-5 mg twice daily. Prophylaxis of stroke: initially 2.5 mg once daily, increased up to 10 mg once daily.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: See under Enalapril

name: IRBESARTAN
indications: Hypertension, hypertension in patients receiving hemodialysis, renal disease in hypertensive with type 2 diabetes mellitus
dosage_schedule: Hypertension: Oral, adult (18–74 years): Initially 150 mg once daily, increased to 300 mg once daily. Oral, adult (>75 years): Initially 75–150 mg once daily, increased to 300 mg. Hemodialysis: Oral, adult: Initially 75–150 mg once daily. Type 2 diabetes renal disease: Oral, adult (18–74 years): Initially 150 mg once daily, increased to 300 mg once daily.
contraindication: Avoid in renal artery stenosis, moderate to severe renal impairment or liver impairment, aortic or mitral valve stenosis.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Fatigue, musculoskeletal pain, nausea, vomiting

name: LOSARTAN
indications: Hypertension, congestive heart failure, diabetic nephropathy in type 2 diabetes mellitus
dosage_schedule: Hypertension: Oral, adult: 50 mg (elderly >75 years: 25 mg) once daily; increase up to 150 mg. Oral, Child: 0.75 mg/kg/dose once daily (Max 50 mg/day). Maximum dose: 1.4 mg/kg/day or 100 mg/day. Diabetic nephropathy: Oral, adult: initially 50 mg (elderly >75 years: 25 mg) once daily, increase up to 100 mg. CHF: Oral, adult: Initially 12.5 mg once daily, increase to 150 mg once daily.
contraindications: Avoid in pregnancy and breast feeding, children of 6 years or younger, CHF, renal impairment (GFR < 30 ml/min/1.73m2), renal artery stenosis.
precautions: Use caution in moderate to severe renal/liver impairment, aortic or mitral valve stenosis. Rise slowly to minimize orthostatic hypotension.
adverse_effects: Hypotension, dizziness, diarrhea, pruritus, rash, taste disturbance, thrombocytopenia, photosensitivity

name: TELMISARTAN
indications: Hypertension, prevention of cardiovascular events in patients with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease or type 2 diabetes mellitus with target-organ damage.
dosage_schedule: Hypertension: Oral, adult: Initially 20–40 mg once daily, increased if necessary up to 80 mg once daily. Prevention of CV events: Oral, adult: 80 mg once daily. Severe renal impairment: Oral, adult: Initial dose of 20 mg once daily.
contraindication: Avoid in bilateral renal artery stenosis, pregnancy and breast feeding, in severe impairment or biliary obstruction.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Arthralgia, back pain, chest pain, eczema, gastro-intestinal disturbances, influenza like symptoms, leg cramps, myalgia, pharyngitis, sinusitis, urinary-tract infection, abnormal vision, anxiety, dry mouth, sweating, tendonitis, vertigo

name: VALSARTAN
indications: Hypertension, myocardial infarction with left ventricular failure or left ventricular systolic dysfunction.
dosage_schedule: Hypertension: Oral, adult: 80 mg once daily (initially 40 mg if intravascular volume depletion); increased up to 160 mg daily. Myocardial infarction: Oral, adult: initially 20 mg twice daily increased up to 160 mg twice daily. Mild to moderate hepatic impairment: maximum dose of 80 mg daily.
contraindications: See under Losartan. Avoid in biliary cirrhosis, cholestasis, severe hepatic impairment, renal impairment when eGFR <10 ml/min/ 1.73m2.
precautions: Use caution in mild to moderate renal and hepatic impairment. Take medicine before meal.
adverse_effects: See under losartan.

name: LABETALOL
indications: Hypertension, Hypertensive emergencies, hypertension following myocardial infarction, hypertension of pregnancy
dosage_schedule: Hypertension: Oral, adult: Initially 100 mg (50 mg for elderly) twice daily; usual dose 200 mg twice daily; maximum 2.4 g per day. Hypertensive emergencies: Intravenous injection: adult: 50 mg over 1 minute; maximum 200 mg. Intravenous infusion: adult: Initially 2 mg/minute; usual dose 50–200 mg. Pregnancy Hypertension: Intravenous infusion: Initially 20 mg/hour, increased to 160 mg/hour. Oral, child: 4 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses. Max 40 mg/kg/day. Hypertensive emergency: Child, IV: 0.2-1.0 mg/kg/dose every 10 min. Max 20 mg/dose.
contraindication: See under contraindication in Atenolol. Avoid in severe liver damage. Hepatic impairment: avoid as reported. Renal impairment: Dose reduction may be required.
precautions: Pregnancy: possibly harmful in first trimester. Monitor infants for signs of alpha-blockade. Stop if laboratory evidence of liver damage or jaundice occurs. Take medicine after food.
adverse_effects: Difficulty in micturition, epigastric pain, liver damage, nausea, postural hypotension, vomiting, weakness, severe hepatocellular injury

name: NEBIVOLOL
indications: Essential hypertension, hypertension in patient with renal impairment, adjunct in stable mild to moderate heart failure
dosage_schedule: Essential hypertension: Oral, adult: 5 mg daily; elderly: Initially 2.5 mg daily. Hypertension with renal impairment: Oral, adult: Initially 2.5 mg once daily. Adjunct in heart failure: Oral, elderly (≥ 70 years): Initially 1.25 mg once daily for 1–2 weeks, then increased up to 10 mg once daily.
contraindication: See under contraindication Atenolol. Avoid in acute or decompensated heart failure requiring intravenous inotropes, severe hepatic impairment. Renal impairment: avoid in heart failure if serum creatinine > 250 micromole/liter.
precautions: Breast feeding: avoid.
adverse_effects: See under adverse effect Atenolol. Depression, edema.

name: AMLODIPINE
indications: Hypertension, angina pectoris
dosage_schedule: Hypertension or angina: Oral, adult: initially 5 mg once daily; maximum dose 10 mg once daily. Oral, child: 0.1-0.6 mg/kg/day in 1-2 divided doses. Maximum dose: 20 mg/day.
contraindication: Cardiogenic shock, unstable angina, significant aortic stenosis. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: avoid.
precautions: In hepatic impairment: dose reduction. Try to avoid large amount of alcohol.
adverse_effects: Abdominal pain, nausea, flushing, edema (ankle edema), headache, dizziness, sleep disturbances, fatigue, alopecia, arthralgia, asthenia, back pain, dry mouth, dyspnea, impotence, gynecomastia, myalgia, muscle cramp, skin discoloration.

name: FELODIPINE
indications: Angina, hypertension
dosage_schedule: Angina: Oral, adult: 5 mg/day, maximum dose 10 mg/day. Oral, elderly: 2.5 mg/day. Hypertension: initially 5 mg (elderly 2.5 mg) daily in the morning; usual maintenance 5-10 mg once daily.
contraindication: Avoid in Cardiac outflow obstruction, aortic stenosis uncontrolled heart failure, unstable angina, within 1 month of myocardial infarction. Pregnancy- avoid.
precautions: Withdraw if cardiogenic shock develops. In hepatic impairment, reduce dose.
adverse_effects: flushing, headache, peripheral edema.

name: NIFEDIPINE
indications: prophylaxis of angina, hypertension, Raynaud’s phenomenon, pulmonary hypertension.
dosage_schedule: Hypertension and angina prophylaxis: Oral, adult: 20 mg twice daily. Usual maintenance 10-40 mg twice daily. Raynaud’s: Oral, adult: initially 5 mg 3 times daily. Pulmonary hypertension: Oral, adult: 120 to 240 mg once daily. Hypertension: Child, sublingual: 0.25-0.5 mg/kg/dose. Maximum 10 mg/dose.
contraindication: Avoid in congestive heart failure or aortic stenosis, especially in those receiving concomitant beta blocking agents.
precautions: In patients with angina, the drug may cause increased angina. To be taken with or after food.
adverse_effects: dizziness, giddiness, flushing, light headedness, peripheral edema and palpitation.

name: CLONIDINE
indications: Hypertension, prevention of recurrent migraine, prevention of vascular headache, treatment for acute withdrawal in opioid dependent patients.
dosage_schedule: Hypertension: Oral, adult: Initially 50–100 mcg 3 times a day, usual maximum 1.2 mg daily. Migraine/Vascular headache: Oral, adult: Initially 50 mcg twice daily for 2 weeks, then 75 mcg twice daily. Opioid withdrawal: Oral, adult: 0.1-0.3 mg every 4-6 hours; maximum 2.4 mg/day.
contraindication: Avoid in severe bradyarrhythmia secondary to second- or third-degree AV block or sick sinus syndrome.
precautions: Withdraw gradually to avoid rebound hypertension. Pregnancy: use caution. Breast feeding: avoid. Renal impairment: reduce initial dose. Drowsiness may affect driving.
adverse_effects: Constipation, depression, dizziness, drowsiness, dry mouth, headache, malaise, nausea, postural hypotension, salivary gland pain, sexual dysfunction, sleep disturbances, vomiting. Bradycardia, delusion, hallucination.

name: HYDRALAZINE HYDROCHLORIDE
indications: Moderate and severe hypertension (adjunct), hypertensive emergencies in pregnant (not a first line agent), hypertension with renal complication and children
dosage_schedule: Mild or moderate hypertension: Oral, adult: 25 mg twice daily, increased to maximum 50 mg twice daily. Hypertensive emergencies: intravenous infusion, adult: initially 200-300 mcg/minute, maintenance 50-150 mcg/minute. Slow intravenous injection, adult: 5-10 mg diluted. Hypertension: Oral, child: 0.75-1.0 mg/kg/day in 2-4 divided doses. Maximum dose: 25 mg/dose. Hypertensive crisis: Child, IV/IM: 0.1-0.2 mg/kg/dose every 4-6 hours. Max 20 mg/dose.
contraindications: Avoid in severe tachycardia, high output heart failure, myocardial insufficiency due to mechanical obstruction, corpulmonale, dissecting aortic aneurysm, porphyria, SLE.
precautions: Use caution in hepatic/renal impairment, coronary artery disease, pregnancy, elderly. Perform CBC and LE cell preparation during therapy. Monitor blood glucose in diabetics.
adverse_effect: Tachycardia, palpitation, hypotension, nausea, vomiting, SLE-like syndrome, weight gain and headache, muscle weakness, cramps, dizziness.

name: METHYLDOPA
indications: Hypertension, hypertension in pregnancy
dosage_schedule: Hypertension: Oral, adult: 250 mg, 2-3 times a day. Maximum 3 g daily. Oral, elderly: initially 125 mg twice daily, max 2 g daily.
contraindications: Avoid in acute porphyria, depression, pheochromocytoma.
precautions: Use cautiously in history of liver disease and renal impairment. Screening for hepatotoxicity at 3 weeks then 3 months. Protect medication from light.
adverse_effects: Sedation, dryness of mouth, decreased libido, parkinsonian signs, hyperprolactinemia, gynecomastia, hepatitis, hepatotoxicity, hemolytic anemia, leucopenia, lupus like syndrome, myocarditis, pancreatitis, malabsorbtion, diarrhea, Bell’s palsy, bone marrow depression.

name: PRAZOSIN
indications: Hypertension, benign prostatic hyperplasia.
dosage_schedule: Hypertension: Oral, adult: 500 mcg 2-3 times daily for 3-7 days, then increased up to maximum 20 mg daily. Benign prostatic hyperplasia: Oral, adult: Initially 500 mcg twice daily, maintenance 2 mg twice daily.
contraindications: Avoid in history of micturition syncope and postural hypotension, congestive heart failure due to mechanical obstruction.
precautions: Use caution in cataract surgery, elderly, renal or hepatic impairment. Breast feeding: use caution. Take first dose at bedtime; do not drive for 4 hr. after first dose.
adverse_effects: Postural hypotension, dizziness, headache, palpitation, nervousness, drowsiness, priapism, blurred vision, depression, dry mouth, dyspnea, gastrointestinal disturbances, edema, syncope, urinary frequency, vertigo, weakness.

name: SODIUM NITROPRUSSIDE
indications: Hypertensive crisis, controlled hypotension in anesthesia, acute or chronic heart failure.
dosage_schedule: Hypertensive crisis: Intravenous infusion, adult: initially 0.5–1.5 mcg/kg/minute, increased to 0.5–6 mcg/kg/minute; maximum, 8 mcg/kg/minute. Heart failure: 10- 15 mcg /minute, usual range 10-200 mcg/minute.
contraindications: Severe hepatic impairment, compensatory hypertension, severe vitamin B12 deficiency, Leber optic atrophy.
precautions: Elderly, hyponatremia, hypothermia, hypothyroidism, renal impairment, ischemic heart disease. Monitor blood pressure and blood cyanide/thiocyanate concentration. Avoid sudden withdrawal.
adverse_effects: severe hypotension; headache, dizziness; retrosternal discomfort, nausea, retching, abdominal pain; perspiration; palpitations, anxiety, reduced platelet count, acute transient phlebitis.

name: TAMSULOSIN
indications: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
dosage_schedule: Oral, adult: 400 mcg daily as once daily.
contraindications: Avoid in micturition syncope, postural hypotension, severe liver impairment.
precautions: Use caution if eGFR <10 ml/min/1.73m2. Do not drive or use machinery until sure of alertness. Not to crush, break, or chew.
adverse_effects: Postural hypotension, dizziness, headache, palpitation, drowsiness, priapism, pruritus, angioedema, asthenia, blurred vision, rash, rhinitis, tachycardia, depression, intraoperative floppy iris syndrome.

name: TERAZOSIN
indications: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), mild to moderate hypertension
dosage_schedule: Hypertension: Oral, adult: Initially 1 mg once daily at bedtime, usual maintenance dose 2-10 mg. BPH: Oral, adult: Initially 1 mg orally once daily. Maintenance 5–10 mg daily; maximum 10 mg per day.
precautions: See under Prazosin
adverse_effects: Postural hypotension and syncope, dizziness, drowsiness, dry mouth, chest pain, pedal edema, palpitation, headache, priapism, thrombocytopenia, decreased libido, erectile disorders, weight gain, dyspnea, Angioedema, pain in extremities, blurred vision

name: PHENYLEPHRINE
indications: Acute hypotension, Priapism
dosage_schedule: Acute hypotension: subcutaneous/intramuscular injection, adult: Initially 2–5 mg, followed by 1–10 mg. Slow intravenous injection: 100–500 mcg. Intravenous infusion: Initially up to 180 mcg/minute, reduced to 30–60 mcg/min. Priapism: Intracavernosal injection, adult: 100–200 mcg every 5–10 minutes; maximum 1 mg per course.
contraindication: Avoid in hypertension, severe hyperthyroidism. Pregnancy: avoid
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Arrhythmias, hypertension, palpitation, tachycardia, angle-closure glaucoma, anorexia, anxiety, bradycardia, confusion, dyspnea, headache, hypoxia, insomnia, nausea, peripheral ischemia, psychosis, tremor, urinary retention, vomiting, weakness

name: DOBUTAMINE
indications: Inotropic support in infarction, cardiac surgery, septic shock, cardiogenic shock and during positive end expiratory pressure ventilation.
dosage_schedule: Intravenous infusion, adult: 2.5-10 mcg/kg/minute, alternatively 0.5-40 mcg/kg/min
precautions: Use caution in severe hypotension, complicating cardiogenic shock, heart failure. Extravasation causes tissue necrosis. Do not mix with sodium bicarbonate or furosemide.
adverse_effect: Tachycardia, increase in systolic blood pressure, phlebitis. Extravasation causes tissue necrosis

name: DOPAMINE
indications: Cardiogenic shock including in myocardial infarction and cardiac surgery.
dosage_schedule: Cardiogenic shock: intravenous infusion, adult: initially 2–5 mcg/kg/minute into a large vein, gradually increased by 5-10 mcg/kg/minute; up to 20–50 mcg/kg/minute in seriously ill patients.
contraindications: Avoid in tachyarrhythmia, ventricular fibrillation, ischemic heart disease; pheochromocytoma, hyperthyroidism.
precautions: Correct hypovolemia, hypoxia, hypercapnia, and metabolic acidosis before starting treatment. Pregnancy: use only if potential benefit outweighs risk. Protect from light.
adverse_effects: Nausea, vomiting, peripheral vasoconstriction; hypotension, tachycardia, ectopic beats, palpitations, anginal pain; headache, dyspnea; hypertension in over dosage. Extravasation causes tissue necrosis.

name: EPINEPHRINE /ADRENALINE
indications: Cardiac arrest, adjunct with local anesthetics, acute anaphylaxis
dosage_schedule: Acute anaphylaxis: intramuscular injection, adult: 0.5-1 ml, repeat every 10 minutes. Child (2-5 years): 0.2-0.4 ml; (6-12 years): 0.5 ml. Acute hypotension: continuous intravenous infusion, neonate and child: 100 nanogram/kg/min adjusted up to 1.5 mcg/kg/min. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation: Intravenous injection, adult: 1 mg every 3-5 min.
contraindications: Shock (other than anaphylactic shock), second stage labor. Do not use if color is cloudy or brownish.
precautions: While using monitor blood pressure, heart rate. Avoid in patients on tricyclic antidepressants.
adverse_effect: Tachycardia, hypertension, tremor, chest pain, irregular heartbeats, headache, nausea, vomiting, nervousness, restlessness, weakness.

name: MILRINONE
indications: Short-term treatment of severe congestive heart failure unresponsive to conventional therapy, acute heart failure following surgery.
dosage_schedule: Intravenous injection, adult: Initially 50 mcg/kg over 10 minutes, followed by infusion 375–750 nanogram/kg/minute; maximum dose: 1.13 mg/kg per day.
precautions: Use caution in hypokalemia, renal impairment, heart failure with HCM or valvular disease. Pregnancy: use with caution. Renal impairment: Reduce dose if eGFR < 50 mL/min/1.73 m2.
adverse_effects: Ectopic beats, headache, hypotension, supraventricular arrhythmias, ventricular tachycardia. Chest pain, hypokalemia, thrombocytopenia, tremor, ventricular fibrillation.

name: NOREPINEPHRINE/NORADRENALINE
indications: Acute hypotension
dosage_schedule: Acute hypotension: intravenous, adult: Initially 0.16–0.33 mL/minute, solution containing 40 mcg (base)/ml, adjusted according to response into large vein. Dilute 2 mg base with 48 mL infusion fluid for syringe pump. Dilute 20 mg base with 480 mL for drip counter.
contraindication: Hypertension. Uncorrected hypovolemia. Pregnancy: Avoid, may reduce placental perfusion.
precautions: Use caution in coronary thrombosis, diabetes, elderly, post-MI, hyperthyroidism, hypoxia. Avoid extravasation. Incompatible with alkalis.
adverse_effects: Angle-closure glaucoma, anorexia, anxiety, arrhythmias, bradycardia, confusion, dyspnea, headache, hypertension, hypoxia, insomnia, nausea, palpitation, peripheral ischemia, psychosis, tachycardia, tremor, urinary retention, vomiting, weakness.

name: BOSENTAN
indications: Pulmonary arterial hypertension, systemic sclerosis with ongoing digital ulcer disease.
dosage_schedule: Pulmonary arterial hypertension: Oral, adult: Initially 62.5 mg twice daily for 4 weeks, then increased up to maximum 500 mg per day in 2 divided doses. Digital ulcer disease: Oral, adult: Initially 62.5 mg twice daily for 4 weeks, then increased to 125 mg twice daily.
contraindication: Avoid in acute porphyria, systemic systolic blood pressure <85 mmHg. Pregnancy (X). Hepatic impairment: avoid in moderate to severe impairment.
precautions: Breast feeding: avoid. Effective hormonal contraception not considered effective. Monthly pregnancy tests advised. Monitor Hemoglobin and Liver function.
adverse_effects: Anemia, diarrhea, flushing, gastro-esophageal reflux, headache, hypotension, edema, palpitation, syncope, liver cirrhosis, liver failure, leucopenia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia.

name: SILDENAFIL
indications: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), erectile dysfunction
dosage_schedule: Erectile dysfunction: Oral, adult: 50 mg 1 hr. before sexual activity, maximum dose 100 mg, 1 dose per day. PAH: Oral, adult: 25 mg three times daily.
contraindication: Avoid in hypotension, myocardial infarction, unstable angina, not for use in children with PAH.
precautions: Avoid use with nitrates. Use caution in anatomic deformation of penis, retinitis pigmentosa, ischemic heart disease. With alcohol may cause dizziness.
adverse_effects: headache, flushing, epistaxis, dyspepsia, insomnia, erythema, diarrhea, migraine, myalgia, nasal congestion, visual disturbance, back pain.

name: ATORVASTATIN
indications: Primary hypercholesterolemia, homozygous or heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia or mixed hyperlipidemia.
dosage_schedule: Primary hyperlipidemia: Oral, adult: 10 mg once daily; increase up to 80 mg. Oral, child (10-13 years): 10 mg once daily. Familial hypercholesterolemia: Oral, adult: initially 10 mg, increased to max 80 mg once daily. Oral, child (10-13 years): up to 20 mg once daily.
contraindications: Avoid in pregnancy, breastfeeding, active liver disease. Use caution in liver disease, elderly or high alcohol intake.
precautions: Liver function tests before and periodically during treatment. Non serious and reversible cognitive side effects may occur.
adverse_effects: reversible myositis, headache, angina, chest pain, arthralgia, anorexia, weight gain, epistaxis, back pain, nasopharyngitis, hyperglycemia.

name: CHOLESTYRAMINE RESINS
indications: Adjunct to dietary therapy to decrease serum cholesterol and LDL concentrations, cholestasis induced pruritus.
dosage_schedule: Lipid reduction: Oral, adult: 12-24 g daily in water, up to 36 g if necessary. Cholestasis pruritus: Oral, adult: 4-8 g daily in water.
precautions: May impair absorption of fat-soluble vitamins, thyroid hormones, warfarin. Suspension should be prepared several hours before ingestion to reduce adverse effects.
adverse_effects: Bloating, dyspepsia, constipation, abdominal pain, anorexia, biliary colic, and skin rash.

name: EZETIMIBE
indications: Adjunct to dietary measures and statin treatment in primary hypercholesterolemia, homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia, or homozygous sitosterolemia.
dosage_schedule: Oral, adult: 10 mg daily
