contraindication: Avoid in moderate to severe hepatic impairment, myopathy, elevated hepatic transaminases, renal impairment (CrCl ≤ 30 ml/min/1.73 m2). Pregnancy (C) Breast feeding: avoid.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Fatigue, gastro-intestinal disturbances, headache, myalgia. Rare: anaphylaxis, angioedema, hepatitis, pancreatitis, rhabdomyolysis.

name: FENOFIBRATE
indications: Severe hypertriglyceridemia.
dosage_schedule: Initially 160 mg once daily dose.
contraindications: Avoid in gall bladder disease, hypoalbuminemia, nephrotic syndrome, pregnancy, breast feeding, severe hepatic impairment.
precautions: Use caution in mild to moderate renal and hepatic impairment. Monitor liver transaminases every 3 month for a year. Restrict fat diet.
adverse_effects: Gastrointestinal disturbances, rash, urticaria, fatigue, headache, impotence.

name: GEMFIBROZIL
indications: Adjunct to dietary therapy in hyperlipidemias of types II a, II b, III, IV and V.
dosage_schedule: Oral, adult: 1.2 g daily usually in 2 divided doses; range 0.9-1.2 g daily.
contraindications: Avoid in preexisting gallbladder disease, hepatic dysfunction, history of hypersensitivity. Breast feeding: Avoid.
precautions: Risk for myopathy increases with renal impairment. Assess liver function, CBC, electrolytes every 3-6 months. Safety not established in children < 18 years. Pregnancy (C).
adverse_effects: abdominal and epigastric pain, diarrhea, nausea, anorexia, headache, sexual dysfunction, myopathy, myositis, urticaria and pruritus.

name: NICOTINIC ACID (NIACIN)
indications: Adjunct to statin in hypertriglyceridemia and or used alone if statin not tolerated.
dosage_schedule: Oral, adult: Initially 100-200 mg 3 times daily, gradually increased to l-2 g 3 times daily.
contraindications: Avoid in arterial hemorrhage, active peptic ulcer, and breast feeding.
precautions: Use caution in liver disease, gout, diabetes, gallbladder disease, renal impairment. Pregnancy (A, C- for doses exceeding RDA). Breast feeding: use caution.
adverse_effects: diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, flushing, palpitations, dizziness, pruritus and rash.

name: SIMVASTATIN
indications: Primary and secondary prevention of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, in high risk individuals (e.g. with diabetes mellitus, post Myocardial infarction)
dosage_schedule: Prevention of cardiovascular events: Oral, adult: initially 20-40 mg once daily at night (maximum 80 mg).
contraindications: Avoid in pregnancy(X), breast-feeding, active liver disease. Use caution in uncontrolled hypothyroidism, perioperative periods.
precautions: Use caution in elderly (>65 years), hepatic or renal dysfunction. Suspend use if myopathy suspected. Reduce dose if used with certain antibiotics or antifungals.
adverse_effects: Upper respiratory tract infection, myalgia, myopathy, rhabdomyolysis, abdominal pain, dyspepsia, hepatitis, jaundice, peripheral neuropathy, rashes, angioedema, cognitive side effects.

name: ROSUVASTATIN
indications: Primary hypercholesterolemia (type IIa), mixed dyslipidemia (type IIb), or homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia, Prevention of cardiovascular events in patients at high risk.
dosage_schedule: Primary/Prevention of CV events: Oral, adult: Initially 5 mg once daily, increased up to 20 mg once daily. Severe primary hypercholesterolemia: Oral, adult: Initially 5–10 mg, increased up to 40 mg once daily. Renal impairment (eGFR 30–60 ml/min/1.73 m2): Initially 5 mg once daily (max 20 mg daily).
contraindication: Avoid in pregnancy, breast feeding, severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 ml/min), hepatic impairment.
precautions: Use caution in mild to moderate renal impairment, patients with high CV risk.
adverse_effects: Flulike symptoms, constipation, urinary tract infection, proteinuria. Gynecomastia, hematuria, peripheral neuropathy, arthralgia.

name: FERROUS FUMARATE
indications: Iron-deficiency anemia.
dosage_schedule: Prophylactic: Oral, > 12 years: 210 mg elemental iron 1–2 times a day. Therapeutic: Oral, 12 years: 210 mg 2–3 times a day.
contraindications: Hemochromatosis, hemosiderosis, hemolytic anemia (unless iron deficiency state is also present), any form of anaemia not caused by iron deficiency; patients receiving repeated blood transfusions; parenteral iron therapy.
precautions: Best absorbed on an empty stomach but may be taken after food to reduce GI effects; may discolour stools.
adverse_effects: Diarrhea, constipation, nausea, epigastric pain, heart burn, discoloration of teeth.
interactions: Antacids and tetracyclines inhibit absorption. Citric acid and ascorbic acid increase absorption.

name: FERROUS FUMARATE WITH FOLIC ACID
indications: Iron deficiency anemia.
dosage_schedule: Oral, adult: 1 tablet/capsule daily, to be taken before food.
contraindications: See FERROUS FUMARATE and FOLIC ACID.
precautions: See FERROUS FUMARATE and FOLIC ACID.
adverse_effects: See FERROUS FUMARATE and FOLIC ACID.
interactions: See FERROUS FUMARATE and FOLIC ACID.

name: FERROUS GLUCONATE
indications: Prophylaxis and treatment of iron deficiency anemia.
dosage_schedule: Prophylaxis: Child (6–11 years): 300–900 mg daily; Child (12–17 years) and Adult: 600 mg daily. Treatment: Child (6–11 years): 300–900 mg daily; Child (12–17 years) and Adult: 1.2–1.8 g daily in divided doses. All doses before food.
precautions: See FERROUS FUMARATE.
adverse_effects: See FERROUS FUMARATE.

name: FERROUS SULPHATE
indications: Iron deficiency anemia.
dosage_schedule: Prophylaxis: 200 mg dried ferrous sulfate daily after food. Treatment: 400-600 mg daily in divided doses after food.
precautions: Tablet (300 mg) contains 60 mg elemental iron; Tablet (200 mg) contains 40 mg elemental iron.
adverse_effects: Diarrhea, constipation, nausea, epigastric pain (dose related).

name: FERROUS SULFATE WITH ASCORBIC ACID
indications: Iron deficiency anemia.
dosage_schedule: Oral, adult: 1 tablet daily, dose to be taken before food.
precautions: Tablet contains Ferrous sulphate 325 mg and Sodium ascorbate 500 mg.
adverse_effects: N/A

name: FERROUS SULPHATE WITH FOLIC ACID
indications: Prevention of iron and folic acid deficiencies in pregnancy; Severe anaemia.
dosage_schedule: Severe anaemia: Child <2 years: elemental iron 25 mg + folic acid 100–400 mcg daily for 3 months; Child 2–12 years: elemental iron 60 mg + folic acid 400 mcg daily for 3 months; Adult: elemental iron 120 mg + folic acid 400 mcg daily for 3 months. Pregnancy prophylaxis: Oral, adult: elemental iron 100 mg + folic acid 350–400 mcg daily throughout pregnancy.
contraindications: Should never be given without vitamin B12 in undiagnosed megaloblastic anaemia; folate-dependent malignant disease. See FERROUS FUMARATE.
precautions: Risk of precipitating subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord.
adverse_effects: See FERROUS SULFATE.

name: IRON DEXTRAN
indications: Iron deficiency anemia, only when oral administration has been found unsatisfactory or impossible.
dosage_schedule: 25-100 mg IV or deep IM every day when necessary, not to exceed 100 mg (2 ml/day).
contraindications: Allergic disorders including asthma, infection, active rheumatoid arthritis.
precautions: Caution in pregnancy and hepatic/renal impairment. Contact physician if fever, chills, malaise, or joint aches occur.
adverse_effects: Nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, arthralgia, fever, urticaria, anaphylactic reactions, headache, hypotension.

name: FOLIC ACID
indications: Folate deficiency megaloblastic anemia; prevention of neural tube defect in pregnancy.
dosage_schedule: Megaloblastic anemia: Oral, adult: 5 mg daily for 4 months. Prevention of neural tube defect (first occurrence): 400-500 mcg daily before conception and during first 12 weeks of pregnancy. Prevention of recurrence: 5 mg daily (reduced to 4 mg) from 4 weeks before conception to 12th week of pregnancy.
contraindications: Should never be given without vitamin B12 in undiagnosed megaloblastic anaemia; folate dependent malignant disease.
precautions: Monitor plasma folic acid levels, hemoglobin, and reticulocyte count.
adverse_effects: Bronchospasm, erythema, malaise, pruritis, rash, slight flushing.
interactions: Pyrimethamine, methotrexate, trimethoprim prevent activation. Absorption decreased by antacids and cholestyramine. Requirements increased by estrogens, phenytoin, carbamazepine.

name: EPOETIN ALFA
indications: Anemia associated with erythropoietin deficiency in chronic renal failure, autologous blood yield increase, symptomatic anaemia in cytotoxic chemotherapy or myelodysplastic syndrome.
dosage_schedule: Chronic renal failure: Initially 20 units/kg SC 3 times a week or 40 units/kg IV 3 times a week. Non-myeloid malignancies: Initially 450 units/kg SC once weekly, increase to 900 units/kg if response inadequate.
contraindications: Uncontrolled hypertension; pure red cell aplasia (PRCA); Subcutaneous route contraindicated in chronic renal failure (per certain sections); Myocardial infarction, stroke, thromboembolism.
precautions: Monitor hemoglobin weekly. Do not shake or vigorously agitate vial. Refrigerate at 2–8°C.
adverse_effects: Hypertension, increased coagulability (thromboembolic events), pure red cell aplasia, seizures, flu-like symptoms, anaphylactic reactions.
interactions: Androgens increase sensitivity of erythroid progenitors. Probenecid: Possible pharmacokinetic interaction. Desmopressin: Potential decrease in bleeding time.

name: HEPARIN (UNFRACTIONATED)
indications: Deep venous thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE), unstable angina, acute myocardial infarction, coronary angioplasty/stent placement.
dosage_schedule: Prophylaxis of DVT/PE: Adult, SC: 5000 units 2 hours before surgery, then every 8-12 hours for 7 days. Treatment of DVT/PE: Adult, IV: loading 5000 units (75 units/kg) then infusion 18 units/kg/hour.
contraindications: Active bleeding, hemophilia, purpura, thrombocytopenia, hypersensitivity to pork products.
precautions: Laboratory monitoring essential (preferably daily). Check for heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT). Reverse with Protamine sulfate (1 mg per 1000 U heparin remaining). Pregnancy: use only if benefit justifies risk.
adverse_effects: Hemorrhage, HIT, alopecia, bleeding, osteoporosis, hyperkalemia.
interactions: Action increased by oral anticoagulants, salicylates, dextran, NSAIDs. Action decreased by digoxin, tetracycline, nicotine.

name: LOW MOLECULAR WEIGHT HEPARINS
indications: Prophylaxis of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism.
dosage_schedule: Administered by SC injection in fixed or weight-adjusted dose regimen once or twice daily (e.g., Dalteparin, Enoxaparin).
contraindications: Reports of congenital anomalies in infants; causal relationship not established.
precautions: See individual drug entries (Dalteparin, Enoxaparin). Routine monitoring not usually done.
adverse_effects: See HEPARIN.

name: DALTEPARIN
indications: Prophylaxis of DVT in surgical and medical patients; treatment of DVT and PE.
dosage_schedule: Surgical prophylaxis: 2500 units SC 1-2 hours before surgery. Medical prophylaxis: 5000 units SC every 24 hours. PE Treatment: SC single daily dose based on weight (<46 kg: 7500 units; 46-56 kg: 10,000 units; 57-68 kg: 12,500 units).
precautions: See HEPARIN.
adverse_effects: See HEPARIN.

name: ENOXAPARIN
indications: Prophylaxis of DVT in surgical and medical patients.
dosage_schedule: Surgical prophylaxis: Moderate risk, 20 mg SC 2 hours before surgery then daily for 7-10 days; High risk, 40 mg SC 12 hours before surgery then daily. Medical prophylaxis: 4000 units SC every 24 hours for at least 6 days.
precautions: See HEPARIN.
adverse_effects: See HEPARIN.

name: WARFARIN
indications: Prevention of progression and recurrence of DVT or PE; thromboembolism prevention in heart valves, acute MI, or atrial fibrillation.
dosage_schedule: Initial dose 10 mg for 2 days, subsequent doses 3-9 mg daily in accordance with prothrombin activity of blood.
contraindications: GI ulcers, severe hypertension, bacterial endocarditis, pregnancy, recent surgery.
precautions: Monitor prothrombin activity (INR). Contraindicated in women who are or may become pregnant.
adverse_effects: Hemorrhage.
interactions: Vitamin K rich food/supplements decrease effect. Metabolism decreased by allopurinol, cimetidine, amiodarone, metronidazole (enhances hemorrhage risk).

name: ACENOCOUMAROL
indications: See WARFARIN.
dosage_schedule: 4-12 mg on first day, 4-8 mg on second day, maintenance 1-8 mg daily.
precautions: See WARFARIN.
adverse_effects: See WARFARIN.

name: APIXABAN
indications: Stroke prophylaxis with atrial fibrillation, postoperative DVT/PE prophylaxis, DVT or PE treatment.
dosage_schedule: Stroke prophylaxis: 5 mg PO twice a day. Post-op DVT/PE: 2.5 mg PO twice a day for 35 days. DVT/PE treatment: 10 mg twice a day for 7 days, then 5 mg twice a day.
contraindications: Active bleeding, malignant neoplasms, oesophageal varices, recent brain/spine surgery, vascular aneurysm.
precautions: Risk of paralysis with indwelling epidural catheter.
adverse_effects: Anaemia, bruising, haemorrhage, nausea.

name: BIVALIRUDIN
indications: Unstable angina/non-ST-segment elevation MI planned for urgent intervention or proceeding to PCI.
dosage_schedule: Early intervention: IV injection 100 mcg/kg, then infusion 250 mcg/kg/hour. PCI without bypass: IV injection 100 mcg/kg for 1 dose, then 500 mcg/kg for 1 dose, then infusion 1.75 mg/kg/hour.
contraindications: Active bleeding, bleeding disorders, severe hypertension, subacute bacterial endocarditis.
precautions: INR monitoring should be done. Discontinue if unexplained fall in blood pressure or hematocrit occurs.
adverse_effects: Bleeding, ecchymosis, allergic reactions, anaemia, headache, hypotension.
interactions: Increase risk of haemorrhage with other analgesics and anticoagulants.

name: DABIGATRAN
indications: Stroke prophylaxis with atrial fibrillation, DVT/PE treatment or prophylaxis.
dosage_schedule: Stroke prophylaxis: CrCl >30 ml/min: 150 mg twice a day. DVT/PE treatment: 150 mg twice a day. DVT/PE prophylaxis (post-surgery): 110 mg 1-4 hr after surgery then 220 mg once a day.
contraindications: Severe renal impairment (CrCl <15 mL/min), active pathologic bleeding.
precautions: Monitor Ecarin clotting time (ECT); if unavailable monitor aPPT, PT, or TT.
adverse_effects: Dyspepsia, gastritis, intracranial hemorrhage, hypersensitivity (urticaria, rash).

name: FONDAPARINUX
indications: DVT, heparin induced thrombocytopenia, unstable angina, ST-segment elevation and non-ST-segment elevation MI, PE.
dosage_schedule: DVT/PE: <50 kg: 5 mg SC once a day; 50-100 kg: 7.5 mg SC once daily; >100 kg: 10 mg SC once daily. HIT: 2.5 mg SC once daily.
contraindications: Active bleeding, bacterial endocarditis, active GI ulcer disease, brain surgery.
precautions: Monitor for sign and symptoms of neurologic impairment in epidural/spinal anesthesia.
adverse_effects: Anaemia, bleeding, purpura, chest pain, dyspnoea, hepatic impairment, oedema.

name: RIVAROXABAN
indications: Prophylaxis of venous thromboembolism (orthopaedic surgery), DVT, PE, nonvalvular atrial fibrillation.
dosage_schedule: Orthopaedic prophylaxis: 10 mg PO once a day for 12 days. DVT/PE treatment: 15 mg twice a day for 21 days, then 20 mg once a day for 6 months.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, active bleeding, malignant neoplasms, GI ulcer, vascular retinopathy.
precautions: Risk of bleeding in patients with haemodynamic instability or severe hypertension.
adverse_effects: Abdominal pain, dizziness, dyspepsia, haemorrhage, renal impairment.
interactions: Increases concentration with antibacterials/antivirals. Antiepileptics decrease plasma concentration.

name: ASPIRIN
indications: Prophylaxis of cerebro vascular diseases, MI, thromboembolic disorder, ischemic stroke and angina.
dosage_schedule: Thromboembolic disorders: Oral 325-650 mg/day. Transient ischemic attack: 50-325 mg/day. Evolving MI: 160-325 mg chewed/swallowed immediately.
contraindications: Haemorrhagic stroke, hypersensitivity to acetylsalicylic, active peptic ulceration, haemophilia, asthma.
precautions: Do not give to children/adolescents due to Reye’s syndrome. Take after food with plenty of water.
adverse_effects: Bronchospasm, GI bleeding, thrombocytopenia, seizures, Reye’s syndrome.
interactions: Increase effects of oral hypoglycemics. Increased chance of bleeding with anticoagulants.

name: CLOPIDOGREL
indications: Prevention of atherothrombotic events in TIA, stroke, or ACS (with or without ST-elevation).
dosage_schedule: TIA/Stroke: 75 mg once daily. ACS without ST-elevation: Initially 300 mg, then 75 mg daily. ACS with ST-elevation: 18–75 years: Initially 300 mg, then 75 mg daily.
precautions: Avoid in pregnancy; caution in renal and hepatic impairment.
adverse_effects: Abdominal pain, bleeding disorders (GI and intracranial), diarrhea, dyspepsia.
interactions: Action increased by anticoagulants, aspirin, NSAIDs. Effect decreased by PPIs.

name: PRASUGREL
indications: Prevention of atherothrombotic events in ACS undergoing PCI; alternative to clopidogrel.
dosage_schedule: Combination with aspirin for PCI: Adult <60 kg: Initially 60 mg then 5 mg once daily; Adult ≥60 kg: Initially 60 mg then 10 mg once daily.
contraindications: Active bleeding, history of stroke or TIA. Body weight < 60 kg (requires caution/dose reduction).
precautions: Discontinue at least 7 days before elective surgery.
adverse_effects: Anemia, GI hemorrhage, hematoma, hematuria, intracranial hemorrhage, rash.
interactions: Increased risk of hypersensitivity when given with other thienopyridines.

name: TICLOPIDINE
indications: Coronary artery stent thrombosis prevention, stroke.
dosage_schedule: Stent thrombosis: 250 mg twice a day with aspirin for 30 days. Stroke: 250 mg twice daily with food.
contraindications: Neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, active bleeding, severe hepatic impairment.
precautions: Monitor CBC and Liver function test every 2 weeks for the first 3 months. Risk of aplastic anemia.
adverse_effects: Diarrhea, elevated alkaline phosphatase/AST/ALT, nausea, rash, neutropenia, purpura.
interactions: Concurrent use of other anticoagulants increases bleeding incidence.

name: ALTEPLASE
indications: Acute myocardial infarction, pulmonary embolism, acute stroke.
dosage_schedule: MI (Accelerated): 15 mg IV bolus, then 0.75 mg/kg infusion over 30 min, then 0.5 mg/kg over 60 min (max 100 mg). Acute Stroke: 900 mcg/kg (max 90 mg) IV infusion, 10% bolus then remainder over 60 min.
contraindications: Current intracranial hemorrhage, subarachnoid hemorrhage, recent stroke, active internal bleeding, recent intracranial/intraspinal surgery.
precautions: Monitor for intracranial hemorrhage and blood pressure (systolic <180, diastolic <105 recommended).
adverse_effects: Risk of cerebral bleeding, reperfusion arrhythmias, pulmonary edema, hypotension.
interactions: Bleeding incidence increased with concurrent anticoagulants.

name: STREPTOKINASE
indications: Pulmonary embolism, deep venous thrombosis, acute myocardial infarction.
dosage_schedule: Acute MI: 1,500,000 units IV infusion over 60 minutes. DVT/PE: 250,000 units IV over 30 minutes, then 100,000 units every 1 hour for 12–72 hours.
contraindications: Surgery within 10 days, severe trauma, GI bleeding within 3 months, history of hypertension (diastolic >110 mmHg).
precautions: Strongly antigenic; repeated administration elicits antibodies.
adverse_effects: Nausea, vomiting, bleeding, arrhythmias, allergic reactions (rash, flushing, anaphylaxis).
interactions: Risk of hemorrhage increased with heparin, oral anticoagulants, or antiplatelets (aspirin).

name: TENECTEPLASE
indications: Acute myocardial infarction.
dosage_schedule: 30–50 mg IV bolus over 10 seconds. Dose varies by weight (e.g., <60 kg: 30 mg; >90 kg: 50 mg).
precautions: Initiate within 6 hours of symptom onset.
adverse_effects: See ALTEPLASE.

name: UROKINASE
indications: See STREPTOKINASE.
dosage_schedule: Pulmonary embolism: Initial 4400 IU/kg IV over 10 minutes; Maintenance: 4400 IU/kg/hr for 12 hours.
contraindications: Must not be given SC or IM. Fibrinogen should not be <100 mg/dl.
precautions: If heparin was given, ensure aPTT is less than twice the normal control value before starting.
adverse_effects: Non-antigenic, but mild allergic reactions (bronchospasm, rash) reported.
interactions: Increased hemorrhage risk with anticoagulants or substances affecting platelet function.

name: ETHAMSYLATE
indications: Blood loss in menorrhagia, post-partum bleeding, post abortion bleeding.
dosage_schedule: Oral, adult: 500 mg 4 times daily during menstruation.
precautions: Caution if patient develops fever or has fibroids in uterus.
adverse_effects: Headache, rashes, hypotension.

name: TRANEXAMIC ACID
indications: Menorrhagia, epistaxis, thrombolytic overdose, hereditary angioedema.
dosage_schedule: Menorrhagia: 1 g PO 3 times daily for 4 days. Epistaxis: 1 g PO 3 times a day for 7 days. Hereditary angioedema: 1–1.5 g PO 2–3 times a day.
contraindications: Severe renal impairment (CrCl < 1.5 mg/dl), thromboembolic disease.
precautions: Do not use with hormonal contraceptives. Do not take for more than 5 days in a row.
adverse_effects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, disturbances in colour vision.

name: PROTAMINE SULPHATE
indications: Heparin overdose.
dosage_schedule: Adult, slow IV: 1 mg neutralises 100 units heparin if given within 15 minutes. Maximum 50 mg.
contraindications: Bleeding that occurs without prior exposure to heparin.
precautions: Caution in fish hypersensitivity or post-vasectomy patients. Monitor with coagulation studies.
adverse_effects: Hypotension, bradycardia, flushing, urticaria, angioedema.

name: PHYTOMENADIONE (VITAMIN K1)
indications: Antagonists to warfarin, prophylaxis against hemorrhagic disease of newborn.
dosage_schedule: Warfarin-induced hypoprothrombinemia: Adult, 5-10 mg slow IV. Newborn prophylaxis: IM 0.5-1 mg as single dose.
contraindications: Avoid IM route if bleeding or in 3rd trimester of pregnancy.
precautions: Rapid IV administration may cause fatal anaphylaxis. Protect from light.
adverse_effects: Facial flushing, bronchospasm, dyspnea, hypotension.
interactions: Decreases effects of warfarin by pharmacodynamic antagonism.

name: HUMAN ALBUMIN
indications: Hypovolemia, hypoalbuminemia, ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome, ARDS, hemolytic disease of the newborn.
dosage_schedule: Hypovolemia (Adult): IV 25 g. Newborns: 1 g/kg. Max daily dose: 2 g/kg of body weight.
contraindications: Severe anemia, hypertension, esophageal varices, pulmonary edema, renal/post-renal anuria.
precautions: Measures of circulating volume adequacy (not plasma levels) should guide dosing.
adverse_effects: Anaphylactic shock, circulatory failure, cardiac failure, pulmonary edema.

name: FACTOR IX COMPLEX
indications: Replacement therapy for factor IX deficiency in haemophilia B; bleeding due to deficiencies of factors II, VII, or X.
dosage_schedule: Treatment: IV 1 unit/kg increases plasma level by 1%. Units needed = weight (kg) x desired % increase x 1 unit/kg.
precautions: Do not exceed infusion rate of 10 mL/minute. Risk of thrombosis. Store at 2-8°C.
adverse_effects: Allergic reactions (chills, fever), flushing, thrombosis.
interactions: Aminocaproic Acid: May increase risk of thrombosis.

name: DESMOPRESSIN
indications: Bleeding control, diabetes insipidus, primary nocturnal enuresis.
dosage_schedule: Diabetes insipidus: Adult/Child PO/IV 1-4 mcg daily. Hemophilia A: Intranasal 150 mcg in each nostril (if >50 kg).
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, pseudo Von Willebrand’s disease, cardiac insufficiency, renal impairment.
precautions: Rhinitis can decrease intranasal effectiveness. Caution in hypertension.
adverse_effects: Fluid retention, headache, nausea, vomiting, epistaxis.
interactions: Enhanced by carbamazepine/clofibrate. Diminished by alcohol/lithium.

name: POLYGELINE
indications: Low blood volume.
dosage_schedule: Adult, IV: initially 500-1000 ml of 3.5% solution.
contraindications: Pregnancy at end of term; severe impairment.
precautions: Avoid hematocrit falling below 25–30%. Monitor urine output.
adverse_effects: Anaphylactic reaction, transient increase in bleeding time.

name: CALCIUM
indications: Hypocalcemia in tetany, osteoporosis
dosage_schedule: Supplement: 1-2 g between meals; daily requirement is greater in childhood, pregnancy, lactation and old age. Acute hypocalcaemia: 1-2 g by slow intravenous injection.
contraindications: Hypercalcemic states, do not use if allergic to any ingredients of calcium preparations
precautions: 1.25 g calcium carbonate is equivalent to 500 mg elemental calcium.
adverse_effects: Constipation, bradycardia, cardiac arrhythmia, hypotension and irritation after parenteral administration
interactions: Reduce absorption of ciprofloxacin, tetracycline, iron, bisphosphonates
patient_info: Requirement is greater in childhood, pregnancy, lactation, and old age.

name: IODINE
indications: Prevention and treatment of iodine deficiency
dosage_schedule: Daily recommended intake: 150 μg (200 μg in pregnant and breast-feeding mothers); under 1 year: 50 μg; 2-6 years: 90 μg; 7-12 years: 120 μg.
precautions: Also see section 12.5 under drugs used in endocrine system.
adverse_effects: See section 12.5 under drugs used in endocrine system
patient_info: Important for pregnant and breast-feeding mothers.

name: IRON
indications: See section 4 under drugs used in blood
dosage_schedule: N/A
precautions: See section 4 under drugs used in blood
adverse_effects: N/A
patient_info: N/A

name: PHOSPHATES
indications: Treatment of hypophosphatemia
dosage_schedule: N/A
precautions: Available as Potassium phosphate or Sodium phosphate salts.
adverse_effects: Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, fluid retention, and hypocalcaemia
patient_info: N/A

name: SODIUM FLUORIDE
indications: Prevention of dental caries
dosage_schedule: Water content <0.3 ppm: child up to 6 months none; 6 months-3 years 250 μg daily; 3-6 years 500 μg daily; over 6 years 1 mg daily. Water content 0.3-0.7 ppm: child up to 3 years none; 3-6 years 250 μg daily, over 6 years 500 μg daily. Prevention: as oral rinse, child over 6 years 10 ml 0.05% solution daily or 10 ml 0.2% solution weekly.
precautions: Advisable to institute artificial fluoridation in areas with drinking water containing less than 700 μg/l (0.7 ppm).
adverse_effects: White flakes on teeth with recommended doses; Yellowish brown discoloration of teeth with more than recommended doses
patient_info: Artificial fluoridation is recommended if water content is low.

name: ZINC
indications: Zinc deficiency, diarrhoea in children (rota virus infection), adjunct to vitamin A therapy
dosage_schedule: Adjunct to oral rehydration solution in acute diarrhoea: Under 6 months: 10 mg (elemental zinc) daily for 10 days; 6 months – 5 years: 20 mg daily for 10 days.
precautions: Must be taken for 2-3 months to be effective. Used with caution in acute renal failure.
adverse_effects: Dyspepsia, abdominal pain, headache, nausea, vomiting, gastritis
interactions: Decreases absorption of floroquinolones; absorption of zinc is reduced when taken with dietary products, caffeine
patient_info: Zinc absorption is reduced by dietary products and caffeine.

name: VITAMIN A (RETINOL)
indications: Deficiency states, prophylaxis in high risk subjects, steatorrhea, severe biliary obstruction, cirrhosis of liver or following total gastrectomy, severe ocular damage
dosage_schedule: Treatment of xerophthalmia: infants (6-11 months) 100,000 U (3 drops) on diagnosis; child over one year and adult 200,000 units on diagnosis (repeat next day and after one month). Prevention of deficiency: child 6 months to 5 years, 200,000 U every 6 months. Measles: 200,000 U. Newly delivered mothers: 200,000 U within 6 weeks.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to vitamin A, malabsorption syndrome, hypervitaminosis A, pregnancy, breastfeeding, impaired renal function, children, hepatic disease, alcoholism, hepatitis
precautions: Avoid high doses in pregnancy due to risk of hypervitaminosis.
adverse_effects: Hypervitaminosis, fatigue, irritability, mental change, anorexia, nausea, vomiting, GI upset
interactions: Mineral oil, cholestyramine, colestipol decrease absorption of Vitamin A
patient_info: Refer to prescriber upon development of adverse effects.

name: VITAMIN D3 (CALCITRIOL)
indications: Hypocalcaemia with chronic renal disease, psoriasis, renal dystrophy, prevention and treatment of rickets, post menopausal osteoporosis
dosage_schedule: Hypocalcaemia (Stage 5 CKD): Adults, oral, 0.25 μg/day; Children 1-5 year, oral, 1-5 μg/day; Rickets, oral, 1 μg/day. Osteoporosis prophylaxis in corticosteroid therapy: oral, 0.5-1 mcg/day.
precautions: Pregnancy, breastfeeding, renal calculi.
adverse_effects: Drowsiness, headache, palpitations, Hypertension, photophobia, hypercalcemia, myalgia, arthralgia, weakness, pain in injection site
interactions: Hypercalcaemia may occur if thiazide diuretics or calcium supplements are concomitantly used; cardiac dysarrythmia may occur with cardiac glycosides or verapamil
patient_info: Avoid over the counter products containing calcium, potassium, sodium; maintain adequate fluid and water intake.

name: VITAMIN E (TOCOPHEROL)
indications: Vitamin E deficiency states, impaired fat absorption, hemolytic anemia in premature neonates, prevention of retrolental fibroplasias, sickle cell anemia, supplementation of malabsorption syndrome
dosage_schedule: Deficiency states: adult, oral, 60-75 IU/day, child, oral, 1 IU/day.
precautions: Avoid in patients with hypoprothrombinaemia.
adverse_effects: Headache, fatigue, increased risk of thrombophlebitis, cramps, diarrhea, gonadal dysfunction, weakness
interactions: Increases actions of oral anticoagulants, concomitant use of cholestyramine, sucralfate decrease absorption of vitamin E
patient_info: Dietary supplement in malabsorption syndrome.

name: VITAMIN K
indications: See under Drugs used in blood disorders
dosage_schedule: N/A
precautions: See under Drugs used in blood disorders
adverse_effects: N/A
patient_info: N/A

name: VITAMIN B1 (THIAMINE)
indications: Vitamin B1 deficiency, polyneuritis, cheilosis, beri-beri, Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome, pellagra, metabolic disorders
dosage_schedule: Adult, oral (males): 1.2-1.5 mg, (females): 1.1 mg, (pregnancy): 1.4 mg, (breast feeding): 1.4 mg; child, oral: 0.5-0.9 mg; infant, oral: 0.2 mg.
precautions: Monitor for hypersensitivity reactions.
adverse_effects: Weakness, restlessness, pulmonary edema, hypotension, collapse, angioneurotic edema, cyanosis, hemorrhage
patient_info: Include foods like yeast, beef, liver, legumes, and whole grains in the diet.

name: VITAMIN B2 (RIBOFLAVIN)
indications: Vitamin B2 deficiency, polyneuritis, cheilosis, migraine prophylaxis
dosage_schedule: Adult: 5-30 mg/day; child >12 yr: PO 3-10 mg/day then 0.6 mg/1000 calories ingested. Migraine prophylaxis: adult- 400 mg/day for three months.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to vitamin B2, pregnancy (caution indicated)
precautions: Higher doses used for migraine prophylaxis.
adverse_effects: Yellow discoloration of urine
interactions: Decrease action of tetracyclines, may cause false elevations of urinary catecholamines
patient_info: Urine may turn bright yellow; Avoid alcohol.

name: VITAMIN B3 (NIACIN)
indications: Pellagra, hyperlipidemias (types 4, 5), peripheral vascular disease
dosage_schedule: Pellagra: adult, up to 500 mg daily in divided doses.
contraindications: Peptic ulcer, hepatic disease, hemorrhage, severe hypotension, glaucoma, coronary artery disease, diabetes mellitus, gout, schizophrenia
precautions: Assess cardiac status, nutritional status, CNS symptoms, Niacin deficiency, Hyperlipidemia.
adverse_effects: Paraesthesia, headache, dizziness, Postural hypotension, vasovagal attacks, dysrhythmias, vasodilation, blurred vision, ptosis, jaundice, hepatotoxicity, hepatitis, glycosuria
interactions: Statins increase risk of rhabdomyolysis. Cholestyramine, erythromycin, insulin decrease blood level of niacin.
patient_info: Flushing and feeling of warmth will occur; remain recumbent if postural hypotension occurs; abstain from alcohol; avoid sunlight if lesions are present.

name: VITAMIN B6 (PYRIDOXINE)
indications: Vitamin B6 deficiency, seizures, isoniazid therapy, oral contraceptives, alcoholic polyneuritis
dosage_schedule: Deficiency states: oral, 25–50 mg up to 3 times daily. Isoniazid neuropathy prophylaxis: oral, 10 mg daily. Treatment: oral, 50 mg 3 times daily. Sideroblastic anemia: oral, 100–400 mg daily in divided doses.
precautions: Patients taking levodopa should avoid supplemental vitamins with >5 mg pyridoxine.
adverse_effects: Paresthesia, flushing, warmth, lethargy, pain at injected site
patient_info: Avoid vitamin supplements unless directed; increase meat, bananas, potatoes, lima beans, whole grains, and cereals in diet.

name: VITAMIN B9 (FOLIC ACID)
indications: Megaloblastic or macrocytic anemia caused by folic acid deficiency; hepatic disease, alcoholism, hemolysis, intestinal obstruction, pregnancy to reduce risk for neural tube defects
dosage_schedule: Treatment of megaloblastic anemia: oral, adult, 5 mg daily for 4 months (up to 15 mg in malabsorption). Prevention of neural tube defects (first occurrence): oral, adult, 400–500 micrograms daily before conception and during first 12 weeks. Prevention of recurrence: oral, adult, 5 mg daily from 4 weeks before conception until 12th week.
contraindications: Anemia other than megaloblastic/macrocytic anemia, vit B12 deficiency anemia, uncorrected pernicious anemia
precautions: Should never be given without vitamin B12 in undiagnosed megaloblastic anemia to avoid subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord.
adverse_effects: Confusion, depression, excitability, irritability, anorexia, nausea, pruritus, rash, erythema, bronchospasm, anaphylaxis
interactions: Interacts with estrogen, hydantoins, carbamazepine, glucocorticoids; decreases levels of methotrexate, sulfonamides, trimethoprim
patient_info: Urine will turn bright yellow; alter nutrition to include high folic acids.

name: VITAMIN B12 (COBALAMIN)
indications: Vitamin B12 deficiency states, malabsorbtion, pernicious anemia, stomach or lower ileal resection; macrocytic anemia
dosage_schedule: Deficiency of dietary origin: oral- adult, 50-150 μg/day; child, 25-50 μg twice daily. IM injection: initially 1 mg repeated 10 times then 1 mg monthly. Pernicious anemia: IM injection, initially 1 mg repeated 5 times at intervals of 2 days, then 1 mg every 3 months.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to Vitamin B12, uremia, folate deficiency, concurrent infections, iron deficiency, renal dysfunction
precautions: Parenteral products should be used when deficiency is due to malabsorption. Switch to oral after remission.
adverse_effects: Dizziness, memory impairment, restlessness, hypertension, chest pain, tachycardia, dry throat, eye redness, diarrhea, dyspepsia, thrombocytosis, hypokalemia, pain at site
interactions: Chloramphenicol/antineoplastics decrease hematologic response; Colchicine, aminosalicylic acid, cimetidine, excess alcohol or Vitamin C decrease absorption
patient_info: Comply with diet recommendations of health care professional.

name: VITAMIN C (ASCORBIC ACID)
indications: Vitamin C deficiency, scurvy, delayed wound, bone healing, chronic disease; urine acidification; before gastrectomy; dietary supplement
dosage_schedule: Prophylaxis of scurvy: oral, 25–75 mg daily. Treatment of scurvy: oral, not less than 250 mg daily in divided doses.
contraindications: Tartrazine/sulfite sensitivity; glucose-6-phosphate deficiency. Pregnancy (caution), gout, diabetes, renal calculi
precautions: Caution in patients with a history of renal calculi or gout.
adverse_effects: Headache, insomnia, dizziness, fatigue, flushing, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, anorexia, heartburn, cramps, polyuria, hemolysis
interactions: Excess intake may decrease effectiveness of Vitamin B12.
patient_info: Addition of citrus fruits; avoid smoking.

name: ACETAZOLAMIDE
indications: Open-angle glaucoma, angle-closure glaucoma (preoperatively if surgery delayed), secondary glaucoma, acute altitude sickness, CHF, drug induced edema.
dosage_schedule: Angle closure glaucoma: 250 mg 24hr and 250 mg BD (oral/IV). Open-Angle glaucoma: 250 mg/day in divided doses (max 1 g/day).
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to sulfonamide, severe renal disease, hepatic disease, electrolyte imbalance (hyponatremia/hypokalemia), hyperchloremic acidosis, Addison’s disease, adrenocortical deficiency, cirrhosis.
precautions: Not recommended in non-congestive angle-closure glaucoma, hypercalciuria, diabetes, respiratory acidosis, pulmonary obstruction, emphysema, COPD. Monitor for impaired alertness.
adverse_effects: Confusion, convulsions, cholestatic jaundice, drowsiness, malaise, metallic taste, metabolic acidosis.
interactions: Increases action of amphetamines, phenytoin, procainamide, quinidine; increases toxicity of salicylate and cyclosporine; cardiac toxicity with arsenic trioxide/cardiac glycosides.

name: AMILORIDE HYDROCHLORIDE
indications: Oedema, CHF/HTN/Thiazide induced hypokalemia.
dosage_schedule: Oedema (alone): initially 10 mg daily (max 20 mg). Oedema (combination): 5 mg daily (max 20 mg). CHF/HTN induced hypokalemia: 5-10 mg/day q day or divided q12h. Renal impairment: CrCl 10-50 ml/min: 50% normal dose.
contraindications: Hyperkalaemia, Addison’s Disease, Renal failure (CrCL<10), Anuria, Diabetic nephropathy.
precautions: Caution in patients with diabetes mellitus, mild renal impairment, elderly, dehydration. Monitor potassium levels regularly.
adverse_effects: Hyponatremia, postural hypotension, diarrhoea, loss of appetite, dizziness.

name: CHLORTHALIDONE
indications: Hypertension, ascites due to cirrhosis, oedema due to nephrotic syndrome, mild to moderate chronic heart failure, nephrogenic diabetes insipidus.
dosage_schedule: Hypertension: 12.5-25 mg daily (max 50 mg). Edema: 50-100 mg daily or on alternate days (max 200 mg). CHF: 25–50 mg daily, increase to 100–200 mg for maintenance. Diabetes insipidus: 100 mg twice daily reduced to 50 mg daily.
precautions: Possible hazards include fetal/neonatal jaundice or thrombocytopenia. Lactation not recommended. Take in the morning with food.
adverse_effects: Hypotension, vasculitis, photosensitivity, electrolyte abnormalities, hyperglycemia, hyperuricemia, pancreatitis (rare).
interactions: Increases toxicity of aminolevulinic acid. Synergistic hypokalemia risk with amisulpride. Contraindicated with cisapride (QTc risk). Avoid with lithium.

name: EPLERENONE
indications: HTN, heart failure post MI, renal impairment, hepatic impairment.
dosage_schedule: HTN: Initial 50 mg PO qDay; may increase to 50 mg PO q12h. Heart failure post MI: Initial 25 mg PO qDay; may titrate to 50 mg daily based on potassium levels.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Serum potassium >5.5 mEq/L at initiation. Renal impairment (CrCl <50ml/min or creatinine >2 mg/dl in males / >1.8 mg/dl in females). Strong CYP3A inhibitors.
precautions: Risk of hyperkalemia is higher in patients with impaired renal function, proteinuria, and diabetes. Monitor for palpitations.
adverse_effects: Hyperkalemia, dizziness, fatigue, albuminuria, abdominal pain.
interactions: Itraconazole, Nefazodone, and Saquinavir increase eplerenone levels (CYP3A4 inhibition).

name: FUROSEMIDE
indications: Edema, heart failure, hypertension resistant to thiazide, AKI/CKD fluid overload, acute pulmonary edema, hypertensive crisis.
dosage_schedule: Edema: 40 mg morning, maintenance 20-40 mg daily (pediatric 1-3 mg/kg). Pulmonary edema/HTN crisis: 0.5 mg/kg (or 40 mg) IV over 1-2 min; max 160-200 mg/dose. ACLS: Hyperkalemia 40-80 mg IV; Hypermagnesemia 20-40 mg IV q3-4h.
contraindications: Renal failure with anuria, comatose/precomatose states with cirrhosis, dehydration, hyperkalemia, hypovolemia, severe hyponatremia.
precautions: Monitor for hypokalemia (high potassium diet recommended). Caution in prostatic enlargement, oliguria, and elderly. Monitor for hearing impairment.
adverse_effects: Hypokalemia, hyponatremia, tinnitus, hearing impairment, vomitting, diarrhea, hyperuricemia gout.
interactions: Predisposes to digitalis toxicity. Hypotensive effects enhanced by ACE inhibitors. Aminoglycosides increase ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity. Contraindicated with cisapride.

name: HYDROCHLORTHIAZIDE
indications: Edema (CHF, cirrhosis, nephritic syndrome, CKD, glomerulonephritis), hypertension, nephrogenic diabetes mellitus, calcium nephrolithiasis.
dosage_schedule: Hypertension: 12.5 mg daily (max 25-50 mg) in morning. Edema: 25-50 mg per oral initially, maintenance 25-50 mg on alternate days.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, anuria, hyponatremia, hypercalcemic states (hyperparathyroidism, malignancies), hypokalemia, hyperuricemia, polymorphic ventricular tachycardia.
precautions: Use caution in gout, elderly; may unmask diabetes. Monitor fluid/electrolyte balance. Monitor SLE status.
adverse_effects: Anaphylaxis, extracellular fluid volume depletion, hypokalemia, hyponatremia, hyperuricemia, hyperlipidemia, erectile dysfunction, hepatotoxicity.
interactions: Amphotericin B and Corticosteroids increase hypokalemia risk. Concomitant use with Quinidine risks fatal arrhythmias. Increases lithium effects.

name: INDAPAMIDE
indications: Hypertension, congestive heart failure.
dosage_schedule: Essential HTN: 2.5 mg daily (immediate-release) or 1.5 mg daily (sustained-release) in the morning. CHF: 2.5 mg daily in the morning.
precautions: Use caution in acute porphyria, hypotension, diabetes, hyperuricemia, gout, SLE. Safety not established in children.
adverse_effects: Skin rash, hypokalemia, anorexia, diarrhea, orthostatic hypotension, palpitation.
interactions: Avoid with arrhythmogenic drugs (e.g., Amiosulpride, Amitriptyline, Chlorpromazine, Cisapride, Fluconazole). Avoid with other diuretics due to hypokalemia risk.

name: MANNITOL
indications: Cerebral edema, raised intraocular pressure, anuria/oliguria.
dosage_schedule: Cerebral/Intraocular edema: 1.5-2 g/kg IV infused over 30-60 minutes. Anuria/Oliguria: Test dose 200 mg/kg (as 20% solution) IV over 3–5 min; re-evaluate if output <30–50 ml/hour.
contraindications: Pulmonary edema, intracranial bleeding (except during craniotomy), severe CHF, metabolic edema with capillary fragility, severe dehydration, renal failure (without test dose response).
precautions: Monitor fluid/electrolyte balance and renal function. Do not give simultaneously with blood. Risk of tissue necrosis on extravasation.
adverse_effects: Acidosis, circulatory overload, pulmonary edema, chest pain, visual disturbances, skin necrosis (extravasation), acute renal failure.
interactions: Increases excretion of salicylates, barbiturates, imipramine, and bromides.

name: METOLAZONE
indications: Hypertension, Edema.
dosage_schedule: Oedema: 5–10 mg daily (max 20 mg; up to 80 mg in resistant cases). Hypertension: 5 mg daily in morning; maintenance 5 mg daily on alternate days.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to sulfonamides, anuria, hepatic coma/precoma, acute porphyrias.
precautions: Drug crosses placenta. Monitor for fetal hypokalemia, hypoglycemia, jaundice. Caution in DM, hypercholesterolemia, gout, SLE, and liver disease.
adverse_effects: Chest pain, chills, electrolyte abnormalities, glucosuria, hyperuricemia, hepatotoxicity.
interactions: Metolazone + Chlorthalidone increases toxicity. Risks hypokalemia with Amisulpride. Contraindicated with cisapride.

name: SPIRONOLACTONE
indications: Edema and ascites in cirrhosis, nephrotic syndrome, CHF, primary hyperaldosteronism.
dosage_schedule: Edema: 100-200 mg daily (max 400 mg in resistance); child 1-3 mg/kg daily. Hyperaldosteronism: 400 mg daily for 3-4 weeks. CHF adjunct: 25 mg daily.
contraindications: Hyperkalemia, hyponatremia, Addison disease, moderate to severe renal impairment.
precautions: Monitor Blood Urea Nitrogen (BUN) and K+ regularly. Risk of breast cancer increased in chronic use.
adverse_effects: Hyperkalemia, metabolic acidosis (cirrhotics), gynecomastia, impotence, decreased libido, hirsutism, gastric bleeding.
interactions: CYP3A4 inhibitors (Clarithromycin, Ketoconazole, Ritonavir) may induce dangerous hyperkalemia by inhibiting catabolism.

name: TORSEMIDE
indications: Congestive heart failure, Chronic renal failure, Hepatic cirrhosis, Hypertension.
dosage_schedule: CHF/CRF: 10-20 mg daily initially, doubled up to max 200 mg. Cirrhosis: 5-10 mg daily (max 40 mg). Hypertension: 2.5-5 mg/day initially.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to torsemide or povidone, anuria, hepatic coma.
precautions: Monitor for hypokalemia, hyponatremia, hyperglycemia. Rise slowly to avoid orthostatic hypotension. Take with food.
adverse_effects: Headache, electrolyte imbalance, rhinitis, constipation, diarrhoea, dyspepsia.

name: TRIAMTERENE
indications: Edema, potassium conservation with thiazides and loop diuretics.
dosage_schedule: Initially 15-250 mg daily, reducing to alternate days after 1 week. Lower initial dose if given with other diuretics.
precautions: Regular monitoring of blood K+ required. May cause blue fluorescence of urine. Avoid high K+ diet (avocado, banana).
adverse_effects: Hyperkalemia, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, muscle cramps, dizziness.
interactions: Dangerous hyperkalemia when used with other K+ sparing diuretics.

name: DESMOPRESSIN
indications: Diabetes insipidus, primary nocturnal enuresis, post-operative polyuria, nocturia in multiple sclerosis.
dosage_schedule: DI: Adult/Child initially 300 μg PO (max 1.2 mg daily); Injection 1-4 μg daily. Enuresis: 200 μg bedtime (max 400 μg). Renal testing: 2 μg (SC/IM).
contraindications: Hyponatremia, cardiac insufficiency, renal impairment. Conditions treated with diuretics. Polydipsia in alcohol dependence.
precautions: Monitor for hyponatremia; therapy may be held if it occurs. Avoid fluid overload. Stop during vomiting/diarrhoea.
adverse_effects: Fluid retention, headache, nausea, epistaxis, allergic reaction.
interactions: Chlorpropamide and dobutamine increase effects (synergism). Demeclocycline, lithium, and alcohol diminish response.

name: VASOPRESSIN (ANTIDIURETIC HORMONE)
indications: Diabetes insipidus, abdominal distension, abdominal roentgenography, bleeding oesophageal varices.
dosage_schedule: DI: 5-20 units SC/IM q4h. Variceal bleeding: 20 units IV over 15 min. Distension: 5 units IM, repeat q3-4h (max 10 units). Roentgenography: 10 units SC/IM 2 hrs before then 10 units IM 30 min before.
precautions: Controlled infusion via device required. Caution in seizure, migraine, asthma, heart failure. Monitor for desire to defecate.
adverse_effects: Angina, fluid retention, sweating, tremor, constriction of coronary arteries, pounding in head, vertigo.
interactions: Amitriptyline, Carbamazepine, and Urea increase effects. Heparin and lithium decrease effects.

name: NITROFURANTOIN
indications: UTI, cystitis, pyelonephritis, postoperative urinary tract infection.
dosage_schedule: Adult: 50-100 mg per oral TID/QID. Child: 3-6 mg/kg body weight per oral in four divided doses.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, infant under 1-month, GFR <30 ml/min, pregnancy at term (38-42 weeks), hepatic dysfunction.
precautions: Avoid long term use in elderly. Caution in gastritis/diabetes. Enters breast milk (discontinue nursing). Do not crush tablets.
adverse_effects: Peripheral neuritis, chest pain, leukopenia, hemolytic anemia, GI intolerance, anorexia, brownish urine.
interactions: Probenecid increases levels. Antagonistic effect with norfloxacin.

name: BETHANECHOL
indications: Urinary retention.
dosage_schedule: Adult: 10-50 mg PO TID/QID. Some may require 50-100 mg PO twice daily. Take 1 hour before or 2 hours after meal.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, hyperthyroidism, peptic ulcer, asthma, bradycardia, AV Conduction defects, vagotonia, epilepsy, parkinsonism, obstructive pulmonary disease, HTN.
precautions: Decision required whether to discontinue nursing. Caution in GI disturbances or anastomosis.
adverse_effects: Abdominal cramps, belching, bronchial constriction, flushing, urinary urgency.
interactions: Ambenonium increases effects. Bethanechol increases and amitriptyline/flavoxate/solifenacin decrease cholinergic transmission.

name: FLAVOXATE
indications: Overactive bladder (OAB).
dosage_schedule: OAB: 100-200 mg PO q6-8hr.
contraindications: Obstructive uropathy, pyloric/duodenal obstruction, ileus, GI bleeding, achalasia.
precautions: May impair ability to perform hazardous tasks. Caution in patients with glaucoma. May cause ocular disturbances.
adverse_effects: Blurred vision, confusion, constipation, drowsiness, dry mouth, increased ocular tension, vertigo.
interactions: Pramlintide increases effects (contraindicated). Flavoxate decreases effects of secretin.

name: MIRABEGRON
indications: Overactive Bladder (OAB) with symptoms of urge urinary incontinence.
dosage_schedule: Adult: 25 mg PO qDay; may increase to 50 mg PO qDay. Severe renal impairment (Crcl 15-29ml/min): max 25 mg/day. ESRD: not recommended.
precautions: Discontinue nursing. May increase BP. Urinary retention may occur with bladder outlet obstruction. Angioedema reported.
adverse_effects: Elevated BP, dry mouth, nasopharyngitis, UTI, Steven Johnson syndrome.
interactions: Mirabegron increases levels of Amitriptyline, Codeine, Metoprolol, and Tramadol (inhibits CYP2D6).

name: OXYBUTYNIN
indications: Overactive bladder (OAB), detrusor overactivity.
dosage_schedule: OAB: IR 5 mg PO BID/TID (max 20mg); ER 5-10 mg PO daily (max 30mg). Pediatric IR (≥5 yrs): 5 mg PO q12h; ER (≥6 yrs): 5 mg daily (max 20mg).
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, gastric/urinary obstruction, paralytic ileus, severe UC, uncontrolled narrow-angle glaucoma.
precautions: Caution in Myasthenia gravis, tachycardia. May aggravate decreased GI motility. May cause memory loss.
adverse_effects: Dry mouth, constipation, somnolence, nausea.
interactions: Avoid solid oral dosage forms of Potassium chloride. Pramlintide increases effects (contraindicated).

name: SOLIFENACIN
indications: Overactive bladder (OAB), Urge incontinence.
dosage_schedule: OAB: 5 mg PO daily; may increase to 10 mg PO daily.
contraindications: Urinary/gastric retention, uncontrolled narrow angle glaucoma, severe hepatic impairment, hypersensitivity.
precautions: Avoid using drug or stop nursing. Monitor for elevated liver enzymes, hyperkalemia, renal impairment, and GERD.
adverse_effects: Dry mouth, Constipation, Abdominal Pain, Blurred Vision, Hallucinations.
interactions: Itraconazole increases levels (CYP3A4 inhibition). Caution with Ondansetron and Ketoconazole.

name: TOLTERODIN
indications: Overactive bladder, Urge incontinence.
dosage_schedule: OAB: IR 2 mg PO q12h; ER 2-4 mg PO once daily.
contraindications: Urinary/gastric retention, uncontrolled narrow angle glaucoma, hypersensitivity.
precautions: Caution in myasthenia gravis and renal impairment. Reduce dose when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Risk of angioedema.
adverse_effects: Dry mouth, blurred vision, constipation, dizziness, drowsiness, dyspepsia.
interactions: Carbamazepine decreases levels. Clarithromycin increases levels (CYP3A4 metabolism).

name: ALBUMIN
indications: Acute nephrosis, acute liver failure, ARDS, burns, hypoproteinemia, renal dialysis, hypovolemic shock, hemolytic disease of newborn.
dosage_schedule: Initial 25 g (5% or 25% solution) IV infusion; repeat q15-30 min if response adequate (max 250 g/48 hr). Daily max: 2 g/kg. Newborns: 1 g/kg prior to exchange transfusion.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to albumin/blood products, severe anaemia, cardiac failure, renal/post-renal anuria.
precautions: Monitor for hypervolaemia/pulmonary edema. Do not use sterile water as diluent (risk of ARF/hemolysis). Use within 4 hr of opening.
adverse_effects: Anaphylaxis, CHF, hypervolemia, tachycardia, pulmonary edema, bronchospasm.

name: GLUCOSE
indications: Fluid replacement without significant electrolyte deficit, hypoglycemia, varicose veins.
dosage_schedule: Fluid replacement: IV infusion based on clinical/electrolyte monitoring. Hypoglycemia: 25 ml of 50% solution into a large vein.
contraindications: Anuria, thiamine deficiency, trauma, intracranial hemorrhage, hemodilution, acute ischemic shock, hypophosphatemia, sepsis.
precautions: Caution in diabetes mellitus; monitor mannitol fluid balance.
adverse_effects: Venous irritation, thrombophlebitis, fluid/electrolyte disturbances, water intoxication (rapid infusion), hyperglycemia.

name: POTASSIUM CHLORIDE
indications: Prevention of hypokalaemia, electrolyte imbalance.
dosage_schedule: Prevention (oral): 2–4 g daily in divided doses. Electrolyte imbalance (IV): 1.5 g (20 mmol) in 10 mL mixed with 500 mL NaCl 0.9%, infused slowly over 2-3 hours.
contraindications: Plasma-potassium concentration >5 mmol/litre, severe renal impairment.
precautions: Overdose can be fatal. Concentration in peripheral IV should not exceed 40 mmol/L. Regularly monitor plasma potassium and ECG.
adverse_effects: Abdominal pain, diarrhea, heart toxicity (rapid infusion).

name: RINGER’S LACTATE
indications: Perioperative fluid/electrolyte replacement, hypovolemic shock, metabolic acidosis, peritoneal dialysis.
dosage_schedule: Adult: 1 to 3 L/day IV infusion based on clinical/electrolyte monitoring.
contraindications: Metabolic or respiratory alkalosis, hypocalcaemia, hypochlorhydria, hypernatremia.
precautions: Caution in renal failure, cardiac failure, hypertension, toxemia of pregnancy, corticosteroid therapy.
adverse_effects: Metabolic alkalosis, edema, tissue necrosis, hypernatremia, hypervolemia.

name: SODIUM BICARBONATE
indications: Metabolic acidosis, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, hyperkalemia, muscle spasm.
dosage_schedule: Metabolic acidosis: IV infusion of strong solution (up to 8.4%) or weak solution (up to 1.4%) as appropriate to body base deficit.
contraindications: Metabolic or respiratory alkalosis, hypocalcaemia, hypochlorhydria, hypoventilation, hypoosmolarity.
precautions: Use caution in cardiac failure, peripheral edema, toxemia of pregnancy. Monitor electrolytes and acid-base status.
adverse_effects: Hypokalemia, metabolic alkalosis, sodium accumulation, edema seizures, lactic acidosis, pulmonary edema, hyperventilation.

name: SODIUM CHLORIDE
indications: Extracellular fluid replacement, metabolic alkalosis with fluid loss, mild sodium depletion, diabetic ketoacidosis, sterile irrigation.
dosage_schedule: Replacement: IV, Adult as per requirement. Diabetic ketoacidosis: 500 mL IV infusion (0.9%) over 10-15 minutes; repeat if BP <90 mmHg.
contraindications: Congestive heart failure, severe renal impairment, hypertension, peripheral/pulmonary edema, conditions of sodium retention, liver cirrhosis.
precautions: Auscultate lungs for crepitations. Monitor JVP and right atrial venous pressure in elderly/seriously ill. Caution in toxemia of pregnancy.
adverse_effects: Sodium accumulation, hyperchloremic acidosis, hypokalemia, edema. Overdose: pulmonary edema, respiratory arrest, coma.

name: IPRATROPIUM BROMIDE
indications: COPD, bronchial asthma.
dosage_schedule: Aerosol pressurized inhalation: 20-40 µg, 3-4 times daily. Pediatric (up to 6 years): 20 µg 3 times daily; (6-12 years): 20-40 µg 3 times daily. Inhalation of powder: 40 µg 3-4 times daily.
contraindications: Closed angle glaucoma, urinary outflow obstruction, enlarged prostate.
precautions: Medical supervision necessary for first dose of nebulized solution (risk of paradoxical bronchospasm); protect eyes from drug powder. Child under 12 years: powder inhalation not recommended.
adverse_effects: Occasionally dry mouth, urinary retention, constipation, tachycardia, and atrial fibrillation.
interactions: Anticholinergic action increased with phenothiazines, antihistamines, disopyramide, belladonna. Bronchodilator effect increased with large amounts of tea.
patient_info: Shake well before use. Prime the inhaler before using for the first time by releasing 2 test sprays in the air away from face; rinse mouth after use.

name: BAMBUTEROL
indications: See under SALBUTAMOL.
dosage_schedule: Tablet: Initially 10 mg once daily at bed time, increased if necessary after 1-2 weeks to 20 mg once daily.
precautions: Not recommended in children.
adverse_effects: See under SALBUTAMOL.
patient_info: N/A

name: FORMOTEROL
indications: Asthma, prophylaxis of exercise-induced bronchospasm, nocturnal asthma, COPD.
dosage_schedule: Aerosol or Dry powder inhalation: Adult 12 µg twice daily; may be increased to 24 µg twice daily in severe airway obstruction.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Very rare QT-interval prolongation, dizziness, nausea, pruritus, taste disturbances.
patient_info: N/A

name: SALBUTAMOL
indications: Bronchial asthma, COPD.
dosage_schedule: Oral: 4 mg 3-4 times daily (Elderly/Sensitive: 2 mg initially). Pediatric (<2 yrs): 100 µg/kg 4 times daily; (2-6 yrs): 1-2 mg 3-4 times daily. Aerosol Inhalation: 100-200 µg (1-2 puffs) up to 3-4 times daily. Inhalation Powder: 200-400 µg 3-4 times daily. Nebulized Solution: 2.5 mg repeated up to 4 times daily.
contraindications: Should not be used to prevent premature labour in cases of pre-eclampsia, placenta previa, or bleeding.
precautions: Monitor blood glucose (risk of ketoacidosis with IV use). Caution in hyperthyroidism, myocardial insufficiency, arrhythmias, and hypertension.
adverse_effects: Muscle cramps, dizziness, headache, muscle tremor, palpitation, ankle edema, hypokalemia.
interactions: Concomitant use with corticosteroids or diuretics increases the risk of hypokalemia.
patient_info: High doses should be given by inhalation because parenteral use can affect the myometrium.

name: SALMETEROL
indications: Reversible airways obstruction (including nocturnal asthma and prevention of exercise-induced bronchospasm), COPD.
dosage_schedule: Aerosol or Dry powder inhalation (Adult): 50 µg (2 puffs or 1 blister) twice daily. Up to 100 µg twice daily in severe airway obstruction. Pediatric (>4 yrs): 50 µg twice daily.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, tachyarrhythmias, severe cardiac disease, pregnancy, breastfeeding, cardiac disorders, hyperthyroidism, diabetes, hypertension, close angle glaucoma, seizure, acute asthma.
precautions: Should not be used in children as monotherapy for asthma; use only in combination with inhaled steroid. Not recommended for children under 4 years.
adverse_effects: Headache, dizziness, tachycardia, palpitation, ventricular arrhythmias, cough.
patient_info: Hold breath for 10 seconds after inhalation. Wash rotahaler only with tap water.

name: TERBUTALINE SULFATE
indications: See under SALBUTAMOL.
dosage_schedule: Oral: 2.5-5 mg 2-3 times daily; Child: 0.1 µg/kg 3 times daily. SC/IM/Slow IV: 250-500 µg up to 4 times daily. Continuous IV Infusion: 1.5-5 µg/minute for 8-10 hours. Aerosol inhalation: 250-500 µg (1-2 puffs) 3-4 times daily.
precautions: Tolerance develops in long-term therapy; monitor for rebound bronchospasm.
adverse_effects: See under SALBUTAMOL.
interactions: Increases hypertensive crisis with MAOIs. Decreases action of beta-blockers. Effect increased with large amounts of green tea.
patient_info: N/A

name: BECLOMETHASONE DIPROPIONATE
indications: Chronic asthma (prophylaxis).
dosage_schedule: Aerosol Inhalation (Standard-dose): Adult 200 µg twice daily or 100 µg 3-4 times daily. Child: 50-100 µg 2-4 times daily. Aerosol Inhalation (High-dose): Adult 500 µg twice daily or 250 µg 4 times daily.
contraindications: Untreated fungal infection, active or quiescent tuberculosis.
precautions: Not for relief of acute symptoms. Monitor height of children receiving prolonged treatment; review therapy if growth is slowed.
adverse_effects: Oropharyngeal candidiasis, cough, dysphonia, adrenal suppression, growth retardation in children, impaired bone metabolism, glaucoma, cataract.
patient_info: Candidiasis can be reduced by using a spacer device and rinsing the mouth with water after inhalation.

name: BUDESONIDE
indications: Bronchial asthma.
dosage_schedule: Inhalation Powder: 0.2-1.6 mg daily in 2 divided doses. Child (<12 yrs): 200-800 µg daily in 2 divided doses. Nebulized Suspension: 1-2 mg twice daily. Child (3 mo - 12 yrs): 0.5-1 mg twice daily.
precautions: Caution in quiescent tuberculosis, osteoporosis, and diabetes. Maintain good oral hygiene. Avoid breastfeeding.
adverse_effects: Oropharyngeal candidiasis, cough, adrenal suppression (higher doses), growth retardation (in children), glaucoma.
interactions: Corticosteroids antagonize the hypotensive effect of ACE inhibitors, alpha-blockers, ARBs, and calcium channel blockers.
patient_info: Products are not always interchangeable due to different delivery routes and dosages. Shake canister well.

name: HYDROCORTISONE
indications: Inflammatory and allergic disorder, asthma, immunosuppression, nephritic syndrome, rheumatic disease, neoplastic disease, adrenal insufficiency.
dosage_schedule: Adult: Slow IV or infusion, 100-500 mg TDS or QID. Child (up to 1 yr): 25 mg daily; (1-5 yr): 50 mg daily; (5-12 yr): 100 mg daily. Local Ointment: 1-2 times daily.
contraindications: Active untreated infectious disease (except tuberculous meningitis), lactation, peptic ulcer, diabetes mellitus, psychiatric disease, undiagnosed fever.
precautions: Avoid live virus vaccines. Long-term therapy requires gradual withdrawal to avoid adrenal crisis.
adverse_effects: Euphoria, depression, seizure, vertigo, peptic ulceration, thromboembolism, hypertension, glaucoma, cataracts.
interactions: Hypokalemia with furosemide, HCTZ, or piperacillin. Reduces action of insulin and oral hypoglycemics.
patient_info: Corticosteroid user emergency card should be carried. Report abdominal pain or black tarry stools immediately.

name: MONTELUKAST
indications: Chronic asthma in adults and children, seasonal allergic rhinitis, bronchospasm prophylaxis.
dosage_schedule: Tablet (Adult/Child >15 yr): 10 mg daily in PM. Child (6-14 yr): 5 mg chewable tablet daily in PM. Child (2-5 yr): 1 packet (4 mg) granules daily in PM.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, children <6 yrs (for acute asthma), acute attack of asthma.
precautions: Alcohol consumption, severe hepatic disease, phenylketonuria, suicidal ideation, depression.
adverse_effects: Dizziness, fatigue, headache, behavior change, hallucinations, seizures, Churg-Strauss syndrome.
patient_info: Avoid hazardous activities as dizziness may occur. Continue using inhaled beta agonists if exercise-induced asthma is present.

name: ZAFIRLUKAST
indications: Prophylaxis and chronic treatment of asthma in adults/children >5yr, allergic rhinitis.
dosage_schedule: Adult and Child (>12 yr): 20 mg twice daily. Child (5-11 yr): 10 mg twice daily.
precautions: Monitor for symptoms of Churg-Strauss syndrome. Liver function test recommended.
adverse_effects: Headache, dizziness, nausea, diarrhea, abdominal pain, vomiting, hepatic failure, hepatitis, angioedema.
patient_info: N/A

name: SODIUM CROMOGLYCATE
indications: Prophylaxis of asthma, allergic rhinitis, allergic conjunctivitis.
dosage_schedule: Inhalation of powder (Adult/Child): 20 mg 4 times daily, increased up to 8 times daily in severe cases.
precautions: Caution in cardiac, hepatic, and renal diseases. Use in old age and children.
adverse_effects: Throat irritation and cough, nasal congestion, headache, dizziness, arthralgia, rashes, bronchospasm.
patient_info: Capsules must be used in an inhaler and not swallowed. Protect from moisture. For aerosol: exhale, place mouthpiece in mouth, breathe in as inhaler is activated.

name: EPHEDRINE HYDROCHLORIDE
indications: Reversible airways obstruction.
dosage_schedule: Tablet (Adult): 15-60 mg 3 times daily. Child: 3 times daily; (up to 1 yr): 7.5 mg; (1-5 yr): 15 mg; (6-12 yr): 30 mg.
precautions: Use with caution in hypertension, severe renal impairment, and prostate hypertrophy.
adverse_effects: Arrhythmias, insomnia, tremor, tachycardia.
patient_info: N/A

name: AMINOPHYLLINE
indications: Bronchial asthma, COPD, Neonatal apnea.
dosage_schedule: Oral: 100-300 mg three times a day. Injection: IV loading dose 6 mg/kg over 20-30 minutes, then maintenance 0.4 to 0.7 mg/kg/hour. Child loading dose: IV 5-6 mg/kg.
precautions: Therapeutic dose is near the toxic dose. Give carefully. Do not give IM or SC. Not for children under one year except in apnea of prematurity.
adverse_effects: Headache, dizziness, extra systoles, sinus tachycardia, anorexia, nervousness, tremor.
interactions: Additive side effects with sympathomimetics. Elevated serum levels with cimetidine, beta-blockers, erythromycin, allopurinol, or oral contraceptives.
patient_info: Take a lot of water with this medicine.

name: DOXOFYLLINE
indications: Asthma, COPD.
dosage_schedule: Adult: 400 mg once or twice daily. Children: 12 mg/kg/day.
precautions: Use with caution in hypoxemia, hyperthyroidism, liver disease, renal disease, and history of peptic ulcer.
adverse_effects: Headache, nausea, vomiting, sleeplessness, dizziness.
interactions: Should not be administered with other xanthine derivatives or caffeine-containing products.
patient_info: N/A

name: THEOPHYLLINE
indications: COPD, Bronchial asthma, Nocturnal asthma.
dosage_schedule: Adult: 200 mg bid, can increase to 300 mg bid. Neonatal apnea: Loading PO 5 mg/kg, maintenance 3-6 mg/kg/day. Bronchospasm: PO 12-14 mg/kg/day (Max 300 mg/day).
precautions: Close monitoring required as the effective dose is very close to the toxic dose.
adverse_effects: Nausea, vomiting, GI upset, headache, dizziness, convulsion.
interactions: Do not combine with ciprofloxacin, corticosteroids, erythromycin, or cimetidine (increases levels). Do not combine with carbamazepine, phenytoin, or barbiturates (decreases levels).
patient_info: Same as AMINOPHYLLINE.

name: CODEINE PHOSPHATE
indications: Non-productive cough, pain.
dosage_schedule: Pain: 30-60 mg every 4 hours (Max 240 mg daily). Child (1-12 yrs): 0.5-1 mg/kg every 6 hours. Cough: 15-30 mg 3-4 times daily. Child (5-12 yrs): 1-1.5 mg/kg 4 times daily.
contraindications: Asthmatics, patients with decreased respiratory reserve, history of drug abuse/drug-seeking behavior.
precautions: Use cautiously in severe prostatic hypertrophy and hepatic disease. Potential for physical dependence on prolonged use.
adverse_effects: Nausea, constipation, drowsiness, confusion, blurred vision, hypotension, bradycardia, respiratory depression (large doses).
interactions: Extreme caution with MAO inhibitors. Additive CNS depression with alcohol, antidepressants, antihistamines, sedatives.
patient_info: Avoid driving or activities requiring high alertness.

name: DEXTROMETHORPHAN
indications: Non-productive cough.
dosage_schedule: Syrup: 10-20 mg every 4-8 hours. Child (6-12 yrs): 5-10 mg every 4-8 hours (Max 60 mg/24h). Child (2-6 yrs): 2.5-5 mg every 4 hours (Max 30 mg/24h).
contraindications: Allergy to dextromethorphan, patients taking MAOIs or SSRIs, chronic productive cough.
precautions: Not for children under four years of age. Caution in patients with history of drug abuse.
adverse_effects: Dizziness, sedation, nausea.
interactions: Use with MAOIs may cause serotonin syndrome. CNS depression increased with alcohol, opioids, amiodarone. Quinidine may increase blood levels.
patient_info: N/A

name: NOSCAPINE
indications: Non-productive cough.
dosage_schedule: Linctus (Adult): 15-30 mg daily. Child (6-12 yr): 15 mg 3 times daily. Infant (2-6 yr): 7.5 mg 3 times daily.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Drowsiness, nausea, bronchospasm (large doses), hypertension.
patient_info: N/A

name: PHOLCODINE
indications: Non-productive cough.
dosage_schedule: Adult: 5-10 ml 3-4 times daily. Child (1-2 yr): 2.5-5 ml; (2-5 yr): 5 ml; (5-12 yr): 5-10 ml.
contraindications: Chronic lung diseases, liver or kidney failure, productive cough, pregnancy, breastfeeding, asthma, children under 5 years.
precautions: Acts for 12 hours. Practically no analgesic or addictive property.
adverse_effects: Dizziness, loss of attention, swelling of face/neck, difficulty in breathing.
interactions: Additive depressant effects with other CNS depressants.
patient_info: Do not drive or operate machines. Do not drink alcohol.

name: BROMHEXINE
indications: Reduction of sputum viscosity in COPD.
dosage_schedule: Oral: 8-16 mg 3 times daily. Child (2-6 yr): 8 mg 2-3 times daily. Child (6-12 yr): 4-8 mg per dose 3 times daily.
contraindications: Not recommended for infants < 1 year, severe hepatic/renal impairment.
precautions: Caution in patients with history of gastric ulceration (may disrupt mucosal barrier) and in pregnancy/breastfeeding.
adverse_effects: Gastrointestinal side effects, transient rise in serum aminotransferase, headache, vertigo, sweating.
interactions: Should not be given with paracetamol (increased risk of hepatitis).
patient_info: Take after meals.

name: CARBOCYSTEINE
indications: Reduction of sputum viscosity in COPD.
dosage_schedule: Adult: 750 mg 3 times daily initially, then 1.5 g daily in divided doses. Child (2-5 yr): 200-500 mg daily. Child (6-12 yr): 300-750 mg daily.
precautions: Caution in children under 2 years and patients with history of peptic ulceration.
adverse_effects: Skin rashes, occasional gastrointestinal irritation.
patient_info: N/A

name: ACETYL CYSTEINE
indications: Mucolytic, management of paracetamol (acetaminophen) overdose.
dosage_schedule: Nebulized: 1-10 mL of 20% solution or 2-20 mL of 10% solution every 2-6 hours.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Stomatitis, nausea, vomiting, fever, rhinorrhea, drowsiness, clamminess, chest tightness.
patient_info: N/A

name: PHENYLEPHRINE
indications: Nasal congestion associated with rhinitis, common cold, and sinusitis.
dosage_schedule: Oral: 5 mg 3-4 times a day. Nasal Spray: Child (1-6 yr) 1-2 drops 0.01%; (6-12 yr) 1-2 drops 0.25%; (>12 yr) 0.25% or 0.5%.
precautions: Caution in patients with diabetes, hypertension, ischemic heart disease, hepatic/renal impairment. Rinse dropper to prevent contamination.
adverse_effects: Increased heart rate, palpitation, tremors, ventricular premature contractions, hypertension.
patient_info: Stinging may occur.

name: PSEUDOEPHEDRINE
indications: Nasal congestion associated with rhinitis, common cold, sinusitis, otic inflammation.
dosage_schedule: Tablet (Adult): 60 mg 3-4 times daily. Child: 4 mg/kg/day per oral in 3-4 divided doses.
precautions: Use cautiously in patients with prostatic hypertrophy, ischemic heart disease, glaucoma, and diabetes.
adverse_effects: Nervousness, restlessness, dizziness, insomnia, headache, drowsiness, lightheadedness, nausea.
interactions: Do not use with MAOIs or tricyclics (risk of hypertensive crisis).
patient_info: Do not crush, divide, chew or dissolve. Avoid taking near bedtime.

name: CAFFEINE CITRATE
indications: Neonatal apnea in preterm infants.
dosage_schedule: Oral or IV: Loading dose 20-25 mg/kg, then 5-10 mg/kg once daily starting 24 hours later; continue for 4-5 days after cessation of apnea.
contraindications: Cardiovascular disorders, hepatic or renal impairment.
precautions: Monitor for CNS stimulation and tachycardia (toxicity).
adverse_effects: Lethargy (withdrawal sign), irritability, excessive CNS stimulation, tachycardia, hyperglycemia/hypoglycemia, hemorrhage, lung edema, renal failure.
patient_info: N/A

name: CARBAMAZEPINE
indications: Treatment of tonic-clonic, mixed and complex partial seizures (not used in absence seizures and myoclonic seizure), management of pain in trigeminal neuralgia or diabetic neuropathy, acute mania.
dosage_schedule: Anticonvulsant: PO (adults) 200mg BD, increase by 200mg/day to 600-1200mg/day (max 1g/day in 12-15 year olds). Antineuralgic: 100mg BD or 50mg QID, increase to 400-800mg/day. Children 6-12yr: 100mg BD, increase by 100mg weekly. Children <6yr: 10-20mg/kg/day.
contraindications: Bone marrow suppression, administration of MAO-I within last 14 days, jaundice, hepatitis.
precautions: Use cautiously in cardiac/hepatic disease, renal failure, glaucoma. Monitor for behavioral changes and suicidal ideation.
adverse_effects: Ataxia, drowsiness, CHF, renal damage, agranulocytosis, dilutional hyponatremia, exfoliative dermatitis, decreased platelets, increased risk of lupus.
interactions: Concurrent MAO-I use may result in hyperpyrexia and death. Induces hepatic enzymes; promotes its own metabolism and that of phenobarbital, phenytoin, oral contraceptives.
patient_info: Report behavioral changes or suicidal ideation immediately. Chewable tablets must be crushed or chewed before swallowing.
pregnancy_category: Risk of fetal carbamazepine syndrome (esp. 1st trimester).

name: CLOBAZAM
indications: Adjunct in epilepsy, anxiety.
dosage_schedule: Epilepsy: 20-30 mg daily (max 60mg); child >3yrs: not more than half adult dose. Anxiety: 20-30 mg daily in divided doses or single dose at bedtime (max 60mg in hospitalized patients); elderly 10-20 mg daily.
precautions: Do not stop the drug abruptly.
adverse_effects: Somnolence, sedation, pyrexia, URTI.
patient_info: Tablets should be swallowed whole; do not crush, break or chew.

name: CLONAZEPAM
indications: Status epilepticus, all types of epilepsy, anxiety disorder.
dosage_schedule: Seizures: 1.5 mg divided into 3 doses, raise by 0.5 mg every 3 days. Panic: 1 mg/day (max 4 mg/day).
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, severe liver diseases, respiratory depression, acute pulmonary insufficiency.
precautions: Do not stop the drug abruptly.
adverse_effects: Suicidal thoughts, dizziness, drowsiness, ataxia, muscle hypotonia, salivary/bronchial hypertension in infants, sexual dysfunction, dependence.
interactions: With verapamil, diltiazem: risk of AV block.
patient_info: Notify if mouth sores, fever, or signs of angioedema occur. Avoid prolonged use beyond prescription.

name: DIAZEPAM
indications: Adjunct in management of anxiety disorder, prior to cardioversion, preoperative sedation, conscious sedation, status epilepticus, skeletal muscle relaxant, alcohol withdrawal.
dosage_schedule: IV injection: 10-20 mg at 2.5 mg per 30 sec; repeat if necessary after 30-60 min; IV infusion max 3mg/kg over 24 hrs. Children: 200-300 μg/kg.
contraindications: Acute alcohol intoxication, myasthenia gravis, acute narrow angle glaucoma, sleep apnea, children <6 months.
precautions: Severe renal/hepatic impairment. Facilities for mechanical ventilation must be available. Administer IV slowly to reduce danger of apnea and hypotension.
adverse_effects: Apnea, hypotension, thrombophlebitis, dizziness, drowsiness, lethargy, ataxia, dependence.
interactions: Concomitant use with opioids and/or other CNS depressants may result in profound respiratory depression.
patient_info: N/A

name: GABAPENTIN
indications: Adjunct treatment of partial seizures, bipolar affective disorder (BPAD), post-herpetic neuralgia, neuropathic pain.
dosage_schedule: Epilepsy: 300mg day 1, 300mg BD day 2, 300mg TID day 3, increase to max 2.4 g/day. Child (6-12yr): 10-35 mg/kg daily. Maintenance: 900 mg daily.
contraindications: Increased blood CPK levels and rhabdomyolysis.
precautions: Safety not established in children <3yrs or pregnant women.
adverse_effects: Ataxia, dizziness, drowsiness, fatigue, somnolence, diplopia, nystagmus, tremor, suicidal thoughts.
interactions: Antacids may decrease absorption. Increased risk of CNS depression with other CNS depressants.
patient_info: Do not drive until experienced with the drug. Do not discontinue abruptly (may increase seizure frequency). Gradually taper over 1 week.

name: LACOSAMIDE
indications: Monotherapy or adjunctive treatment of focal seizures with or without secondary generalization.
dosage_schedule: Monotherapy: 100 mg PO/IV 12hrly initially, increase at weekly intervals to 150-200 mg BID (300-400 mg/day). Adjunctive: Initial 50 mg PO/IV 12hrly.
precautions: Conduction problems, elderly, severe cardiac disease. Caution in renal/hepatic impairment.
adverse_effects: Abnormal gait, tremor, impaired coordination, nystagmus, blurred vision, headache, agitation, cardiac arrhythmias.
patient_info: N/A

name: LAMOTRIGINE
indications: Partial, secondarily generalized tonic-clonic seizures, Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, bipolar affective disorder.
dosage_schedule: Monotherapy: 25mg daily initially, increased to 100-200mg maintenance. Adjunct with valproate: initially 25mg every other day. Adjunct with carbamazepine: initially 50mg/day.
precautions: Cardiac/renal/hepatic disease, severe depression, blood dyscrasias.
adverse_effects: Dizziness, ataxia, blurred or double vision, nausea, vomiting, rash, Stevens-Johnson syndrome.
patient_info: Take with food if GI upset occurs. Do not discontinue abruptly. Stop drug and consult doctor at first sign of rashes.

name: LEVETIRACETAM
indications: Monotherapy or adjunctive therapy of focal seizures, myoclonic seizures, and tonic-clonic seizures.
dosage_schedule: N/A (Refer to primary entry in formulary for specific titration).
precautions: Monitor carefully during pregnancy. Cautions in hepatic and renal impairment; monitor renal function regularly.
adverse_effects: Abdominal pain, anorexia, agitation, anxiety, convulsion, alopecia, amnesia, diplopia, leucopenia, thrombocytopenia, suicidal ideation.
patient_info: Consult therapist in case of suicidal ideation or chest pain.

name: OXCARBAZEPINE
indications: Monotherapy or adjunctive therapy of partial seizures.
dosage_schedule: Initial 300 mg BD, increase to 0.6-2.4 g daily in divided doses. Child >6yr: 8-10mg/kg daily in 2 divided doses.
precautions: Renal impairment. Monitor for behavior changes associated with suicidal thoughts. Monitor for hyponatremia.
adverse_effects: Suicidal thoughts, dizziness, diplopia, nystagmus, ataxia, abnormal gait, tremor, SJS.
interactions: May render oral contraceptives ineffective. Increased CNS depression with CNS depressants.
patient_info: Immediate release tablets should be taken on empty stomach. Extended release should be swallowed whole; do not crush, break or chew.

name: PHENOBARBITAL
indications: Anti-convulsant in tonic-clonic, partial and febrile seizures; pre-operative sedative; hypnotic (short term).
dosage_schedule: Status epilepticus: 15-18 mg/kg. Maintenance (Adults): 1-3mg/kg/day. Sedation (Adult): 30-120 mg/day in 2-3 divided doses. Hypnotic: 100-300 mg at bedtime.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, porphyria, severe hepatic impairment, COPD, dyspnea, pregnancy and lactation.
precautions: Hepatic/renal dysfunction; history of suicide or drug abuse. Monitoring of drug levels in plasma. Be aware of risk of fall among elderly and children.
adverse_effects: Ataxia, dizziness, nystagmus, impairment in cognitive function, respiratory depression, hypotension, angioedema, serum sickness.
interactions: Induces hepatic microsomal enzymes; decreases plasma concentrations of carbamazepine, warfarin, OCPs, and corticosteroids.
patient_info: N/A
pregnancy_category: Chronic use results in drug dependency in infant; risk of fetal malformations and coagulation defects.

name: PHENYTOIN
indications: All forms of epilepsy (except absence, myoclonic, drug-induced), trigeminal neuralgia.
dosage_schedule: Oral: initially 3-4 mg/kg or 150-300mg daily; child 4-8 mg/kg daily. Status epilepticus: Slow IV injection 15mg/kg at max 50mg/min.
precautions: Pharmacokinetic variability; needs therapeutic drug level monitoring. Monitor for suicidal thoughts and gingival hypertrophy. Not recommended by IM injection.
adverse_effects: Suicidal thoughts, agranulocytosis, aplastic anemia, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, gingival hyperplasia, hirsutism.
