interactions: Metabolism inhibited by isoniazid, chloramphenicol, sulfonamides. Inducers like carbamazepine/alcohol result in low plasma levels. Induces metabolism of OCPs.
patient_info: Inform physician in case of suicidal thoughts or swelling of gums.

name: TOPIRAMATE
indications: Monotherapy or adjunctive treatment of generalized tonic-clonic or focal seizures, Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, migraine prophylaxis, substance dependence.
dosage_schedule: N/A (Refer to primary entry for specific titration).
precautions: Risk of metabolic acidosis and nephrolithiasis; ensure adequate hydration.
adverse_effects: Anxiety, cognitive impairment, sleep disturbance, GI distress, paraesthesia, speech disorder.
patient_info: Ensure adequate hydration; consult doctor if flank pain or burning micturition occurs.

name: VALPROIC ACID
indications: All forms of epilepsy, bipolar affective disorder.
dosage_schedule: Initial 600 mg daily; increase by 200 mg/day every 3 days (max 2.5 g/day). Child up to 20 kg: 20 mg/kg daily. IV initiation: 400-800 mg (up to 10 mg/kg).
precautions: Monitor hepatic function tests before treatment and every 2 months for first six months.
adverse_effects: Suicidal thoughts, tremor, gastric irritation, weight gain, thrombocytopenia, transient hair loss, drug induced hepatitis.
interactions: Increased risk of bleeding with warfarin.
patient_info: Monitor weight and blood sugar. Avoid conception.

name: AMANTADINE
indications: Parkinsonism, post-herpetic neuralgia.
dosage_schedule: 100mg daily, increase after 1 week to 100mg twice daily (max 400mg daily).
precautions: In patients with cardiac, hepatic or renal disease. Watch for confusion or mottling of skin.
adverse_effects: Restlessness, insomnia, excitement, livedo reticularis, peripheral edema, postural hypotension.
interactions: Increases anticholinergic response of atropine. Metoclopramide and phenothiazines decrease effect.
patient_info: Take after meals. Avoid hazardous activities if dizziness or blurred vision occurs.

name: BENZTROPINE
indications: Parkinsonism, EPS associated with neuroleptic drugs, acute dystonic reactions, hypersalivation.
dosage_schedule: 0.5-1 mg at bedtime, increase by 0.5 mg q5-6 days (max 6mg/day).
contraindications: Children <3yrs, closed angle glaucoma, dementia, tardive dyskinesia, GI/GU obstruction, peptic ulcer, prostrate hypertrophy.
precautions: Pregnancy, renal/hepatic disease, myasthenia gravis.
adverse_effects: Hallucinations, delirium, palpitation, tachycardia, paralytic ileus, hyperthermia, heat stroke.
interactions: Amantadine, TCAs, and antihistamines increase effects. Antacids decrease absorption.
patient_info: Do not discontinue abruptly; taper over 1 week. Avoid driving. Take plenty of fluids.

name: BROMOCRIPTINE
indications: Parkinsonism, hyperprolactinemia, galactorrhoea, infertility, acromegaly.
dosage_schedule: Parkinsonism: 1-1.25 mg OD at bedtime (1st week), increase to 7.5-30 mg/day maintenance.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to ergot alkaloids, breast carcinoma, severe ischemic heart disease, uncontrolled HTN.
precautions: History of psychosis, peptic ulcer, DM. Ability to drive may be impaired.
adverse_effects: Nausea, vomiting, postural hypotension, altered taste, cardiac arrhythmia, psychosis.
interactions: May result in failure of OCPs. Disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol.
patient_info: Raise slowly from lying/sitting. Take with food to reduce GI upset.

name: ENTACAPONE
indications: Adjunct in Parkinson’s disease with ‘end-of-dose’ motor fluctuations.
dosage_schedule: Oral, adult: 200 mg with each dose of levodopa (max 2 g/day).
contraindications: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome, non-traumatic rhabdomyolysis, phaeochromocytoma, hepatic failure.
precautions: Avoid in pregnancy; avoid in breastfeeding (present in milk).
adverse_effects: Abnormal dreams, dyskinesia, dystonia, ischaemic heart disease.
interactions: Avoid iron-containing products at the same time of day.
patient_info: May colour urine reddish-brown with concomitant iron products.

name: LEVODOPA AND CARBIDOPA
indications: Parkinsonism.
dosage_schedule: 100mg levodopa + 25mg carbidopa TID before meal. Increase by 1 tab every 1-2 days (max 8 tabs/day).
contraindications: Acute angle closure glaucoma, psychotic illness, malignant melanoma.
precautions: MI, cerebrovascular accidents. Monitor skin lesions for malignant melanoma.
adverse_effects: Altered taste, cardiac arrhythmia, angina, delusion, nightmares.
interactions: Pyridoxine promotes metabolism. Phenothiazines and butyrophenones antagonize effects.
patient_info: Inform patient of 'wearing off' effect. Take 30 mins before meals.

name: PRAMIPEXOLE
indications: Parkinson’s disease, restless leg syndrome.
dosage_schedule: N/A (Refer to primary entry in formulary for specific titration).
contraindications: Severe cardiovascular disease. Avoid in breast feeding.
precautions: Psychotic disorders, risk of visual disorders (ophthalmological testing recommended).
adverse_effects: Sudden onset of sleep, dyskinesia, visual disturbances, impulse control disorders (pathological gambling, hypersexuality).
patient_info: N/A
pregnancy_category: Use in pregnancy only if potential benefit outweighs risk.

name: RASAGILINE
indications: Parkinson’s disease, adjunct for ’end-of-dose’ fluctuations.
dosage_schedule: Oral, adult: 1 mg daily.
precautions: Avoid abrupt withdrawal.
adverse_effects: Weight loss, vertigo, skin carcinoma.
interactions: May cause serotonin syndrome when used with antidepressants.
patient_info: Avoid high tyramine containing food.

name: ROPINIROLE
indications: Parkinson’s disease.
dosage_schedule: N/A (Refer to primary entry for specific titration).
precautions: Monitor blood pressure (risk of hypotension). Monitor for impulsive behavior.
adverse_effects: Gastro-oesophageal reflux, sudden onset sleep, impulse control disorders.
patient_info: Caution when driving. Consult in case of impulsive behavior.
pregnancy_category: Avoid in pregnancy unless benefit outweighs risk (toxicity in animal studies).

name: SELEGILINE HYDROCHLORIDE
indications: Parkinson’s disease.
dosage_schedule: Tablet: 5 mg daily, increase to 10 mg daily. Lyophilisate: 1.25 mg daily before breakfast.
contraindications: Active duodenal or gastric ulceration, avoid in postural hypotension (with levodopa).
precautions: Caution in renal and hepatic impairment. Lyophilisates should be allowed to dissolve on tongue.
adverse_effects: Movement disorders, impaired balance, mouth ulcers, stomatitis.
interactions: Increased risk of serotonin syndrome with SSRIs.
patient_info: Do not drink, rinse, or wash mouth for 5 minutes after taking tablet.

name: TRIHEXYPHENIDYL HYDROCHLORIDE (BENZHEXOL)
indications: Drug induced parkinsonism.
dosage_schedule: 1 mg daily, gradually increased to maintenance 5-15mg daily in 3-4 divided doses.
precautions: Not recommended in children. Monitor fluid intake and urine output ratio.
adverse_effects: Atropine like effects (dry mouth, constipation, impaired vision).
patient_info: Take plenty of fluids and bulk forming food. Monitor urine output.

name: ERGOTAMINE TARTARATE
indications: Acute attack of migraine unresponsive to analgesics; menopausal hot flushes.
dosage_schedule: Migraine: 2mg sublingual then 1.2mg every 30mins (max 6mg/day, 10mg/week). Menopausal flushes: 0.6mg PO q12h.
contraindications: PVD, CAD, Raynaud’s disease, pregnancy/lactation, severe HTN. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors (ritonavir, macrolides, antifungals).
precautions: Sepsis, malnutrition, impaired renal/hepatic function. Should be initiated at first sign of vascular headache.
adverse_effects: Arterial spasm, intermittent claudication, neck stiffness, numbness or tingling.
interactions: CYP3A4 inhibitors may produce life-threatening peripheral ischemia.
patient_info: Discontinue if signs of impaired circulation occur.

name: RIZATRIPTAN
indications: Acute migraine.
dosage_schedule: Oral, adult: 10 mg as soon as possible, follow with 10 mg after 2 hours if required (max 20 mg/day).
contraindications: Severe hypertension, coronary vasospasm, ischaemic heart disease, peripheral vascular disease, history of MI/TIA/CVA.
precautions: Hepatic/renal impairment, pregnancy. Drowsiness may affect performance of skilled tasks.
adverse_effects: Decreased alertness, drowsiness, pharyngeal discomfort.
interactions: May enhance toxic effects of serotonin modulators.
patient_info: Orodispersible tablets should be placed on tongue, allowed to disperse and swallowed.
pregnancy_category: Present in milk; withhold breast-feeding for 24 hours.

name: SUMATRIPTAN
indications: Acute migraine attacks, cluster headache.
dosage_schedule: Oral: 50-100 mg. SC injection: 6 mg (max 12 mg in 24 hours). Cluster headache: 6mg SC; may repeat in > 1hr.
contraindications: Ischemic cardiac/cerebrovascular/peripheral vascular syndromes, WPW syndrome, uncontrolled HTN, use within 2 weeks of MAO-A inhibitors.
precautions: Should not be given intravenously (may cause vasospasm). Avoid breast feeding for 8-12 hrs after administration.
adverse_effects: Injection site reaction, jaw or neck tightness, diaphoresis.
patient_info: May cause depression/drowsiness; caution when operating machinery.

name: FLUNARIZINE
indications: Migraine prophylaxis.
dosage_schedule: Oral, adult: 10-20 mg once daily; child: 5 mg once daily.
contraindications: Depression, acute phase of stroke, extrapyramidal symptoms or Parkinson’s disease.
precautions: May cause CNS depression. Monitor for extrapyramidal symptoms.
adverse_effects: Drowsiness, extrapyramidal effects, depression in elderly, weight gain, galactorrhea.
interactions: Effects of alcohol and sedating drugs can be increased.
patient_info: Administer with water at bedtime.

name: PREGABALIN
indications: Peripheral and central neuropathic pain, adjunct for focal seizures, generalized anxiety disorder.
dosage_schedule: Neuropathic pain: initially 150 mg daily, increase to 600 mg. Focal seizures: initially 25 mg twice daily. GAD: initially 150 mg daily.
precautions: Conditions that may precipitate encephalopathy, severe CHF, renal impairment. Avoid abrupt withdrawal (taper over 1 week).
adverse_effects: Appetite changes, weight gain, visual field defects, impaired memory, speech disorder.
interactions: Increased CNS depression if taken with alcohol.
patient_info: Medicine may cause sleepiness, weight gain and dizziness.

name: BUPRENORPHINE
indications: Perioperative analgesia; moderate to severe pain; withdrawing opioid addicts; chronic non-malignant pain.
dosage_schedule: IM/Slow IV: 300-600 µg every 6-8hrs. Sublingual tablet: 200-400 µg every 8hrs.
contraindications: Drug overdose can result in coma/death.
precautions: Controlled substance; potential for addiction. Keep naloxone on hand.
adverse_effects: See under Morphine; less abuse potential than Morphine.
patient_info: Do not chew or swallow sublingual tablet; hold under tongue until it dissolves. Warning: possibility of dependence.

name: CODEINE PHOSPHATE
indications: Management of mild to moderate pain, headache, non-productive cough, opioid withdrawal.
dosage_schedule: Pain: 30-60mg 3-4 times a day.
contraindications: Respiratory depression, obstructive airway disease, acute asthma attack, paralytic ileus.
precautions: BPH, head trauma, dependence. Breastfeeding children <1 year. Protected from light.
adverse_effects: Constipation, sedation, nausea/vomiting; less liable than morphine to produce tolerance/dependence.
patient_info: Take with food to minimize GI upset. Increase intake of fluid and fiber.

name: METHADONE HYDROCHLORIDE
indications: Severe pain, adjunct in treatment of opioid dependence, cough in terminal disease.
dosage_schedule: Opioid dependence: initially 10-40mg daily, increase by max 10mg daily to usual range 60-120 mg.
precautions: Controlled substance; potential for addiction. Not recommended to children.
adverse_effects: See under Morphine.
interactions: Rifampicin and Phenytoin accelerate metabolism (can precipitate withdrawal).
patient_info: N/A

name: MORPHINE SULPHATE
indications: Severe pain, MI, acute pulmonary edema, adjunct during major surgery and post-operative analgesia.
dosage_schedule: Acute pain (SC/IM): 10mg every 4 hours. MI (IV): 2mg/min, 10mg followed by further 5-10mg.
contraindications: Respiratory insufficiency, bronchial asthma, undiagnosed acute abdominal pain, head injury.
precautions: Elderly/debilitated, dependence, convulsive disorders. Obtain baseline respiratory rate and pupil size. Bedside rails advisable.
adverse_effects: Classic triad: pinpoint pupil, respiratory depression, coma. Mental clouding, urinary retention, apnoea in newborn.
patient_info: Sustained release tablets should not be crushed.

name: PETHIDINE HYDROCHLORIDE (MEPERIDINE)
indications: Moderate to severe pain and for obstetric analgesia.
dosage_schedule: PO: 50-150mg every 4 hours. IM/SC: 25-100mg. Obstetrical analgesia: 50-100mg (max 400mg in 24 hours).
precautions: May cause life-threatening respiratory depression. Potential for addiction and abuse.
adverse_effects: Similar to morphine; more severe nausea and hypotension. Equianalgesic doses produce similar respiratory depression.
interactions: With MAO-I may cause serious (possibly fatal) reaction.
patient_info: N/A

name: TRAMADOL HYDROCHLORIDE
indications: Moderate pain, adjunct in chronic pain.
dosage_schedule: Oral: 50-100mg q4h (total >400mg not usually required). IM/IV/Infusion: 50-100mg every 4-6hrs.
precautions: Do not confuse with Toradol (Ketorolac). Monitor for seizure.
adverse_effects: Seizures, somnolence, nausea.
interactions: CNS depressants (increased risk); B-Lactam antibiotics (increased seizure risk).
patient_info: Tablets should be swallowed whole; do not crush, break or chew.

name: NALOXONE
indications: Opioid overdose (coma and respiratory depression), neonatal asphyxia, postoperative opioid reversal.
dosage_schedule: Adult IV: 0.4-2mg repeated at 2-3 min intervals (max 10mg). Child: 10μg/kg.
precautions: Physical dependence on opioids (may precipitate acute withdrawal).
adverse_effects: Sweating, withdrawal symptoms in opioid abusers.
interactions: Antagonizes the effects of opioid analgesics.
patient_info: Watch for signs of opioid withdrawal.

name: NALTREXONE
indications: Opioid dependence, alcohol dependence, herpetic neuralgia, Crohn’s disease in children.
dosage_schedule: Chronic opioid dependence: PO 25mg day 1, then 50mg once daily. IM: 380mg every 4 weeks.
contraindications: Currently dependent on opioids; acute hepatitis or liver failure.
precautions: Risk of hepatotoxicity with increasing doses. Discontinue if signs of acute hepatitis develop.
adverse_effects: Injection site reaction, decreased appetite, arthralgia.
patient_info: Must be opioid free for 7-10 days before therapy. Do not use opioids while taking.

name: PENTAZOCINE
indications: Moderate to severe pain, preoperative/pre-anesthetic supplement.
dosage_schedule: Oral: 50mg q3-4h. Severe pain: 45-60mg IM/IV q3-4h.
contraindications: Toxin-mediated diarrhea, Pseudomonas enterocolitis, respiratory depression, MI.
precautions: Use cautiously in acute asthma, bradycardia. May produce acute withdrawal symptoms in opioid-dependent users.
adverse_effects: Pulmonary artery hypertension, tolerance, dependence.
patient_info: Do not consume alcohol while taking.

name: MIRTAZAPINE
indications: Major depression, PTSD (off label), insomnia (off label).
dosage_schedule: Depression (Adult): 15 mg PO HS; increase to max 60 mg HS. Geriatric: 7.5 mg PO HS.
precautions: Start slowly in hepatic/renal dysfunction. Discontinue if neutropenia/agranulocytosis occur.
adverse_effects: Somnolence, xerostomia, weight gain, reversible agranulocytosis.
interactions: Do not use within 14 days of MAOI.
patient_info: May cause dizziness/weakness.

name: FLUOXETINE
indications: Major depression, OCD, bulimia nervosa, panic disorder.
dosage_schedule: Adult Depression/OCD: Initial 20 mg PO daily; max 80 mg/day. Bulimia: 60 mg once daily.
precautions: Monitor closely for suicidal tendencies. Discontinue if symptomatic hyponatremia occurs.
adverse_effects: Insomnia, sexual dysfunction, taste disturbances, serotonin syndrome.
interactions: Do not use with MAO inhibitors (within 14 days). Do not use with linezolid or pimozide.
patient_info: Effect may take 1-4 weeks. Take in the morning to reduce insomnia risk.

name: LITHIUM
indications: Prophylaxis and treatment of mania, prophylaxis of bipolar disorder, hyperthyroidism.
dosage_schedule: Up to 1.5 g daily in single or divided doses; adjusted by plasma concentration.
contraindications: Hypothyroidism, sick sinus syndrome, heart blocks, renal diseases.
precautions: Regularly monitor serum lithium levels and thyroid/renal function. Lithium crosses placenta.
adverse_effects: Fine tremor, polydipsia, weight gain, acne, oedema.
interactions: NSAIDs (ibuprofen, diclofenac) and ACE inhibitors increase serum concentrations by reducing excretion.
patient_info: Avoid drinking coffee as caffeine decreases lithium levels. Monitor salt intake.
pregnancy_category: Use during pregnancy only in life-threatening situations.

name: ALPRAZOLAM
indications: Anxiety disorders, agoraphobia, panic disorders, depression.
dosage_schedule: 0.25 to 0.5 mg TID; max total daily 3 mg. Elderly: 0.25 mg BID/TID.
contraindications: Respiratory depression, severe hepatic impairment, angle closure glaucoma.
precautions: Monitor respiratory function. Watch for signs of tolerance and dependence.
adverse_effects: Confusion, physical dependence, changes in libido.
interactions: Increases sedative effect of opioid analgesics.
patient_info: May impair mental alertness. Do not share medicine.

name: ZOLPIDEM
indications: Insomnia.
dosage_schedule: 10 mg at bedtime; elderly 5 mg.
contraindications: Children, severe hepatic/pulmonary insufficiency, myasthenia gravis, obstructive sleep apnea.
precautions: Use with caution in depression.
adverse_effects: Nightmares, asthenia, memory disturbances, ataxia.
patient_info: See under alprazolam.

name: HALOTHANE
indications: Induction and maintenance of general anaesthesia
dosage_schedule: Induction: Done using a special calibrated vaporizer, increased gradually to 2-4% in oxygen or nitrous oxide-oxygen; child: 1.5-2%. Maintenance: 0.5-2%.
contraindications: History of unexplained jaundice or pyrexia in a patient following exposure to halothane. Avoid repeated exposure to halothane in less than three months.
precautions: Careful anaesthetic history should be taken to determine previous exposure and previous reaction to halothane.
adverse_effects: Nausea and vomiting, acidosis, dehydration and fever in children (may predispose to convulsions under ether anaesthesia). May cause excessive bleeding during caesarean section and post-partum haemorrhage.
interactions: With adrenaline, heart is sensitized to the actions of catecholamines.

name: ISOFLURANE
indications: Induction and maintenance of general anesthesia (usually not preferred for induction due to ether-like odor)
dosage_schedule: Using a special calibrated vaporizer. Induction: Increased gradually from 0.5% to 3% in oxygen or nitrous oxide-oxygen. Maintenance: 1-2.5% in nitrous oxide-oxygen; an additional 0.5-1% may be required when given with oxygen alone.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to isoflurane and halogenated agents, genetic susceptibility to malignant hyperthermia. Coronary artery disease; should not be used as a sole agent of induction in patients with ventricular dysfunction.
precautions: Use cautiously in lactation. Safety and efficacy not established in pediatric patients.
adverse_effects: Nausea, vomiting, shivering, dose-dependent hypotension, arrhythmia, respiratory depression (rare), risk of perioperative hyperkalemia and malignant hypertension (especially in Duchenne’s muscular dystrophy).
interactions: Concomitant use of succinylcholine has been associated with hyperkalemia and potentiation of muscle relaxant action.

name: NITROUS OXIDE
indications: Used as a carrier gas for more powerful general anesthetic drugs like desflurane and sevoflurane
dosage_schedule: Mixture with 50% O2 during labor.
contraindications: Pneumothorax, pneumoperitoneum, middle ear or sinus disease, bowel obstruction.
precautions: Should be used cautiously in 1st and 2nd trimester of pregnancy and in patient with decreased level of consciousness or in violently disturbed psychiatric patient.
adverse_effects: Megaloblastic anemia due to Vit. B12 and folate deficiency; teratogenic (avoid in 1st and 2nd trimester).
interactions: When given with other strong anesthetic drugs like desflurane and isoflurane, effect of both drugs increases.

name: OXYGEN
indications: Along with inhalational anesthesia, cluster headache, hyperbaric oxygen (decompression sickness, air/gas embolism, gas gangrene, necrotising fasciitis, radiation therapy), respiratory failure.
dosage_schedule: During anesthesia/general: Nasal prongs or face mask (up to 60%); Tight-fitting masks or ETT (up to 100%). Respiratory failure: Face masks at 5 L/min. Cluster headache: Inhalation of 100% oxygen. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy: Intermittent inhalation of 100% oxygen under pressure >1 atmosphere in a specialized chamber.
contraindications: Avoid high concentrations in patients whose respiration is dependent upon hypoxic drive.
precautions: Valves and taps should not be lubricated with oil or grease. Any fire or spark is highly dangerous in the presence of increased oxygen concentrations.
adverse_effects: Concentrations >80% have toxic lung effects (pulmonary congestion, exudation, atelectasis). Retinopathy of prematurity. Hyperbaric therapy may cause barotrauma or CNS/pulmonary toxicity.

name: SEVOFLURANE
indications: Anesthesia
dosage_schedule: Surgical anaesthesia: Inhalation. 0.5 months full term neonate: 3.3% in O2; 1-6 months: 3% in O2; 6 mo-3 years: 2.8% in O2; 25-40 years: 2.1% in O2; 60-80 years: 1.4% in O2 (detailed age-based ranges in formulary).
contraindications: Should not be used as a sole agent for induction in patients with ventricular dysfunction. Susceptibility to malignant hyperthermia, hypersensitivity, lack of ventilatory support.
precautions: Caution in patients with anemia, hepatic impairment, myxedema, renal impairment, or QTc prolongation.
adverse_effects: Malignant hyperthermia, dose-dependent hypotension, bradycardia, tachycardia, apnea, increased BUN/ALT, nephrotoxicity, glycosuria, proteinuria.
interactions: Concomitant use of succinylcholine associated with hyperkalemia.

name: KETAMINE
indications: Induction and maintenance of anesthesia for minor surgical or diagnostic procedures; Analgesia for painful procedures of short duration for patients at risk of hypotension and bronchospasm.
dosage_schedule: IM injection (short procedures): Initially 6.5-13 mg/kg. IV injection (diagnostic): Initially 4 mg/kg over at least 60 seconds. IV infusion (short procedures): Initially 1-4.5 mg/kg. Induction: 0.5-2 mg/kg. Maintenance: 10-45 mcg/kg/minute.
contraindications: Patients with epilepsy, hypertension, and in patients with increased ICP.
precautions: Use cautiously in CNS abnormalities, hydrocephalus, increased IOP, CAD, catecholamine depletion. To be administered only by experienced personnel with immediate availability of respiratory/cardiovascular support.
adverse_effects: Emergence reactions (dreams, hallucinations, delirium), hypertension, increased cardiac output, increased ICP, tachycardia, tonic clonic movements, increased salivation, dependence.
interactions: With diazepam, may cause ventricular tachycardia or ventricular fibrillation.

name: MIDAZOLAM
indications: Status epilepticus, febrile convulsions, conscious sedation for procedures, sedative in combined anaesthesia, premedication, sedation in intensive care, confusion/restlessness in palliative care.
dosage_schedule: Status epilepticus (buccal): Child 1–11 months: 2.5 mg; 1–4 years: 5 mg; 5–9 years: 7.5 mg; Adult: 10 mg. Conscious sedation (slow IV): Adult: Initially 2–2.5 mg (max 7.5 mg/course); Elderly: Initially 0.5–1 mg (max 3.5 mg/course). Premedication (IM): Adult: 70–100 mcg/kg. Induction (slow IV): Adult: 150–200 mcg/kg daily.
contraindications: CNS depression, compromised airway, severe respiratory depression.
precautions: Concentration in children under 15 kg not to exceed 1 mg/mL. Monitor neonates under 6 months for airways obstruction. Caution in hepatic/renal impairment. To be avoided in breastfeeding women. Keep patient supine.
adverse_effects: Decreased respiratory rate, apnea, drowsiness, seizure-like activity, nausea/vomiting, sedation, delirium, euphoria.

name: PROPOFOL
indications: Induction and maintenance of anesthesia, sedation for surgical and diagnostic procedures.
dosage_schedule: Induction (IV injection): 1.5-2.5 mg/kg (1-1.5 mg/kg in those >55 years); child 3-16 yrs: 2.5-3.5 mg/kg. Maintenance: IV injection 25-50 mg repeat OR IV infusion 4-12 mg/kg/hour. Sedation: IV injection 0.5-1 mg/kg; IV infusion 1.5-4.5 mg/kg/hour.
contraindications: Lack of ventilator support, severe cardiac dysfunction, egg/soybean/soy allergy. Sedation of ventilated children and adolescents <17 years. Use in labor and delivery (causes neonatal depression).
precautions: Proper aseptic technique imperative. Risk of fatal propofol infusion syndrome in ICU patients. Closely monitor patients with anemia, hepatic impairment, myxedema, or renal impairment.
adverse_effects: Bradycardia, hypotension, apnea, involuntary movements, injection site burning/stinging, respiratory acidosis during weaning, hypertriglyceridemia.
interactions: Additive CNS and respiratory depression with alcohol, antihistamines, opioid analgesics, and sedative/hypnotics.

name: THIOPENTAL SODIUM
indications: Induction of anesthesia, rapid control of convulsions like status epilepticus
dosage_schedule: Induction of anesthesia: Adult: 100-150 mg (4-6 ml of 2.5% solution); repeat after 30-60 sec depending on response. Child dose: 2-7 mg/kg.
contraindications: Porphyria, hypersensitivity, breast feeding, hypotension, status asthmaticus, severe cardiovascular diseases, hepatic or renal dysfunction.
precautions: Anesthesia is deeper whenever protein binding is less (e.g., in liver disease). Slight extravasation risk (severe pain, necrosis). Never give into the arteries.
adverse_effects: Respiratory and myocardial depression, cardiac arrhythmias, bronchospasm and laryngospasm with cough, rash, prolonged somnolence.
interactions: Chemically reacts with succinylcholine; never give in same syringe.

name: BUPIVACAINE
indications: Local infiltration, peripheral nerve block, epidural block, sympathetic block.
dosage_schedule: Adjusted per site. Local infiltration: 0.25% (up to 60 ml). Peripheral nerve block: 0.25% (max 60 ml) or 0.5% (max 30 ml). Epidural: 0.5% (max 20-30 ml). Labour (lumbar): 0.25-0.5% (max 12 ml).
contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Do not use for IV anesthesia (QT interval prolongation risk). Do not use for obstetric paracervical block.
precautions: Caution in severely debilitated patients, liver disease, renal impairment, pregnancy, impaired cardiac condition, and myasthenia gravis.
adverse_effects: Headache, bradycardia, hypotension, cardiac arrhythmias, cardiac arrest, anxiety, restlessness, tremor, dizziness, respiratory arrest.

name: LIDOCAINE (LIGNOCAINE)
indications: Arrhythmia, Local anaesthesia
dosage_schedule: Infiltration (by injection): Maximum dose 200 mg (or 500 mg with adrenaline; maximum adrenaline dose 500 µg). Nerve blocks: 1% to maximum of 40 ml (with adrenaline 1 in 200,000). Surface anaesthesia: Mouth/throat max 200 mg; Urethra 2% gel max 400 mg.
precautions: Store at 8-15º C. Discard any gel not used in a single application.
adverse_effects: See Bupivacaine.

name: PRILOCAINE HYDROCHLORIDE
indications: Infiltration for dentistry, nerve block
dosage_schedule: Adjusted per site. 100-200 mg/minute to maximum 400 mg.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: See Lidocaine.

name: PROCAINE HYDROCHLORIDE
indications: Infiltration, peripheral nerve block, sympathetic nerve block, spinal anesthesia
dosage_schedule: Adjusted per site. By injection: up to 1g (200ml of 0.5% solution or 100ml of 1% solution).
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: See Bupivacaine.

name: FENTANYL
indications: Induction and maintenance of anesthesia, analgesia (pre-operative and post-operative)
dosage_schedule: IV for spontaneous respiration: Adult: 50-100 μg then 50 μg as required; children: 3-5 μg/kg then 1 μg as required. For assisted ventilation: Adult: 0.3-3.5 mg then 100-200 μg as required; children: 15 μg/kg then 1-3 μg as required.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, myasthenia gravis, within 2 hours of MAOI use. Do not use fentanyl within 2 weeks of use of MAOIs.
precautions: Pregnancy, breast feeding, geriatric patients, increased ICP, seizure disorders, cardiac dysrhythmias, severe respiratory disorders.
adverse_effects: Confusion, delirium, Paradoxical excitation, bradycardia, hypotension/HTN, respiratory depression/arrest, laryngospasm, double vision, miosis, constipation, biliary spasm, muscle rigidity.
interactions: With MAOI may produce fatal reactions. CYP3A4 inhibitors increase plasma levels leading to risk of CNS/respiratory depression.

name: PANCURONIUM
indications: Neuromuscular blockade (long duration) during surgery, intubation, or intensive care.
dosage_schedule: Surgery/Intubation (IV injection): Adult: Initially 100 mcg/kg, then 20 mcg/kg as required. Intensive care (IV injection): Adult: Initially 100 mcg/kg, then 60 mcg/kg every 60–90 minutes. Use ideal body weight for obese patients.
contraindications: Avoid in neuromuscular disease, hypersensitive to drug and/or bromides.
precautions: Ventilator support is mandatory. In renal impairment: avoid use if CrCl <10 mL/min; administer 50% normal dose if CrCl 10-50 mL/min.
adverse_effects: Acute myopathy (after prolonged use in intensive care), hypertension, tachycardia.
interactions: With or following an opioid, sedative, or anesthetic agent: additive/synergistic effects.

name: ROCURONIUM BROMIDE
indications: Neuromuscular blockade (intermediate duration) during surgery, intubation, or intensive care.
dosage_schedule: Surgery/Intubation (IV injection): Adult: Initially 600 mcg/kg; maintenance 150 mcg/kg OR IV infusion 300–600 mcg/kg/hour. Elderly maintenance injection: 75–100 mcg/kg. Intensive care: Adult: Initially 600 mcg/kg; maintenance IV infusion 300–600 mcg/kg/hour for first hour then adjusted.
contraindications: Avoid in neuromuscular disease, hypersensitive to drug and/or bromides.
precautions: Ventilator support is mandatory. Hepatic/Renal impairment: reduce dose/maintenance dose; risk of prolonged paralysis.
adverse_effects: Anaphylactoid reactions, acute myopathy (ICU), bronchospasm, hypotension, skin flushing, tachycardia.
interactions: With or following an opioid, sedative, or anesthetic agent: additive/synergistic effects.

name: VECURONIUM
indications: Neuromuscular blockade (intermediate duration) during surgery or intubation.
dosage_schedule: Surgery/Intubation (IV injection): Adult: 80–100 mcg/kg; maintenance injection: 20–30 mcg/kg. Maximum dose in caesarean section: 100 mcg/kg. Maintenance IV infusion: 0.8–1.4 mcg/kg/minute. Use ideal body weight for obese patients.
contraindications: Avoid in neuromuscular disease, hypersensitive to drug and/or bromides.
precautions: Ventilator support is mandatory. Hepatic/Renal impairment: reduce dose/use caution. Do not dilute reconstituted solution with sterile water alone (risk of fatal hemolysis).
adverse_effects: Anaphylactoid reactions, acute myopathy (ICU), bronchospasm, hypotension, skin flushing, tachycardia.
interactions: With or following an opioid, sedative, or anesthetic agent: additive/synergistic effects.

name: NEOSTIGMINE
indications: Treatment of myasthenia gravis, reversal of non-depolarising (competitive) neuromuscular blockade.
dosage_schedule: Myasthenia gravis (Oral): Adult: Initially 15-30 mg repeated (max 180 mg daily). SC/IM injection: Adult: 1-2.5 mg repeated (usual daily 5–20 mg). Reversal (IV injection): Adult: 2.5 mg (max 5 mg) over 1 minute.
precautions: Renal impairment: reduce dose. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: use with caution.
adverse_effects: Anaphylactoid reactions, acute myopathy, bronchospasm, hypotension, skin flushing, tachycardia.
interactions: With or following an opioid, sedative, or anesthetic agent: additive/synergistic effects.

name: ALLOPURINOL
indications: Primary hyperuricemia of gout, secondary hyperuricemia due to haematological malignancies or anti-neoplastic therapy; recurrent renal stones.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 300 mg/day after meal initially, gradually increased to maximum 800 mg/day. Maintenance dose: 200-300 mg (mild), 400-600 mg (moderate to severe). Children: 150-300 mg/day once daily.
precautions: Caution in pregnancy, breast feeding, hepatic and renal impairment. Maintain high fluid intake (2 L/day). Risk of hypersensitivity increased with thiazides.
adverse_effects: Nausea, vomiting, maculopapular rash, rarely exfoliative dermatitis, Steven’s Johnson syndrome, aplastic anaemia, acute hepatic failure.
interactions: Increased risk of hypersensitivity with aspirin, azathioprine, captopril, enalapril, warfarin. Reduce dosages of azathioprine/mercaptopurine to 25-33% of usual.

name: COLCHICINE
indications: Treatment of acute gout, prophylaxis of recurrent acute attacks during initiation of allopurinol therapy.
dosage_schedule: Acute: 1 mg initially followed by 0.25-0.5 mg every 2-3 hours until attack is controlled or diarrhoea starts (max 4 mg). Prophylaxis: 0.5 mg/day.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity, blood disorders, cardiac disease, pregnancy, lactation.
precautions: Renal diseases, elderly. Do routine blood tests during medication.
adverse_effects: GI disturbance, bloody diarrhoea, abdominal cramps, kidney damage, agranulocytosis, myopathy, hair loss.
interactions: Clarithromycin, darunavir, itraconazole, ritonavir, aspirin, atorvastatin, carbamazepine.

name: FEBUXOSTAT
indications: Chronic gout.
dosage_schedule: Initially: 40 mg/day oral. Maintenance: 40-80 mg/day (increased if serum uric acid >6 mg/ml after 2 weeks). Use prophylactic colchicine or NSAID for at least 3 months.
contraindications: Co-administration with azathioprine, mercaptopurine, or theophylline.
precautions: Pregnancy, congestive heart failure, ischemic heart disorders, transplant recipients. Not for monotherapy in acute gouty arthritis.
adverse_effects: Elevated liver function tests, GI disturbances, headache, oedema, rash, atrial fibrillation, bronchitis.

name: PROBENECID
indications: Chronic gout, secondary hyperuricemia, prolonging penicillin action in SABE and gonorrhoea.
dosage_schedule: Gout: 250 mg BD for 1 week followed by 500 mg BD. Gonorrhoea: 1 g oral with 2 g cefotaxime IM.
contraindications: Peptic ulcer, hypersensitivity, renal impairment, history of renal calculi.
precautions: May precipitate an acute gouty attack; used concomitantly with NSAID or colchicine.
adverse_effects: Gastric irritation, hypersensitivity, seizures and respiratory failure (overdose).

name: SULPHINPYRAZONE
indications: Chronic gout, secondary hyperuricemia (Same as probenecid).
dosage_schedule: 100-200 mg/day taken with food initially; increased to 600-800 mg/day over 2-3 weeks until serum acid is normal.
precautions: Same as probenecid.
adverse_effects: Acute renal failure, GI bleeding, ulceration, jaundice, elevated liver enzymes.

name: ABATACEPT
indications: Moderate to severe Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA), psoriatic arthritis.
dosage_schedule: Wt <60 kg: 500 mg IV (on day 1, then day 15, then 4 weekly); Wt 60-100 kg: 750 mg IV; Wt >100 kg: 1000 mg IV.
precautions: COPD patients (higher infection risk), latent TB. Do not give live vaccines within 3 months of discontinuation.
adverse_effects: Infection, nasopharyngitis, nausea, cough, back pain, hypertension, UTI.
interactions: Increased risk of side-effects when given with adalimumab.

name: ADALIMUMAB
indications: Moderate to severe active RA, psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, Crohn’s disease, ulcerative colitis.
dosage_schedule: RA (Adult): 40 mg SC every 2 weeks. Crohn’s/UC (Accelerated): 160 mg initially (divided over 2 days), then 80 mg after 2 weeks, then 40 mg every 2 weeks.
contraindications: Moderate to severe heart failure, severe infection, active tuberculosis.
precautions: Screen for latent TB/HBV before therapy. Risk of malignancy and demyelinating disorders.
adverse_effects: Anxiety, benign tumours, chest pain, GI haemorrhage, impaired healing, skin cancer, reactivation of latent TB.
interactions: Increased side-effects with abatacept; avoid use with anakinra.

name: ANAKINRA
indications: Rheumatoid arthritis (in combination with methotrexate) not responding to methotrexate alone.
dosage_schedule: 100 mg SC once daily.
precautions: History of asthma, chronic infections, immunosuppression. Discontinue if severe infection develops.
adverse_effects: Neutropenia, antibody formation, headache, injection site reactions, malignancy.

name: ETANERCEPT
indications: Ankylosing arthritis, RA, polyarticular idiopathic juvenile arthritis, plaque psoriasis.
dosage_schedule: Ankylosing spondylitis/RA: 50 mg SC once weekly or 25 mg SC twice weekly. Plaque psoriasis: 50 mg SC twice weekly for 3 months, then once weekly.
precautions: Concomitant use of live vaccines.
adverse_effects: Serious infection and malignancy risk, headache, rhinitis.

name: HYDROXYCHOLOROQUINE SULFATE (HCQS)
indications: Early and mild acute rheumatoid arthritis, dermatologic conditions aggravated by sunlight.
dosage_schedule: Oral: 400 mg once daily for 4-6 weeks; maintenance dose 200 mg daily.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to 4-aminoquinoline derivatives, retinal or visual field changes.
precautions: G6PD deficiency, neurological disorders, psoriasis. Discontinue if ocular toxicity suspected. Monitor for retinal changes.
adverse_effects: GI disturbances, skin reactions, convulsions, ECG changes, ototoxicity, retinal damage, keratopathy.
interactions: Avoid concurrent use of hepatotoxic drugs.

name: INFLIXIMAB
indications: Severe active Crohn’s Disease, ulcerative colitis, RA (with methotrexate), ankylosing spondylitis, psoriatic arthritis, plaque psoriasis.
dosage_schedule: RA: IV initially 3 mg/kg, then 3 mg/kg at 2 and 6 weeks, then every 8 weeks. Crohn's/UC: initially 5 mg/kg at 0, 2, and 6 weeks, then maintenance every 8 weeks.
precautions: Conception avoided for 6 months after last dose. Active TB screening required. Risk of demyelinating disorders and colon cancer.
adverse_effects: Risk of infection (TB, HBV), long-term risk of lymphoma and skin cancer, GI haemorrhage, paraesthesia.
interactions: Abatacept, adalimumab, anakinra, live vaccines, cyclosporine.

name: LEFLUNOMIDE
indications: Active rheumatoid arthritis, active psoriatic arthritis.
dosage_schedule: Adult: 10-20 mg once a day. Refractory polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis: up to 10 mg once a day.
contraindications: Active serious infection, severe hypoproteinaemia, liver disease, severe immunodeficiencies, significant anaemia.
precautions: Avoid in pregnancy for 3 years after treatment. Monitor liver enzymes and CBC. Avoid live vaccines.
adverse_effects: Hepatotoxicity, alopecia, oral mucosal disorders, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, tenosynovitis.

name: METHOTREXATE
indications: Rheumatoid arthritis, choriocarcinoma, acute leukaemia, psoriasis, juvenile idiopathic arthritis.
dosage_schedule: Adult RA: 15 mg ONCE WEEKLY initially (increases by 5 mg every 4-6 weeks). Pediatrics: 5-7.5 mg ONCE WEEKLY (increases by 2.5 mg every 4-6 weeks).
contraindications: Pregnancy (X), alcoholism, alcoholic liver disease, immunodeficiency.
precautions: Monitor closely for hepatic, renal, and bone marrow toxicity. Taking with folic acid (1 mg/day) reduces toxicity. Administer folic acid 5 mg once a week preceding methotrexate dose.
adverse_effects: Bone marrow toxicity, pancytopenia, mucositis, pneumonitis, pulmonary fibrosis, hepatic cirrhosis.

name: PENICILLAMINE
indications: Wilson’s disease, autoimmune hepatitis, cystinuria, chronic lead and arsenic poisoning.
dosage_schedule: Wilson’s: 1.5-2 g/day divided. Autoimmune hepatitis: 500 mg/day initially, increased to 1.25 g/day. Cystinuria: 1 g/day.
contraindications: Lupus erythematosus, simultaneous with gold therapy.
precautions: Monitor for neurologic involvement and hematologic disorders.
adverse_effects: Anorexia, taste loss, myasthenia gravis precipitation, proteinuria, kidney damage, Stevens-Johnson syndrome.
interactions: Ferrous fumarate, ferrous gluconate, MgSO4, sodium bicarbonate.

name: RITUXIMAB
indications: Moderate to severe active RA not responsive to methotrexate, NHL, CLL, refractory lupus, vasculitis.
dosage_schedule: RA: 1 g IV infusion on Day 1 and Day 15, then repeat after 6 months. Pre-medicate with glucocorticoid 30 mins before infusion.
precautions: Caution in angina, arrhythmia. Avoid pregnancy for at least 12 months after treatment. No immunization without consent.
adverse_effects: Tumour lysis syndrome, reactivation of hepatitis B, Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML), cardiac arrest, neuropathy.
interactions: Concomitant cisplatin increases risk of fatal infusion reaction.

name: SULFASALAZINE
indications: Rheumatoid arthritis, IBD, ankylosing spondylitis, juvenile chronic arthritis.
dosage_schedule: RA: oral 2-3 g/day (enteric coated). Crohn’s: 3-6 g/day.
precautions: Caution in bronchial asthma, blood dyscrasias. Risk of neural tube defects and neonatal jaundice.
adverse_effects: Reversible oligospermia, GI distress, haemolytic anaemia, rash, pruritus.
pregnancy_category: B (D if used for prolonged periods or near term)

name: TOCILIZUMAB
indications: Moderate to severe active RA.
dosage_schedule: IV infusion: 4-8 mg/kg every 4 weeks (max dose 800 mg). SC infusion: Wt <100 kg: 162 mg every other week; Wt >100 kg: 162 mg per week.
precautions: Discontinue if ANC <500/mm3, Platelets <50,000/mm3, or ALT/AST >5x normal. Do not give live vaccines.
adverse_effects: Infections, gastritis, elevated lipid levels, infusion related skin reactions.

name: TOFACUTINIB
indications: Moderate to severe active RA with inadequate response to methotrexate, psoriatic arthritis, refractory JIA.
dosage_schedule: 5 mg twice a day or 11 mg (extended release) once daily.
precautions: Renal and hepatic impairment. Do not give live vaccines.
adverse_effects: Infections.
interactions: CYP3A4 inhibitors (fluconazole, erythromycin, omeprazole) increase levels; do not exceed 5 mg/day.

name: ACELECOFENAC
indications: Non-selective COX inhibitor: Rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, fibromyalgia.
dosage_schedule: 100 mg twice daily.
contraindications: Active GI bleeding, active GI ulceration, history of recurrent GI haemorrhage, severe heart failure.
precautions: Avoid in acute porphyria, cardiac impairment, coagulation defects. Use caution in hypertension, elderly.
adverse_effects: Allergy and cross-sensitivity, exacerbation of asthma, angioedema, colitis, pancreatitis.

name: ASPIRIN
indications: Non-selective COX inhibitor: Mild to moderate pain and fever, rheumatic fever.
dosage_schedule: 300-900 mg every 4-6 hours when necessary (max 4 g daily). Child/Adolescent: not recommended.
contraindications: Haemophilia, children under 16 years, breast-feeding, gout, heart disease, erosive gastritis.
precautions: Impaired renal/hepatic function, asthma. Not for children with flulike symptoms (Reye’s syndrome risk).
adverse_effects: Dyspepsia, GI bleeding, mucosal lesions, tinnitus, hearing loss (high dose), prolongation of bleeding time.
interactions: Acetazolamide (toxicity), Heparin (enhanced anticoagulation), Methotrexate (reduced excretion), Spironolactone (antagonism of diuretic effect).

name: DICLOFENAC
indications: Non-selective COX inhibitor: Rheumatic disease, osteoarthritis, juvenile arthritis, acute gout, post-operative pain, dysmenorrhea.
dosage_schedule: Adult: Oral 75-150 mg daily in 2-3 divided doses. Acute exacerbations/Post-op pain: 75 mg once daily. Ureteric colic: 75 mg, then further 75 mg after 30 mins if needed. Max total dose: 150 mg daily. Child (1yr+): 1-3 mg/kg daily.
contraindications: Active GI bleeding/ulceration, ischemic heart disease, heart failure, 3rd trimester pregnancy, breast-feeding.
precautions: Withdraw if cardiogenic shock develops. Take with food, milk or antacids.
adverse_effects: Fluid retention (precipitating heart failure), GI ulceration and bleeding, renal failure, NSAID induced headache.
interactions: Increases hyperkalaemia with K-sparing diuretics; increases toxicity of phenytoin, lithium, methotrexate, digoxin.

name: FLURBIPROFEN
indications: Non-selective COX inhibitor: Rheumatic disease, musculoskeletal disorders, mild to moderate pain, dysmenorrhea.
dosage_schedule: Oral: 150-200 mg daily in divided doses (increased in acute conditions to 300 mg daily). Dysmenorrhea: initially 100 mg then 50-100 mg q4-6h (max 300 mg daily).
precautions: Regular lab tests (Hgb, LFT, KFT, audiometry, eye test). Monitor for GI bleeding.
adverse_effects: Similar to ibuprofen but with more GI adverse effects.

name: IBUPROFEN
indications: Non-selective COX inhibitor: RA, OA, primary dysmenorrhea, dental pain, musculoskeletal disorders, fever, migraine.
dosage_schedule: Adult: initially 1.2-1.8 g daily in 3-4 divided doses (max 2.4 g daily). Child: 20-30 mg/kg daily. Not for children under 5 kg.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to NSAIDs, asthma, severe renal/hepatic disease, 3rd trimester pregnancy.
precautions: Caution in bleeding disorders, cardiac disorders. Use sunscreen to prevent photosensitivity.
adverse_effects: GI irritation, bleeding, angioedema, bronchospasm, tinnitus, fluid retention.

name: INDOMETHACIN
indications: Non-selective COX inhibitor: Rheumatic disease, musculoskeletal disorders, acute gout, dysmenorrhea, closure of ductus arteriosus.
dosage_schedule: Rheumatic: 50-200 mg daily in divided doses. Rectum: 100 mg twice daily. Acute gout: 150-200 mg daily divided. Dysmenorrhea: up to 75 mg daily.
contraindications: Active GI bleeding/ulceration, severe heart failure, neonates, aortic coarctation, lactating mother, 3rd trimester pregnancy.
precautions: Epilepsy, parkinsonism, renal impairment. Ophthalmic and blood exams advisable during long-term therapy.
adverse_effects: Nausea (oral), rectal irritation/bleeding (rectal). General side effects same as diclofenac.

name: MEFENAMIC ACID
indications: Non-selective COX inhibitor: RA, OA, postoperative pain, dysmenorrhea/menorrhagia.
dosage_schedule: 500 mg 3 times a day.
contraindications: Active GI bleeding/ulceration, IBD, severe heart failure, lactating mother.
precautions: Pregnancy Category C and D. Caution in acute porphyria, renal/cardiac impairment.
adverse_effects: Diarrhea (withdraw treatment), rashes (withdraw), stomatitis, aplastic anemia, glucose intolerance.

name: NAPROXEN
indications: Non-selective COX inhibitor: Rheumatic disease, musculoskeletal disorders, dysmenorrhea, acute gout.
dosage_schedule: Rheumatic: 0.5-1 g daily in 1-2 divided doses. Dysmenorrhea: initially 500 mg then 250 mg q6-8h. Acute gout: initially 750 mg then 250 mg every 8 hours.
contraindications: Active GI bleeding/ulceration, severe heart failure, children <2 years.
precautions: Uncontrolled hypertension, asthma, breastfeeding.
adverse_effects: See under NSAIDs as general.

name: PARACETAMOL
indications: Non-selective COX inhibitor: Mild to moderate pain or fever, arthralgia, dysmenorrhea, headache, OA.
dosage_schedule: Adult: 0.5-1 g every 4-6 hours (max 4 g/day). Adult IV (50 kg+): 1 g q4-6h. Children: 10-15 mg/kg/dose every 4-6 hours (max 5 doses/day).
precautions: Hepatic toxicity risk at doses >0.4 g/day with chronic use.
adverse_effects: See under Indomethacin.
interactions: Alcohol, barbiturates, isoniazid, and carbamazepine increase hepatotoxicity. Warfarin (long-term high dose paracetamol increases hypoprothrombinemia).

name: PIROXICAM
indications: Non-selective COX inhibitor: RA, juvenile RA, OA, ankylosing spondylitis.
dosage_schedule: Oral: Up to 20 mg once daily. Topical (Gel 0.5%): apply 3-4 times a day.
precautions: Increases risk of asthma, cardiac disease, CHF. For topical use, avoid excessive sunlight on treated area.
adverse_effects: Indigestion, upper respiratory infection, anemia, dizziness. Topical: photosensitivity, rash.

name: CELECOXIB
indications: Selective COX-2 inhibitor: Acute pain, primary dysmenorrhoea, ankylosing spondylitis, OA, RA.
dosage_schedule: Acute pain/Dysmenorrhoea: initially 400 mg then 200 mg. Ankylosing spondylitis: 200-400 mg/day. OA: 200 mg/day. RA: 100-200 mg/day.
contraindications: Aspirin allergy, chronic hepatitis, perioperative pain in CABG surgery.
precautions: Increased risk of adverse cardiovascular events. Risk of GI bleeding and perforation.
adverse_effects: Headache, hypertension, fever, dyspepsia, peripheral oedema.

name: ETORICOXIB
indications: Selective COX-2 inhibitor: Ankylosing spondylitis, osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, acute gout.
dosage_schedule: OA: 30-60 mg once daily. RA/Ankylosing spondylitis: 90 mg once daily. Acute gout: 120 mg once daily (max 8 days).
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, active GI ulceration/bleeding, heart failure, ischaemic heart disease, uncontrolled HTN.
precautions: History of bronchospasm, acute rhinitis, nasal polyps.
adverse_effects: Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis, upper GI ulceration, alveolar osteitis, increased ALT/AST.

name: DIACEREIN
indications: Anthraquinone: Osteoarthritis.
dosage_schedule: Oral: 50 mg twice daily.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to anthraquinone derivatives, renal/hepatic impairment.
precautions: Monitor CBC, LFT and urinalysis every 6 months. Take with food.
adverse_effects: Diarrhea, pain abdomen, intense yellow coloring of urine.
interactions: Aluminium/magnesium hydroxide antacids decrease absorption; laxatives increase diarrhea risk. Avoid fibers/phytates co-administration.

name: ALENDRONATE
indications: Bisphosphonate: Osteoporosis, Paget’s disease.
dosage_schedule: 5-10 mg OD or 35-70 mg weekly.
contraindications: Hypocalcaemia, oesophageal stricture or achalasia, serum kidney problem.
precautions: Take in empty stomach in morning. Do not lie down or take food for at least 30 min to prevent oesophagitis.
adverse_effects: Heart burn, gastric erosion, retrosternal pain, fall in serum Ca2+ level.
interactions: NSAID, prednisolone, calcium, iron, antacids, tea, coffee, fruit juice.

name: ETIDRONATE
indications: Bisphosphonate: Paget’s disease, total hip replacement, spinal cord injury, PTH-induced bone resorption.
dosage_schedule: Paget's: 5-10 mg/kg qday (max 6 months). Hip replacement: 20 mg/kg qday (1 month pre- and 3 months post-surgery).
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Convulsion, fever, hypocalcaemia, abnormal renal function.
interactions: Aluminium hydroxide, calcium carbonate, sodium bicarbonate.

name: IBANDRONATE
indications: Bisphosphonate: Treatment and prevention of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women.
dosage_schedule: Oral: 150 mg every month. IV: 3 mg every 3 months administered over 15-30 seconds.
precautions: Adequate intake of calcium and vitamin D recommended. Do not lie down after taking.
adverse_effects: URI, back pain, dyspepsia, bronchitis, tooth disorder.
interactions: Human parathyroid hormone, calcium, ferrous fumarate.

name: PAMIDRONATE
indications: Bisphosphonate: Hypercalcemia of malignancy, Paget’s disease, osteolytic bone metastasis, multiple myeloma.
dosage_schedule: Hypercalcemia: 90 mg single IV infusion (2-24 hrs). Paget’s: 30 mg IV infusion (4 hrs qday) for 3 days. Metastases: 90 mg IV infusion every month.
precautions: Monitor for electrolyte abnormalities and myelosuppression.
adverse_effects: Anaemia, hypokalaemia, hypophosphatemia, seizure, osteonecrosis.

name: RISEDRONATE
indications: Bisphosphonate: Postmenopausal osteoporosis, glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis, Paget’s disease.
dosage_schedule: Postmenopausal: 5 mg daily or 35 mg weekly or 150 mg monthly. Glucocorticoid-induced: 5 mg/day. Paget's: 30 mg/day for 2 months.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, angioedema, hypocalcemia, esophagus stricture, osteonecrosis of jaw.
precautions: Monitor for SJS, toxic epidermal necrolysis.
adverse_effects: Arthralgia, rash, pharyngitis, prostatic hyperplasia, nephrolithiasis, arrhythmia.

name: ZOLEDRONATE
indications: Bisphosphonate: Hypercalcemia, cancer chemotherapy, multiple myeloma, osteoporosis.
dosage_schedule: Hypercalcemia: 4 mg IV (repeatable in 7 days). Myeloma/Metastases: 4 mg IV every 3-4 weeks. Postmenopausal prevention: 5 mg IV every 2 years.
contraindications: Pregnancy, severe renal impairment, shock hypocalcemia.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Bone pain, fever, fatigue, anaemia, urinary tract infection, hypomagnesemia.

name: BACLOFEN
indications: Centrally acting muscle relaxant: Chronic severe spasticity (MS, spinal cord section), pain of muscle spasm in palliative care, hiccup.
dosage_schedule: Oral spasticity: initially 5 mg TID, maintenance up to 60 mg daily (max 100 mg/day). Intrathecal: test dose 25-50 mcg, then titrated maintenance dose.
precautions: Stroke, seizure disorder, diabetes mellitus, geriatric patients. Do not discontinue quickly (taper over 1-2 weeks).
adverse_effects: Cardiovascular depression, hallucinations, hyperhidrosis, respiratory depression, urinary disturbances.
interactions: Increase CNS depression with alcohol, tricyclics, opiates, MAOIs. Increase hypotension with anti-hypertensives.

name: DEXMEDETOMIDINE
indications: Centrally acting muscle relaxant: Maintenance of sedation during intensive care.
dosage_schedule: IV infusion: 0.7 mcg/kg/hour adjusted to response (usual range 0.2-1.4 mcg/kg/hour).
precautions: Direct supervision by anesthesia-trained personnel required. Monitor cardiac/respiratory function.
adverse_effects: Blood pressure changes, hyperthermia, myocardial infarction, abdominal distension, AV block, hypoalbuminemia.

name: TIZANIDINE
indications: Centrally acting muscle relaxant: Spasticity associated with multiple sclerosis or spinal cord injury.
dosage_schedule: Initially 2 mg for 1 dose, then increased by 2 mg every 3-4 days (usual dose up to 24 mg daily, max 36 mg/day).
precautions: Monitor liver function monthly for first four months. Discontinue gradually.
adverse_effects: Somnolence, dizziness, dyskinesia, psychosis, increased ALT, urinary frequency, pharyngitis.
interactions: Alcohol increases CNS depression. Fluvoxamine and ciprofloxacin increase tizanidine levels (avoid concurrent use). Rasagiline effect increased.

name: DENOSUMAB
indications: Osteoporosis, androgen deprivation induced bone loss, giant cell tumour, hypercalcemia of malignancy.
dosage_schedule: Osteoporosis: 60 mg SC every 6 months (with Ca/Vit D supplements). Bone loss (Prostate cancer): 60 mg SC every 6 months. Giant cell tumour: 120 mg SC q4wk (loading: extra doses on Day 8 and 15 of 1st month).
precautions: History of systemic hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis. Monitor for cellulitis and dermatologic reactions.
adverse_effects: Back pain, cystitis, sciatica, osteonecrosis of jaw, pruritus, hypocalcaemia.
interactions: Increased infection risk with adalimumab, abatacept, corticosteroids, immunosuppressants.

name: DILOXANIDE FUROATE
indications: Asymptomatic cyst passers and extra intestinal amoebiasis (together with tissue amoebicide).
dosage_schedule: Adult: 500 mg every 8 hours for 10 days. Child: 20 mg/kg daily in 3 divided doses for 10 days.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Flatulence, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, pruritus, urticaria.

name: METRONIDAZOLE
indications: Giardiasis, amoebic dysentery, extra-intestinal amoebiasis (amoebic liver abscess), Trichomonas vaginalis, Giardia lambia, Helicobacter pylori, Balantidium coli, anaerobic bacterial infections, surgical and gynaecological sepsis due to colonic anaerobes (Bacteroides fragilis).
dosage_schedule: Invasive intestinal amoebiasis: oral 800 mg q8h for 5 days; Child 1-3 yrs: 200 mg q8h; 3-7 yrs: 200 mg q6h; 7-10 yrs: 400 mg q8h. Extra-intestinal/cyst passers: oral 400-800 mg q8h for 5-10 days. Giardiasis: oral 2 g daily for 3 days or 400 mg TID for 5 days. Anaerobic infections: oral 800 mg initially then 400 mg q8h (usually 7 days). Bacterial vaginosis: 400 mg BID for 5-7 days or 2 g single dose. Acute ulcerative gingivitis: 200 mg q8h for 3 days. Surgical prophylaxis: 400 mg started 2 hours before surgery, then q8h.
precautions: Carcinogenic in rats and mice but no clinical evidence of increased malignancy risk in humans. Avoid alcohol during use or for 4-8 hours after. Nursing mothers should not breastfeed during high-dose treatment. Caution in geriatric patients, candida infections, heart failure, and CNS disorders.
adverse_effects: Metallic taste, nausea, headache, furred tongue, dizziness, vertigo, dark brown urine, reversible peripheral neuropathy.
interactions: Avoid use with zalcitabine, norfloxacin, disulfiram. Potentiates effects of oral anticoagulants.

name: SECNIDAZOLE
indications: Trichomoniasis, amoebiasis, giardiasis, invasive (hepatic) amoebiasis.
dosage_schedule: Trichomoniasis/Amoebiasis/Giardiasis: oral, adult: single dose 2000 mg; child: single dose 30 mg/kg. Invasive (hepatic) amoebiasis: oral, adult: 1.5 g daily in single or divided doses for 5 days; child: 30 mg/kg daily for 5 days.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to secnidazole or other nitroimidazole derivatives.
precautions: Avoid chronic use.
adverse_effects: Vulvovaginal candidiasis, nausea, headache, dysgeusia, diarrhea, vomiting, abdominal pain, vulvovaginal pruritus.

name: TINIDAZOLE
indications: Amoebic infections, bacterial vaginosis, acute ulcerative colitis, intestinal amoebiasis.
dosage_schedule: Anaerobic infections: oral 2 g initially, then 1 g daily or 500 mg BID for 5-7 days. Prophylaxis: 2 g dose ~12 hours before surgery. Intestinal amoebiasis: 2 g daily for 2-3 days; Child: 50-60 mg/kg for 3 days. Liver involvement: 1.5-2 g daily for 3-6 days. Urogenital: single 2 g dose.
contraindications: Pregnancy, breastfeeding, hypersensitivity, CNS depression, blood dyscrasias.
precautions: Avoid in alcoholism.
adverse_effects: See under METRONIDAZOLE.
interactions: Don’t use within 2 weeks of disulfiram. Cimetidine and ketoconazole increase effects. Phenobarbital and rifampin decrease effects. Increases action of anticoagulants, cyclosporine, tacrolimus.

name: CEFACLOR
indications: Susceptible gram-positive and gram-negative infections, pneumonia, lower UTI.
dosage_schedule: 250 mg every 8 hours (doubled for severe infection); max 4 g daily. Child (>1 month): 20 mg/kg daily in 3 divided doses (doubled for severe infections); max 1 g daily.
precautions: Cross-allergenicity with penicillins (10% of cases). Prolonged use may result in overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms (Pseudomonas, Enterococci, Candida).
adverse_effects: Urticaria, pruritus, rash, fever, joint pain, exfoliative dermatitis, nausea, vomiting, positive Coomb’s test, elevated liver enzymes.

name: CEFADROXIL
indications: Skin and soft tissue infection, uncomplicated UTI, pharyngitis, tonsillitis, endocarditis.
dosage_schedule: 250 mg oral q6h or 500 mg q8-12h (max 1-1.5 g q6-8h for severe infections). Child: 30 mg/kg daily divided; max 100 mg/kg daily. UTI Prophylaxis (Adult): 125 mg at night.
precautions: See under CEFACLOR.
adverse_effects: See under CEFACLOR.

name: CEFALEXIN
indications: Susceptible gram-positive and gram-negative infections, pneumonia, lower UTI.
dosage_schedule: 250 mg oral every 8 hours (doubled for severe); max 4 g daily. Child (>1 month): 25-50 mg/kg daily in 3 divided doses. UTI Prophylaxis (Adult): 125 mg at night; Child: 10 mg/kg at night.
precautions: See under CEFACLOR.
adverse_effects: See under CEFACLOR.
interactions: Increases effects of anticoagulants; increases toxicity of aminoglycosides, loop diuretics, probenecid. Decreases effects of oral contraceptives.

name: CEFAZOLIN
indications: Surgical prophylaxis, susceptible gram-positive and gram-negative infections.
dosage_schedule: IM/IV: 0.5-1 g every 6-12 hours. Child: 25-50 mg/kg daily in divided doses (up to 100 mg/kg in severe cases).
precautions: Adjust dose in severe renal insufficiency. Caution in patients with seizures.
adverse_effects: See under CEFACLOR.

name: CEFEPIME
indications: See under CEFACLOR.
dosage_schedule: IV: 2 g every 12 hours. Child: 100-150 mg/kg/day.
precautions: See under CEFACLOR.
adverse_effects: See under CEFACLOR.

name: CEFIXIME
indications: See under CEFACLOR.
dosage_schedule: Adult/Child (>10 yrs): 200-400 mg daily in 1-2 divided doses. Child: 8 mg/kg in 1-2 divided doses. Gonorrhoea: 400 mg single dose.
precautions: See under CEFACLOR.
adverse_effects: See under CEFACLOR.

name: CEFOPERAZONE
indications: Pelvic infections, urinary-tract infections, bone and joint infections.
dosage_schedule: IM/IV: 1-2 g (base) every 12 hours.
precautions: May produce disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol.
adverse_effects: See under CEFACLOR.

name: CEFOTAXIME
indications: URTI, uncomplicated UTI, gonorrhea.
dosage_schedule: IM/IV: 1 g q12h (2 g q6h for severe/less sensitive organisms). Child: 100-150 mg/kg/day in 3-4 divided doses (max 200 mg/kg/day).
precautions: See under CEFACLOR.
adverse_effects: See under CEFACLOR.

name: CEFPODOXIME
indications: URTI, sinusitis, uncomplicated UTI, skin and soft tissue infections, uncomplicated gonorrhea.
dosage_schedule: URTI: 100-200 mg BID for 10 days; Child: 8 mg/kg/day divided. UTI: 100-200 mg BID. Gonorrhea: 200 mg single dose. Skin: 400 mg BD 7-14 days.
precautions: Renal impairment.
adverse_effects: See under CEFACLOR.

name: CEFTAZIDIME
indications: See under CEFPODOXIME; Pseudomonal lung infection in cystic fibrosis, meningitis, surgical prophylaxis (prostatic surgery), febrile neutropenia.
dosage_schedule: IM/IV: 1 g q8h (2 g q12h for severe). Child (<2 mo): 25-60 mg/kg daily; (>2 mo): 30-100 mg/kg daily (max 6 g/day in meningitis/immunocompromised). Cystic Fibrosis (Adult): 100-150 mg/kg daily; (Child): up to 150 mg/kg. Prostatic surgery: 1 g at induction.
precautions: See under CEFACLOR.
adverse_effects: See under CEFACLOR.

name: CEFTRIAXONE
indications: See under CEFPODOXIME, epiglottitis, early syphilis, meningitis.
dosage_schedule: IM/IV: 1 g daily single dose (2-4 g in severe). Surgical Prophylaxis: 1 g 30 min before procedure. Early syphilis: IM 500 mg daily for 10 days. Meningitis (Child 1 mo - 11 yrs): IV 50-75 mg/kg (max 100 mg/kg/day). Epiglottitis: 1 g BID + steroid, then step down to cefixime.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, hyperbilirubinemic neonates, neonates <28 days receiving calcium-containing products.
precautions: Risk of fatal calcium-ceftriaxone precipitant in lungs/kidneys of neonates. May increase INR in nutritionally deficient patients.
adverse_effects: Headache, dizziness, fever, seizures, nausea, vomiting, agranulocytosis, anaphylaxis, TEN.
interactions: Increases cyclosporine level. Increases bleeding with anticoagulants/NSAIDS. Increases toxicity of aminoglycosides and probenecid. Decrease absorption with iron-rich cereals.

name: CEFUROXIME
indications: Surgical prophylaxis, Haemophilus influenzae, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, tonsillitis, pharyngitis, UTI, pyelonephritis.
dosage_schedule: Oral (as axetil): 250 mg BID. UTI: 125 mg BID. Gonorrhoea: 1 g single dose. Child: IV 50-100 mg/kg/day and Oral 20-40 mg/kg/day. Prophylaxis: 1.5 g IV at induction. Tonsillitis/Pharyngitis (Adult): 250 mg daily for 4 days; (Child): 10 mg/kg BID for 4-10 days.
precautions: If diabetic, use blood glucose test.
adverse_effects: See under CEFACLOR.
interactions: Increases toxicity of aminoglycosides, furosemide, probenecid. Increases bleeding with anticoagulants. Decreases oral contraceptive effects. Absorption decreased by antacids/H2 blockers.

name: AMOXICILLIN
indications: URTI (S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae), otitis media, sinusitis, pneumonia, pharyngitis, skin/soft tissue, UTI, H. pylori, diphtheria.
dosage_schedule: Mild-Moderate: 500 mg q12h or 250 mg q8h (10-14 days). Severe: 875 mg q12h or 500 mg q8h. Tonsillitis: 875 mg daily for 10 days. H. pylori (Triple therapy): 1 g BID for 14 days. Diphtheria: 500 mg TID for 2 weeks.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to penicillins, cephalosporins, or imipenem.
precautions: Monitor for Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhoea (CDAD). Use cautiously in infectious mononucleosis. Medication can be taken regardless of meals.
adverse_effects: Anaphylaxis, mucocutaneous candidiasis, AST/ALT elevation, pseudomembranous colitis.
interactions: BCG/Cholera vaccines, tetracyclines, mycophenolate, allopurinol, warfarin, methotrexate.

name: AMOXICILLIN with CLAVULANATE
indications: LRTI (beta-lactamase producing H. influenzae/Moraxella), acute bacterial sinusitis, mastoiditis, bite wounds, erysipelas, pyelonephritis, skin abscess, diabetic foot.
dosage_schedule: Mild-Moderate LRTI: 500/125 mg q12h or 250/125 mg q8h for 10 days. Severe: 875/125 mg q12h. Sinusitis: 2000 mg (ER tabs) q12h. Mastoiditis: 1.2 g IV q8h then step down. Group A Streptococci: 40 mg/kg/day divided q8h (max 2000 mg/day).
contraindications: Allergy to penicillins, previous history of cholestatic jaundice/hepatic dysfunction with this combination.
precautions: Hepatic dysfunction more common in elderly/males. Take with meals.
adverse_effects: Diarrhea, mycosis, rash, candidiasis, vaginitis.
interactions: Decreases BCG vaccine effects. Doxycycline/Minocycline decrease effects. Allopurinol increases hypersensitivity risk.

name: AMPICILLIN
indications: UTI (E. coli, Proteus), chronic bronchitis, otitis media, invasive salmonellosis.
dosage_schedule: Oral: 0.25-1 g q6h (at least 30 min before food). UTI: 500 mg q8h. IM/IV: 500 mg q4-6h. Meningitis (Child <10 yrs): half adult dose.
precautions: Adjust dose in renal failure. Take on empty stomach with a full glass of water.
adverse_effects: Erythema multiforme, exfoliative dermatitis, enterocolitis, agranulocytosis, increased AST.

name: AMPICILLIN with SULBACTAM
indications: Gynecological, intra-abdominal, skin, orbital cellulitis, PID, pneumonia (aspiration/community).
dosage_schedule: IM/IV: 1.5 g (1 g amp + 0.5 g sulb) to 3 g (2 g amp + 1 g sulb) q6h; max 12 g/day. Pneumonia: treat for 5+ days.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, previous history of cholestatic jaundice with this drug.
precautions: Monitor hepatic function in hepatic impairment. May cause TEN or SJS.
adverse_effects: Diarrhea, thrombophlebitis, rash, abdominal distension.

name: BACAMPICILLIN
indications: See under AMPICILLIN.
dosage_schedule: 400-800 mg daily; Child (>5 yrs): 200 mg TID. Uncomplicated gonorrhoea: 1.6 g single dose + 1 g probenecid.
precautions: See under AMPICILLIN.
adverse_effects: See under AMPICILLIN.

name: BENZYL PENICILLIN (PENICILLIN G)
indications: Otitis media, meningitis, cellulitis, endocarditis, pneumococcal pneumonia, streptococcal infections, diphtheria.
dosage_schedule: IM: 2.4-4.8 g daily in 4 divided doses. Neonate: 50 mg/kg daily. Infant (1-4 wks): 75 mg/kg. Child: 100 mg/kg. Bacterial Endocarditis: 7.2 g daily in 4-6 divided doses. Diphtheria: 1200 mg IV q6h for 2 weeks.
contraindications: Only deep IM administration; do not administer IV, SC, or IT. Do not inject near nerve or artery.
precautions: Serious and occasionally fatal reactions reported. Caution in neonates.
adverse_effects: Skin rashes, serum-sickness like reactions, Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction, pseudomembranous colitis.

name: CARBENICILLIN
indications: Infections due to Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Proteus.
dosage_schedule: Slow IV/Infusion: 5 g q4-6h; Child: 250-400 mg/kg divided. IM: 2 g q6h; Child: 50-100 mg/kg divided.
precautions: Use immediately after preparation.
adverse_effects: Hypokalaemia, prolonged bleeding/prothrombin time, abnormal platelet aggregation.

name: CLOXACILLIN
indications: Exclusively for infection caused by Staphylococcus aureus.
dosage_schedule: Oral: 500 mg 4 times daily (doubled in severe). IM: 250 mg q4-6h (doubled in severe). IV: 1-2 g q6h. Child (<2 yrs): quarter adult dose; (2-10 yrs): half adult dose.
precautions: Monitor PT if taking warfarin concurrently. Superinfection risk with prolonged use.
adverse_effects: Abdominal pain, impaired LFTs, nephritis.

name: FLUCLOXACILLIN
indications: Otitis externa, furunculosis, pneumonia, impetigo, osteomyelitis, staphylococcal endocarditis.
dosage_schedule: Adult: 250-500 mg q6h (oral/IM). Child (<2 yrs): quarter dose; (2-10 yrs): half dose. Furunculosis: 1 g q6h for 5 days. Endocarditis (<85 kg): 8 g daily in 4 divided doses.
precautions: See under BENZYL PENICILLIN.
adverse_effects: See under BENZYL PENICILLIN.

name: PHENOXY METHYL PENICILLIN (PENICILLIN V)
indications: Streptococcal pharyngitis, actinomycosis, erysipelas, periodontal infections, recurrent rheumatic fever.
dosage_schedule: Pharyngitis: 500 mg q12h or 250 mg q6h for 10 days. Actinomycosis (Mild): 2-4 g/day oral q6h for 8 weeks (Surgical: 6-12 months). Prophylaxis: 250 mg q12h.
contraindications: Allergy to penicillins, cephalosporins, or imipenem.
precautions: IgE mediated anaphylaxis reported in severe renal impairment and asthma. Use with caution in neonates; some forms contain sodium benzoate (risk of gasping syndrome).
adverse_effects: Interstitial nephritis, anaphylaxis, positive Coomb's reaction.
interactions: Decreases effects of BCG vaccine. Tetracyclines decrease its effects.

name: PIPERACILLIN
indications: Urinary tract infection (uncomplicated), community acquired pneumonia, acute cholangitis, uncomplicated gonorrhea, Pseudomonas infections.
dosage_schedule: Usual: IV 3-4 g/dose q4-6h (max 24 g/day); IM 2-3 g/dose q6-12h (max 24 g/day). UTI/Pneumonia: 100-125 mg/kg/day divided q6-12h. Cholangitis: 4 g IV q6h. Gonorrhea: 2 g once + 1 g probenecid. Pseudomonas: 4 g IV/IM q4h. Renal Adjust: CrCl 20-40: 3-4 g q8h; CrCl <20: 3-4 g q12h.
precautions: Risk of bleeding complications in renal impairment. Monitor hematopoietic functions during prolonged treatment. IVPreparation: reconstitute each gram w/ 5ml NS/D5W.
adverse_effects: Hemolytic anemia, interstitial nephritis, prolonged prothrombin time, injection site pain.
interactions: Increases effects/toxicity of antithrombin alfa, argatroban, heparin, vancomycin. Azithromycin and Doxycycline decrease effects. Piperacillin decreases BCG vaccine effects.

name: PIPERACILLIN with TAZOBACTAM
indications: Severe infections, nosocomial pneumonia, community acquired pneumonia, intra-abdominal abscess, skin/soft tissue, malignant otitis externa.
dosage_schedule: Severe: IV 3.375 g q6h (Total 13.5 g) for 7-10 days. Nosocomial: 4.5 g IV + aminoglycoside for 7-14 days. Complicated Intra-abdominal: 3.375 g q6h for 4-7 days. Malignant Otitis Externa: 4.5 g IV q8h then step down to ciprofloxacin.
contraindications: Allergy to penicillin, cephalosporins, imipenem, beta-lactamase inhibitors.
precautions: Discontinue if thrombocytopenia or bleeding occurs. Serious skin reactions (SJS, TEN) reported.
adverse_effects: Diarrhea, constipation, headache, insomnia, nausea, fever, oral candidiasis.

name: AMIKACIN
indications: Serious gram-negative infections resistant to gentamicin.
dosage_schedule: Adult: IV once daily 15 mg/kg/day (max 1.5 g/day); max 15 g per course. Child: 15 mg/kg daily in 2-3 doses. Neonate: loading 10 mg/kg then 15 mg/kg daily in 2 divided doses.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: See under GENTAMICIN.

name: GENTAMICIN
indications: Pseudomonas UTIs, meningitis/neonatal sepsis, endocarditis, biliary tract disease, prostatitis, surgical prophylaxis, medical labyrinthectomy, otitis externa.
dosage_schedule: IM/IV: 3-5 mg/kg daily (divided q8h). Child (<2 wks): 3 mg/kg q12h; (2 wks-12 yrs): 2 mg/kg q8h. Intrathecal: 1 mg daily (max 5 mg). Endocarditis: 1 mg/kg q8h. Surgical Prophylaxis: 1.5 mg/kg (max 3 min before procedure); can repeat q8h. Medical Labyrinthectomy: intra tympanic 2-3 drops, 3-4 times daily.
precautions: Monitor blood levels in neonates, elderly, and renal impairment. Report hearing loss, ringing in ears, or head fullness. Myasthenia gravis and parkinson's disease risk.
adverse_effects: Vestibular damage, reversible nephrotoxicity, muscle weakness, respiratory paralysis.
interactions: Do not mix with penicillins. Increased ototoxicity/nephrotoxicity with vancomycin, cisplatin, furosemide, mannitol. Increases effects of non-depolarizing neuromuscular blockers.

name: CHLORAMPHENICOL
indications: Life threatening infections (Hemophilus influenza), typhoid fever, acute otitis externa.
dosage_schedule: Adult: 12.5 mg/kg every 6 hours (can double in septicemia/meningitis). Otitis externa: intra-aural 2-3 drops, BID/TID for 7 days.
precautions: Monitor blood counts regularly; discontinue if leucopenia or anemia appears. Do not give IM (ineffective). Take on empty stomach.
adverse_effects: Erythema multiforme, optic neuritis, grey baby syndrome.

name: CLINDAMYCIN
indications: Staphylococcal bone/joint infections (osteomyelitis), peritonitis, MRSA, bronchiectasis, skin/soft tissue, pneumocystis pneumonia (with primaquine), falciparum malaria (after quinine), acne vulgaris, tonsillitis/pharyngitis (penicillin allergy).
dosage_schedule: Infections: Adult 150-300 mg q6h (max 450 mg). Child: 3-6 mg/kg 4 times daily. IM/IV: Adult 0.6-2.7 g daily; max 4.8 g. Pneumocystis: 600 mg q8h. Malaria (Child): 7-13 mg/kg q8h; (Adult): 450 mg q8h. Acne: 2% gel BID.
precautions: Severe skin reactions (DRESS, SJS, TEN) reported. Endocarditis prophylaxis: use only for high-risk.
adverse_effects: Antibiotic-associated colitis (discontinue), jaundice, esophageal ulcers, vesiculobullous dermatitis.
interactions: Increases effects of atracurium (pharmacodynamic synergism). Risk of respiratory depression.

name: LINEZOLID
indications: Pneumonia (when glycopeptides/vancomycin cannot be used), complicated skin/soft tissue infections.
dosage_schedule: Adult: 600 mg q12h (10-14 days; max 28 days). Child: 10 mg/kg TID. Preterm infant: 10 mg/kg BID. IV: 600 mg q12h.
precautions: Monitor visual function if >28 days. Weekly FBC monitoring. Avoid tyramine-rich foods (mature cheese, yeast, soy, undistilled alcohol). Plasma concentration reduced by rifampin.
adverse_effects: Diarrhea, pseudomembranous colitis, vaginal candidiasis, visual field defect, pancytopenia.
interactions: Reduced by rifampicin. Avoid with MAOI, SSRIs, TCAs (wait 2 weeks).

name: AZITHROMYCIN
indications: Community-acquired pneumonia, lyme disease, URTI, otitis media, skin/soft tissue, non-gonococcal urethritis, multi-drug resistant typhoid, pharyngitis (penicillin allergy).
dosage_schedule: Susceptible: 500 mg once daily for 3 days; Child: 10 mg/kg. Prophylaxis: 15 mg/kg stat. Non-gonococcal: 1 g single dose. Typhoid: 500 mg once daily for 7 days. Lyme: 500 mg daily for 7-10 days.
precautions: Caution in renal/cardiac disease. Not for otitis media <6 months or pharyngitis <2 years. Avoid sunlight. Take suspension 1 hour before or 2 hours after meal.
adverse_effects: Headache, drowsiness, arthralgia, taste/vision disturbance, pancreatitis.

name: CLARITHROMYCIN
indications: URTI, skin/soft tissue, otitis media, H. pylori eradication (with PPI), pharyngitis.
dosage_schedule: URTI: Adult 250 mg q12h for 7 days (Severe: 500 mg q12h for 14 days). Child: 15 mg/kg BID for 10 days. H. pylori: 250-500 mg BID. Tonsillitis (penicillin allergy): 250 mg q12h for 10 days.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to macrolides, torsade de pointes, QT prolongation.
precautions: Use in pregnancy only if benefit outweighs risk.
adverse_effects: Tooth and tongue discoloration, smell and taste disturbances, hyperhydrosis, insomnia.

name: ERYTHROMYCIN
indications: Lyme disease, chronic prostatitis, pertussis, diphtheria, rheumatic fever recurrence, acute laryngitis.
dosage_schedule: Lyme: 500 mg QID for 14-21 days. Prostatitis: 250-500 mg QID. Diphtheria (non-immune): 500 mg q6h for 7-17 days. Acne: 500 mg BID for 3 months. Syphilis: 500 mg QID for 14 days. Child (Amoebiosis): 30-50 mg/kg/day.
contraindications: Macrolide hypersensitivity, history of cholestatic jaundice.
precautions: Monitor hepatic function in previous liver disease. QT prolongation risk.
adverse_effects: Nausea, vomiting, skin rashes, fever, cholestatic hepatitis (primarily with estolate form).
interactions: Potentiates effects of carbamazepine, corticosteroids, digoxin, theophylline, sildenafil.

name: CIPROFLOXACIN
indications: Complicated/uncomplicated UTIs, prostatitis, airway disease, typhoid, gonorrhea, diffuse otitis externa, surgical prophylaxis.
dosage_schedule: URTI/UTI: 250-500 mg BID. Gonorrhea: 500 mg single dose. Prostatitis: 500 mg BID for 28 days. Otitis externa: 500 mg BID for 7 days. Surgical Prophylaxis: 750 mg 60-90 min before procedure. Child (UTI): 10-30 mg/kg daily divided.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to quinolones, children under 12 years (unless benefit outweighs risk), breastfeeding.
precautions: Caution in epilepsy or history of epilepsy, renal/hepatic impairment.
adverse_effects: Pancreatitis, tachycardia, tinnitus, joint/cartilage damage, tendinitis, tendon rupture.
interactions: Antacids reduce absorption. Concomitant use with warfarin prolongs PT.

name: LEVOFLOXACIN
indications: Prostatitis, UTI, chronic bronchitis, community-acquired pneumonia, skin/soft tissue, bacterial sinusitis, pharyngitis.
dosage_schedule: UTI: 250 mg daily for 7-10 days. Bronchitis: 250-500 mg daily. Prostatitis: 500 mg once daily for 28 days. Pneumonia: 500 mg daily for 7-14 days. Child (Pneumonia): 10-15 mg/kg single dose.
precautions: Monitor convulsions, tendon weakness, MI, atrial fibrillation, colitis. Administer 4 hours before or 2 hours after antacids, iron, zinc.
adverse_effects: See under CIPROFLOXACIN; also hypoglycemia and pneumonitis.

name: MOXIFLOXACIN
indications: Sinusitis, pneumonia, bronchitis, PID, tuberculosis.
dosage_schedule: Adult: 400 mg once daily. Sinusitis: 7 days. Pneumonia/PID: 7-14 days. Bronchitis: 5-10 days.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, uncontrolled hypokalemia, prolonged QT interval.
precautions: Assess ECG, renal impairment, epilepsy. Monitor for pseudomembranous colitis.
adverse_effects: Angina, arrhythmias, hyperlipidemia, vasodilation, xerostomia.
interactions: Probenecid increases levels. Increases warfarin and cyclosporine effect. Seizure risk with NSAIDs.

name: NALIDIXIC ACID
indications: Urinary tract infections.
dosage_schedule: 900 mg q6h for 7 days (reduce to 600 mg for chronic). Child (>3 mo): max 50 mg/kg daily divided. Prolonged: 30 mg/kg daily.
precautions: See under CIPROFLOXACIN.
adverse_effects: Cranial nerve palsy, increase in intra-cranial pressure, metabolic acidosis, toxic psychosis.

name: NORFLOXACIN
indications: Uncomplicated UTI, recurrent UTI prophylaxis, chronic prostatitis.
dosage_schedule: UTI: 400 mg BID for 7-10 days. Chronic Relapsing: 400 mg BID for 12 weeks. Prostatitis: 400 mg BID for 28 days. Child: 10-15 mg/kg/day divided.
precautions: Risk of tendon rupture.
adverse_effects: Epiphora. See under CIPROFLOXACIN.

name: OFLOXACIN
indications: UTI, prostatitis, MDR-TB, PID, septicemia, skin, otitis externa/media.
dosage_schedule: Skin: 400 mg BID for 10 days. PID: 400 mg BID for 14 days. Septicemia: Inj 200 mg BID (up to 400 mg). UTI: 200-400 mg daily. Non-gonococcal: 400 mg daily for 7 days. Otitis externa: 10 drops daily for 7 days.
precautions: See under CIPROFLOXACIN.
adverse_effects: See under CIPROFLOXACIN.

name: COTRIMOXAZOLE (SULPHAMETHOXAZOLE and TRIMETHOPRIM)
