indications: Uncomplicated lower UTI, prostatitis, bronchitis (H. influenzae/Strep), otitis media, maxillary sinusitis, Pneumocystis carinii pneumonia.
dosage_schedule: Oral (Adult): 960 mg q12h. Child: 5-8 mg/kg/day trimethoprim + 25-50 mg/kg/day sulfamethoxazole divided. Pneumocystis (High dose): 120 mg/kg daily for 14 days. Prophylaxis (Adult): 960 mg daily.
contraindications: Blood donors, infants <6 weeks, G-6PD deficiency, hypersensitivity, pregnancy, lactation.
precautions: Monitor for pseudomembranous colitis. Risk of crystalluria; maintain 1.5L urine output daily.
adverse_effects: Erythema multiform (SJS), leucopenia, granulocytopenia, glossitis, megaloblastic anaemia.

name: DOXYCYCLINE
indications: UTI, acne, early syphilis, late latent syphilis, non-gonococcal urethritis, anthrax prophylaxis, Lyme disease, periodontitis, lymphangioma.
dosage_schedule: UTI: 200 mg day 1, then 100 mg daily. Acne: 100 mg daily (6-12 weeks). Syphilis (Early): 100 mg BID for 14 days; (Late): 200 mg BID for 28 days. Non-gonococcal: 100 mg BID for 7 days. Periodontitis: 20 mg BID for 3 months. Lymphangioma: 10-20 mg/ml injection.
precautions: Avoid breastfeeding. Caution in hepatic impairment, excessive sunlight, and sulfite hypersensitivity.
adverse_effects: See under Tetracyclines.
interactions: Increases effects of digoxin, anticoagulants, methotrexate. Decreased by antacids, dairy, iron, cholestyramine, rifampin. Decreases effects of penicillin and OCPs.

name: MINOCYCLINE
indications: Acne vulgaris, Gonococcal Infection.
dosage_schedule: Gonococcal: 100 mg BID. Acne: 50 mg BID for min 6 weeks.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, breastfeeding, children, renal/hepatic impairment, bladder obstruction.
precautions: Monitor dialysis and hypertension.
adverse_effects: N/A
interactions: Increases effects of warfarin, digoxin, insulin, neuromuscular blockers. Risk of pseudo-tumor cerebri with retinoids.

name: OXYTETRACYCLINE
indications: See under TETRACYCLINE.
dosage_schedule: 250-500 mg every 6 hours.
precautions: See under TETRACYCLINE.
adverse_effects: See under TETRACYCLINE.

name: TETRACYCLINE
indications: Chronic bronchitis, sinusitis, chlamydial infections (NGU, trachoma), acne, brucellosis, cholera, syphilis (penicillin allergy), diabetic diarrhea, rosacea.
dosage_schedule: Infections: 250 mg q6h (up to 500 mg q8h severe). Acne (Adult/Child 12-17): 500 mg BID for 3 months. Syphilis: 500 mg q6h for 15 days. Rosacea: 500 mg BID for 6-12 weeks.
precautions: Renal/Hepatic impairment, UV exposure.
adverse_effects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, urticaria, glossitis, fungal superinfection (in periodontitis).
interactions: Fatal nephrotoxicity with methoxyflurane. Increases digoxin/warfarin effects. Decreased by iron, antacids, cimetidine, dairy.

name: VANCOMYCIN
indications: Clostridium difficile infection, gram-positive infections (endocarditis, osteomyelitis, septicaemia, soft-tissue), surgical prophylaxis (MRSA risk).
dosage_schedule: C. difficile (Oral): 125 mg 4 times daily for 10-14 days (max 500 mg TID). Gram-positive (IV): Adult 1-1.5 g q12h; Elderly 500 mg q12h. Prophylaxis: 1 g IV.
precautions: Monitor plasma trough levels: 10-15 mg/L (15-20 in MRSA). Avoid extravasation (necrosis). Adjust dose in renal impairment. Use caution in pregnancy.
adverse_effects: Red man syndrome (flushing upper body), blood disorders (reversible neutropenia), ototoxicity (discontinue if tinnitus occurs), cardiac arrest on rapid infusion.
interactions: Cross-sensitivity with teicoplanin. Avoid with bacitracin, BCG, typhoid vaccine.

name: AMPHOTERICIN B
indications: Intestinal candidiasis, oral/perioral infections, severe systemic/deep mycosis, aspergillosis, visceral leishmaniasis, febrile neutropenia.
dosage_schedule: Aspergillosis (Liposomal): IV test dose 1 mg, then 3 mg/kg daily. Visceral Leishmaniasis: 1-3 mg/kg daily for 10-21 days (cumulative 21-30 mg/kg) or 3 mg/kg for 5 days. Systemic (Adult): IV test 1 mg, then 250 mcg/kg increasing to 1 mg/kg. Oropharyngeal: 0.1 mg/ml rinse q8h.
precautions: Monitor hepatic/renal function tests and plasma electrolytes. Notify doctor of soft tissue swelling or bruising.
adverse_effects: Chills, fever, hypokalemia, convulsions, anaphylactoid reactions.
interactions: Increased hepatotoxicity/ototoxicity with cidofovir. Increased nephrotoxicity with aminoglycosides, vancomycin, cisplatin. Hypokalemia with steroids, digoxin, diuretics.

name: CLOTRIMAZOLE
indications: Candidiasis, Tinea infections, Otomycosis.
dosage_schedule: Vaginal: 100 mg for 6 days or 200 mg for 3 days or 500 mg single dose. Otomycosis: 3 drops TID for 7-10 days. Oropharyngeal: 10 mg tablet mix in water 5 times daily.
adverse_effects: Vaginal burning, rash, pruritus.
precautions: Ophthalmic use. Do not use near eyes, nose, or mouth.

name: FLUCONAZOLE
indications: Invasive candidal infections, cryptococcal infections (meningitis), balanitis, dermal/oropharyngeal candidiasis.
dosage_schedule: Recurrent Vaginal: 150 mg q12h (3 doses) then 150 mg weekly for 6 months. Mucosal: 50-100 mg daily (7-14 days). Tinea: 50 mg daily for 2-4 weeks. Cryptococcal (Adult): 400 mg day 1, then 200-400 mg daily (min 8 weeks). Child: 6-12 mg/kg. Prevention in immunocompromised: 50-400 mg daily.
precautions: Monitor liver function. If used for oral candidiasis, don’t rinse mouth for 15-30 mins after use. Use alternative contraception.
adverse_effects: Diarrhoea, headache, nausea, rash.
interactions: Increases anticoagulation (warfarin), increases levels of phenytoin, theophylline, zidovudine, methadone, fentanyl. PPIs decrease fluconazole effects.

name: GRISEOFULVIN
indications: Dermatophyte infections.
dosage_schedule: Tinea capitis (Adult): 1 g daily. Child: 15-20 mg/kg daily (max 1 g). Failed topical therapy: 500 mg daily.
precautions: Avoid breastfeeding. May impair driving. Use alternative contraception.
adverse_effects: Heartburn, photosensitivity, skin rashes.
interactions: Decreases effect of warfarin and OCPs. Phenobarbitone decreases griseofulvin effects. Enhances alcohol effects.

name: ITRACONAZOLE
indications: Systemic candidiasis, onychomycosis, aspergillosis, histoplasmosis, esophageal candidiasis (HIV+), cryptococcal meningitis.
dosage_schedule: Recurrent Vulvovaginal: 50-100 mg daily for 6 months. Onychomycosis: 200 mg daily for 3 months (alternately 200 mg BID for 7 days then 21-day break). Aspergillosis: 200 mg BID. Histoplasmosis: 200 mg TID for 3 days then 200 mg 1-2 times daily. Oropharyngeal (HIV+): 100 mg BID for 2 weeks.
precautions: Caution in renal/hepatic impairment, achlorhydria, dialysis, hearing loss. Potential for life-threatening hepatotoxicity.
adverse_effects: Hyperglycemia (IV use), hepatitis, hypokalemia, SJS, visual disturbances.
interactions: Increased toxicity with benzodiazepines, digoxin, statins, warfarin. Decreased by antacids, H2 antagonists, PPIs.

name: KETOCONAZOLE
indications: Candidiasis, coccidioidomycosis, histoplasmosis, paracoccidioidomycosis, tinea, seborrheic dermatitis, dandruff.
dosage_schedule: Systemic/Candidiasis (Adult): 200-400 mg/day for 1-2 weeks. Seborrheic: foam/gel BID for 4 weeks. Dandruff (Shampoo): massage for 1 min, rinse; 2 times per week for 8 weeks.
precautions: Hepatic impairment (monitor ALT/AST/bilirubin). Avoid driving if dizziness occurs. Topical: wash hands before/after; don't wash area for 3 hours after application.
adverse_effects: Irritation, stinging, pustules, pruritus.
interactions: Decreased by H2 blockers, PPIs, antacids. Increases effect of phenytoin, warfarin, digoxin, omeprazole, statins.

name: NYSTATIN
indications: Oral, esophageal, intestinal, vaginal, cutaneous, corneal candidiasis.
dosage_schedule: Vaginal: Pessary 100,000 IU at night. Intestinal (Adult): 500,000 units q6h; (Child): 100,000 units QID. Cutaneous: apply cream BID.
precautions: If used for oral candidiasis, don't rinse mouth for 15-30 mins after use.
adverse_effects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea (at high doses).

name: ALBENDAZOLE
indications: Ascaris, pinworm, hookworm, whipworm, strongyloides, Echinococcus granulosus, neurocysticercosis.
dosage_schedule: Single/Mixed Nematode: 400 mg single dose. Strongyloidiasis: 400 mg BID for 3 days. Enterobiasis (Child 2+): 400 mg repeated after 14 days. E. granulosus: 800 mg daily (divided) for 1-6 months; Child: 15 mg/kg. Neurocysticercosis (>60 kg): 800 mg daily for 8-30 days; (<60 kg): 15 mg/kg daily.
contraindications: First trimester of pregnancy, children <1 year.
precautions: Avoid pregnancy for one month after use (fetal harm risk). Take with food.
adverse_effects: Gastro-intestinal discomfort, headache.
interactions: Reduced by carbamazepine, phenytoin, ritonavir. Increased by corticosteroids.

name: MEBENDAZOLE
indications: Threadworm, roundworm, hookworm, whipworm.
dosage_schedule: Whipworm (Adult/Child): 100 mg BID for 3 days. Threadworm (Child 2+): 100 mg single dose (repeat after 2 weeks). Round/Hookworm: 100 mg BID for 3 days.
precautions: Breast-feeding, IBD, hepatic disease. Monitor AST, ALT, ALP, BUN, CBC.
adverse_effects: Abdominal pain, diarrhea, rash. Worms may be expelled through mouth/nose in heavy infection.
interactions: Decreased effect by carbamazepine, hydantoins. Increased absorption with high fat meal.

name: MILTEFOSINE
indications: Visceral and cutaneous leishmaniasis.
dosage_schedule: Oral (>25 kg): 100 mg daily for 28 days. Child: 2.5 mg/kg daily.
adverse_effects: Vomiting, diarrhea, reversible rise in hepatic transaminases/serum creatinine.
precautions: Encourage fluid intake. Advise effective non-hormonal contraception.
interactions: Combination with paromomycin/Amphotericin B prevents resistance.

name: NICLOSAMIDE
indications: Tapeworm (Taenia solium, saginata, H. nana, Diphyllobothrium latum).
dosage_schedule: T. solium (Adult/Child 6+): 2 g single dose after breakfast + purgative 2 hours later; (Child 2-6): 1 g; (<2): 500 mg. H. nana (Adult/Child 6+): 2 g day 1, then 1 g daily for 6 days.
precautions: Inactive against cysticercosis cellulose; danger of cysticercosis in T. solium. Avoid alcohol during treatment.
adverse_effects: Nausea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort, pruritus.
interactions: Alcohol enhances its absorption and adverse effects.

name: PENTAMIDINE
indications: Visceral leishmaniasis, Pneumocystis pneumonia.
dosage_schedule: Leishmaniasis: deep IM 3-4 mg/kg on alternate days (max 10 injections). Pneumonia: IV infusion 4 mg/kg daily for 14 days.
precautions: Blood dyscrasias, renal/hepatic disease, diabetes, hypocalcemia. Monitor blood counts.
adverse_effects: Acute renal failure, hyperkalaemia, megaloblastic anaemia, acute pancreatitis, pain at site.
interactions: Increases nephrotoxicity of vancomycin/cisplatin. QT prolongation with class III antiarrhythmics/chloroquine. Myelosuppression with radiation.

name: PIPERAZINE
indications: Ascariasis, enterobiasis.
dosage_schedule: Ascariasis: max 3.5 g/day; Child 75 mg/kg for 2 consecutive days. Enterobiasis: max 2.5 g/day; Child 65 mg/kg for 7 days.
precautions: Pregnancy, breastfeeding (use only if no alternative). Treat all household members concurrently for pinworms. Wash bedding/nightclothes.
adverse_effects: Nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, urticaria.
interactions: Enhances phenothiazines; risk of seizures. Antagonistic to Pyrantel Pamoate.

name: PRAZIQUANTEL
indications: Taeniasis (T. solium/saginata), hymenolepiasis, diphyllobothriasis, Schistosoma haematobium/japonicum.
dosage_schedule: T. solium: 10-20 mg/kg single dose. H. nana: 25 mg/kg single dose. S. haematobium: oral 20 mg/kg, then 20 mg/kg after 4-6 hours. S. japonicum: 20 mg/kg TID for 1 day.
precautions: Discontinue if cerebral cysticercosis present. Do not drive for 24 hours after treatment.
adverse_effects: Rectal bleeding, urticaria, dizziness.
interactions: Reduced by chloroquine/dexamethasone. Increased by grapefruit/cimetidine.

name: PYRANTEL PAMOATE
indications: Ascariasis, hookworm, pinworm.
dosage_schedule: Adult/Child (>2 yrs): single 10 mg/kg (max 1 g). Pinworms: repeat after 2 weeks. Treat entire household.
precautions: Hepatic impairment, lactation. Wear tight underwear both day and night while taking.
adverse_effects: Headache, dizziness, drowsiness, mild GI disturbance.

name: SODIUM STIBOGLUCONATE
indications: Leishmaniasis.
dosage_schedule: 20 mg/kg daily (max 850 mg) for at least 20 days (IM/IV). Skin lesions: treat for 10 days.
precautions: Withdraw if conduction disturbances occur. Monitor ECG. Rapid IV injection can result in cardiovascular collapse.
adverse_effects: Skin rashes, vomiting, abdominal pain, severe cough.

name: CLOFAZIMINE
indications: Multibacillary leprosy (with rifampicin/dapsone), Type II lepra reaction.
dosage_schedule: Adult (Multibacillary): supervised 300 mg once a month + self-administered 50 mg daily for 1 year.
precautions: Avoid if persistent abdominal pain/diarrhea. May discolor soft contact lenses. Risk of ventricular arrhythmias with bedaquiline.
adverse_effects: Red discoloration of skin, feces, urine, and infant skin; dry eyes, dry skin, phototoxicity.

name: DAPSONE
indications: Leprosy, dermatitis herpetiformis, Pneumocystis pneumonia prophylaxis, rhinosporidiosis recurrence.
dosage_schedule: Multibacillary: 100 mg daily for 1 year. Paucibacillary: 100 mg daily for 6 months. Child (<35 kg): 50 mg or 1-2 mg/kg. Pneumocystis: 100 mg daily.
contraindications: Cardiac disease, G6PD deficiency, pulmonary disease.
adverse_effects: Hemolytic anaemia (G6PD deficiency), anorexia, nausea, vomiting.
interactions: Pregnancy- Neonatal methemoglobinemia reported in 3rd trimester.

name: ARTEMETHER with LUMEFANTRINE
indications: Acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria, chloroquine-resistant non-falciparum malaria.
dosage_schedule: Adult/Child (>12 yrs): 4 tabs then 5 doses of 4 tabs at 8, 24, 36, 48, 60 hrs (Total 24 tabs) with food. Child (5-14 kg): 1 tab initially then 5 further doses. (Detailed weight brackets in formulary).
precautions: If trouble swallowing, tablet may be crushed. Dizziness may affect tasks.
adverse_effects: Palpitation, anorexia, abdominal pain, rash.

name: ARTESUNATE
indications: P. falciparum malaria, especially multidrug resistance.
dosage_schedule: IV/IM: Loading 2 mg/kg, then 1 mg/kg at 4 and 24 hours. Thereafter 1 mg/kg daily until patient tolerates oral (max 7 days).
precautions: Must be used immediately after reconstitution; discard if cloudy. Protect from light.
adverse_effects: Drug induced fever, neutropenia, cardiotoxicity (high dose), hemolysis (2 wks post-treatment).

name: CHLOROQUINE
indications: Malaria chemoprophylaxis/treatment, RA, lupus erythematosus.
dosage_schedule: Prophylaxis: 300 mg base once weekly (start 1 wk before, end 4 wks after). Presumptive Treatment: 600 mg base + 45 mg primaquine. Radical Cure (Relapsing): 600 mg base, then 300 mg at 6, 24, 48 hrs + 15 mg primaquine (15 days). RA/Lupus: 150 mg daily.
contraindications: Retinal field changes, auditory damage, torsade de pointes, G6PD deficiency, seizures.
precautions: Baseline and periodic ophthalmic test (>150 mg/day).
adverse_effects: Epigastric discomfort, pruritus, reversible visual disturbance.
interactions: Cimetidine reduces clearance. Increases QT with antiarrhythmics. Increases 2D6 inhibitors/CYP3A inhibitors. Chloroquine decreases rabies vaccine effects.

name: MEFLOQUINE
indications: Treatment and prophylaxis of Malaria (P. falciparum/P. vivax).
dosage_schedule: Prophylaxis: 250 mg weekly (start 2.5 wks before, end 4 wks after). Long term (>3 mo): on individual assessment. Child (<15 kg): not recommended.
contraindications: History of convulsion, psychiatric disorder, infants <3 months, pregnancy.
precautions: Cardiac conduction disorder, brain injury. Disturbed balance may persist for months after stopping.
adverse_effects: Tinnitus, bradycardia, extrasystoles, dizziness, vertigo.
interactions: Avoid beta-blockers/calcium channel blockers (risk of bradycardia).

name: PRIMAQUINE
indications: Adjunct in P. vivax and P. ovale malaria.
dosage_schedule: Presumptive: 45 mg single dose. Radical cure: 15 mg daily for 5 days; child 250 mcg/kg daily.
contraindications: Children <1 yr, lupus, RA, methemoglobin reductase deficiency, bone marrow suppression.
precautions: G6PD deficiency risk. Always give in conjunction with chloroquine.
adverse_effects: Abdominal cramps, vomiting, leucocytosis, haemolytic anaemia.
interactions: Grapefruit decreases effect. Don't use with other drugs liable to induce hemolysis.

name: QUININE
indications: Treatment of uncomplicated malaria.
dosage_schedule: Oral: Adult 300-600 mg q8h for 5-7 days; Child 25 mg/kg. IV Infusion (if unable to swallow): Loading 900 mg - 1.4 g over 4 hrs, then 300-600 mg q8h.
contraindications: Myasthenia gravis, optic neuritis, digoxin toxicity, blood dyscrasia.
precautions: Monitor blood glucose/electrolytes during IV use.
adverse_effects: Cinchonism (tinnitus, temporary blindness, blurred vision, hot skin), hypoglycemia, nephrotoxicity.
interactions: Additive vagolytic effect with anticholinergics. QT prolongation by macrolides/quinolones.

name: SULFADOXINE and PYRIMETHAMINE
indications: Combination therapy in P. falciparum malaria.
dosage_schedule: Treatment: adult 3 tablets single dose; child: 1.25 mg/kg pyrimethamine and 25 mg/kg sulphadoxine.
contraindications: Acute porphyrias, sulfonamide allergy, infants <6 weeks.
precautions: Predisposition to folate deficiency or hyperkalemia. Maintain fluid intake to avert crystalluria.
adverse_effects: Hyperkalemia, rash, headache.
interactions: Folic acid decreases effects. Increases chlorpromazine levels.

name: ETHAMBUTOL
indications: Tuberculosis in combination.
dosage_schedule: 15-25 mg/kg daily.
contraindications: Children <5 yrs, optic neuritis, severe renal impairment.
precautions: Check visual acuity (Snellen chart) and renal function before treatment. Monitor children ophthalmologically.
adverse_effects: Optic neuritis (reversible; dose-dependent), hyperuricemia, joint pain.
interactions: Decreases live BCG vaccine effects. Aluminium hydroxide increases levels.

name: ISONIAZID
indications: Tuberculosis in combination, TB prophylaxis.
dosage_schedule: 300 mg daily; Child: 10 mg/kg daily (max 300 mg).
precautions: Assessment of liver damage monthly. Administer Pyridoxine (25-100 mg daily) to prevent peripheral neuropathy. Caution in alcohol dependence (assess liver in first 2 months).
adverse_effects: Peripheral neuritis (common), hepatic damage, skin rash.
interactions: Increases toxicity with alcohol, cycloserine, rifampin, phenytoin. Serotonin syndrome risk with SSRIs. Aluminium antacids decrease absorption.

name: PYRAZINAMIDE
indications: Tuberculosis.
dosage_schedule: Adult (<50 kg): 1.5 g/day; (>50 kg): 2 g/day. Child: 25-35 mg/kg daily.
precautions: Assess RFT and LFT at onset. Monitor for gout.
adverse_effects: Hepatotoxicity, hyperuricemia, sideroblastic anaemia, thrombocytopenia.

name: RIFAMPIN
indications: Short course chemo for TB and leprosy, meningococcal prophylaxis, H. influenzae, atrophic rhinitis.
dosage_schedule: TB (>50 kg): 600 mg daily. Leprosy (Multibacillary): 600 mg once monthly supervised. Meningococcal Prophylaxis: 600 mg q12h for 2 days. Child (>1 yr): 10 mg/kg. Atrophic Rhinitis: 600 mg daily for 12 weeks.
precautions: Induces hepatic enzymes. Urine, saliva, feces, sputum, sweat, and tears may be colored red-orange; soft contact lenses permanently stained. Avoid alcohol.
adverse_effects: Flu-like syndrome, thrombocytopenic purpura, transient rise in bilirubin.
interactions: Accelerates metabolism of corticosteroids, digitalis, OCPs, oral hypoglycemics. Increases hepatotoxicity with isoniazid. Don't use with protease inhibitors.

name: STREPTOMYCIN
indications: TB resistant to other treatment, brucellosis, bacterial endocarditis.
dosage_schedule: Adult: 0.75 g daily; child 15-20 mg/kg IM.
precautions: Avoid whenever possible in pregnancy/elderly. See under GENTAMICIN.
adverse_effects: Vestibular damage (increases with dose and age >40), nephrotoxicity, skin rashes.

name: BEDAQUILINE
indications: Combination regimen for pulmonary MDR-TB when other treatments are not available.
dosage_schedule: Adult: 400 mg once daily for 2 weeks, then 200 mg 3 times a week (at least 48 hrs between doses) for 22 weeks.
precautions: Monitor ECG baseline and at least monthly (QT prolongation risk). Caution in cardiac impairment, heart failure, syncope, thyroid disease.
adverse_effects: Arthralgia, nausea, QT interval prolongation, myalgia.
interactions: Increases QT with class IA/III antiarrhythmics, haloperidol, chloroquine. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase effect (avoid >14 days). Lopinavir/ritonavir increase adverse reactions.

name: CAPREOMYCIN
indications: TB resistant to 1st line drugs.
dosage_schedule: Deep IM (Adult): 1 g daily (max 20 mg/kg) for 2-4 months, then 1 g 2-3 times a week.
precautions: Monitor renal, hepatic, auditory and vestibular function. Caution in breastfeeding/elderly.
adverse_effects: Induration at site, hearing loss with tinnitus/vertigo, leucocytosis, leucopenia, nephrotoxicity.
interactions: Increased nephrotoxicity/ototoxicity with colistin, polymyxins, vancomycin, aminoglycosides.

name: CYCLOSERINE
indications: TB resistant to 1st line drugs.
dosage_schedule: Initially 250 mg q12h for 2 weeks, then 500 mg q12h. Child: 10 mg/kg/day divided.
contraindications: Alcohol dependence, depression, epilepsy, psychotic states.
precautions: Blood concentration monitoring required (should not exceed 30 mg/litre). Monitor hematological/renal function.
adverse_effects: Confusion, convulsions, tremor, allergic dermatitis, megaloblastic anemia.
interactions: Alcohol increases convulsion risk. Isoniazid increases CNS toxicity.

name: ETHIONAMIDE
indications: Second line drug for TB.
dosage_schedule: Initial 250 mg/day for 1-2 days, then 250 mg BID for 1-2 days, then gradual increase to highest tolerated. Avg 750 mg/day; max 1 g/day in divided doses.
precautions: Pregnancy, lactation, psychiatric cases.
adverse_effects: Gynaecomastia, hypoglycemia, impotence, peripheral neuropathy, optic neuritis.
interactions: Increases toxicity with cycloserine. Increases isoniazid levels. Decreases magnesium oxide effect.

name: KANAMYCIN
indications: 2nd line drug in TB.
dosage_schedule: IM: 250 mg q6h or 500 mg q12h. IV Infusion: 15-30 mg/kg q8-12h.
contraindications: Pregnancy, renal impairment, myasthenia gravis, cochlear implant.
precautions: See under GENTAMICIN.
adverse_effects: See under GENTAMICIN.

name: P-AMINOSALICYLIC ACID (PAS)
indications: 2nd line drugs in TB.
dosage_schedule: Granules: 4 g or 9.2 g sachet. Tablet: 500 mg.
precautions: Take with meals to decrease epigastric pain.
adverse_effects: Epigastric pain, goiter, blood dyscrasias.

name: ENTECAVIR
indications: Chronic hepatitis B (HBV).
dosage_schedule: Compensated liver (Naive): 0.5 mg once daily. Lamivudine-resistant: 1 mg once daily. Decompensated liver: 1 mg once daily.
precautions: Reduce dose if eGFR <50 ml/min. Monitor liver function every 3 months. Recurrent hepatitis may occur on discontinuation.
adverse_effects: Raised serum amylase/lipase, sleep disturbances, alopecia, thrombocytopenia.

name: PEGINTERFERON ALFA
indications: Combined with ribavirin for chronic Hep C, monotherapy for Hep C or Hep B.
dosage_schedule: Adult: SC 1.5 mcg/kg/week (max 150 mcg/week). Naive/Relapsed: 12 weeks. Non-responders: up to 24 weeks.
precautions: Monitor lipid concentration. Monitoring closely in mild-moderate hepatic impairment. Renal impairment: reduce dose.
adverse_effects: Anorexia, lethargy, arrhythmias, cardiovascular problems, myelosuppression, psoriasiform rash, seizures (elderly high dose).

name: SOFOSBUVIR
indications: Chronic hepatitis C.
dosage_schedule: Oral: 400 mg once daily.
precautions: Use two forms of reliable contraceptives. Avoid breastfeeding.
adverse_effects: Hyperbilirubinemia, headache, fatigue, anaemia.
interactions: Decreased by P-glycoprotein inducers (carbamazepine, rifampin). Bradycardia with amiodarone. Increased by carvedilol.

name: ACYCLOVIR
indications: Herpes infections, mucocutaneous HSV, infectious mononucleosis, Varicella, Herpes zoster.
dosage_schedule: HSV Treatment: 200 mg 5 times daily (5 days). Recurrence prevention: 200 mg QID or 400 mg BID. Varicella/Zoster (Adult): 800 mg 5 times daily (7 days); (Child): 20 mg/kg. Mucocutaneous: 400 mg 5 times daily. Topical: apply every 4 hrs.
precautions: Caution in renal impairment. Do not give concurrently with live vaccines. Immunization should be up to date before treatment.
adverse_effects: Rashes, urticaria, increase in blood urea/creatinine, fatigue.
interactions: Increases serious infections when used with TNF-alpha blockers.

name: OSELTAMIVIR
indications: Prevention and treatment of influenza A or B.
dosage_schedule: Influenza: 75 mg twice daily for 5 days. Prevention: 75 mg once daily for 10 days. Post-exposure Prophylaxis: up to 6 weeks.
precautions: Avoid use with H1N1 virus vaccine or intranasal influenza vaccine.
adverse_effects: Seizures, toxic epidermolysis necrolysis, SJS.

name: DIDANOSINE
indications: HIV infection.
dosage_schedule: Oral Adult (60 kg): 250 mg daily (1-2 divided doses); (>60 kg): 400 mg daily. Take 2 hours before or after food.
precautions: Monitor annually: visual acuity, color vision, dilated fundus. Risk of peripheral neuropathy (dose-related). Sodium restricted diets caution. Monitor amylase.
adverse_effects: Acute renal failure, optic nerve changes, parotid gland enlargement, gynaecomastia.
interactions: Increased by allopurinol, tenofovir. Pancreatitis risk increased by stavudine. Decreased absorption by antacids, ketoconazole, dapsone, quinolones.

name: EFAVIRENZ
indications: HIV infections.
dosage_schedule: 600 mg once daily (Adult/Child >40 kg).
precautions: Moderate-severe hepatic impairment. Monitor liver function if co-administering hepatotoxic drugs. If dose missed, take as remembered; do not double.
adverse_effects: Rash, SJS, depression, ataxia, cognitive impairment.
interactions: Increased CNS depression with alcohol, antidepressants. Increases ritonavir/estrogens. Increases warfarin/statins. Decreases OCPs, ketoconazole.

name: INDINAVIR
indications: See under SAQUINAVIR.
dosage_schedule: 800 mg q8h. Child: 500 mg/m2 q8h (max 800 mg q8h).
precautions: Ensure adequate hydration (risk of nephrolithiasis). Caution in diabetes, hemophilia, chronic Hep B/C.
adverse_effects: Hyperglycemia, pancreatitis, paraesthesia.
interactions: Dysrhythmias with ergots, amiodarone. Increases statins (myopathy risk). Increased by CYP3A4 inhibitors. Decreased by CYP3A4 inducers (St. John's wort, rifamycins).

name: LAMIVUDINE
indications: HIV infection in combination.
dosage_schedule: Adult: 150 mg BID or 300 mg daily. Infant (<1 mo): 2 mg/kg BID. Child (1 mo+): 4 mg/kg BID (max 300 mg).
precautions: Renal disease, pancreatitis, peripheral neuropathy. Caution in Hep B/C co-infection.
adverse_effects: Alopecia, anaemia, peripheral neuropathy.
interactions: Increased by cotrimoxazole, amiloride, entecavir, metformin. Interferons decrease its effects.

name: LOPINAVIR + RITONAVIR
indications: HIV infection.
dosage_schedule: Adult: Oral 400/100 mg BID (Alternatively 800/200 mg once daily if <3 protease mutations).
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to polyoxyethylated castor oil (oral solution).
precautions: Monitor LFT, blood glucose, lipid profile. Monitor for cardiomyopathy, immune reconstitution syndrome. Not a cure; others can contract HIV from patient.
adverse_effects: Amenorrhoea, neuropathy, weight changes, anaphylaxis, myalgias.
interactions: Increases toxicity of amiodarone, cisapride, clozapine, ergotamine, triazolam. Increases QT with local anesthetics/tricyclics. Ritonavir increases didanosine. Decreases OCPs.

name: NELFINAVIR
indications: HIV infection.
dosage_schedule: 750 mg TID or 1250 mg BID.
precautions: Monitor serum lipids/blood glucose. Loperamide can be used for nelfinavir-induced diarrhea.
adverse_effects: Suicidal ideation, flatulence, hyperlipidemia.
interactions: Severe dysrhythmias with amiodarone, quinidine. Increased by ketoconazole. Decreased by rifampicin, phenytoin, nevirapine. Decreases methadone and OCPs.

name: NEVIRAPINE
indications: HIV infection, PMTCT of HIV.
dosage_schedule: 200 mg daily for first 14 days, then 200 mg BID. Child (1 mo - 13 yrs): 120 mg/m2 daily for 14 days, then 200 mg/m2 BID.
precautions: Monitor liver function every 2 weeks for 2 months. Monitor skin reactions closely (first 18 weeks). Females at greater risk of hepatic side effects.
adverse_effects: SJS, hepatitis, fever, anaemia.
interactions: Increased by cimetidine, macrolides. Decreases OCPs, ketoconazole, methadone. Decreased by rifamycins, anticonvulsants.

name: RITONAVIR
indications: HIV infections.
dosage_schedule: High-dose: Initially 300 mg q12h (3 days), increase to 600 mg q12h (within 14 days). Low-dose booster: 100-200 mg 1-2 times daily.
contraindications: Hepatic impairment, pancreatitis, hemophilia, AV block, immune reconstitution syndrome.
precautions: Monitor AST/ALT every 3 months in hepatic impairment.
adverse_effects: Decreased blood thyroxine, menorrhagia, seizures, syncope.
interactions: Increases fluconazole. Decreased by rifamycins, phenytoin. Decreases anticoagulants, OCPs, divalproex.

name: SAQUINAVIR
indications: HIV infection in combination.
dosage_schedule: In combo with low-dose ritonavir: Adult 1 g q12h. In combo without low-dose ritonavir: Adult 500 mg q12h for 7 days, then 1 g q12h.
contraindications: Bradycardia, congenital QT prolongation, severe hepatic impairment.
precautions: Monitor ECG (do not initiate if QT >450ms). Safety not established in children <16 yrs.
adverse_effects: Buccal and mucosal ulceration, peripheral neuropathy, changes in libido.
interactions: Decreases anti-parkinsonism effects of levodopa. Clozapine increases risperidone effects.

name: STAVUDINE
indications: HIV infection in combination.
dosage_schedule: Adult (<60 kg): 30 mg q12h; (>60 kg): 40 mg q12h.
precautions: High risk of lipotrophy (especially with didanosine). Monitor for bone marrow suppression.
adverse_effects: Peripheral neuropathy (dose-related), pancreatitis, gynaecomastia, elevated serum amylase.
interactions: Decreased by probenecid, methadone. Increased peripheral neuropathy with lithium, dapsone, isoniazid, hydralazine.

name: TENOFOVIR DISOPROXIL
indications: HIV infection.
dosage_schedule: Adult: 245 mg once daily.
precautions: Monitor RFT and serum phosphate before and during treatment (monthly for 1 yr). Not to breastfeed.
adverse_effects: Pancreatitis, neutropenia, hypophosphataemia, polyuria, renal failure.
interactions: Increased by acyclovir, valacyclovir. Increases didanosine.

name: ZIDOVUDINE
indications: Prevention of maternal-fetal HIV transmission, HIV infections in combination.
dosage_schedule: Adult: 250-300 mg BID. Oral Child: 500-600 mg daily divided. IV: 0.8-1 mg/kg q4h. Maternal-Fetal: Mother (if CD4 <250) 300 mg + lamivudine 150 mg BID + nevirapine 200 mg once daily (start ASAP in pregnancy; for life). Neonate: 4 mg/kg BID for 7 days (continue for 4 weeks if mother had <4 wks HAART).
contraindications: Granulocyte count <1000/mm3 or Hb <9.5 g/dl, severe renal disease.
precautions: Monitor FBC monthly (initially) then q3 months.
adverse_effects: Bone marrow depression with severe anaemia, granulocytopenia, pancreatitis, gynaecomastia, myopathy.
interactions: Increased risk of toxicity with nephrotoxic/myelosuppressive drugs. Increased bone marrow depression with anti-neoplastics, clotrimazole. Increased by fluconazole, probenecid, valproic acid. Decreased by interferons, NRTIs.

name: BECLOMETHASONE
indications: Prophylaxis of bronchial asthma, prophylaxis and treatment of allergic rhinitis.
dosage_schedule: See under respiratory system (Chapter 7).
precautions: See under respiratory system.
adverse_effects: Bronchospasm and wheezing, rash, Candida infections in mouth or throat.
patient_info: Gargle mouth after each use.

name: BETAMETHASONE
indications: Replacement therapy in adrenocortical insufficiency states, Cushing's syndrome, inflammatory and allergic conditions.
dosage_schedule: Oral: 0.5-5 mg daily; IM or slow IV injection/infusion: 4-20 mg, repeated up to 4 times in 24 hours; child: by slow IV injection, up to 1 year 1 mg, 1-5 years 2 mg, 6-12 years 4 mg.
contraindications: Untreated serious infections (except tubercular meningitis or septic shock), ITP, premature infants, baby on live vaccine.
precautions: Caution in cirrhosis, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, ocular herpes simplex, peptic ulcer.
adverse_effects: Hypertension, sodium retention, potassium loss, muscle weakness, diabetes, osteoporosis, increased susceptibility to infection, mental disturbance, suppression of growth in children.
interactions: Barbiturates, phenytoin, rifampicin may increase metabolism; antagonizes hypotensive effect of alpha-blockers, beta-blockers, and calcium channel blockers.

name: CORTISONE ACETATE
indications: Adrenocortical insufficiency.
dosage_schedule: Oral, for replacement therapy: 25-37.5 mg in divided dose.
precautions: See under glucocorticoids general entry.
adverse_effects: See under glucocorticoids general entry.

name: DEXAMETHASONE
indications: Inflammatory conditions, adrenal crisis, bacterial meningitis, cerebral edema.
dosage_schedule: Physiological replacement (oral): Adult: 0.03-0.15 mg/kg/day in 2-4 divided doses; Anti-inflammatory (oral): adult: 0.75-9mg/day; Adrenal crisis: 4-10 mg/day as single dose; Bacterial meningitis (children >2 months): 0.6 mg/kg/day in 4 divided doses for 4 days; Cerebral edema: 10 mg IV followed by 4 mg 6 hourly.
precautions: Should be protected from light.
adverse_effects: See under glucocorticoids general entry.

name: FLUDROCORTISONE ACETATE
indications: Mineralocorticoid replacement in adrenocortical insufficiency.
dosage_schedule: Adrenocortical insufficiency: adult 50-300 µg daily; child 5 micrograms/kg daily.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: See under glucocorticoids general entry.

name: HYDROCORTISONE
indications: Adrenocortical insufficiency, inflammatory and allergic conditions.
dosage_schedule: Adult: by IM injection or slow IV injection or infusion: 100-500 mg, 3-4 times in 24 hours or as required; Child: by slow IV injection up to 1 year 25 mg, 1-5 year 50 mg, 6-12 years 100 mg.
precautions: Hydrocortisone acetate injection should be protected from light; container should be gently shaken before dose is withdrawn.
adverse_effects: See under glucocorticoids general entry.

name: METHYLPREDNISOLONE
indications: See under prednisolone.
dosage_schedule: Oral: 2-40 mg daily; IM injection or slow IV injection or infusion: initially 100-500 mg.
precautions: See under prednisolone.
adverse_effects: See under prednisolone.

name: PREDNISOLONE
indications: Replacement therapy in adrenocortical insufficiency, inflammatory and allergic conditions.
dosage_schedule: Oral: Adult 5-60 mg/day; children: 0.14-2 mg/kg/day in 3-4 divided doses. IV: 10-40 mg, 1-2 times weekly; IM: 100 mg, 1-2 times weekly.
precautions: Cushingoid side effects more likely with doses above 7.5 mg daily; should be protected from light.
adverse_effects: See under glucocorticoids general entry.
patient_info: Preferably taken in the morning after breakfast or food.

name: TRIAMCINOLONE ACETONIDE
indications: Inflammatory and allergic conditions.
dosage_schedule: By deep IM injection: 40 mg for depot effect, repeated at intervals according to response, maximum single dose 100 mg.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: See under glucocorticoids general entry.

name: INSULIN ASPART
indications: Diabetes mellitus.
dosage_schedule: By SC injection: immediately before meals or when necessary shortly after meals, according to requirements; By IV injection or infusion according to requirements.
precautions: Can be given during pregnancy and breastfeeding. Should be taken before meal or immediately after meal.
adverse_effects: Hypoglycaemia, localised allergic reactions, fat hypertrophy at injection sites.

name: INSULIN GLARGINE
indications: Diabetes mellitus.
dosage_schedule: By SC injections: start as 1/3rd of total daily insulin dose; use remaining 2/3 of daily dose on short-acting, premeal insulin. Usual initial dose: 0.2-0.4 units/kg.
precautions: Should be injected with evening meal. Optimal glucose lowering effect may take 5 days to fully manifest.
adverse_effects: Hypoglycaemia, localised allergic reactions, fat hypertrophy at injection sites.

name: INSULIN ISOPHANE (NPH)
indications: Diabetes mellitus.
dosage_schedule: By SC injection: according to patient’s requirements.
precautions: Intermediate duration of action.
adverse_effects: Hypoglycaemia, localised allergic reactions, fat hypertrophy at injection sites.

name: INSULIN LISPRO
indications: Diabetes mellitus.
dosage_schedule: SC injection: Start with 0.2-0.6 unit/kg/day in divided doses. Total maintenance daily requirement is usually between 0.5 and 1 unit/kg/day.
precautions: Recommended to start with lower dose to reduce risk of hypoglycemia.
adverse_effects: Hypoglycaemia, localised allergic reactions, fat hypertrophy at injection sites.

name: INSULIN PROTAMINE ZINC (PZI)
indications: Diabetes mellitus.
dosage_schedule: By SC injection: according to patient’s requirement as described under insulin glargine.
precautions: Long duration of action.
adverse_effects: Hypoglycaemia, localised allergic reactions, fat hypertrophy at injection sites.

name: INSULIN SOLUBLE
indications: Diabetic ketoacidosis, diabetes mellitus.
dosage_schedule: By SC, IM or IV injection: according to patient’s requirements.
precautions: Short duration with relatively rapid action.
adverse_effects: Hypoglycaemia, localised allergic reactions, fat hypertrophy at injection sites.

name: INSULIN ZINC SUSPENSION (LENTE)
indications: Diabetes mellitus.
dosage_schedule: By SC injection: according to patient’s requirements.
precautions: Intermediate (Lente) or Long (Ultralente) duration of action.
adverse_effects: Hypoglycaemia, localised allergic reactions, fat hypertrophy at injection sites.

name: ACARBOSE
indications: Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
dosage_schedule: Initially 50 mg/day, increased to 50 mg 3 times daily; then increased if necessary to 100 mg 3 times daily; maximum 200 mg 3 times daily.
contraindications: <18 years age, pregnancy, breast-feeding, hepatic impairment and severe renal impairment.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Abdominal pain, flatulence, diarrhoea, jaundice.
interactions: Used with caution with insulin and sulphonylureas (enhance hypoglycaemia).

name: METFORMIN
indications: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, gestational diabetes, polycystic ovarian syndrome.
dosage_schedule: Adult and child over 10 years: initially 500 mg with breakfast for at least 1 week, then 500 mg q12h with or after food for at least 1 week; maximum 2 g daily in divided doses.
contraindications: Renal impairment, hepatic impairment, recent MI, pregnancy, chronic alcoholics, ketoacidosis, general anaesthesia.
precautions: Suspend metformin on the morning of surgery and restart when baseline returns to normal.
adverse_effects: Anorexia, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, metallic taste, abdominal discomfort, vitamin B12 deficiency, hepatitis, and lactic acidosis (rare).

name: SITAGLIPTIN
indications: Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
dosage_schedule: Oral: 100 mg/day.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Hypoglycemia, acute pancreatitis, acute kidney injury, bundle branch block, exfoliative dermatitis, arthralgia.

name: LIRAGLUTIDE
indications: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, chronic weight management.
dosage_schedule: Chronic weight management: SC injection 0.6 mg once daily for one week, increase weekly to target 3 mg once daily. Type 2 DM: SC 0.6 mg daily for 1 week then 1.2 mg once daily, may increase up to 1.8 mg daily.
contraindications: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 (MEN-2), personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC), breastfeeding.
precautions: Delay dose escalation if not tolerated. Discontinue if 3 mg dose not tolerated for weight management.
adverse_effects: Hypoglycemia, tachycardia, headache, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, constipation.

name: REPAGLINIDE
indications: Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
dosage_schedule: Initially 500 µg within 30 minutes before main meals, adjusted according to response at intervals of 1-2 weeks.
contraindications: Ketoacidosis, pregnancy, breast-feeding, severe hepatic impairment.
precautions: Substitute by insulin during peri-operative period and during intercurrent illness (MI, coma, infection); child and adolescent under 18 years not recommended.
adverse_effects: Hypoglycaemia, diarrhoea, constipation, abdominal pain, nausea, pruritus, vasculitis.

name: CHLORPROPAMIDE
indications: Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
dosage_schedule: Initially 250 mg/day with breakfast or meal; maximum 500 mg daily.
contraindications: Ketoacidosis, diabetic coma, severe infection, severe kidney or liver impairment.
precautions: Safety during pregnancy and breast-feeding has not been established.
adverse_effects: Hypoglycaemia, nausea, vomiting, disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol, water intoxication (mental confusion, decreased sodium).

name: GLIBENCLAMIDE
indications: Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
dosage_schedule: Initially 5 mg/day (elderly 2.5 mg) with breakfast or meal; maximum 15 mg daily.
precautions: See under chlorpropamide.
adverse_effects: Hypoglycaemia, photosensitivity, hyponatremia, neonatal hypoglycaemia in first trimester use.
interactions: Signs of hypoglycaemia masked by beta-blockers. Flushing if taken with alcohol.

name: GLICLAZIDE
indications: Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
dosage_schedule: Initially 40-80 mg daily with breakfast or meal; maximum 320 mg daily.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: See under glibenclamide.

name: GLIMEPERIDE
indications: Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
dosage_schedule: Initially 1 mg daily, max up to 4 mg daily.
precautions: Comparatively safer than other sulphonylureas.
adverse_effects: Hyponatremia. Also see under glibenclamide.

name: GLIPIZIDE
indications: Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
dosage_schedule: Initially 2.5-5 mg daily before breakfast or meal; maximum 20 mg daily.
precautions: To be ingested 30 min before breakfast because food decreases its absorption.
adverse_effects: Dizziness, drowsiness, hyponatremia, hepatic/renal impairment.

name: PIOGLITAZONE
indications: Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
dosage_schedule: Initially 15-30 mg/day, increased to 45 mg/day according to response.
contraindications: Ketoacidosis, pregnancy, breast-feeding, hepatic impairment, cardiac failure, bladder cancer, uninvestigated macroscopic hematuria.
precautions: Substitute insulin during peri-operative period; ask patient to immediately report hematuria.
adverse_effects: Anemia, peripheral edema, weight gain, impotence, risk of bladder cancer.

name: GLUCAGON
indications: Acute hypoglycaemia, insulin induced hypoglycemia, beta-blocker poisoning.
dosage_schedule: SC, IM, or IV injection: adult/child over 8 years 1 mg. If no response after 15 minutes, IV glucose should be given.
precautions: Should be used immediately after preparation; discard if it shows gel formation.
adverse_effects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, hypotension, hypokalaemia.

name: LEVOTHYROXINE (L-THYROXINE)
indications: Cretinism, adult hypothyroidism, myxoedema coma, non-toxic goitre, thyroid carcinoma after surgery.
dosage_schedule: Initially 50-100 µg/day (before morning meal); Neonate (up to 1 month): 5-10 µg/kg/day; Child (>1 month): initially 5 µg/kg adjusted in steps of 25 µg.
contraindications: Angina pectoris and other cardiovascular disorders, diabetes mellitus, hypertension.
precautions: Protect from light. Pregnancy/breast-feeding.
adverse_effects: Palpitation, tachycardia, diarrhoea, cardiac arrhythmias, tremor, weight loss, sweating, insomnia, increased appetite.

name: CARBIMAZOLE
indications: Hyperthyroidism,控制 Grave’s disease and toxic nodular goitre, pre-operatively, thyroid storm.
dosage_schedule: 15-40 mg daily until euthyroid (4-8 weeks), then maintenance 5-15 mg for 12-18 months.
precautions: Pregnancy, breastfeeding.
adverse_effects: Hepatitis, SLE like syndrome, agranulocytosis (serious but reversible), hypothyroidism, skin rashes, loss of hair/taste.

name: IODINE
indications: Prevention and treatment of iodine deficiency.
dosage_schedule: Iodine deficiency (IM): infant 190 mg; child/adult 380 mg; (Oral): infant <1 year 100 mg; child (1-5 years) 200 mg yearly; adult/child (>6 years) 400 mg yearly; pregnancy 200 mg single dose.
precautions: Breast-feeding.
adverse_effects: Hypothyroidism, goitre, hypersensitivity, mucous membrane inflammation.

name: LUGOL’S IODINE
indications: Thyrotoxicosis (pre-operative).
dosage_schedule: 0.1-0.3 ml 3 times daily well diluted with water or milk.
precautions: Keep in closed container resistant to iodine.
adverse_effects: Angioedema, fever, arthralgia, metallic taste, salivary gland swelling.

name: PROPYLTHIOURACIL
indications: Hyperthyroidism (See under carbimazole).
dosage_schedule: 200-400 mg daily until euthyroid, then maintenance 50 to 150 mg daily.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Thrombocytopenia, aplastic anaemia, hypoprothrombinaemia and bleeding.

name: OCTREOTIDE
indications: Acromegaly, carcinoid tumor, VIPoma, esophageal variceal bleeding.
dosage_schedule: Acromegaly: 50 µg SC q8-12h, titrate up to 500 µg; maintenance: 20 mg IM every 4 weeks. Variceal bleeding: 50 µg IV bolus, then 25-50 µg/hr for 1-5 days.
contraindications: Inhibition of gallbladder contractility, gallstone formation.
precautions: Caution in renal/hepatic impairment. Pregnancy Category B.
adverse_effects: Gallstones, cholecystitis, cholestatic hepatitis, dysglycemia, bradycardia.

name: SOMATROPIN
indications: Pituitary dwarfism, Turner’s syndrome, renal failure, adult GH deficiency, AIDS related wasting.
dosage_schedule: Pituitary dwarfism: 0.03-0.06 mg/kg daily in the evening. Adult GH deficiency: 150-300 µg/day SC adjusted accordingly.
precautions: May increase intracranial tension.
adverse_effects: Pain at injection site, lipodystrophy, glucose intolerance, hand stiffness, salt/water retention.

name: CALCITONIN
indications: Postmenopausal osteoporosis (greater than 5 years post menopause).
dosage_schedule: Nasal spray: 1 spray per day intranasally, alternating nostrils daily.
precautions: Known hypersensitivity, hypocalcaemia, nasal changes, malignancy.
adverse_effects: Facial/peripheral edema, hypertension, syncope, chest pain, loss of taste/smell, rhinitis, epistaxis.

name: SODIUM ALDRONATE
indications: Prevention and treatment of post-menopausal osteoporosis, osteoporosis in men, corticosteroid-induced osteoporosis.
dosage_schedule: Prevention: 5 mg daily; Treatment: 10 mg daily or 70 mg once weekly.
contraindications: Pregnancy, breast-feeding, stricture or achalasia of oesophagus.
precautions: Caution in history of ulcers, GI bleeding, renal impairment.
adverse_effects: Oesophageal ulcers/stricture, dyspepsia, melaena, severe skin reactions (SJS).
interactions: NSAID, prednisolone, calcium, iron, antacids, tea, coffee, fruit juice.
patient_info: Take in empty stomach in morning and do not lie down for 30 min.

name: TERIPARATIDE
indications: Severe osteoporosis with fractures.
dosage_schedule: 20 µg SC daily into thigh or abdominal wall.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Arthralgia, rhinitis, nausea, dizziness, leg cramps.

name: ORLISTAT
indications: Obesity management (BMI >30 kg/m2 or >27 kg/m2 with risk factors).
dosage_schedule: 120 mg 3 times daily with each main meal containing fat (up to 1 hour after meal).
contraindications: Pregnancy, chronic malabsorption, cholestasis, renal impairment.
precautions: Fat soluble vitamin supplementation >=2hrs before/after orlistat.
adverse_effects: Oily rectal leakage, steatorrhea, frequent bowel movements, infectious diarrhoea, cholelithiasis, acute renal failure, calcium oxalate nephrolithiasis.
patient_info: Avoid high fat diet; distribute fat intake over 3 main meals.

name: MESTEROLONE
indications: Androgen deficiency, male infertility associated with hypogonadism.
dosage_schedule: Orally, 25 mg 3-4 times daily for several months; maintenance 50-75 mg daily in divided doses.
contraindications: Breast cancer in men, prostate cancer, pregnancy, breastfeeding, hypercalcaemia, history of primary liver tumours.
precautions: Ischaemic heart disease, hypertension, elderly, diabetes, pre-pubertal boys.
adverse_effects: Prostate abnormalities, gynaecomastia, increased bone growth, male-pattern baldness, weight gain.
patient_info: Swallow tablet whole. Do not take double dose if missed.

name: METHYL-TESTOSTERONE
indications: Hypogonadism, breast cancer.
dosage_schedule: Hypogonadism: orally 10-50 mg per day. Breast cancer: 50 mg one to four times a day.
contraindications: Carcinoma of prostate, male breast, liver/kidney disease, pregnancy.
precautions: See under testosterone.
adverse_effects: Jaundice, frequent erection, changes in menstrual periods.

name: TESTOSTERONE
indications: Hypogonadism, breast cancer in females.
dosage_schedule: Hypogonadism: IM Propionate 50 mg 2-3 times weekly; Enanthate 250 mg every 2-3 weeks. Breast cancer: IM Propionate 100 mg 2-3 times weekly; Enanthate 250 mg every 2-3 weeks.
contraindications: Males with carcinoma of breast or prostate, pregnancy, breastfeeding.
precautions: Renal/hepatic impairment, ischaemic heart disease, diabetes; extreme caution in children.
adverse_effects: Virilization, excessive body hair, menstrual irregularity, changes in libido, gynaecomastia, premature closure of epiphyses.
patient_info: Report priapism, gynaecomastia, or virilism promptly.

name: NANDROLONE
indications: Aplastic anaemia, antineoplastic.
dosage_schedule: Deep IM injection: 50 mg every 3 weeks.
precautions: Cardiac, hepatic, renal impairment. Possible premature closure of epiphysis.
adverse_effects: Virilism, oedema, acne, amenorrhoea, inhibition of spermatogenesis, liver tumour.
patient_info: Administer IM only. Protect from light.

name: OXYMETHOLONE
indications: Aplastic anaemia.
dosage_schedule: 1-5 mg/kg daily in divided doses; child 0.175 mg/kg daily as a single dose.
precautions: Protect from sunlight.
adverse_effects: See under nandrolone.

name: STANOZOLOL
indications: Hereditary angioedema.
dosage_schedule: Initially 2-4 mg daily orally.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: See under nandrolone.

name: BICALUTAMIDE
indications: Prostate cancer (advanced/high-risk).
dosage_schedule: 50 mg daily.
precautions: Monitor serum PSA levels. Impaired glucose tolerance.
adverse_effects: Pruritus, asthenia, alopecia, dry skin, hypersensitivity reaction (angioedema).
patient_info: Take at same time each day.

name: DANAZOL
indications: Endometriosis, palliative treatment of fibrocystic breast disease, menorrhagia, gynaecomastia.
dosage_schedule: Endometriosis: initially 400 mg daily (up to 4 divided doses). Menorrhagia: 200 mg daily for 3 months. Gynaecomastia: 400 mg daily for 6 months.
contraindications: Abnormal genital bleeding, pregnancy, renal/cardiac dysfunction.
precautions: Unsuitable for those desiring conception. Start during menstruation.
adverse_effects: Hirsutism, decreased breast size, weight gain, oedema, cholestatic jaundice.
patient_info: Use non-hormonal contraception.

name: FINASTERIDE
indications: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), male-pattern baldness.
dosage_schedule: BPH: 5 mg daily. Baldness: 1 mg daily.
precautions: Review BPH treatment after 6 months.
adverse_effects: Impotence, decreased libido, breast tenderness/enlargement, decrease volume of ejaculate.
patient_info: Take as directed even if symptoms improve.

name: CONJUGATED ESTROGEN
indications: Menopausal symptoms.
contraindications: See under ethinyl estradiol; also breast cancer and thromboembolism.
precautions: Risk of endometrial cancer if used long-term without progesterone.
adverse_effects: See under ethinyl estradiol.

name: ESTRADIOL
indications: Menopausal symptoms.
dosage_schedule: 1-2 mg daily.
precautions: Assess BP before and periodically during therapy.
adverse_effects: See under ethinyl estradiol.

name: ETHINYL ESTRADIOL
indications: Female hypogonadism, post-menopausal HRT, primary ovarian failure, contraception, dysmenorrhea, prostate/breast cancer.
dosage_schedule: Estrogen deficiency: 10-50 µg daily for 21 days, repeated after 7 days tablet free. Prostate cancer: 0.15 to 1.5 mg daily.
contraindications: Estrogen dependent neoplasm, undiagnosed vaginal bleeding, thromboembolic disorder, liver disease, pregnancy, heavy smokers.
precautions: Obesity (BMI >= 30), family history of breast cancer, cardiovascular disease.
adverse_effects: Nausea, bloating, breast tenderness, ankle swelling, spotting, thromboembolic disorder.
interactions: Endometrial/breast cancer risk reduced when combined with progesterone.
patient_info: Report signs of fluid retention or thromboembolism. Stop if pregnancy suspected.

name: CHORIONIC GONADOTROPHIN (HCG)
indications: Treatment of infertility in women.
dosage_schedule: 5000-10000 units IM injection once 1 day following the last dose of menotropins.
precautions: Cardiac/renal impairment, epilepsy, asthma, migraine.
adverse_effects: Headache, multiple pregnancy, gynaecomastia.
patient_info: Report signs of ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (pelvic pain, dyspnoea).

name: CLOMIPHENE
indications: Anovulatory infertility in females.
dosage_schedule: 50 mg daily for 5 days, starting within 5 days of onset of menstruation.
contraindications: Ovarian cysts, liver disease, pregnancy, uterine fibroids, ectopic pregnancy.
precautions: May cause visual disturbances.
adverse_effects: Ovarian enlargement, hot flushes, blurred vision, abdominal discomfort, weight gain.
patient_info: Attempt intercourse every other day starting 48hr prior to ovulation.

name: DYDROGESTERONE
indications: Endometriosis, dysfunctional uterine bleeding, dysmenorrhoea, amenorrhoea, HRT.
dosage_schedule: Endometriosis: 10 mg 2-3 times daily (cycle days 5-25). DUB: 10 mg BID for 5-7 days to arrest; 10 mg BID (days 11-25) to prevent.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: See under norethisterone.

name: HYDROXYPROGESTERONE
indications: Secondary amenorrhoea, dysfunctional uterine bleeding, induction of menses.
dosage_schedule: Amenorrhoea/DUB: IM 375 mg. Induction: IM 125-250 mg on day 10 of cycle.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: See under norethisterone.
patient_info: Administer IM only. Protect from light.

name: MEDROXYPROGESTERONE
indications: Contraceptive, secondary amenorrhoea, DUB, endometriosis.
dosage_schedule: Contraception: Deep IM 150 mg within first 5 days of cycle, repeated every 3 months. Endometriosis: 10 mg TID for 90 days.
precautions: Delay until 6 weeks after parturition if breast-feeding.
adverse_effects: See under norethisterone.
patient_info: Take at same time each day.

name: NORETHISTERONE
indications: DUB, contraception, endometriosis, PMS, postponement of menstruation.
dosage_schedule: Endometriosis: 10-15 mg daily starting 5th day of cycle. Postponement: 5 mg TID starting 3 days before anticipated onset.
contraindications: Pregnancy, breast/genital cancer, conditions aggravated by fluid retention, liver function impairment.
precautions: Protect from light.
adverse_effects: Virilising effects, liver disturbances, jaundice, weight gain, breast discomfort.

name: COMBINED ORAL CONTRACEPTIVE PILLS (OCPS)
indications: Temporary contraception.
dosage_schedule: One tablet daily starting within 0-5 day of menstruation.
contraindications: <6 weeks postpartum, smoker >35, hypertension (>160/100), history of thromboembolism, ischemic heart disease, breast cancer, diabetes with complications.
precautions: Smoker >35 (<15 cigs/day), controlled hypertension, migraine >35, gallbladder disease, mild cirrhosis.
adverse_effects: Spotting, nausea, breast tenderness, headache, increased risk of stroke/gallbladder disease/cervical cancer (>5yr use).
patient_info: Missed pill: Single missed = take as soon as remembered; continue dose. >2 missed = use additional barrier method and begin new cycle.

name: LEVONORGESTREL
indications: Emergency contraceptive.
dosage_schedule: 1.5 g as a single dose as soon as possible after sex (preferably within 12 hours but not later than 72 hours).
precautions: Less effective than IUD insertion.
adverse_effects: Nausea, low abdominal pain, dizziness, menstrual irregularities.
patient_info: Report severe abdomen pain (investigate ectopic pregnancy).

name: ERGOT ALKALOIDS (ERGOMETRINE, METHYL ERGOMETRINE)
indications: Postpartum haemorrhage, post abortion haemorrhage.
dosage_schedule: IM or IV: 0.2 mg (Methyl ergometrine) or 0.25 mg (Ergometrine), can repeat every 15 min; max 5 doses.
contraindications: Induction of labour, cardiac disease, eclampsia, multiple pregnancy, Rh-negative mother.
precautions: Given only after foetal delivery; may decrease milk secretion.
adverse_effects: Nausea, vomiting, rise in BP, gangrene of toes, bowel infarction (high dose).
patient_info: Requires cold chain (2-8 C). Protect from sunlight.

name: MIFEPRISTONE
indications: Medical termination of intra-uterine pregnancy up to 63 days gestation.
dosage_schedule: Oral: 200 mg single dose, followed 24-48 hours later by misoprostol 800 μg.
contraindications: Suspected ectopic pregnancy, uncontrolled severe asthma.
precautions: Caution in renal/hepatic impairment, age over 35.
adverse_effects: Vaginal bleeding, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, headache.
patient_info: If treatment fails, pregnancy must be terminated surgically.

name: OXYTOCIN
indications: Induction of labour, augmentation of labour, management of 3rd stage, postpartum haemorrhage.
dosage_schedule: Induction: 2.5 units in 500ml Dextrose/NS at 10 drops/min. Increase by 10 drops every 30 min (max 60 drops/min). Post-partum: IM 10 IU; IV infusion 20 units in 1L at 40 drops/min.
contraindications: Cephalo-pelvic disproportion, malpresentation, placenta previa, obstructed labour, foetal distress.
precautions: Uterine hypertonia. Avoid IV bolus injection. Use only if cervix has ripened.
adverse_effects: Uterine hyperstimulation, foetal asphyxia, uterine rupture, water intoxication.
patient_info: Expect contractions similar to menstrual cramps.

name: MISOPROSTOL
indications: Termination of pregnancy, induction of labour, active management of 3rd stage, postpartum haemorrhage.
dosage_schedule: Induction: 25-50 μg every 4-6 hours (max 200 μg). 3rd stage: 600 μg oral (if no injectable access).
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, previous uterine scar, bronchial asthma, active cardiac/renal disease.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Nausea, fall in blood pressure, tachycardia, uterine cramps, fever, rigor.

name: NIFEDIPINE
indications: Inhibit uncomplicated premature labour (24-33 weeks gestation).
dosage_schedule: Sublingual (IR): 10 mg every 15 min (max 40 mg in 1st hour), then oral (SR) 60-160 mg daily in 3-4 divided doses.
contraindications: Within 1 month of MI, cardiogenic shock, acute angina, breast feeding.
precautions: Sublingual route is not practiced now.
adverse_effects: Tachycardia, flushing, headache, oedema, tremor.
patient_info: Monitor pulse; contact professional if heart rate <50 bpm. Change position slowly.

name: ISOXSUPRINE
indications: Premature labour.
dosage_schedule: IV infusion: 200-300 μg/minute until control. Prophylaxis: oral 40-80 mg daily.
contraindications: Recent arterial haemorrhage, premature detachment of placenta, severe anaemia.
precautions: Monitor BP, pulse.
adverse_effects: Flushing, hypotension, foetal tachycardia, maternal pulmonary oedema.

name: SALBUTAMOL
indications: Arrest uncomplicated premature labour (24-33 weeks gestation).
dosage_schedule: IV infusion: 10 μg/min, increase at 10-min intervals until contractions cease (max 45 μg/min). Maintain for 1 hour, then reduce by 50% every 6 hours; then oral 4 mg q6-8h.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: See general salbutamol entry.

name: TERBUTALINE
indications: Premature labour.
dosage_schedule: IV infusion: 10 to 25 μg/min (max 80 μg/min). Then 2.5 to 7.5 mg orally every 6 hours until 36-37 weeks gestation.
contraindications: Renal/liver diseases, diabetes, hyperthyroidism, hypertension, myocardial insufficiency.
precautions: Caution in lactation.
adverse_effects: Chest pain, arrhythmia, allergic reactions, headache, tremor.
patient_info: Notify professional if labor resumes.

name: ALUMINIUM PHOSPHIDE POISONING
clues_symptoms: Severe pulmonary irritation, pulmonary edema, hepatic and myocardial injury, breathlessness, cyanosis.
risk_assessment: Phosphine gas is released from tablets in the presence of atmospheric moisture; can be fatal up to 36 hours after exposure.
management_protocol: Supportive management; Oxygen for pulmonary edema; Assisted ventilation in serious cases; Patients must be kept under observation.

name: ASPIRIN (SALICYLATE) POISONING
clues_symptoms: Salicylism with tachypnoea, tinnitus, vomiting, metabolic acidosis, altered mental state, seizures.
risk_assessment: <150 mg/kg: Minimal symptoms; 150-300 mg/kg: Mild to moderate; 300-500 mg/kg: Severe intoxication; >500 mg/kg: Potentially lethal.
management_protocol: Resuscitation (ventilation, seizure control); Fluid and electrolyte balance; Decontamination: Activated charcoal in repeated doses (50 g 4 hourly) for overdose >150 mg/kg; Intravenous sodium bicarbonate (optimum urinary pH 7.5 to 8.5); Hemodialysis for severe cases.
investigations: 12-lead ECG, Serum electrolytes, blood glucose level, Arterial blood gas analysis (metabolic acidosis).

name: ATROPINE AND BELLADONNA POISONING
clues_symptoms: Antimuscarinic features: Dry and flushed skin, dry mucous membrane, dilated pupils, hyperthermia, tachycardia, decreased bowel sounds, ileus, urinary retention, drowsiness, stupor, convulsions, coma.
risk_assessment: Dose of 10 mg or more causes excitement, hallucinations, delirium, and coma; in children 10 mg or less may be fatal.
management_protocol: Resuscitation and symptomatic support; Antidote administration.
antidote_dosage: Adult dose 2 mg I.M. or I.V. or S.C., followed by 1 mg every 20 to 30 minutes until desired effect is obtained (up to 4 mg total). Effect lasts less than an hour, so dose should be repeated.

name: BARBITURATE POISONING
clues_symptoms: CNS depression, toxic neurological symptoms, profound coma.
risk_assessment: Ingestion of >8 mg/kg produces toxic neurological symptoms; multiples of this dose produce profound coma. CNS depression correlates with serum levels: >80-100 mg/L suggests coma requiring intubation.
management_protocol: Resuscitation (intratracheal tube if in coma); Monitor blood gases and electrolytes; Gastric lavage; Multiple dose activated charcoal (MDAC); Hemodialysis for severe cases.
investigations: Screening 12-lead ECG, blood glucose level, Serum barbiturate levels.

name: BENZODIAZEPINE POISONING
clues_symptoms: Mild sedation; risk increases significantly if co-ingested with other CNS depressants (alcohol, opioids).
risk_assessment: Benzodiazepines have a large therapeutic index; isolated overdose usually only causes mild sedation.
management_protocol: Supportive treatment; Resuscitation; Activated charcoal is usually not indicated; Specific antidote administration if not contraindicated.
antidote_dosage: Initial dose of 0.1-0.2 mg IV, repeat every minute until reversal of sedation, maximum 2 mg. Resedation occurs at ~90 minutes; repeat if required. (Contraindicated in seizure disorders, pro-convulsant co-ingestion, or QRS prolongation).

name: CARBAMATE POISONING
clues_symptoms: Symptoms closely resemble organophosphates (DUMBBELS: Diarrhoea, Urination, Miosis, Bronchorrhea, Bronchospasm, Emesis, Lacrimation, Salivation).
risk_assessment: Reversible acetylcholinesterase inhibitors used as insecticides (e.g., Baygon, aldicarb).
management_protocol: Skin decontamination (wash with warm water and soap); Gastric lavage if within the past hour.
antidote_dosage: Refer to ORGANOPHOSPHORUS INSECTICIDE protocol (Note: Pralidoxime is not recommended for Carbamate).

name: CARBON MONOXIDE POISONING
clues_symptoms: Neurological complications; risk of long-term neuropsychological sequelae.
risk_assessment: High concentration CO for short duration: low risk; Lower concentration CO for longer duration: high risk of sequelae.
management_protocol: Immediate treatment; Remove from exposure; Administer high-flow 100% oxygen; Correct acidosis and maintain BP; Cerebral edema in severe cases may require IV mannitol.
investigations: Screening 12-lead ECG, blood glucose, Carboxyhemoglobin levels, Arterial blood gas, serum lactate, Cranial CT or MRI.

name: CHLORINATED HYDROCARBON INSECTICIDES POISONING
clues_symptoms: CNS depression, cardiac dysrhythmias, hepatic or renal damage, chemical pneumonitis (if aspirated).
risk_assessment: Includes DDT, BHC, chlordane, aldrin, dieldrin.
management_protocol: Decontamination (remove clothing, wash skin); GI decontamination contraindicated; Activated charcoal has no role; Avoid milk and oils (facilitate absorption); Diazepam IV for convulsions.

name: CORROSIVES (ACIDS AND ALKALIS)
clues_symptoms: Visible burns in mouth/throat, respiratory distress.
risk_assessment: Includes Hydrochloric, Sulfuric, Nitric acid and Ammonia, Caustic soda.
management_protocol: Prehospital: dilution with water or milk; Emesis and gastric lavage are contraindicated; Maintain airway; Analgesics (pethidine); Corticosteroids and prophylactic antibiotics suggested; Oesophagoscopy within 24h; Endoscopically guided dilation if strictures develop.

name: ETHYLENE GLYCOL POISONING
clues_symptoms: Initial (1-2 hrs): Euphoria, nystagmus, vomiting; Subsequent (4-12 hrs): Dyspnea, tachycardia, hypertension, progressing to coma and death. Flank pain/oliguria suggests renal failure.
management_protocol: Resuscitation; Correct metabolic acidosis with IV bicarbonate (Bolus 1-2 mmol/kg); IV benzodiazepines for seizures; Hemodialysis is definitive; Administer Thiamine and Pyridoxine.
antidote_dosage: Ethanol (Oral/NG): Load 1.8 ml/kg of 43% ethanol, Maintain 0.2-0.4 mL/kg/hour. Ethanol (IV): Load 8 mL/kg of 10% ethanol, Maintain 1-2 mL/kg/hour. Fomepizole: Load 15 mg/kg IV over 30 mins, then 10 mg/kg every 12 hrs for 48 hrs.
investigations: Serum electrolytes, urea, creatinine, lactate, osmolality, ABG (Anion gap acidosis).

name: INSECT STINGS (ANTS, BEES, WASPS)
clues_symptoms: Local pain and swelling; seldom cause severe systemic toxicity unless anaphylactic.
management_protocol: Clean area with antiseptics; Remove stings immediately; Topical corticosteroids or oral antihistaminics; Anaphylactic reactions require adrenaline.

name: KEROSENE POISONING
risk_assessment: Aspiration risk is the primary concern.
management_protocol: Gastric lavage is contraindicated; Treatment is supportive; Furosemide (25-100 mg IV) for pulmonary edema; Ventilatory support; Antibiotics for aspiration pneumonia.

name: METHANOL POISONING
clues_symptoms: Initially (1hr): Nausea, vomiting, CNS depression. Latent (12-24 hrs): headache, dizziness, blurred vision, photophobia. Severe: tachypnoea, progressive blindness, papilloedema, coma. Extrapyramidal movement disorders in survivors.
risk_assessment: Ingestion of >0.5 ml/kg is potentially lethal; >0.25 ml/kg is toxic.
management_protocol: Similar to Ethylene Glycol management; Bicarbonate in 50 mmol aliquots if pH <7.30; Dialysis recommended if >30 ml pure methanol ingested.
antidote_dosage: Same as for Ethylene Glycol poisoning.

name: MORPHINE AND OTHER OPIOIDS POISONING
clues_symptoms: Classical triad: CNS depression, respiratory depression, and miosis (pinpoint pupils).
risk_assessment: Toxicity occurs just above analgesic dose. High risk in opioid-naive patients or co-ingestion with CNS depressants. Dextropropoxyphene >20mg/kg causes cardiac dysrhythmias. Tramadol >500mg causes seizures.
management_protocol: Resuscitation; Monitor respiratory rate, GCS, and oxygen saturation; IV bolus sodium bicarbonate for dysrhythmias in dextropropoxyphene intoxication.
antidote_dosage: Initial bolus 100 mcg IV (or 400 mcg IM/SC). Repeated doses of 100 mcg IV every 30-60 seconds until respiration re-established. Infusion rate at 2/3rd of the initial dose required per hour.

name: MUSHROOM POISONING
clues_symptoms: Early GI (<2 hrs): Abdominal pain, vomiting, diarrhea. Delayed GI (5-12 hrs): intractable vomiting, watery diarrhea, hypoglycemia, hepatotoxicity. Neurological: Hallucinations, loss of co-ordination, seizures.
risk_assessment: Delayed symptoms (5-12 hours) are associated with higher risk of fulminant hepatic failure and death.
management_protocol: Adequate fluid and electrolyte replacement; Antiemetics (promethazine); GL or AC if presents early; Continuous glucose monitoring; Monitor liver function; IV benzodiazepines for seizures.
investigations: Liver function tests, Blood glucose levels.

name: ORGANOPHOSPHORUS INSECTICIDE POISONING
clues_symptoms: Muscarinic (DUMBBELS): Diarrhoea, Urination, Miosis, Bronchorrhea, Bronchospasm, Emesis, Lacrimation, Salivation; Bradycardia. Nicotinic: Fasciculation, tremor, respiratory muscle paralysis. CNS: Agitation, coma, seizures.
risk_assessment: Manifestations may be delayed up to 12 hours. Risk of Intermediate Syndrome (delayed paralysis 2-4 days) or OPIDN (1-5 weeks post-exposure).
management_protocol: Resuscitation and support; Skin decontamination; Activated charcoal usually not beneficial.
antidote_dosage: Atropine: 1.8 mg IV, double dose every 5 minutes until atropnization (dry armpit, dilated pupil, clear chest). Maintenance: 10-20% of required dose per hour. Pralidoxime: Initial 2 g in 100 ml NS IV over 20 mins; followed by infusion 0.5 g/hour (6 g in 500 ml NS) for at least 24 hours.
investigations: Red cell and plasma cholinesterase levels.

name: PARACETAMOL POISONING
clues_symptoms: Initially asymptomatic or mild GI distress; latent period followed by hepatic necrosis.
risk_assessment: Single dose 7.5 g (adult) or 150 mg/kg (child) can cause severe necrosis. Predict risk via Rumack-Matthew nomogram (Serum level >200 mg/L at 4h or >25 mg/L at 16h).
management_protocol: Resuscitation; Activated charcoal within 1st hour of overdose.
antidote_dosage: IV 150 mg/kg in 200 ml D5 over 15 mins; then 50 mg/kg in 500 ml D5 over 4 hours; then 100 mg/kg in 1 liter D5 over 16 hours.
investigations: Serum paracetamol (not before 4h), Hepatic transaminases (>1000 IU/L), Coagulation studies, Renal function, Urinalysis.

name: TRICYCLIC ANTIDEPRESSANT POISONING
clues_symptoms: CNS: Sedation, delirium, seizures. CVS: Sinus tachycardia, hypotension, broad complex tachyarrhythmias/bradycardia. Anticholinergic: Agitation, mydriasis, urinary retention, dry/flushed skin.
risk_assessment: Ingestion >10 mg/kg life-threatening; symptoms appear within 2h. Toxicity: <5 mg/kg minimal; 10-30 mg/kg major effects; >30 mg/kg severe/lethal.
management_protocol: Continuous cardiac monitoring for 6h; Ventilator support for CNS depression; AC if >10 mg/kg; Sodium bicarbonate 100 mEq (2 mEq/kg) IV repeated q1-2 min for dysrhythmias (target pH 7.50-7.55); Lignocaine (1.5 mg/kg) second-line; IV benzodiazepines for seizures. Avoid type 1a antiarrhythmics, amiodarone, beta-blockers.
antidote_dosage: 100 mEq (2 mEq/kg) IV, repeated every 1-2 minutes until restoration of normal rhythm.
investigations: Serial ECGs (Monitoring for PR/QRS prolongation, QRS >100ms predicts seizures, >160ms predicts VT).

name: ZINC PHOSPHIDE POISONING
clues_symptoms: Typical garlic odor, severe gastro-intestinal irritations, coughing, hepatic necrosis.
risk_assessment: Common rodenticide; reacts with stomach acid to produce phosphine gas.
management_protocol: Supportive management; Decontamination may help; Patients must be kept under observation.

name: ACTINOMYCIN D (DACTINOMYCIN)
indications: Cytotoxic drug: Wilm’s tumor, trophoblastic neoplasms, testicular cancer.
dosage_schedule: Wilm’s tumor/Ewing sarcoma: 15 mcg/kg I.V. once a day for five days.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, active chickenpox or herpes zoster.
precautions: VESICANT: Administer slowly by IV push to avoid extravasation. Caution in hepatic/renal impairment. Toxic effects may take 1-2 weeks to reach maximum severity; discontinue if severe diarrhoea, myelosuppression, or stomatitis occur. Avoid use within 2 weeks of radiation. Avoid live virus vaccines.
adverse_effects: Pancytopenia, thrombocytopenia, myelosuppression, stomatitis, hypocalcaemia, hepatotoxicity, anaphylaxis, hyperpigmentation of radiated areas.
interactions: Increased risk of hepatotoxicity when used within 2 weeks of radiation treatment for right-sided tumors.
patient_info: Avoid inhalation of vapours or contact with skin, mucous membranes, or eyes. Report severe diarrhea or mouth sores immediately.

name: ARSENIC TRIOXIDE
indications: Cytotoxic drug: Refractory or relapsed acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL).
dosage_schedule: Induction cycle: 0.15 mg/kg IV qDay until bone marrow remission (max 60 days) in combination with Oral Tretinoin 22.5 mg/m² twice daily. Consolidation cycle: 0.15 mg/kg IV daily on Days 1-5 of Weeks 1-4 of an 8-week cycle for 4 cycles.
precautions: Prolongs QTc interval; risk of APL differentiation syndrome and hyperleukocytosis. Monitor ECG, RFT, electrolytes, and weight regularly. Human carcinogen; monitor for second primary malignancies.
adverse_effects: Prolonged QTc interval, APL differentiation syndrome, tachycardia, hyperglycemia, hypomagnesemia, hypokalemia, weight gain, hypoxia.
interactions: Maintain potassium > 4 mEq/L and magnesium > 1.8 mg/dL to avoid cardiac conduction abnormalities.
patient_info: Report unusual fever, shortness of breath, or weight gain immediately. Effective contraception is mandatory.

name: AZATHIOPRINE
indications: Cytotoxic drug: Refractory rheumatoid arthritis, renal transplants to prevent graft rejection.
dosage_schedule: Rheumatoid arthritis: 1 mg/kg/day IV/PO initially; after 6-8 weeks, increase by 0.5 mg/kg/day every 4 weeks (max 2.5 mg/kg/day). Maintenance: Reduce daily dose by 0.5 mg/kg every 4 weeks until lowest effective dose reached.
precautions: Monitor CBC frequently; discontinue if leukocytes <3000/mm³ or platelets <100,000/mm³. Discontinue if signs of hepatotoxicity (dark urine, jaundice) occur. Avoid live vaccines.
adverse_effects: Dose-related myelosuppression, liver impairment, cholestatic jaundice, interstitial nephritis, hair loss, nausea, pancreatitis.
interactions: Increased leukopenia with ACE inhibitors and sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim. Increased myelosuppression with cyclosporine and mercaptopurine.
patient_info: Report unexplained bruising, bleeding, or fever. Avoid crowds and people with infections. Use a soft-bristled toothbrush. Take with food.

name: CALCIUM FOLINATE (CALCIUM LEUCOVORIN)
indications: Cytotoxic support: Prevention of methotrexate-induced adverse effects, suspected methotrexate overdosage.
dosage_schedule: Prevention: 15 mg IM/IV every 6 hours for 24 hours, usually starting 12–24 hours after start of methotrexate infusion. Overdosage: Initial dose equal to or exceeding dose of methotrexate at max rate of 160 mg/minute.
precautions: Use caution in pernicious anaemia or other B12 deficiency megaloblastic anemias.
adverse_effects: Agitation, depression, pyrexia (after parenteral use).
interactions: Avoid concurrent use with methotrexate unless following specific rescue protocols.
patient_info: N/A

name: CAPECITABINE
indications: Cytotoxic drug: Colorectal cancer, breast cancer.
dosage_schedule: 1250 mg/m² twice daily for 2 weeks followed by a 1-week rest period (q21 days).
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to capecitabine or 5-FU, DPD deficiency, severe renal impairment.
precautions: Stop drug in case of grade 2-4 hyperbilirubinemia. Monitor for hand-foot syndrome.
adverse_effects: Diarrhea, hand-foot skin reaction, liver dysfunction, vomiting.
interactions: Increases bleeding risk with anticoagulants, NSAIDS, salicylates, and thrombolytics. Aluminium/Magnesium laxatives may affect absorption.
patient_info: Take with a glass of water within 30 minutes after a meal. Avoid foods with citric acid or rough textures if stomatitis is present. Notify prescriber if pregnancy is planned.

name: CARBOPLATIN
indications: Cytotoxic drug: Advanced ovarian cancer, germ cell tumours, small and non-small cell lung cancers, bladder cancer, endometrial cancer.
dosage_schedule: Single agent: 360 mg/m² IV every 4 weeks. Combination: 300 mg/m² IV (with cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² IV) every 4 weeks.
precautions: Must be administered in a specialized care setting. Renal and hepatic studies required monthly. When using with paclitaxel, carboplatin should be given AFTER paclitaxel. Risk of hypersensitivity increases with number of cycles.
adverse_effects: Significant and dose-limiting myelosuppression (thrombocytopenia), renal toxicity, peripheral neuropathy, mild elevation of liver enzymes.
interactions: Increases nephrotoxicity or ototoxicity with aminoglycosides and amphotericin B. Bleeding risk with aspirin, NSAIDS, and anticoagulants.
patient_info: Report ringing/roaring in the ears, numbness, or tingling in extremities. Do not breastfeed. Avoid aspirin and live vaccinations.

name: CHLORAMBUCIL
indications: Cytotoxic drug: Waldenstrom macroglobulinaemia, chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), non-Hodgkin lymphomas, Hodgkin disease.
dosage_schedule: CLL: 0.1 mg/kg/day for 3-6 weeks OR 0.4 mg/kg biweekly or monthly OR 0.03-0.1 mg/kg/day continuously.
contraindications: Pregnancy, gout, radiation or cytotoxic therapy within 1 month, severe renal/hepatic impairment.
precautions: Reduce initial dose if given within 4 weeks of radiation or if bone marrow is diseased. Not to exceed 0.1 mg/kg/day if bone marrow is infiltrated with lymphocytes.
adverse_effects: Bone marrow suppression, rashes, Steven-Johnson syndrome, hyperuricemia, GI upset.
interactions: Interaction with nalidixic acid. Avoid concomitant use with allopurinol or colchicines.
patient_info: Avoid contact with people who have active infections (flu, chickenpox). Use caution with sharp objects (razors/nail cutters).

name: CISPLATIN
indications: Cytotoxic drug: Metastatic testicular tumor, ovarian carcinoma, advanced bladder cancer, cancer of cervix, endometrium, prostate, and oesophagus.
dosage_schedule: Usual dose: 20 mg/m²/day IV for 5 days per cycle.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to platinum compounds, severe myelosuppression, renal impairment, hearing impairment, pregnancy, lactation.
precautions: Avoid aluminium needles or equipment (reacts with cisplatin). Maintain vigorous hydration (1-2 L fluid 8-12 hr before dose). Monitor for neuromuscular disease.
adverse_effects: Nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, myelosuppression, nausea, vomiting, alopecia.
interactions: Increased risk of nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity with aminoglycosides and loop diuretics.
patient_info: N/A

name: CYCLOPHOSPHAMIDE
indications: Cytotoxic drug: Chronic lymphatic leukaemia, non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma, ovarian carcinoma, breast carcinoma, Hodgkin’s diseases, neuroblastoma, sarcomas.
dosage_schedule: Daily IV injection: 3-6 mg/kg twice weekly. Massive intermittent therapy: 20-40 mg/kg over 2-5 days with 10-20 day intervals OR 10-15 mg/kg with 7-10 day intervals. Oral dose: 1-5 mg/kg/day.
precautions: Fetal harm. Monitor temperature every 4 hr (infection sign). Chest x-ray every 2 weeks. Monitor CBC weekly. Ensure high fluid intake (2-3 L/day) to prevent hemorrhagic cystitis.
adverse_effects: Myelosuppression, hemorrhagic cystitis, myocardial fibrosis, alopecia, sterility, SIADH.
interactions: Decreases digoxin levels. Increases anticoagulant effects. Toxic effects increased by rifampicin, phenobarbitone, and allopurinol.
