patient_info: Drink 2-3 liters of fluid daily. Report changes in breathing or coughing. Avoid foods with citric acid, hot spices.

name: CYTARABINE
indications: Cytotoxic drug: Acute myelocytic leukemia (AML), acute non-lymphocytic leukemia, chronic myelocytic leukemia, lymphomatous meningitis.
dosage_schedule: AML: Continuous IV infusion 100 mg/m²/day for 7 days every 2 weeks. Meningeal leukemia: Intrathecal 5-70 mg/m² daily for 4 days every 2-7 days.
precautions: Monitor for tumor lysis syndrome. Administer allopurinol and alkalinise urine to maintain uric acid levels. Give antiemetic 30-60 min before treatment.
adverse_effects: Myelosuppression (leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, anaemia), nausea, vomiting, alopecia.
interactions: Do not use with live virus vaccines. Increased toxicity with methotrexate and radiation.
patient_info: Report coughing, chest pain, or difficulty breathing (pneumonia risk). Avoid use of razors.

name: DAUNORUBICIN
indications: Cytotoxic drug: Combined treatment of acute leukemia.
dosage_schedule: Acute non-lymphocytic leukemia: (In combo with cytarabine) 30-45 mg/m² IVP on Days 1, 2, 3. Acute lymphocytic leukemia: 45 mg/m² IVP on Days 1, 2, 3.
precautions: VESICANT: Irritant to tissues; apply pressure to venipuncture sites for 10 minutes. Monitor for cardiotoxicity (CHF may occur 1-6 months after therapy). Periodic ECG and ejection fraction monitoring required.
adverse_effects: Cardiotoxicity, myelosuppression, red urine (harmless), alopecia, phlebitis, irreversible gonadal suppression.
interactions: Increased myelosuppression with other antineoplastics or radiation. Increased adverse effects with live vaccines.
patient_info: Notify doctor of irregular heartbeat or shortness of breath. Brush and rinse mouth after eating. Urine may be reddish for 1-2 days.

name: DOCETAXEL
indications: Cytotoxic drug: Breast cancer, non-small cell lung cancer, metastatic prostate cancer, gastric cancer, bladder cancer.
dosage_schedule: Adult: IV 60-100 mg/m² given over 1 hr every 3 weeks. Reduce dose by 25% if neutrophil count <500/mm³ for >1 week.
precautions: Should receive steroid premedication. Monitor LFT, CBC, and daily I/O chart for peripheral edema (fluid retention syndrome).
adverse_effects: Myelosuppression, hepatotoxicity, seizures, sinus tachycardia, pulmonary fibrosis, SJS, hypersensitivity reactions (common in first two cycles).
patient_info: Report signs of infection, sore throat, or extreme fatigue. Use barrier contraception for several months after treatment.

name: DOXORUBICIN
indications: Cytotoxic drug: Acute leukemia, carcinoma of breast, bladder, stomach, ovary, thyroid, neuroblastoma, Hodgkin’s/non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma, soft tissue sarcoma.
dosage_schedule: 60-75 mg/m² of body surface area.
precautions: VESICANT: Care must be taken during extravasation. Avoid sun exposure. Rapid injection causes facial flushing. Monitor CBC weekly. Monitor ECG for ST-T wave changes.
adverse_effects: Cardiomyopathy, acute left ventricular failure, myelosuppression, alopecia, facial flushes, red discoloration of urine.
interactions: Precipitates with dexamethasone, 5-FU, and heparin. Increased cardiomyopathy with calcium channel blockers.
patient_info: Urine will be red. Report mouth ulceration. Avoid pregnancy and crowds during low granulocyte counts.

name: EPIRUBICIN
indications: Cytotoxic drug: Adjuvant therapy for breast cancer; bladder, gastric, lung, ovarian cancer.
dosage_schedule: Adjuvant breast cancer: Day 1: Epirubicin 100 mg/m² IV + 5-FU 500 mg/m² IV + cyclophosphamide 500 mg/m² IV. Repeat q21 days for 6 cycles.
contraindications: Pregnancy, breastfeeding, heart failure, recent MI, cardiomyopathy.
precautions: VESICANT: Severe tissue necrosis if given IM/SC. Rapid injection (<3 min) causes facial flushing. Monitor CBC weekly (Nadir at 10-14 days). Monitor cardiac function at baseline.
adverse_effects: Bone marrow depression, heart failure, tumor lysis syndrome, amenorrhea, alopecia, red-orange urine.
interactions: Increased toxicity with radiation/cimetidine. Risk of heart failure with Trastuzumab and calcium channel blockers.
patient_info: Urine will be red-orange.

name: ETOPOSIDE
indications: Cytotoxic drug: Germ cell tumors, small cell carcinoma of lungs, Non Hodgkin lymphoma, acute non-lymphocytic leukemia, Kaposi sarcoma.
dosage_schedule: Testicular neoplasms: IV 50-100 mg/m² daily for 5 days OR 100 mg/m² on days 1, 3, 5; repeat q3-4 weeks. SCLC: Oral 70-100 mg/m² daily for 4-5 days; IV 35-50 mg/m² daily for 4-5 days.
precautions: Administer over 30-60 minutes to reduce hypotension risk. Caution in liver disease and renal/hepatic impairment.
adverse_effects: Myelosuppression, stomatitis, alopecia, anaphylaxis, secondary malignancies.
interactions: Bone marrow depression increased by other antineoplastics and radiation. May alter immune response to live vaccines.
patient_info: N/A

name: FLUDARABINE
indications: Cytotoxic drug: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia, non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
dosage_schedule: Adult: IV 25 mg/m² over 30 min for 5 days.
contraindications: Pregnancy, breastfeeding, hypersensitivity, decreased kidney functions.
precautions: Monitor CNS toxicity.
adverse_effects: CNS toxicity, myelosuppression, visual disturbance, gastrointestinal hemorrhage, edema.
patient_info: N/A

name: FLUOROURACIL
indications: Cytotoxic drug: Colorectal cancer, GI neoplasms, breast, pancreatic, head and neck cancer.
dosage_schedule: Oral maintenance: 15 mg/kg weekly; maximum in one day 1 g.
contraindications: Bone marrow suppression, active ischemic heart disease, pregnancy, lactation.
precautions: Caution in infections and patients with oedema or ascites.
adverse_effects: Hand-foot syndrome (erythema, desquamation, pain), mucosal ulcers, myelosuppression, alopecia, myelopathy.
interactions: Additive myelosuppression with other depressants. Increased risk of toxicity with combination therapy (e.g., irinotecan).
patient_info: N/A

name: HYDROXYUREA
indications: Cytotoxic drug: Melanoma, chronic myelogenous leukaemia, recurrent/metastatic ovarian cancer, head and neck cancer, sickle cell anaemia.
dosage_schedule: Ovarian cancer/Melanoma: Adult PO 80 mg/kg as single dose q3Days or 20-30 mg/kg daily. CML/AML: Adult PO 10-75 mg/kg/day adjusted to WBC count. Child: 10-20 mg/kg/day.
precautions: Monitor CBC weekly. Severe myelosuppression risk. Reduce dose in polycythemia vera. Monitor renal function.
adverse_effects: Seizures, hepatotoxicity, increased BUN, uric acid, megaloblastic erythropoiesis, tumor lysis syndrome.
interactions: Increased risk of pancreatitis/hepatotoxicity with didanosine or stavudine. Probenecid/sulfinpyrazone increase uric acid levels.
patient_info: Report signs of infection (fever, sore throat) or anemia (fatigue). Avoid razors. Notify prescriber if pregnancy suspected.

name: IRINOTECAN
indications: Cytotoxic drug: Metastatic colorectal carcinoma, epithelial lung cancers.
dosage_schedule: Adult IV: 125 mg/m² once weekly for 4 weeks followed by 2 weeks rest; OR 350 mg/m² every 3 weeks.
precautions: Risk of life-threatening diarrhea accompanied by dehydration. Use caution in patients >65 years or those with previous pelvic irradiation.
adverse_effects: Severe diarrhea, myelosuppression, colonic ulcerations, pancytopenia.
interactions: CYP3A4 inhibitors increase toxicity. Combination with 5-FU may cause serious sepsis/dehydration.
patient_info: Report occurrence of diarrhoea immediately, especially if it occurs 24 hours after administration.

name: INTERFERON BETA
indications: Cytotoxic (Immunomodulator): Relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis.
dosage_schedule: Subcutaneous: Initially 0.0625 mg every other day, gradually increasing over 6 weeks to 0.25 mg every other day.
contraindications: Decompensated liver disease, severe depressive illness.
precautions: Use caution in history of cardiac disorders or suicidal ideation. Monitor for hepatic injury, TMA, and new onset hypertension. Effective contraception required.
adverse_effects: Flu-like symptoms, depression, suicide attempts, thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA), thyroid dysfunction, necrosis at injection site.
patient_info: N/A

name: INTERFERON GAMMA-1B
indications: Cytotoxic (Immunomodulator): Reduce frequency of infection in chronic granulomatous disease, severe malignant osteoporosis.
dosage_schedule: Subcutaneous: 50 mcg/m² 3 times a week.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to interferon gamma or E. coli-derived products.
precautions: Caution in cardiac disease, seizure disorders, or arrhythmias. Monitor CBC, renal, and liver function every 3 months. Use effective contraception.
adverse_effects: Myalgia, arthralgia, flu-like symptoms, systemic lupus erythematosus, proteinuria.
interactions: Avoid simultaneous administration of foreign proteins (exaggerated immune response).
patient_info: N/A

name: LOMUSTINE
indications: Cytotoxic drug: Brain tumors, lymphomas.
dosage_schedule: Used alone: 120-130 mg/m² every 6-8 weeks.
precautions: Severe myelosuppression and hepatotoxicity. Avoid pregnancy.
adverse_effects: Permanent bone marrow damage, vomiting.
patient_info: Take on empty stomach. Avoid alcohol.

name: MELPHALAN
indications: Cytotoxic drug: Multiple myeloma, advanced ovarian adenocarcinoma, advanced breast cancer.
dosage_schedule: Breast cancer: Oral 150 mcg/kg daily for 5-6 days, repeated every 6 weeks.
precautions: Monitor CBC for marrow toxicity.
adverse_effects: Marrow toxicity, hepatitis, pulmonary fibrosis, secondary malignancies.
interactions: Should be taken on an empty stomach.
patient_info: Sterility and amenorrhea may occur (reversible). Avoid aspirin, alcohol, NSAIDS.

name: MERCAPTOPURINE (6-MERCAPTOPURINE)
indications: Cytotoxic drug: Severe acute Crohn’s disease, maintenance of remission of Crohn’s/UC, acute leukaemias, CML.
dosage_schedule: Crohn’s/UC: Oral 1-1.5 mg/kg daily. Acute leukemia: Initially 2.5 mg/kg daily or 50-75 mg/m² daily.
precautions: Consider measuring TPMT activity before starting. Monitor liver function and CBC. Pregnancy Category X.
adverse_effects: Pancreatitis, transient oligospermia, intestinal ulceration, bone-marrow suppression, hyperuricaemia.
patient_info: N/A

name: METHOTREXATE
indications: Cytotoxic drug: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia, gestational trophoblastic neoplasm, lymphomas, breast/lung cancer, RA, Crohn’s disease.
dosage_schedule: Leukemia in children (maintenance): 15 mg/m² ONCE WEEKLY.
precautions: Monitor CBC, RFT, LFT. Consider titration in pleural effusion/ascites to prevent nephrotoxicity. Monitor for pneumonitis.
adverse_effects: Bone marrow suppression, mucositis, renal toxicity, dermatitis, interstitial pneumonitis, defective spermatogenesis, abortion.
interactions: Toxicity increased by Sulfonamides, Salicylates, Tetracyclines, Chloramphenicol, Phenytoin, NSAIDs, Cisplatin, and PPIs.
patient_info: Stop folic acid supplementation while on methotrexate. Report any breathing/coughing changes.

name: MITOMYCIN
indications: Cytotoxic drug: Upper gastro-intestinal and breast cancers, superficial bladder cancer.
dosage_schedule: IV infusion usually q6-weekly.
precautions: VESICANT: Causes delayed bone marrow toxicity; use with care at injection site.
adverse_effects: Thrombocytopenia, leucopenia, mouth ulcers, thrombophlebitis, lung fibrosis.
patient_info: Report redness or burning pain at IV site. Report urine retention or jaundice.

name: MITOXANTRONE
indications: Cytotoxic drug: Acute myelogenous leukemia (adult), relapsed leukemia, advanced prostate cancer, multiple sclerosis.
dosage_schedule: MS: 12 mg/m² short IV infusion q3Months. AML: 12 mg/m²/day IV on Days 1-3. Prostate: 12-14 mg/m² q21Days in combination with corticosteroids.
precautions: Do not exceed lifetime cumulative dose of 140 mg/m².
adverse_effects: Myelosuppression, cardiotoxicity, alopecia, secondary AML.
patient_info: N/A

name: OXALIPLATIN
indications: Cytotoxic drug: Colorectal carcinoma, gastro-oesophageal, lung, pancreatic cancers.
dosage_schedule: Colon carcinoma: Day 1: 85 mg/m² IV + leucovorin 200 mg/m² IV; then 5-FU. Repeat q2weeks.
precautions: Administer under specialist supervision. Avoid cold exposure following administration (triggers neurotoxicity). Monitor for Grade 2/3 neuropathy.
adverse_effects: Acute and chronic neurotoxicity, myelosuppression, hepatotoxicity.
interactions: Increased nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity with Bacitracin.
patient_info: Use blankets/gloves for cold prevention. Monitor temperature.

name: PACLITAXEL
indications: Cytotoxic drug: Ovarian, breast, NSCLC, SCLC, prostate, bladder cancer, AIDS related Kaposi sarcoma.
dosage_schedule: Ovarian Ca: 175 mg/m² over 3 hours every 3 weeks.
contraindications: Anaphylaxis, solid tumors with baseline neutrophil <1500/mm³.
precautions: Give premedication to prevent hypersensitivity. Monitor LFTs.
adverse_effects: Myelosuppression, neurotoxicity, myalgia, alopecia, mucositis.
interactions: Inhibitors of CYP3A4 affect metabolism. Quinidine and Amiodarone increase toxicity.
patient_info: Report fever or sore throat. Hair loss is expected. Pain in muscles/joints is common 2-5 days post-infusion.

name: PEMETREXED
indications: Cytotoxic drug: Malignant pleural mesotheliomas, non-squamous NSCLC.
dosage_schedule: Mesothelioma: 500 mg/m² IV on Day 1 of each 21 day cycle with cisplatin. NSCLC: 500 mg/m² IV Day 1.
precautions: Premedication regimen mandatory: Folic acid, B12, and dexamethasone. Monitor CBC, RFT, LFT.
adverse_effects: Interstitial pneumonitis, severe myelosupression, fatigue, chest pain.
interactions: Renal toxicity increased with NSAIDs (Aspirin, Diclofenac). Increased nephron/oto toxicity with Bacitracin.
patient_info: N/A

name: PROCARBAZINE
indications: Cytotoxic drug: Hodgkin’s disease, non-Hodgkin’s lymphomas, brain tumors.
dosage_schedule: Initially 50 mg daily, increased to 250-300 mg daily in divided doses; cumulative total max 6 g.
precautions: Avoid alcohol. Monitor for CNS toxicity.
adverse_effects: Myelosuppression, CNS toxicity, neuropathies, mental depression, ascites.
interactions: Disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol. Hypertensive crisis with tyramine foods. Potentiates hypoglycemic effects of insulin.
patient_info: Avoid sunlight. Avoid driving (dizziness). Use effective contraception. May cause infertility.

name: TACROLIMUS
indications: Cytotoxic (Immunosuppressant): Prophylaxis of graft rejection following kidney transplantation.
dosage_schedule: Initially 200–300 mcg/kg daily in 2 divided doses.
precautions: Use only with transplant specialist prescription. Increased risk of infection and lymphoma. Monitor serum drug concentration closely.
adverse_effects: Renal tubular necrosis, hyperglycemia, hypertension, tremor, visual disturbances, bile-duct abnormalities.
interactions: Avoid with amphotericin B, cidofovir. Caution with nephrotoxic drugs and calcium channel blockers. Dose adjustment required with CYP3A inducers/inhibitors.
patient_info: N/A

name: TEMOZOLOMIDE
indications: Cytotoxic drug: Anaplastic astrocytoma with relapse, glioblastoma multiforme, malignant glioma, metastatic melanoma.
dosage_schedule: Initial: 150 mg/m² PO/IV qDay for 5 days of 28-day cycle. Maintenance: 200 mg/m² qDay if counts stable. Infuse IV over 90 minutes.
precautions: Assess CBC on day 22. PCP prophylaxis required when used with radiotherapy. Avoid sun exposure.
adverse_effects: Thrombocytopenia, leucopenia, seizures, anaphylaxis, secondary malignancy.
interactions: Avoid use within 24 hr of G-CSF or filgrastim. NSAIDS and anticoagulants increase bleeding risk.
patient_info: Report fever or extreme fatigue immediately. Avoid use of razors. Do not breastfeed.

name: TOPOTECAN
indications: Cytotoxic drug: Ovarian, small cell lung, and cervical cancer.
dosage_schedule: Cervical: 0.75 mg/m² IV Days 1-3 q21days with cisplatin. Ovarian: 1.5 mg/m² IV qDay x 5 days q21days.
contraindications: Pregnancy, breastfeeding, severe bone marrow suppression.
precautions: Avoid live vaccines. Reduce dose to 0.75 mg/m² in moderate renal dysfunction.
adverse_effects: Myelosuppression, hair loss, elevated liver transaminase, mouth sores.
interactions: Avoid use with P-glycoprotein inhibitors (amiodarone, clarithromycin).
patient_info: Avoid crowds or people with colds. Limit or avoid alcoholic beverages.

name: TRETINOIN
indications: Cytotoxic (Retinoid): Acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL).
dosage_schedule: 45 mg/m²/day PO divided q12h until 30 days after complete remission.
contraindications: Pregnancy, hypersensitivity to retinoids or parabens.
precautions: Monitor hepatic function and coagulation. Assess for retinoic acid syndrome.
adverse_effects: Retinoic acid syndrome, cardiac arrhythmia, hemorrhage, dyspepsia.
patient_info: Do not crush, chew or dissolve capsules.

name: VINCRISTINE
indications: Cytotoxic drug: Acute leukemia, combination therapy for various cancers.
dosage_schedule: IV Adult: 1.4 mg every week. Child: 2 mg/m² every week. (<10 kg: 0.05 mg/kg/week).
precautions: VESICANT: Caution during administration. FATAL IF GIVEN INTRATHECAL. Monitor for neuromuscular disease.
adverse_effects: Peripheral neuropathy, loss of deep tendon reflexes, acute uric acid nephropathy, gait change, jaw pain, paralytic ileus.
interactions: Use caution with neurotoxic or ototoxic agents.
patient_info: Report any numbness or tingling in fingers/toes immediately.

name: VINBLASTINE
indications: Cytotoxic drug: Hodgkin’s lymphoma, testicular cancer, Kaposi’s sarcoma, bladder cancer.
dosage_schedule: Adult IV: Initially 3.7 mg/m² then increase weekly until WBC equals 3000/mm³ (max dose 18.5 mg/m²).
precautions: VESICANT: Avoid intrathecal administration. Caution in pulmonary disease and liver impairment.
adverse_effects: Myelosuppression, alopecia, bronchospasm, aspermia, cranial neuropathy (jaw pain).
patient_info: Report jaw pain or hoarseness.

name: VINORELBINE
indications: Cytotoxic drug: Non-small cell lung carcinoma, Hodgkin’s disease, breast/ovarian cancer.
dosage_schedule: Monotherapy: 30 mg/m² IV over 6-10 minutes weekly.
precautions: VESICANT: Irritant to veins. Assess BP during administration. Monitor AST, ALT, LDH.
adverse_effects: Myelosuppression, paresthesias, GI perforation, acute bronchospasm, ARDS.
patient_info: Report change in gait or numbness in extremities. Avoid vaccinations.

name: BEVACIZUMAB
indications: Targeted drug: Metastatic colorectal cancer, non-small cell lung cancer, renal cell carcinoma, cervical cancer.
dosage_schedule: 5-10 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks.
precautions: Serious bleeding risk, GI perforation, wound dehiscence. Discontinue permanently if GI perforation occurs or for wound dehiscence requiring medical intervention.
adverse_effects: Fatal hemorrhage, hemoptysis, CNS hemorrhage, proteinuria, thromboembolic events.
patient_info: Report shortness of breath or severe abdominal pain immediately. Use contraception.

name: BORTEZOMIB
indications: Targeted drug: Mantle cell lymphoma, multiple myeloma.
dosage_schedule: 1.3 mg/m²/dose IV twice weekly for 2 weeks (Days 1, 4, 8, 11) followed by a 10-day rest period.
precautions: DO NOT ADMINISTER INTRATHECAL (fatal events reported). Use subcutaneous route to reduce neuropathy risk. Monitor for high tumor burden.
adverse_effects: Neuropathy, thrombocytopenia, pyrexia, anemia, dehydration.
interactions: Green tea and supplements block efficacy and should be avoided.
patient_info: N/A

name: CETUXIMAB
indications: Targeted drug: RAS-wild metastatic colorectal carcinoma, head and neck cancer.
dosage_schedule: Initial: 400 mg/m² IV. Subsequent: 250 mg/m² IV weekly. Not to exceed infusion rate of 10 mg/min.
contraindications: Use only in metastatic setting. Don’t use if RAS mutations are present.
precautions: RAS-testing is mandatory. Monitor for infusion reactions.
adverse_effects: Infusion reactions, rashes, hypomagnesemia, interstitial lung disease.
patient_info: Use contraception. Do not breastfeed.

name: ERLOTINIB
indications: Targeted drug: EGFR mutant non-small cell lung cancer.
dosage_schedule: Adult: 150 mg/day oral.
precautions: EGFR mutation testing mandatory. Use only if EGFR positive.
adverse_effects: Interstitial pneumonitis, increased serum transaminases, diarrhea, dry skin.
interactions: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice. Inhibitors of CYP3A4 increase toxicity.
patient_info: Report severe diarrhea or black, furry tongue.

name: GEFITINIB
indications: Targeted drug: EGFR mutant non-small cell lung cancer (same as erlotinib).
dosage_schedule: Oral: 250 mg once a day.
contraindications: Concurrent use of strong inhibitors of CYP3A4.
precautions: Monitor LFTs and PT/INR if taking warfarin.
adverse_effects: Corneal erosion, conjunctivitis, skin rashes, hepatotoxicity.
interactions: Rifampin and Phenytoin decrease blood levels. Itraconazole increases toxicity. Ranitidine decreases absorption.
patient_info: Consult health professional if severe persistent diarrhoea occurs.

name: IMATINIB
indications: Targeted drug: Ph+ CML, GIST, myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative disease.
dosage_schedule: CML: Adult PO 400-600 mg daily. GIST: 400 mg daily. Oral Children: 340 mg/m²/day.
precautions: Monitor liver function monthly. Monitor for general fluid retention (common in blast crisis).
adverse_effects: Fluid retention (edema), hepatotoxicity, muscle cramps, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia.
interactions: Toxicity increased by CYP3A4 inhibitors (clarithromycin, ritonavir). Efficacy decreased by CYP3A4 inducers (dexamethasone, rifampin).
patient_info: Take with food and a large glass of water. Avoid grapefruit juice.

name: NILOTINIB
indications: Targeted drug: Imatinib-resistant Ph+ CML, GIST.
dosage_schedule: New CML: 300 mg oral BD. Resistant/Intolerant: 400 mg BD.
precautions: Correct hypokalemia/hypomagnesemia before administration. Monitor Mg++ and K+ levels.
adverse_effects: QT prolongation, pleural effusion, neutropenia.
interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase levels; decrease dose if must be used. Food interferes with absorption.
patient_info: Take on empty stomach at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal.

name: OSIMERTINIB
indications: Targeted drug: EGFR T790M mutation-positive NSCLC.
dosage_schedule: 80 mg oral daily until disease progression.
precautions: Monitor for cardiomyopathy. Monitor patients with prior renal/hepatic disease closely.
adverse_effects: Lymphopenia, cardiomyopathy, diarrhea.
interactions: Strong CYP3 inhibitors increase toxicity. Strong CYP3 inducers decrease concentration.
patient_info: Do not breastfeed.

name: RITUXIMAB
indications: Targeted drug: B-cell lymphoma, mantle cell lymphoma, CML, rheumatoid arthritis, Wegener’s granulomatosis.
dosage_schedule: CLL/NHL: 237 mg/m² infusion weekly for 4 weeks. RA: 2 infusions of 1000 mg each separated by 2 weeks.
precautions: DO NOT ADMINISTER AS IV PUSH OR BOLUS. High risk of fatal infusion reactions. Reactivation of Hepatitis B. Caution if malignant cell count >10^9/L.
adverse_effects: Infusion reactions, late-onset neutropenia, transient hypotension, bleeding gum.
patient_info: Avoid pregnancy for 12 months after treatment.

name: SUNITINIB
indications: Targeted drug: GIST, advanced renal carcinoma, pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor.
dosage_schedule: GIST: 50 mg PO qDay for 4 weeks, followed by 2 weeks drug-free.
precautions: Assess ANC and Platelets; stop if ANC <1x10^9/L or Platelets <50x10^9/L. Monitor LFTs monthly.
adverse_effects: Left ventricular dysfunction, hypertension, hypothyroidism, bleeding.
interactions: Toxicity increased by Bevacizumab. Erythromycin and haloperidol interactions.
patient_info: Avoid grapefruit juice. Report SOB immediately.

name: TRASTUZUMAB
indications: Targeted drug: HER2-overexpressing breast cancer and gastric cancer.
dosage_schedule: Metastatic breast cancer: 4 mg/kg IV over 90 min, then 2 mg/kg IV weekly.
precautions: Evaluate cardiac function (LVEF) every 3 months. Discontinue if LVEF decrease >16%. High risk of pulmonary toxicity.
adverse_effects: Cardiotoxicity, interstitial pneumonitis, ARDS, oligohydramnios (in pregnancy).
patient_info: Effective contraception is vital. Exposure during pregnancy can cause neonatal death.

name: ANASTROZOLE
indications: Hormonal drug: ER+ breast cancer, uterine leiomyoma, endometriosis.
dosage_schedule: 1 mg daily.
precautions: Assess bone mineral density regularly. Avoid if CrCl < 20 ml/min.
adverse_effects: Hot flushes, osteoporosis, vaginal bleeding, thrombophlebitis, altered taste.
interactions: Do not use with oral contraceptives or tamoxifen.
patient_info: Take calcium and Vitamin D to prevent bone loss.

name: EXEMESTANE
indications: Hormonal drug: ER+ breast cancer in postmenopausal women.
dosage_schedule: Adult: 25 mg/day after meals.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Hot flashes, diaphoresis, lymphopenia.
patient_info: Use reliable contraception.

name: FULVESTRANT
indications: Hormonal drug: Advanced ER+ breast carcinoma.
dosage_schedule: IM 500 mg on Days 1, 15, 29 and monthly thereafter.
precautions: Caution in hepatic disease and coagulopathy.
adverse_effects: Hepatic failure, hyperbilirubinemia, angioedema.
patient_info: Premenopausal women must use birth control as ovulation may be induced.

name: TAMOXIFEN
indications: Hormonal drug: Breast cancer, endometrial cancer, anovulatory infertility.
dosage_schedule: Breast cancer: 20 mg daily. Infertility: 20 mg daily on Days 2-5 of cycle.
precautions: Regularly assess CBC. Withdraw if WBC <3500 or Platelets <100,000. Periodic eye exams required.
adverse_effects: Endometrial polyps, vaginal bleeding, hot flushes, cataracts.
interactions: Increased risk of bleeding with anticoagulants. Decreased level with rifampin.
patient_info: Use non-hormonal contraception during and for 2 months after treatment.

name: TUBERCULIN, PURIFIED PROTEIN DERIVATIVE (PPD)
indications: Mantoux test; test for hypersensitivity to tuberculoprotein.
dosage_schedule: Intradermal injection: 10 units for 1 dose. (Note: 2 units is equivalent to 0.1 mL of 20 units/mL strength; 10 units is equivalent to 0.1 mL of 100 units/mL strength).
contraindications: Should not be used within 4 weeks of receiving live viral vaccination.
precautions: Avoid in patients with viral and bacterial infections (including HIV and severe tuberculosis), malignant disease, or those on corticosteroid/immunosuppressive therapy. Malnourished or elderly patients may show suppressed responses.
adverse_effects: Headache, nausea, malaise, rash, itch, vesicle formation, ulceration, necrosis, or pain at the administered site.
interactions: Effectiveness may be decreased by corticosteroids, immunosuppressives, or live vaccines (e.g., measles).

name: ANTI-D IMMUNOGLOBULIN (HUMAN)
indications: Prevention of formation of antibodies to rhesus positive blood cells in rhesus negative patients.
dosage_schedule: Post-abortion/birth of Rh+ infant: Deep IM injection 500 units within 72 hours; for transplacental bleed >4 ml, extra 100-125 units per ml fetal red cells. Sensitizing episodes (e.g., still birth): Up to 20 weeks gestation 250 units; after 20 weeks 500 units. Antenatal prophylaxis: Deep IM 500 units at weeks 28 and 34 of pregnancy.
precautions: Caution in Rh+ patients being treated for blood disorders and Rh- patients already possessing anti-D antibodies. Use only adequately screened preparations.
adverse_effects: Soreness at injection site, fever, anemia, intravascular hemolysis, renal insufficiency.

name: ANTIRABIES HYPERIMMUNE SERUM
indications: Passive immunization post-exposure or suspected exposure in unimmunized individuals (in conjunction with rabies vaccine).
dosage_schedule: Pre-exposure: IM/Intradermal: 3 doses on days 0, 7, and 21 or 28. Post-exposure: IM: 5 doses on days 0, 3, 7, 14, and 28. Adult/Child: 20 units/kg by infiltration in and around the cleansed wound; remainder given IM into anterolateral thigh.
precautions: Safety in pregnancy not established (use only if benefits outweigh risks). Skin test should be performed before administration. Inquiry for history of allergy.
adverse_effects: Soreness at injection site, mild temperature elevations, angioedema, skin rash, nephrotic syndrome, and rarely anaphylactic shock.
interactions: Antibodies may interfere with live vaccines (measles, mumps, polio, rubella); live vaccines should not be given within 3 months after serum administration.

name: POLYVENUM ANTISNAKE SERUM
indications: Venomous snake bite with clear indication of systemic or severe local involvement.
dosage_schedule: Depends on the specific antivenom used. Refer to the specific product insert leaflet.
precautions: Resuscitation facilities must be available. NEVER inject into a finger or toe. Inject IM into a large muscle mass (gluteal region). Avoid nerve trunks. Notify physician if pregnant (venom may cause spontaneous abortion).
adverse_effects: Anaphylaxis with urticaria, hypotension, dyspnea, shock thermal sickness, and serum sickness.

name: TETANUS IMMUNOGLOBULIN (HUMAN)
indications: Passive immunization against tetanus as part of management for tetanus-prone wounds.
dosage_schedule: IM injection: 250 units. Increase to 500 units if the wound is older than 24 hours, heavily contaminated, or following burns.
precautions: Should NOT be given intravenously. Caution in patients with severe thrombocytopenia or coagulation disorders. Notify physician if pregnancy is planned/suspected.
adverse_effects: Soreness at injection site, temperature elevation, angioederma, nephrotic syndrome, and rare anaphylactic shock.
interactions: May interfere with live viral vaccines (measles, mumps, polio, rubella); defer these vaccines for 3 months after injection.

name: PENTAVALENT VACCINE (DPT-HepB-Hib)
indications: Universal immunization for all newborns against Diphtheria, Tetanus, Pertussis, Hepatitis B, and Haemophilus influenzae type B.
dosage_schedule: IM injection, child: 0.5 ml in 3 doses at 6, 10, and 14 weeks of birth.
precautions: Start for any child aged >6 weeks up to 1 year. Children initiated with DPT/HepB continue with those, not pentavalent.
adverse_effects: Mild local reactions, fever, malaise.

name: MEASLES VACCINE
indications: Active immunization against measles.
dosage_schedule: Infant: At 9 months: 0.5 ml. Prophylaxis (exposure): Over 9 months: 0.5 ml within 72 hours of contact.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to antibiotics in vaccine, egg, or gelatin. Avoid in TB, AIDS, or respiratory infections.
precautions: Caution in febrile illness, seizure, or cerebral injury.
adverse_effects: Local lymphadenopathy, rash, rarely thrombocytopenia purpura.

name: MEASLES, MUMPS, RUBELLA (MMR) VACCINE
indications: Primary immunization against MMR; rubella immunization for seronegative women; pre-school booster.
dosage_schedule: First dose: IM/Deep SC, child 12-13 months: 0.5 ml. Second dose: IM/Deep SC, child 40 months - 5 years: 0.5 ml.
precautions: Leave an interval of 3 months after immunoglobulin or blood transfusion before vaccination.
adverse_effects: Parotid swelling (3rd week), sleep disturbances, arthropathy (2-3 weeks post-immunization), optic/peripheral neuritis.
interactions: Do not administer on the same day as Yellow Fever vaccine; maintain a minimum 4-week interval.

name: NORMAL IMMUNOGLOBULIN
indications: Hepatitis A, measles, mumps, rubella, varicella; ITP, Kawasaki disease, Guillain-Barre syndrome, allogenic bone marrow transplantation prophylaxis.
dosage_schedule: ITP: Adult IV: 400 mg/kg/day for 2-5 days. Kawasaki: Adult IV: 1.6-2 g/kg divided over 2-5 days. Guillain-Barre: Adult IV: 400 mg/kg daily for 5 days. Hep A (Outbreak): Adult IM: 500 mg; Child <10yr: 250 mg.
contraindications: Patients with selective IgA deficiency who have known antibody against IgA.
precautions: Monitor for acute renal failure. Preparations containing maltose may falsely elevate blood glucose tests (GDH-PQQ methods).
adverse_effects: Dizziness, light-headedness, nausea, vomiting, chills, fever, local pain at injection site.
interactions: May interfere with live vaccines (measles, mumps, rubella, varicella); give vaccines 3 weeks before or 3 months after immunoglobulin.

name: POLIOMYELITIS VACCINE (ORAL)/OPV (LIVE ATTENUATED)
indications: Active immunization against poliomyelitis.
dosage_schedule: Primary (Child): Oral: 3 drops at birth and at 6, 10, and 14 weeks. Reinforcing (Child): 3 drops at least 3 years after primary course and another 3 drops at 15-19 years. Unimmunized Adult: 3 doses of 3 drops with 4-week intervals.
precautions: Do not take with food containing preservatives; hypersensitivity to antibiotics in vaccine.
adverse_effects: Rarely, vaccine-associated poliomyelitis in recipients or contacts.

name: ROTAVIRUS VACCINE
indications: Immunization against gastro-enteritis caused by rotavirus.
dosage_schedule: Oral, 6-24 weeks: 1.5 ml at least every 4 weeks for 2 doses. First dose must be given between 6-15 weeks of age; course must be completed before 24 weeks.
contraindications: History of intussusception, severe combined immunosuppression.
precautions: Postpone vaccination in cases of diarrhea or vomiting.
adverse_effects: Abdominal cramps, abdominal pain, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting.

name: TETANUS TOXOID
indications: Active immunization against tetanus and neonatal tetanus; wound management prophylaxis.
dosage_schedule: Primary (Adults/Adolescents): IM: 3 doses (0.5 ml) with 4 weeks between 1st/2nd dose and 6 months between 2nd/3rd dose. Reinforcing (Adult): 2 doses (0.5 ml) 10 years apart. Pregnant women (unimmunized): IM: 2 doses (0.5 ml) 4 weeks apart (2nd dose at least 2 weeks before delivery). Wounds: IM: 0.5 ml single dose.
precautions: Use separate syringes and sites if given with antitetanus immunoglobulin.
adverse_effects: Rarely associated with peripheral neuropathy, seizures, fever, loss of appetite.

name: DIPHTHERIA ANTITOXINS
indications: Passive immunization in suspected cases of diphtheria.
dosage_schedule: Therapeutic use (pharyngeal/laryngeal): IV infusion, adult: 20,000 to 40,000 units; child (<10 years): half of adult dose.
precautions: Initial test dose should be given; full dose must be under observation with resuscitation facilities available. Patients allergic to horse serum are at high risk.
adverse_effects: Anaphylaxis, urticaria, hypotension, dyspnea, shock thermal sickness, serum sickness (up to 12 days post-injection).

name: HEPATITIS B IMMUNOGLOBULIN
indications: Post-exposure prophylaxis for healthcare workers, accidental inoculation, or babies of infected mothers.
dosage_schedule: IM injection (as soon as possible, ideally within 7 days): Adult/Child >10 yr: 500 units; Child <5 yr: 200 units; 5-9 yr: 300 units; Neonate: 200 units as soon as possible after birth.
contraindications: Anaphylactic reaction to human globulin, thrombocytopenia, or coagulation disorders contraindicating IM injection.
precautions: Skin test must be done prior to giving the sera. Give at the same time as the vaccine if exposure is certain.
adverse_effects: Hypertension, hypotension, malaise, agitation, amnesia, aphthous stomatitis, ecchymosis, splenomegaly.

name: HUMAN PAPILLOMA VIRUS VACCINE
indications: Prevention of premalignant genital (cervical, vulvar, vaginal) and anal lesions, cancers, and genital warts.
dosage_schedule: Intramuscular, female >9 years: 0.5 ml for 1 dose, follow with 0.5 ml after 1 month, then 0.5 ml after 3 months (Total 3 doses within 12 months). Alternative (9-13 years): 0.5 ml for 1 dose, follow with 0.5 ml after 6 months.
precautions: If course is interrupted, resume but do not repeat. Vaccination should be postponed until completion of pregnancy.
adverse_effects: N/A

name: INFLUENZA VACCINE
indications: Annual immunization against seasonal influenza.
dosage_schedule: IM injection (Children 6 mo - 9 yr): 0.5 ml for 1 dose, followed by 0.5 ml after 4 weeks. Intranasal (Child 2-9 yr): 0.1 ml (total) into each nostril, followed by 0.1 ml after 4 weeks. General: IM: 0.5 ml for 1 dose.
precautions: Child under 5 years at increased risk of febrile convulsions. Egg-free vaccine required for those with egg allergy.
adverse_effects: Epistaxis, febrile convulsions, transient thrombocytopenia, vasculitis (adults).

name: RABIES VACCINE
indications: Active immunization; pre-exposure prophylaxis and post-exposure treatment.
dosage_schedule: Pre-exposure: IM: 3 doses (0, 7, 28 days) OR Intradermal: 3 doses (0.1 ml) on same days. Post-exposure (Unimmunized): IM: 1 dose on days 0, 3, 7, 14, 28 (Total 5 doses). Post-exposure (Fully Immunized): IM/Intradermal: 2 doses separated by 3 days.
precautions: Use separate syringes and sites if given with rabies immunoglobulin.
adverse_effects: Mild gastrointestinal disturbance, headache, dizziness.

name: TYPHOID VACCINE
indications: Active immunization against typhoid.
dosage_schedule: Oral (Capsules, >5 yrs): One dose on days 1, 3, 5, and 7. Oral (Suspension, >2 yrs): One dose on days 1, 3, and 5. Vi capsular polysaccharide vaccine: SC/IM: 0.5 ml (child >=2 yrs and adults), reinforce every 3 years.
precautions: Proguanil, mefloquine and antibiotics must be stopped 3 days before and after administration of Ty21a oral vaccine.
adverse_effects: Anaphylactoid reaction, nausea, vomiting, fever, redness, itching, abdominal pain.
interactions: Antibiotics, Proguanil, and Mefloquine interfere with oral vaccine.

name: YELLOW FEVER VACCINE
indications: Active immunization against yellow fever.
dosage_schedule: Child (9-12 months): 0.5 ml single dose by deep SC/IM. Adult/Child (>9 months): 0.5 ml single dose by deep SC/IM.
contraindications: Infants under 9 months, pregnancy, severe immunodeficiency, egg allergy.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Headache, myalgia, weakness; rarely encephalitis (infants), viscerotropic disease, multiple organ failure (elderly).

name: NEPAL EPI SCHEDULE (2017)
indications: Routine infant immunization protocol in Nepal.
dosage_schedule: At Birth: BCG (Tuberculosis). 6 Weeks: Rota (1st), Polio (1st), FIPV (1st), PCV (1st), Pentavalent (1st). 10 Weeks: Rota (2nd), Polio (2nd), PCV (2nd), Pentavalent (2nd). 14 Weeks: Polio (3rd), FIPV (2nd), Pentavalent (3rd). 9 Months: PCV (3rd), Measles-Rubella (1st). 12 Months: Japanese Encephalitis. 15 Months: Measles-Rubella (2nd).
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: N/A

name: BENZOIC ACID AND SALICYLIC ACID
indications: Antibacterial/Antifungal: Superficial dermatophyte infections - Tinea corporis, Tinea cruris.
dosage_form_strength: Ointment/Cream: 6% w/w benzoic acid and 3% w/w salicylic acid.
dosage_schedule: Apply twice daily until the infected skin is shed (usually at least 4 weeks).
precautions: Salicylate toxicity may occur if applied on large areas of skin. Avoid broken or inflamed skin. Avoid contact with eyes and mucous membranes.
adverse_effects: Erythema, hypersensitivity reactions, itching, mild burning sensation, occasional local irritation.
patient_info: Treatment should be discontinued if side effects are severe.

name: FUSIDIC ACID
indications: Antibacterial: Staphylococcal skin infection (impetigo, folliculitis), erythrasma, pitted keratolysis.
dosage_schedule: Apply 3–4 times a day to the skin.
contraindications: Allergy to fusidic acid or its salts.
precautions: Avoid contact with eyes. To avoid development of resistance, do not use for longer than 10 days.
adverse_effects: Hypersensitivity reactions.
patient_info: Avoid contact of cream or ointment with eyes.

name: METRONIDAZOLE
indications: Antibacterial: Rosacea, malodorous gravitational and decubitus ulcers.
dosage_schedule: Acute rosacea: Apply twice daily for 8 weeks. Malodorous ulcers: Apply 1-2 times a day to clean wound with non-adherent dressing.
precautions: Avoid exposure to strong sunlight or UV light. Use with caution in patients with blood dyscrasias or hepatic disease.
adverse_effects: Dryness, itching, burning, stinging, metallic taste in mouth, paraesthesias.
patient_info: Topical skin products are not for intravaginal therapy. Avoid exposure to strong sunlight or UV light.

name: MUPIROCIN
indications: Antibacterial: Bacterial skin infections (Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pyogenes), excluding pseudomonal infection.
dosage_schedule: Apply up to 3 times a day for up to 10 days.
precautions: Renal impairment, burns, large open wounds. Discontinue if chemical irritation occurs.
adverse_effects: Burning sensation, local reactions, pruritus, rash, urticaria.
patient_info: Avoid contact with eyes. Contact health care provider if impetigo has not improved by 3-5 days.

name: SILVER SULFADIAZINE
indications: Antibacterial: Minor burns.
dosage_schedule: Apply once daily or twice daily if exudative.
precautions: G-6PD deficiency. Stop treatment immediately if blood disorders or rashes develop.
adverse_effects: Allergic reactions, argyria (after large area/prolonged use), leucopenia, burning.
patient_info: N/A

name: AMOROLFINE
indications: Antifungal: Fungal nail infections, dermatophyte infections, yeast infections.
dosage_schedule: Nails: Apply 1–2 times a week (6 months for fingers, 9–12 months for toes). Skin: Apply once daily for 4 weeks.
precautions: Hypersensitivity. Avoid contact with ears, eyes, and mucous membranes. Caution in children likely to suck digits.
adverse_effects: Burning sensation, erythema, hypersensitivity reactions, itching.
patient_info: Avoid nail varnish or artificial nails during treatment. Filing and cleansing nails before lacquer application is necessary.

name: CLOTRIMAZOLE
indications: Antifungal: Tinea pedis, T. cruris, T. corporis, T. versicolor, Cutaneous candidiasis.
dosage_form_strength: Cream: 1% w/w; Gel: 1% w/w; Solution: 1% w/w.
dosage_schedule: Apply 2-3 times daily for 4-6 weeks.
precautions: Avoid contact with eyes and mucous membranes.
adverse_effects: Local irritation, erythema, hypersensitivity reactions, mild burning sensation.
patient_info: Treatment should be discontinued if side effects are severe.

name: GENTIAN VIOLET
indications: Antifungal: Cutaneous/mucocutaneous infections caused by Candida albicans.
dosage_schedule: Local application: Apply locally 2-3 times daily.
contraindications: Avoid use in ulcerated lesions, broken skin, or mucous membranes.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Irritation, mucous membrane ulcerations.
patient_info: N/A

name: MICONAZOLE NITRATE
indications: Antifungal: Fungal skin infections, nail infections, oral fungal infection, vaginal candidiasis.
dosage_schedule: Skin: Apply twice daily for 10 days after lesions heal. Nails: Apply 1-2 times a day.
precautions: Avoid contact with eyes and mucous membranes.
adverse_effects: Local irritation and burning.
patient_info: Contact with eyes and mucous membranes should be avoided.

name: NYSTATIN
indications: Antifungal: Mucocutaneous infection, vaginal infections.
dosage_schedule: Mucocutaneous: Apply q8-12h for 2 weeks. Vaginal: Insert 1 tab/day qHS for 2 weeks.
precautions: Cream is preferred over ointment for intertriginous areas. Moist lesions best treated with powder.
adverse_effects: Contact dermatitis, SJS (rare).
patient_info: Report if hypersensitivity occurs.

name: SERTACONAZOLE
indications: Antifungal: Tinea pedis.
dosage_schedule: Apply BID for 4 weeks.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Not for ophthalmic, oral, or intravaginal use.
precautions: Cross-reactivity with other imidazole antifungals may occur.
adverse_effects: Contact dermatitis, dry skin, burning, hyperpigmentation.
patient_info: Apply enough to cover affected area and surrounding healthy skin.

name: TERBINAFINE
indications: Antifungal: Tinea infections (pedis, corporis, cruris).
dosage_schedule: Apply 1–2 times a day for 1–2 weeks.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Not for oral, intravaginal, or ophthalmic use.
precautions: Maximum treatment duration: 4 weeks.
adverse_effects: Erythema, hypersensitivity reactions, itching, local irritation.
patient_info: Avoid contact with eyes and mucous membranes.

name: BENZYL BENZOATE
indications: Parasitic: Scabies.
dosage_schedule: Apply over whole body; wash off after 24 hours. A third application may be required.
precautions: Dilute for use in children. Avoid contact with eyes and mucous membranes. Avoid broken or infected skin.
adverse_effects: Burning sensation (especially on genitalia), rashes, skin irritation.
patient_info: Suspend breastfeeding until product is washed off.

name: IVERMECTIN
indications: Parasitic/Anti-acne: Lice, inflammatory lesions of Rosacea.
dosage_schedule: Lice: Apply 0.5% lotion to dry hair for 10 minutes then rinse. Rosacea: Apply 1% cream to affected area once daily.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Not for oral, ophthalmic, or intravaginal use.
precautions: Administer to children only under direct adult supervision to prevent ingestion.
adverse_effects: Conjunctivitis, ocular hyperemia, eye irritation, dry skin, burning.
patient_info: For Rosacea, use a pea-size amount for each area of face. Avoid eyes and lips.

name: PERMETHRIN
indications: Parasitic: Scabies, body lice, head lice.
dosage_schedule: Scabies/Lice: Apply over whole body and wash off after 8-12 hours; repeat after 7 days if necessary.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Do not use on broken or infected skin.
precautions: Avoid contact with eyes. Medical supervision required for infants 2 months – 2 years.
adverse_effects: Local irritation, rashes, itching, erythema.
patient_info: Avoid contact with eyes. For external use only.

name: ACICLOVIR
indications: Viral: Herpes labialis, genital herpes, herpetic keratitis.
dosage_schedule: Labialis: Apply 5 times daily for 4 days. Genital: Apply every 3 hours (6 times daily) for 7 days.
precautions: Not for use on eye or inside mouth. Caution in immunocompromised patients.
adverse_effects: Burning, stinging, pruritus, dry lips, angioedema.
patient_info: Avoid physical contact when lesions are present. Use rubber gloves when applying to prevent autoinoculation.

name: CLOBETASONE BUTYRATE
indications: Inflammatory: Eczemas and dermatitis of all types.
dosage_schedule: Apply 1–2 times a day thinly. Limit treatment to 2 weeks.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Monotherapy for primary bacterial infections. Use on face, axilla, or groin.
precautions: Do not use with occlusive dressings. Maintenance between more potent steroid courses.
adverse_effects: Hyperglycemia, folliculitis, hypertrichosis, skin irritation.
patient_info: Apply thinly as directed.

name: CLOBETASOL PROPIONATE
indications: Inflammatory: Corticosteroid responsive dermatoses, scalp psoriasis, plaque psoriasis.
dosage_schedule: Apply 1–2 times a day for up to 2 weeks; max 50g per week.
precautions: Do not use with occlusive dressings. Limit use to 2 weeks.
adverse_effects: Hyperglycemia, burning, skin atrophy, acne.
patient_info: Avoid prolonged use.

name: DITHRANOL (ANTHRALIN)
indications: Inflammatory: Psoriasis.
dosage_schedule: 0.1–0.5% suitable for overnight treatment. 1–2% cream for maximum 1 hour.
precautions: Avoid sensitive areas of skin; avoid use near eyes.
adverse_effects: Local burning, irritation, stains hair and skin.
patient_info: Hands should be protected by gloves. Avoid contact with normal skin. Can stain fabrics.

name: FLUOCINOLONE ACETONIDE
indications: Inflammatory: Severe inflammatory skin disorders, Psoriasis.
dosage_schedule: Apply 1–2 times a day thinly.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity; use on face, axillae, or groin.
precautions: Do not use with occlusive dressings.
adverse_effects: Hyperglycemia, burning, folliculitis.
patient_info: Do not apply medicine for long periods of time.

name: FLUTICASONE
indications: Inflammatory: Dermatitis and eczemas unresponsive to less potent steroids, Psoriasis.
dosage_schedule: Apply 1–2 times a day thinly.
contraindications: Children under 2 months, skin infections, skin atrophy.
precautions: Not to use with occlusive dressings.
adverse_effects: HPA axis suppression, Cushing syndrome, hypertrichosis.
patient_info: Apply sparingly in a thin film and rub gently.

name: HYDROCORTISONE
indications: Inflammatory: Mild inflammatory skin disorders, nappy rash.
dosage_schedule: Apply 1–2 times a day for 2 weeks. Nappy rash: Max 1 week.
contraindications: Broken or infected skin (cold sores, athlete's foot). Use on face or ano-genital region.
precautions: HPA suppression risk if used >2 weeks at high potency.
adverse_effects: Burning, folliculitis, striae.
patient_info: Apply for short period only.

name: MOMETASONE FUROATE
indications: Inflammatory: Severe inflammatory skin disorders, Psoriasis.
dosage_schedule: Apply once daily thinly.
precautions: Avoid application over large areas or under occlusive dressings (systemic absorption risk).
adverse_effects: Burning, tingling, pruritus, adrenal suppression (if overused).
patient_info: Discontinue use if irritation occurs.

name: TACROLIMUS
indications: Inflammatory: Atopic eczema, Seborrheic Dermatitis, Vitiligo, Lichen sclerosus.
dosage_schedule: Short-term: Apply twice daily until lesion clears. Prevention: Apply twice weekly.
contraindications: Lactation. Malignant skin lesions. Congenital epidermal barrier defect.
precautions: Avoid UV light (sunlight, sunlamps). Avoid contact with eyes and mucous membranes.
adverse_effects: Application-site infections, Kaposi’s varicelliform eruption, rash.
interactions: Risk of facial flushing and skin irritation with alcohol consumption.
patient_info: Avoid use in case of burning sensation or known hypersensitivity.

name: ACITRETIN
indications: Retinoid: Psoriasis, severe congenital ichthyosis, Darier’s disease.
dosage_schedule: Initially 25–30 mg daily for 2–4 weeks; adjusted to 25–50 mg daily; max 75 mg.
precautions: Highly teratogenic. Avoid excessive sunlight. Monitor liver function and serum lipids.
adverse_effects: Cheilitis, alopecia, hypertriglyceridemia, skin peeling, hyperostosis.
interactions: Alcohol converts acitretin to etretinate (remains in body for years). Tetracyclines increase intracranial pressure.
patient_info: Females must avoid pregnancy for 3 years after last dose. Totally abstain from ethanol during and 2 months after treatment.

name: ADAPALENE
indications: Retinoid/Anti-acne: Mild to moderate acne vulgaris.
dosage_schedule: Apply once daily thinly in the evening.
contraindications: Pregnancy. Apply to cuts, abrasions, or sunburnt skin.
precautions: Avoid accumulation in angles of nose, eyes, or mouth. Avoid UV light exposure.
adverse_effects: Skin irritation, erythema, scaling, stinging.
patient_info: Use appropriate sunscreen. If skin is dry, start with alternate day application.

name: ISOTRETINOIN
indications: Retinoid/Anti-acne: Acne vulgaris, ichthyosiform disorders.
dosage_schedule: Initially 500 micrograms/kg daily; increased if necessary to 1 mg/kg for 16–24 weeks.
precautions: Monitor for depression. Risk of dry eye/keratitis. Avoid use with abrasive cleaners.
adverse_effects: Anaemia, epistaxis, skin scaling, epidermal fragility, raised triglycerides/LFTs.
interactions: Alcohol increases teratogenicity. Tetracyclines increase intracranial hypertension risk.
patient_info: Report signs of depression. Do not crush or chew capsules. Urine may be reddish.

name: TAZAROTENE
indications: Retinoid: Psoriasis and acne.
dosage_schedule: Apply once daily usually for 12 weeks, apply in the evening.
precautions: Avoid contact with eczematous skin, eyes, face, or hair-covered scalp. Effective contraception required.
adverse_effects: Burning, contact dermatitis, desquamation, worsening of psoriasis.
patient_info: Avoid excessive UV light. Do not apply emollients within 1 hour. Wash hands immediately after use.

name: COAL TAR
indications: Coal tar: Psoriasis, Chronic atopic eczema, Seborrhoeic dermatitis.
dosage_schedule: Eczema (Paste): 1–3 times a day. Shampoo: 100 ml per bath. Seborrhoeic: Shampoo every 2–3 days.
contraindications: Broken or inflamed skin; avoid eye area, genital area, or mucosal areas.
precautions: Avoid application to face or skin flexures.
adverse_effects: Acne-like eruptions, photosensitivity, skin irritation.
patient_info: May stain skin, hair and fabric.

name: CALCIPOTRIOL
indications: Vitamin D analogue: Psoriasis.
dosage_schedule: Apply 1–2 times a day. Max 5 mg (100g ointment) per week.
precautions: Avoid exposure to sunlight/sun lamps. Avoid use on face. Risk of hypercalcaemia in erythrodermic psoriasis.
adverse_effects: Local skin reactions, paraesthesia, aggravation of psoriasis.
patient_info: Wash hands thoroughly after application to avoid transfer to other areas.

name: ALUMINIUM CHLORIDE HEXAHYDRATE
indications: Antiperspirant: Hyperhidrosis, bromidrosis, prevention of tinea pedis.
dosage_schedule: Apply once daily at night to dry skin; wash off next morning.
precautions: Avoid contact with eyes/mucous membranes. Do not shave axillae within 12 hours of use.
adverse_effects: Skin irritation.
patient_info: Avoid contact with clothing. Do not use near open flame.

name: GLYCOPYRRONIUM BROMIDE (GLYCOPYRROLATE)
indications: Antimuscarinic: Hyperhidrosis of axilla/face, Frey’s syndrome.
dosage_schedule: Treat only 1 site at a time; max 2 sites in 24 hours. Do not wash for 3-4 hours.
precautions: Avoid contact with nose, mouth, and eyes.
adverse_effects: Tingling at site, dryness.
patient_info: Cream based products have short expiry (3 months).

name: FLUOROURACIL
indications: Antimetabolite/Photodamage: Actinic keratoses, superficial malignant lesions.
dosage_schedule: Apply 1–2 times a day for 3–4 weeks. Max skin area 500 cm².
precautions: Avoid contact with eyes and mucous membranes. Do not apply to bleeding lesions.
adverse_effects: Burning, crusting, soreness at application site.
patient_info: Apply with nonmetallic applicator or gloved hands. Wash hands immediately if fingertips are used.

name: DOXEPIN
indications: Antipruritus: Pruritus (eczema).
dosage_schedule: Apply up to 3 g 3–4 times a day thinly. Max 12 g per day.
contraindications: Urinary retention, closed-angle glaucoma, prostatic hypertrophy.
precautions: Risk of QT prolongation. Coverage should be <10% of body surface area.
adverse_effects: Dizziness, drowsiness.
interactions: Potentiated by alcohol. Do not use with MAO inhibitors.
patient_info: Drowsiness may affect performance of skilled tasks like driving.

name: AZELAIC ACID
indications: Anticomedonal/Depigmenting: Facial acne vulgaris, rosacea, melasma.
dosage_schedule: Apply twice daily.
precautions: Avoid contact with eyes, mouth, and mucous membranes. Monitor for hypopigmentation in dark complexions.
adverse_effects: Local irritation, burning, stinging.
patient_info: Avoid concurrent use of alcoholic cleansers or peeling agents.

name: SELENIUM SULPHIDE
indications: Essential trace element: Seborrhoeic dermatitis, dandruff, Tinea versicolor.
dosage_schedule: Seborrhoeic: Twice weekly for 2 weeks. Tinea versicolor: Daily for 7 days (leave on for 10 min).
precautions: Not for ophthalmic, oral, or anal use.
adverse_effects: Local irritation, tremors, lower abdominal pain.
patient_info: Avoid using 48 hours before or after hair coloring or perming.

name: MINOXIDIL
indications: Alopecia: Androgenetic alopecia.
dosage_schedule: Apply 1 ml twice daily to affected areas of scalp.
precautions: Avoid contact with broken or inflamed skin. Avoid inhalation of spray mist. Avoid occlusive dressings.
adverse_effects: Headache, local irritation.
interactions: Avoid topical drugs which enhance absorption.
patient_info: Ensure hair and scalp are dry before application. Treatment must continue long term or new hair will be lost.

name: EFLORNITHINE
indications: Hirsutism: Adjunct to laser therapy for facial hirsutism in women.
dosage_schedule: Apply twice daily thinly.
precautions: Discontinue if no improvement after 4 months.
adverse_effects: Stinging at site, rash, alopecia, anorexia.
patient_info: Must be rubbed in thoroughly. Do not wash treated area for 4 hours after application.

name: CHLORHEXIDINE
indications: Cleanser/Antiseptic: Skin disinfection, umbilical cord stump care.
dosage_schedule: Pre-op: Dilute 1 in 10 (0.5%). General disinfection: Dilute 1 in 100 (0.05%).
contraindications: Do not use in body cavities (deep wound cleansing). Not for presurgery of face/head.
precautions: Avoid contact with brain, eyes, meninges, and middle ear.
adverse_effects: Chemical burns in preterm neonates.
patient_info: External use only. Avoid contact with eyes.

name: POTASSIUM PERMANGANATE
indications: Cleanser/Antiseptic: suppurating eczematous reactions and wounds.
dosage_schedule: Wet compress twice daily. For dressings, use 1 in 40,000 to 1:25,000 solution.
precautions: Irritant to mucous membranes. Concentrated solution causes erosion.
adverse_effects: Corrosion, burns, pain.
patient_info: Can stain clothing, skin and nails. Dilute in tub until light pink. Discard if too red.

name: CAPSAICIN
indications: Depigmenting/Pain relief: Post-herpetic neuralgia, musculoskeletal pain, diabetic neuropathy, psoriasis.
dosage_schedule: Apply to affected area TID or QID for 3-4 weeks.
precautions: Do not apply to face or scalp. Avoid eyes and mucous membranes.
adverse_effects: Transient increased pain, burning, erythema.
patient_info: Treated area may be sensitive to heat (hot water, sunlight) for several days.

name: HYDROQUINONE
indications: Depigmenting: Melasma, post inflammatory hyperpigmentation.
dosage_schedule: Local application twice a day or at night.
precautions: Exogenous ochronosis risk in black skin. Do not apply near eyes or to abraded skin.
adverse_effects: Mild skin irritation, sensitization, inflammatory reaction.
patient_info: Avoid unnecessary exposure to sunlight.

name: PSORALENS
indications: Depigmenting: Vitiligo, psoriasis, cutaneous T cell lymphoma.
dosage_schedule: Local application 30 min before UVA exposure. Oral: 0.5-0.7 mg/kg twice a week, 2 hours before exposure.
precautions: Ensure skin is clean and dry. Avoid other artificial UV treatments.
adverse_effects: Irritation, blistering, nausea, cataract formation (if eyes unprotected).
patient_info: UV400 standard eye protection must be worn for 24 hours from taking tablets. Use high SPF sunscreen. Risk of sun burning.

name: CHLORAMPHENICOL
indications: Superficial bacterial infection (broad spectrum antibiotics).
dosage_schedule: Bacterial conjunctival infection: Eye drop: 1 drop 4-6 times a day for 5 to 7 days; Eye ointment: apply twice daily (at night if drops used during day).
precautions: Avoid unless essential; theoretical risk of bone marrow toxicity.
adverse_effects: Transient stinging.
patient_info: N/A

name: CIPROFLOXACIN
indications: Superficial bacterial infections, corneal ulcer.
dosage_schedule: Superficial infection: Eye drop: 1 drop 4-6 times daily (max 5-7 days). Eye ointment: 1.25 cm 3 times daily for 2 days then twice daily for 5 days. Corneal ulcer: 1 drop 2 hourly until ulcer heals (titrated to response).
precautions: Avoid wearing contact lens.
adverse_effects: Corneal deposits (reversible), ocular discomfort, ocular hyperemia, taste disturbance, contact dermatitis.
interactions: Not to be given with tizanidine (α2 agonist).
patient_info: Remove contact lenses before use.

name: GENTAMICIN
indications: Bacterial eye infection, corneal ulcer.
dosage_schedule: Bacterial conjunctival infection: 1 drop 4-6 times daily; reduce frequency as controlled and continue for 48 hrs after healing. Fortified gentamicin can be used for corneal ulcer.
precautions: Monitoring for overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms.
adverse_effects: Transient irritation, burning, itching, overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms including fungi.
patient_info: N/A

name: LEVOFLOXACIN
indications: Bacterial corneal ulcer.
dosage_schedule: Bacterial corneal ulcer: apply every 2 hours for first 2 days (8 times a day), then 4 times a day for 3 days. Titrated according to response.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Dry eye, corneal deposits, contact dermatitis.
patient_info: N/A

name: OFLOXACIN
indications: Bacterial conjunctivitis, corneal ulcer.
dosage_schedule: Bacterial conjunctivitis/corneal ulcer: Apply every 2-4 hours for first 2 days then reduce to 4 times a day for maximum 10 days.
precautions: See under ciprofloxacin.
adverse_effects: Irritation and contact dermatitis.
patient_info: N/A

name: POLYMYXIN B
indications: Superficial infection of eye (effective for pseudomonas aeruginosa), prophylaxis of infection in ocular surgery.
dosage_form_strength: Eye ointment containing polymyxin B sulfate (190,000 units) and bacitracin zinc (500 units/gm).
dosage_schedule: Same as ciprofloxacin.
precautions: Not given systemically.
adverse_effects: Irritation and contact dermatitis.
patient_info: N/A

name: TETRACYCLINE
indications: Superficial bacterial infection, chlamydial infection, trachoma, chemical injury, blepharitis.
dosage_form_strength: Eye ointment 1%; Tablet/capsule 250 mg or 500 mg.
dosage_schedule: Given once or twice a day.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity; lactation; children less than 12 years.
precautions: Topical use may result in overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms like fungi; SLE.
adverse_effects: N/A
interactions: With topical corticosteroid, may mask clinical signs of infection.
patient_info: N/A

name: ACYCLOVIR
indications: Herpes simplex epithelial keratitis and herpes zoster ophthalmicus associated keratitis.
dosage_form_strength: Eye ointment 3%, Tablet 400 mg and 800 mg.
dosage_schedule: Ointment: apply 5 times a day for 2 weeks to 3 weeks.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Local burning and stinging, blepharitis, superficial punctate keratitis.
patient_info: Can be used in immunocompromised.

name: GANCICLOVIR
indications: Herpes simplex epithelial keratitis, Herpes zoster ophthalmicus, CMV retinitis.
dosage_schedule: Herpes simplex: 5 times a day until complete re-epithelization, then 3 times daily for 7 days (total 21 days). CMV retinitis: IV 5 mg/kg infusion over 1 hour q12 hrly for 14-21 days; maintenance 1000 mg 3 times a day.
precautions: Use with caution in pregnancy and lactation.
adverse_effects: Local irritation and visual disturbance.
patient_info: N/A

name: IDOXURIDINE
indications: HSV keratitis, CMV, varicella zoster.
dosage_schedule: 1 drop every hour during day and every 2 hrs at night until lesions do not stain with fluorescence (usual 21 days). Ointment: q4hrly during day and once before bedtime.
precautions: Do not give steroid with it locally. Caution in pregnancy and lactation.
adverse_effects: Local irritation, edema of eyelids, photophobia, superficial punctate keratitis, corneal filaments.
patient_info: N/A

name: FLUCONAZOLE
indications: Keratomycosis (fungal keratitis).
dosage_schedule: 1 drop instilled on affected eye every 2-4 hours according to severity.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Conjunctival hyperemia and irritation.
patient_info: Miconazole can be administered as subconjunctival and intra-vitreal injection for fungal endophthalmitis.

name: NATAMYCIN
indications: All keratitis especially fusarium solani keratitis, aspergillus.
dosage_schedule: Start with 1 drop every 1-2 hours on day 1, then reduce to 1 drop every 3-4 hourly for 2-3 weeks.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Conjunctival hyperemia and irritation.
patient_info: N/A

name: BETAMETHASONE
indications: Severe ocular inflammation, uveitis, endophthalmitis, post-operative inflammation.
dosage_schedule: Eye drop: apply every 1-2 hour until controlled then decrease frequency. Eye ointment: apply 2-4 times a day (alternately apply at night in combination with drops).
contraindications: Acute untreated purulent bacterial, viral and fungal infections.
precautions: Check intra-ocular pressure frequently in prolonged therapy. Protect from light.
adverse_effects: Glaucoma, posterior capsular cataract, adrenal suppression (prolonged use), corneal thinning, scleral thinning, blurred vision.
patient_info: Check intra-ocular pressure frequently.

name: DICLOFENAC
indications: Inhibits intra-operative miosis, post-operative inflammation, seasonal allergic conjunctivitis, mild ocular surface inflammation.
dosage_schedule: For post-op. inflammation: 1 drop 4 times a day for 1-2 weeks.
precautions: Caution in pregnancy, lactation, and children. Protect from light.
adverse_effects: Ocular irritation, burning, tearing, conjunctival hyperemia, superficial punctate keratitis, retardation of re-epithelialization.
patient_info: N/A

name: FLUOROMETHOLONE
indications: Local treatment of inflammation (short term).
dosage_schedule: Child/adult: apply 1 drop 2 to 6 hours according to severity.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Adrenal suppression (prolonged use), glaucoma, corneal/scleral thinning.
patient_info: N/A

name: FLURBIPROFEN
indications: Ocular surface inflammation, inhibition of intra-operative miosis.
dosage_schedule: Before surgery: 1 drop every 30 min for 4 times (max 4 drops). For inflammation: 1 drop 4 times a day for 2-4 weeks.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to NSAIDS; HSV keratitis (dendritic); pregnancy.
precautions: Caution in lactation.
adverse_effects: Ocular irritation, conjunctival hyperemia, superficial punctate keratitis.
patient_info: N/A

name: INDOMETHACIN
indications: Cystoid macular degeneration, anterior uveitis, vernal conjunctivitis, prevention of intra-op miosis, episcleritis, scleritis, gastric ulcer.
dosage_form_strength: Tablets 25 mg; Sustained release tablets 75 mg.
dosage_schedule: 25 mg TDS or SR 75 mg OD for 7-10 days.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Corneal changes and deposits, ocular irritation, conjunctival hyperemia, superficial punctate keratitis.
patient_info: N/A

name: KETOROLAC
indications: Superficial ocular surface inflammation, pain, ocular itching (allergic conjunctivitis), postoperative inflammation, cystic macular edema.
dosage_form_strength: Eye drops 0.5%; Tablet 10 mg; Injectable solution 15-30 mg/ml.
dosage_schedule: Ophthalmic: 1 drop 4 times daily (7-10 days for inflammation; 3-4 weeks for edema). Oral: 10 mg every 4-6 hourly (max 40 mg/day, 7 days). Parenteral: 60 mg IM/30 mg IV (max 120 mg daily, 2 days).
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to aspirin/NSAIDS; asthma; coagulation disorders; labor; renal impairment; cerebrovascular bleeding.
precautions: Elderly, weight <50 kg, heart failure. Monitor renal function closely.
adverse_effects: GI ulcer/bleeding, bronchospasm, psychosis, dry mouth, fever, bradycardia, transient stinging, local irritation.
patient_info: N/A

name: PREDNISOLONE
indications: Anti-inflammatory agent (external/intra ocular), post-operative inflammation.
dosage_schedule: 1 drop every 1-2 hour until controlled then taper.
precautions: Lactation, old age, children. Long term therapy: check Potassium, blood/urine glucose, and H-P-A axis suppression.
adverse_effects: Adrenal suppression (prolonged use), glaucoma, corneal/scleral thinning.
patient_info: Monitor glucose levels and BP.

name: KETOTIFEN
indications: Allergic conjunctivitis.
dosage_schedule: 2 times daily.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Punctate corneal epithelial erosions, transient burning, headache, photophobia, dry eyes.
patient_info: N/A

name: OLOPATADINE
indications: Allergic conjunctivitis, vernal keratoconjunctivitis.
dosage_schedule: 2 times (0.1%) daily for max 4 months; 0.2% once daily only.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Ocular-local irritation, hyperemia, headache, rhinitis.
patient_info: N/A

name: SODIUM CHROMOGLYCATE
indications: Allergic conjunctivitis, allergic keratoconjunctivitis.
dosage_schedule: 4 times daily (2%) and 2 times daily (4%).
precautions: Do not exceed frequency of administration.
adverse_effects: Transient burning.
patient_info: N/A

name: ACETAZOLAMIDE
indications: Open-angle glaucoma, angle-closure glaucoma (preoperatively if surgery delayed).
dosage_schedule: Acute attack: Adult: PO/IV 500 mg stat followed by 250mg TID or QID.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to sulfonamide; severe renal/hepatic disease; electrolyte imbalance; hypercalciuria; COPD.
precautions: Long-term use in non-congestive angle-closure glaucoma.
adverse_effects: Seizures, confusion, cholestatic jaundice, metabolic acidosis.
interactions: Increases action of Amphetamines, Phenytoin, quinidine; toxicity of salicylate and cyclosporine; cardiac toxicity with arsenic trioxide.
patient_info: N/A

name: BIMATOPROST
indications: Open angle glaucoma or ocular HTN, Hypotrichosis of eyelashes.
dosage_schedule: 1 drop in affected eye OD evening.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity; children <16 years; aphakia/pseudoaphakia with torn posterior lens capsule.
precautions: Risk factors for macular edema, active intraocular inflammation (uveitis).
adverse_effects: Cataract, increased iris pigmentation, blepharitis, eyelid darkening, conjunctival edema, hypertrichosis, macular edema.
patient_info: N/A

name: BRIMONIDINE
indications: Glaucoma (IOP lowering) with increase in optic nerve head perfusion.
dosage_schedule: 1 drop twice daily.
precautions: Coronary and cerebral insufficiency, hepatic and renal impairment; safety not established in children.
adverse_effects: Conjunctival blending, eyelid retraction, discomfort, ocular allergy (blepharoconjunctivitis), dry mouth, headache, lethargy.
patient_info: Wait 15 mins after instilling drops before putting on contact lenses.

name: DORZOLAMIDE
indications: Elevated intraocular pressure, ocular hypertension, open-angle glaucoma.
dosage_schedule: Instill 1 drop of a 2% solution into affected eye TDS.
precautions: Hepatic/renal disease; electrolyte disturbance. Notify if vision changes.
adverse_effects: Headache, blurred vision, allergy, burning/stinging, corneal epithelial toxicity.
interactions: Increased effects of carbonic anhydrase inhibitors, salicylate.
patient_info: N/A

name: LATANOPROST
indications: Open angle glaucoma, ocular hypertension.
dosage_schedule: Instill 1 drop in each affected eye every night.
precautions: Eye infection, renal/hepatic function impairment, intra ocular inflammation.
adverse_effects: Conjunctival hyperemia, iris color change (brown pigmentation), ocular pruritis, xerophthalmia, blepharitis, cataract, rash.
patient_info: N/A

name: MANNITOL
indications: Reduce elevated IOP.
dosage_schedule: 1-2 g/kg or 5ml/kg IV infused over 30-60 minutes up to 4 times/day.
contraindications: Anuria, severe renal disease, pulmonary edema, intracranial bleeding, heart failure, dehydration.
precautions: Use with caution in CCF and Hypertension.
adverse_effects: Renal impairment, pulmonary edema, heart failure, hyponatremia, headache.
patient_info: N/A

name: PILOCARPINE
indications: Acute-angle-closure glaucoma, open angle glaucoma.
dosage_schedule: 1 drop 4 times a day.
contraindications: Avoid in nuclear/subcapsular cataract, neovascular/uveitis glaucoma, asthma, retinal detachment, iritis.
precautions: Use with caution in pregnancy and lactation.
adverse_effects: Accommodative spasm, miosis, follicular conjunctivitis, band keratopathy, retinal detachment, nausea, bronchial spasm.
patient_info: Systemic side effects minimized by punctal occlusion.

name: TIMOLOL
indications: Open angle glaucoma, angle closure glaucoma, lowering IOP after cataract surgery.
dosage_schedule: 1 drop twice daily.
precautions: Caution in DM, thyroid disorders, and diminished myocardial contractility.
adverse_effects: Itching, conjunctivitis, keratitis, bradycardia, heart block.
patient_info: N/A

name: TRAVOPROST
indications: Reduction of elevated IOP in open angle glaucoma or ocular HTN.
dosage_schedule: N/A
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Ocular hyperemia, decreased visual acuity, cataract, keratitis, hypercholesterolemia, HTN, hypotension.
patient_info: N/A

name: ATROPINE
indications: Cycloplegic refraction in children, cyclospasm, neovascular glaucoma.
dosage_schedule: 1 drop up to 3 times daily.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Local irritation, raised IOP, dermatitis, flushing, dryness of skin, blurred vision.
patient_info: N/A

name: CYCLOPENTOLATE
indications: Same as atropine.
dosage_schedule: 1 drop every 5-10 minutes, not to exceed maximum 3 times for cycloplegic refraction.
precautions: Same as atropine.
adverse_effects: Same as atropine.
patient_info: N/A

name: HOMATROPINE
indications: Same as atropine.
dosage_schedule: 1 drop twice to thrice daily.
precautions: Same as atropine.
adverse_effects: N/A
patient_info: N/A

name: PHENYLEPHRINE
indications: Uveitis to prevent posterior synechia, mydriatics.
dosage_schedule: N/A
contraindications: Angle closure glaucoma; children and elderly.
precautions: Hypertension, cardiac disorders, diabetes mellitus.
adverse_effects: Burning eye pain, blurred vision, allergic conjunctivitis, systemic sympathomimetic effects.
patient_info: N/A

name: TROPICAMIDE
indications: Refraction procedure, mydriasis for fundus evaluation, corneal ulcer, uveitis.
dosage_schedule: 1 drop every 5-10 minutes three times for fundus evaluation; 1 drop three times for therapeutic purpose.
precautions: Store at 8-15°C.
adverse_effects: Increased IOP, burning, photophobia, systemic effects.
patient_info: N/A

name: ACETYLCYSTEINE
indications: Dry eye.
dosage_schedule: Instill 1 drop 3-4 times a day and as required.
precautions: Usually used together with hypromellose.
adverse_effects: Temporary blurring of vision.
patient_info: N/A

name: BEVACIZUMAB
indications: Choroidal neovascularization, macular edema (CRVO, diabetic).
dosage_schedule: 1.25 mg by intra-vitreal injection repeated after 4-6 weeks.
precautions: Ocular/peri-ocular infection, irreversible ischemic visual loss, diabetic patients with HbA1C>12%, history of strokes/TIA.
adverse_effects: Transient rise in IOP, sterile/bacterial endophthalmitis, iridocyclitis, superficial punctate keratitis, cataract, retinal disorders.
patient_info: N/A

name: BUPIVACAINE
indications: Local anaesthesia.
dosage_schedule: 0.5% infiltrated.
precautions: Hepatic impairment.
adverse_effects: N/A
patient_info: N/A

name: CARBOMER
indications: Dry eyes including keratoconjunctivitis, unstable tear film.
dosage_schedule: Apply 3-4 times a day or when required.
precautions: Remove contact lens before use.
adverse_effects: N/A
patient_info: Do not touch the tip of the vial.

name: CYCLOSPORINE
indications: Corneal melting (autoimmune), graft rejection prevention, keratoconjunctivitis (Vernal/HSV), dry eye.
dosage_schedule: 1 drop two times a day approximately 12 hours apart in each eye.
precautions: May be used with artificial tears; allow 15 minutes interval between products.
adverse_effects: Ocular burning, conjunctival hyperemia, discharge, eye pain, pruritus.
patient_info: N/A

name: FLUORESCEIN SODIUM
indications: Diagnostic staining, ophthalmic angiography.
dosage_schedule: N/A
precautions: Protect from light.
adverse_effects: N/A
patient_info: N/A

name: HYPROMELLOSE
indications: Dry eye, moisten hardened contact lens.
dosage_schedule: Put 1 drop 3-4 times a day as required (may be used hourly).
precautions: Hypersensitivity. Contains Benzalkonium chloride (discolors soft contact lens).
adverse_effects: Eye irritation, blurred vision, stickiness of eyelashes.
patient_info: Remove contact lens prior to application and wait at least 15 min before reinserting. Discontinue if headache/vision changes occur.

name: LIQUID PARAFFIN
indications: Dry eyes (night use), recurrent epithelial erosion.
dosage_schedule: Usually applied at bedtime.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Should not be used while wearing contact lens.
precautions: Apply other drops first then wait 5 mins before ointment.
adverse_effects: Irritation, burning, stinging, temporary blurring of vision.
patient_info: N/A

name: POLYVINYL ALCOHOL
indications: Tear deficiency (useful when ocular surface mucin decreased).
dosage_schedule: Child/adult: apply as required.
contraindications: Concomitant droxidopa, MAOI, or furazolidone in last 14 days.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: See under hypromellose.
patient_info: N/A

name: SODIUM CHLORIDE
indications: Short term relief of corneal edema, comfort drops for lens removal, tear deficiency, bullous keratopathy.
dosage_schedule: Apply as required.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Eye discomfort, burning, redness, temporary blurred vision.
patient_info: Remove contact lens; do not touch the tip of the vial.

name: TRIAMCINOLONE
indications: Sympathetic ophthalmia, uveitis (unresponsive to steroids), hemangioma, chalazion, macular edema.
dosage_form_strength: Injectable suspension 4 mg/0.05 ml or 4 mg/0.1 ml.
dosage_schedule: N/A
precautions: Prolonged use: subcapsular cataracts, glaucoma (optic nerve damage risk), secondary fungal/viral infections. Proper aseptic technique is mandatory.
adverse_effects: Abnormal sensation, cataract, exophthalmos, glaucoma, increased IOP, vitreous detachment, secondary intraocular infection.
patient_info: N/A

name: CHLORAMPHENICOL
indications: Bacterial infection in otitis externa.
dosage_schedule: Intra-aural: 2–3 drops in affected ear, 2–3 times a day. For maximum benefit, the patient should lie with the affected ear up for several minutes.
precautions: Avoid prolonged use.
adverse_effects: Rash, headache.
patient_info: Avoid touching the ear with the tip of the dropper to prevent contamination.

name: CIPROFLOXACIN
indications: Bacterial infection in otitis externa.
dosage_schedule: Intra-aural: 2–3 drops in affected ear, 2 times a day for 7 days.
precautions: Concurrent tizanidine administration. Avoid prolonged use.
adverse_effects: Local sensitivity.
patient_info: Report any signs of local irritation or worsening symptoms.

name: GENTAMICIN
indications: Chronic suppurative otitis media with perforated tympanic membranes.
dosage_schedule: Intra aural: 2–3 drops in the affected ear 4–5 times a day (including a dose at bedtime).
contraindications: Patent grommet, perforated tympanic membrane (as a general rule for non-specialist use).
precautions: Avoid prolonged use to prevent aminoglycoside-induced ototoxicity.
adverse_effects: Local sensitivity.
patient_info: Follow dosing instructions strictly to avoid potential inner ear damage.

name: OFLOXACIN
indications: Chronic suppurative otitis media (CSOM) with perforated tympanic membranes, otitis externa.
dosage_schedule: CSOM with perforated membranes: 10 drops 2 times a day in affected ear for 14 days. Otitis externa: 10 drops 2 times a day in the affected ear for 7 days.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Local sensitivity, taste perversion, pruritus, dizziness, vertigo.
patient_info: Complete the full course of 14 days for CSOM even if symptoms resolve earlier.

name: CLOTRIMAZOLE
indications: Fungal infection in otitis externa.
dosage_schedule: Intraaural: 2-3 drops in the affected ear 2–3 times a day; continue for at least 14 days after disappearance of infection.
precautions: Local irritation may occur.
adverse_effects: Local irritation, local sensitivity.
patient_info: Duration of therapy is key to preventing fungal recurrence.

name: CHLORAMPHENICOL WITH DEXAMETHASONE
indications: Chronic suppurative otitis media.
dosage_schedule: Intraaural: 2-3 drops in the affected ear 2-3 times a day for 7-10 days.
contraindications: Untreated viral, fungal, or tubercular infections.
precautions: Limit duration to 10 days to avoid steroid side effects and resistance.
adverse_effects: Local irritation, steroid-related effects with prolonged use.
patient_info: Shake the suspension well before each use.

name: ALMOND OIL
indications: Soften dry or hardened ear wax and for ear wax removal.
dosage_schedule: Intraaural: Use 3-4 drops twice daily for 3-5 days. The patient should lie with the affected ear up for 5-10 minutes after the oil has been introduced.
precautions: Allow drops to warm to room temperature before use.
adverse_effects: N/A
patient_info: Lie with the affected ear facing up for 5-10 minutes after instilling.

name: SODIUM BICARBONATE
indications: Soften dry or hardened ear wax and for ear wax removal.
