dosage_schedule: Intraaural: Use 3-4 drops twice daily for 3-5 days. Allow the solution to remain in the ear (patient lying with ear up) for 5-10 minutes.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Dryness of the ear canal.
patient_info: N/A

name: ICHTHAMMOL IN GLYCERINE PACK
indications: Acute otitis externa, diffuse otitis externa.
dosage_schedule: Intraaural: Soaked thin ribbon gauge is to be placed in the ear canal for 24-48 hrs.
contraindications: Allergic to glycerin or topical medicine.
precautions: Use cautiously in pregnancy. Don’t use on broken skin.
adverse_effects: Local irritation.
patient_info: Store below 25°C.

name: AMOXICILLIN
indications: Systemic treatment for otitis media, sinusitis.
dosage_schedule: Oral, Child (1–11 months): 125 mg 3 times a day. Child (1–4 years): 250 mg 3 times a day. Child (5–11 years): 500 mg 3 times a day. 12 years and above: 500 mg 3 times a day. Dose can be increased up to 30 mg/kg or 1 g TID in severe infections.
precautions: Monitor for allergic reactions.
adverse_effects: Diarrhea, rash.
patient_info: Complete the full course even if feeling better.

name: BETAHISTINE
indications: Ménière’s disease (Chronic stage vertigo).
dosage_schedule: Oral, adult: Initially 16 mg 3 times daily, preferably with food; maintenance 24- 48 mg daily.
precautions: Use with caution in asthma or history of peptic ulcer. Not recommended in children.
adverse_effects: Gastrointestinal disturbances, headache, pruritus, rashes.
patient_info: Take with food to minimize GI upset.

name: CINNARIZINE
indications: Vestibular disorders (vertigo, tinnitus, nausea, vomiting) in Ménière’s disease, motion sickness.
dosage_schedule: Ménière’s: 12 years and above: 25 mg 3 times a day for 5-7 days. Motion sickness: child (5–11 yrs): 15 mg 2 hours before travel, then 7.5 mg every 8 hrs; 12 years and above: 30 mg 2 hours before travel, then 15 mg every 8 hrs.
contraindications: Avoid in acute porphyria, neonates, and severe liver disease.
precautions: Use with caution in renal impairment, epilepsy, glaucoma, Parkinson’s, and prostatic hypertrophy.
adverse_effects: Drowsiness, paradoxical stimulation (children), angioedema, hypotension, lichen planus, lupus-like skin reactions.
patient_info: May cause drowsiness; avoid driving or operating machinery until effect is known.

name: MUPIROCIN
indications: Eradication of nasal carriage of staphylococci, including MRSA.
dosage_schedule: Intranasal: 2–3 times a day for 5 days.
precautions: A sample should be taken 2 days after treatment to confirm eradication.
adverse_effects: Local irritation.
patient_info: Course may be repeated if sample remains positive.

name: IPRATROPIUM BROMIDE
indications: Intrinsic rhinitis.
dosage_schedule: Intranasal, >12yrs of age: 2 sprays, 2–3 times a day into each nostril.
precautions: Avoid spraying near eyes. Caution in bladder outflow obstruction, cystic fibrosis, and prostatic hyperplasia.
adverse_effects: Epistaxis, nasal dryness, pharyngitis (in children), headache, nausea.
patient_info: Point the spray nozzle away from the nasal septum.

name: OXYMETAZOLINE
indications: Acute rhinitis.
dosage_schedule: Intranasal drop, adult (0.05%): 2-3 drops into each nostril 2-3 times daily (max 7 days). Child >3 months (0.025%): 1-2 drops into each nostril twice daily (max 7 days).
precautions: Hyperthyroidism, heart disease/hypertension, diabetes, children < 3 months, glaucoma, dysuria.
adverse_effects: Local burning, sneezing; prolonged use: rebound congestion, tachycardia, arrhythmias, high BP.
patient_info: Do not use for more than 7 days continuously to avoid rebound congestion.

name: XYLOMETAZOLINE
indications: Nasal congestion.
dosage_schedule: Intranasal drop, adult (0.1%): 1-2 drops in each nostril, 1-2 times a day (max 7 days). Child >6 years (0.1%): 2–3 drops in each nostril, 2–3 times a day (max 7 days).
precautions: Use with caution in pregnancy, lactation, and elderly.
adverse_effects: Local burning, rebound congestion, palpitations, arrhythmias.
patient_info: N/A

name: GLUCOSE IN GLYCERINE
indications: Atrophic rhinitis.
dosage_schedule: Cotton swab dipped in glucose 25% in glycerine and apply in bilateral nasal cavity for 1 month twice daily; then continue once daily dosing for life or until underlying cause treated.
precautions: Ensure gentle application with cotton swabs.
adverse_effects: N/A
patient_info: N/A

name: CETIRIZINE
indications: Symptomatic treatment of allergic conditions related to ENT, urticaria, chronic idiopathic urticaria.
dosage_schedule: Oral, child (2-5 yrs): 2.5 mg twice daily. Child (6–11 yrs): 5 mg twice daily. 12 years and above: 10 mg once daily.
precautions: Use with caution in epilepsy. Renal impairment (GFR 30-50): use half dose. Renal impairment (GFR 10-30): use half dose every other day.
adverse_effects: Dry mouth, psychomotor impairment, urinary retention, blurred vision.
patient_info: May cause drowsiness.

name: TRANEXAMIC ACID
indications: Epistaxis.
dosage_schedule: Epistaxis: 1000-1500 mg every 8-12 hours for 10 days.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: See under Chapter 3 (Drugs Used in Blood).
patient_info: N/A

name: BENZALKONIUM CHLORIDE + CHOLINE SALICYLATE
indications: Aphthous ulcer, oral ulcers.
dosage_schedule: Local application, three times a day for 5 to 10 days.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Hypersensitivity reactions.
patient_info: N/A

name: CHLORHEXIDINE
indications: Aphthous ulcer, acute tonsillitis, oropharyngitis, tonsillar keratosis, gingivitis.
dosage_schedule: Gingivitis: oral rinse 15mL two times a day.
precautions: Do not use in patients who cannot gargle.
adverse_effects: Hypersensitivity reactions.
patient_info: Do not swallow the solution.

name: CHLORHEXIDINE + LIDOCAINE + METRONIDAZOLE
indications: Oral cavity laceration, aphthous ulcer, oral ulcers with high risk of infection (sutured wound).
dosage_schedule: Oral cavity lesion, local application, three times a day for 5-7 days.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Hypersensitivity reaction.
patient_info: N/A

name: HYDROGEN PEROXIDE
indications: Hemostasis in tonsillectomy, remove unhealthy slough from wounds.
dosage_schedule: Oral gargle: diluted with water (10 mL in 1L of water), used 3-4 times a day. Unhealthy wound: diluted in povidone iodine (4-5 drops in 10mL 10% PI).
precautions: Should not be used in healthy tissue. Avoid exposure to eye.
adverse_effects: Erythema, stinging, edema, pruritus, vesiculation.
patient_info: N/A

name: NYSTATIN
indications: Oropharyngeal candidiasis.
dosage_schedule: Adult and child: swish and swallow, 4-6 mL, 5 times a day for minimum 7 days (or 2 days after symptoms improve). Infant: 1-2 mL local application 4 times daily.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Irritation, sensitization (rash, urticaria, contact dermatitis).
patient_info: Keep the suspension in the mouth for as long as possible before swallowing.

name: POVIDONE IODINE
indications: Oral ulcer, wound dressing.
dosage_schedule: Oral ulcer: gargle, dilute with water and 3-4 times a day.
contraindications: Burn skin, renal impairment, thyroid disorders.
precautions: Cautious in children.
adverse_effects: Hyperthyroidism, irritation, pruritus, rashes.
patient_info: Do not swallow.

name: CEFDINIR
indications: Acute tonsillitis, acute oropharyngitis.
dosage_form_strength: Capsule: 300 mg; Oral suspension: 125 mg/5mL, 250 mg/5mL.
dosage_schedule: Adult: 600 mg once a day or 300 mg twice a day for 10 days. Child: 14 mg/kg once daily for 10 days.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Urticaria, skin rash.
patient_info: N/A

name: PENICILLIN V
indications: Tonsillitis and pharyngitis, quinsy (with metronidazole).
dosage_form_strength: Tablet: 250 mg, 500 mg; Oral suspension: 125 mg/5mL, 250 mg/5mL.
dosage_schedule: Adult (penicillin susceptible): 500 mg twice a day or 250 mg four times a day for 10 days. Child: 25-50 mg/kg/day divided q6h for 10 days.
precautions: Renal impairment.
adverse_effects: Diarrhea, nausea, vomiting.
patient_info: Take on an empty stomach (1 hour before or 2 hours after meals).

name: VALACYCLOVIR
indications: Herpes labialis.
dosage_schedule: Oral: 2 grams twice a day for one day.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Hypersensitivity reaction.
patient_info: Ensure adequate hydration during treatment.

name: PANTOPRAZOLE
indications: Laryngopharyngeal reflux.
dosage_schedule: Oral: 40 mg twice a day for 6 weeks with/without domperidone.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: N/A
patient_info: Take before meals.

name: ADRENALINE/EPINEPHRINE
indications: Anaphylaxis; As a vasoconstrictor for haemostasis.
dosage_form_strength: Prefilled syringes 0.3-0.5 ml of 1:1000; 1 ml ampoules.
dosage_schedule: Adult: 0.3 mg IM up to 0.5 mg per dose as soon as anaphylactic shock occurs. May be repeated every 5-10 minutes (total 3 doses). Children: 0.01 mg/kg.
contraindications: Do not use if the solution is colored, cloudy, or contains particulate matter.
precautions: Do not administer repeated injections at the same site (risk of tissue necrosis). Inject IM or SC into the anterolateral aspect of the thigh.
adverse_effects: Vasoconstriction, tissue necrosis.
patient_info: Always use adrenaline auto-injector first, then asthma reliever if breathing difficulty occurs. Carry an auto-injection device if there is a history of severe reactions.

name: SALBUTAMOL/ALBUTEROL
indications: Relief of bronchospasm during dental procedures in patients with reversible obstructive airway disease.
dosage_schedule: 1-2 puffs per dose. For children 6 years of age and older.
precautions: Discontinue immediately if paradoxical bronchospasm occurs.
adverse_effects: Paradoxical bronchospasm (life-threatening).
patient_info: Report immediate breathing difficulty after use.

name: ASPIRIN
indications: Suspected myocardial infarction (MI) during dental treatment.
dosage_form_strength: Tablet: 75 mg non-enteric coated; Chewable tablet 81 mg.
dosage_schedule: Administer 1 to 4 tablets (chewed and swallowed) as soon as MI attack occurs.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: N/A
patient_info: Chew the tablet thoroughly before swallowing for faster absorption during an emergency.

name: GLUCAGON
indications: Treatment of hypoglycemic shock during dental procedures.
dosage_schedule: Children (<20 kg): 0.5 mg IM, IV or SC. Adults and children (>20 kg): 1 mg IM, IV or SC. If weight unknown: children <6yrs: 0.5 mL; children 6yrs and older: 1 mL.
contraindications: Hypoglycemic patients experiencing starvation or adrenal insufficiency.
precautions: Use only if the person is unable to eat, is unconscious, or having a seizure. If conscious, oral glucose is preferred.
adverse_effects: N/A
patient_info: Blood glucose measurements should be obtained until the patient is stable.

name: GLYCERYL TRINITRATE (GTN)
indications: Relief of chest pain associated with angina pectoris during dental treatment.
dosage_form_strength: Sublingual tablet 0.5 mg; Spray 0.4 mg; Injection 1 mg/ml.
dosage_schedule: Place one sublingual tablet or 1-2 sprays under the tongue. May repeat at 5-minute intervals (total 3 doses).
precautions: If symptoms do not resolve after 3 doses, treat as acute MI.
adverse_effects: Local burning or tingling sensation.
patient_info: Must be placed under the tongue and retained until dissolved. Seek prompt medical attention if pain persists after 3 doses.

name: MIDAZOLAM
indications: Status tonic-clonic seizures in patients undergoing dental treatment.
dosage_form_strength: Injectable solution 5 mg/mL IV; Buccal (oromucosal) injection.
dosage_schedule: Adults: 10 mg. Pediatric: 1-5 years: 5 mg; 5-10 years: 7.5 mg; >10 years: 10 mg.
precautions: Rapid IV injection in neonates can result in low blood pressure and seizures.
adverse_effects: Low blood pressure, respiratory depression.
patient_info: During emergency administration, the injection can be given buccally between the cheek and gum.

name: DIPHENHYDRAMINE
indications: Allergic reactions to materials or medications used during dental procedures; alternative anesthetic agent for 'caine' allergies.
dosage_schedule: Oral: 25-50 mg q6-8h (max 300 mg/day). IV/IM: 10-50 mg (max 100 mg per dose) q4-6h (max 400 mg/day).
precautions: For local anesthesia, dilute 1 mL of 50 mg/mL with 4 mL of 0.9% NaCl to yield a 1% concentration.
adverse_effects: Greater perception of pain at injection site relative to 1% Lidocaine; risk of local tissue necrosis.
patient_info: N/A

name: AMOXICILLIN
indications: Standard general prophylaxis for endocarditis; Orodental infections; Actinomycosis; Maxillary sinusitis.
dosage_schedule: General Prophylaxis: Adult 2 g; Child 50 mg/kg (single dose 30-60 min before procedure). Infection: Adult 250-500 mg TID; Child 20-40 mg/kg/day in 3 divided doses.
contraindications: Allergy to β-lactam antibiotics (penicillins and cephalosporins).
precautions: Caution in patients with chronic renal dysfunction.
adverse_effects: GI disturbances.
patient_info: Prophylaxis is usually continued for 2 days after the procedure.

name: CLINDAMYCIN
indications: Prophylaxis for patients allergic to penicillin; Systemic treatment of dental infections.
dosage_schedule: Oral Prophylaxis: Adult 600 mg; Child 20 mg/kg (30-60 min before procedure). Infection: Adult 150-300 mg 6 hourly; Child 3-6 mg/kg 6 hourly.
precautions: N/A
adverse_effects: Diarrhoea, colitis.
patient_info: Inform doctor immediately if persistent diarrhea occurs.

name: TETRACYCLINE
indications: Aphthous ulcers; Periodontal diseases.
dosage_schedule: Adult: 1 g daily in 2-4 divided doses (max 2 g/day). Children: 20-40 mg/kg/day in 2-4 divided doses.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to tetracycline; Renal failure; SLE; Pregnant women and nursing mothers; Children less than 8 years of age.
precautions: Deposits in teeth causing yellow discoloration; avoid in late pregnancy and young children.
adverse_effects: Permanent tooth discoloration; diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, light-sensitive rashes, Benign Intracranial hypertension, Pancreatitis, Pseudomembranous colitis.
patient_info: Do not take during pregnancy as it affects the unborn baby's tooth development.

name: NYSTATIN
indications: Oral candidiasis (Oral thrush); Denture stomatitis; Candidal angular cheilitis.
dosage_form_strength: 5,00,000 unit tablets; 100,000 unit/gm cream; Oral pastille (200,000 units).
dosage_schedule: Thrush: Hold 5 ml (infant 2 ml) of suspension in oral cavity for several minutes 4 times daily before swallowing. Pastille: Dissolve slowly in mouth 5 times a day.
precautions: For denture stomatitis, may be used as a gel with 0.2% chlorhexidine.
adverse_effects: N/A
patient_info: Stool may become green or black; this is harmless. Do not swallow suspension immediately.

name: ACYCLOVIR
indications: Cold sores (Herpes Simplex); oral lesions related to chicken pox and shingles.
dosage_schedule: 200 mg 5 times daily for 10 days. Recurrent prophylaxis: 400 mg twice daily for 10 days.
precautions: Should be administered within the first 72 hours of symptom onset.
adverse_effects: Stinging and burning sensation after application; mouth pain (buccal tablet).
patient_info: Take for the entire length of time prescribed. Seek medical advice as soon as a lesion appears.

name: POTASSIUM NITRATE
indications: Dentinal hypersensitivity.
dosage_schedule: Apply as directed by a dentist; do not use longer than 4 weeks without consultation.
precautions: Use cautiously in case of pregnancy or lactation. Pre-existing diseases should be ruled out.
adverse_effects: Vertigo, headache, hypotension, convulsions, cyanosis, methemoglobinemia.
patient_info: Stop immediately and report to the doctor if an allergic reaction occurs.

name: GLUTARALDEHYDE
indications: Symptomatic relief from dentinal hypersensitivity; Disinfectant.
dosage_schedule: Blot area dry; apply with cotton pellet or applicator tip by rubbing for 30 seconds and dry thoroughly.
precautions: Should not be given to neonates. Wearing respirators and protective clothing is mandatory when handling.
adverse_effects: Headache, nausea, rashes, brownish discolouration of skin, asthma, eye irritation.
patient_info: Avoid contact with soft tissue as it causes irritation. If contacts eyes/mucosa, rinse immediately with copious water.

name: SILVER NITRATE
indications: Desensitizing agent; Caries control; Healing oral ulcers; Astringent/Hemostatic; Disinfectant.
dosage_schedule: Apply a cotton applicator dipped in solution to the affected area 2-3 times/week for 2-3 weeks.
precautions: Patients and staff must wear eye protection and masks. Reacts rapidly with chloride to precipitate silver chloride.
adverse_effects: Dark purple or brown staining of skin; burns; argyria (blue-gray skin color) with long-term exposure.
patient_info: Do not ingest. Staining of skin and clothing can occur.

name: SODIUM FLUORIDE
indications: Caries prevention; Dentinal hypersensitivity.
dosage_schedule: In-office: Four-visit procedure at intervals of approximately one week. NaF recommended at ages 3, 7, 11, and 13.
contraindications: Children unable to expectorate; Infants younger than 6 months.
precautions: Do not use if drinking water fluoride >0.6ppm. No more than 2g of gel per tray (40% capacity).
adverse_effects: Rashes, itching, difficulty breathing, chest tightness, swelling of mouth/face.
patient_info: Do not swallow. Do not eat, drink, or rinse for at least one hour after application.

name: CHLORHEXIDINE
indications: Anti-plaque; Initial periodontal therapy; Postsurgical oral hygiene; Gingival enlargements; Post-extraction bacteremia prevention.
dosage_form_strength: Mouthwash (0.12% or 0.2%); Gel (1%); Spray (0.2%); Periochip (2.5 mg).
dosage_schedule: Rinse with 10ml of 0.2% mouthwash twice daily for 2 weeks.
contraindications: Not usually indicated for patients under 18 years; Allergic to Chlorhexidine.
precautions: Do not add water to the rinse. Do not swallow. Categorised under Category B and C for pregnancy.
adverse_effects: Extrinsic brown staining of teeth and restorations; impaired taste sensation; dryness and soreness of mucosa; painful desquamative lesions.
patient_info: Rinse 30 minutes after brushing teeth. Swish for at least 30 seconds. Avoid eating or drinking immediately after use.

name: DOXYCYCLINE HYCLATE (SDD)
indications: Adjunct to scaling and root planing (SRP) for chronic or aggressive periodontitis.
dosage_schedule: 20 mg taken twice a day for 3 months (maximum 9 months).
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to tetracyclines; Pregnancy and lactation; Children < 12 years.
precautions: Should not be used as a stand-alone therapy. Prescribe to coincide with first episode of SRP.
adverse_effects: Generally well tolerated.
interactions: Reduces efficacy of oral contraceptive pills.
patient_info: Compliance with maintenance regimen is critical. Use alternative birth control measures.

name: GELFOAM
indications: Control of minor bleeding in oral and dental surgery.
dosage_schedule: Place dry or moistened rolled pack into the cavity/socket. Apply light finger pressure for 1-2 minutes.
contraindications: Closure of skin incisions (interferes with healing); Allergy to porcine collagen.
precautions: Not recommended in presence of frank infection. Avoid over-packing as it expands when fluid is absorbed.
adverse_effects: Giant cell granuloma, hematoma formation, toxic shock syndrome, failure of absorption.
patient_info: Do not wash mouth vigorously within 24 hours of placement.

name: BONE WAX
indications: Local hemostasis of bone (tamponade) in visualized vascular channels ('bone bleeders').
dosage_form_strength: Sterile beeswax, paraffin, and isopropyl palmitate mixture.
dosage_schedule: Warm to desired consistency and apply to bone edges.
contraindications: Procedures where rapid osseous regeneration and fusion are desired.
precautions: Use sparingly. Do not manipulate with latex gloves (latex proteins may cause allergic reaction). Do not resterilize.
adverse_effects: Mild inflammatory reactions; may enhance existing infection; inhibits osteogenesis.
patient_info: N/A

name: TRANEXAMIC ACID
indications: Dental extractions in patients with hemophilia to reduce hemorrhage.
dosage_form_strength: 5% mouthwash (500 mg tablet in 10ml water); 10mg/kg body weight IV.
dosage_schedule: 10 mg/kg IV repeated every 4-6 hourly for 2-8 days.
contraindications: Active intravascular clotting; acquired defective colour vision; hypersensitivity.
precautions: Reduce dose in renal insufficiency. Caution in upper urinary tract bleeding.
adverse_effects: Nausea, diarrhoea, headache, giddiness, thrombophlebitis of injected veins, convulsions.
patient_info: May cause dizziness; use caution while driving.

name: PILOCARPINE
indications: Treatment of dry mouth (xerostomia) secondary to drug/radiation induction or Sjogren’s syndrome.
dosage_schedule: Adult: Initially 2.5 mg to 5 mg TID. Titration up to 30 mg per day at variable intervals.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity; uncontrolled asthma; cardiovascular diseases; narrow angle glaucoma.
precautions: Caution in cholelithiasis or biliary tract disease. Monitor in renal/liver impairment.
adverse_effects: Sweating, nausea, flushing, rhinitis, increased salivation, tachycardia, taste perversion.
patient_info: May cause visual disturbances, especially at night; avoid driving. If excessive sweating occurs, drink plenty of fluids to avoid dehydration.

name: TACROLIMUS
indications: Autoimmune mucosal lesions; vesiculobullous lesions; second-line therapy for moderate to severe atopic dermatitis.
dosage_schedule: Apply topically morning and evening twice daily as a thin layer to affected areas.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity; long-term use (risk of lymphoma/skin malignancy).
precautions: Avoid UV light/sunlight. Avoid contact with eyes and mucous membranes.
adverse_effects: Application-site infections, burning, stinging, rash.
patient_info: N/A
